## Revised prompt template

Ordered so the highest-value instructions sit early. Fits comfortably in 7,000 characters.

```
[FORMAT]
{duration} seconds, 16:9, one continuous unbroken take.

[CAMERA]
Locked-off camera on a tripod, {focal length}, {height}. The framing is
identical in the first frame and the last frame. No pan, tilt, zoom, dolly,
push, rack, or reframe at any point. Do not cut. Do not change angle.

[REFERENCES]
Image 1 is the exact opening frame. Image 2 is the exact closing frame.
[Image 3 is the identity reference for {character} — match face, hair,
facial hair and build only; take nothing else from it.]

[CAST — EXACT COUNT]
Exactly {N} people are in this shot for its entire duration: {list them}.
No one else appears at any time. No one enters or leaves frame. No person
appears in a doorway, window, mirror, reflection, or background.

[IDENTITY]
{existing per-character feature lists — keep verbatim}

[SET AND PROPS]
{room, furniture, and their fixed positions}. Every object stays where it
is. {Named prop} keeps the same shape, size, colour, and count for the
whole shot.

[LIGHTING]
{explicit, and bright — see note below}

[SHOT LIST]
[0–2 s] {what the picture does}
[2–5 s] {what the picture does}
[5–{duration} s] {what the picture does}

[DIALOGUE TIMING]
{existing dialogue blocks — keep verbatim}

[AUDIO]
{existing audio suppression line — keep verbatim}

[DO NOT]
No cut, no camera move, no angle change, no dissolve, no morph.
No additional person at any time. No duplicate of any character.
No text, lettering, signage, captions, subtitles, watermarks, or logos
anywhere in frame, including on furniture, walls, screens, and packaging.
No object appearing, disappearing, or changing shape.
No change to any face between the first frame and the last.
```

Two notes on filling it in.

**Lighting.** Write it explicitly and write it bright. The dim interiors are where identity fails — scene 13's night table, scene 16, scene 17 — while the daylight driving clip `14D` is among the cleanest in the film. A dark scene compresses face contrast into a narrow tonal band on top of an already tiny face, and the two effects compound. Keep a scene's mood by all means, but lift the key.

**The text prohibition needs to be that specific.** `11C` put "MiniMAX H3 BRNTWOOD" on the counter front and `12C` wrote "SNS RPJE SR1" on a screen. A generic `text artifacts` did not stop either. Name the surfaces.

## What to leave alone

- **Identity feature lists.** Already exactly what technique 5 asks for.
- **Audio suppression.** Already specific and correctly aimed.
- **Dialogue timecodes.** Already in the format the guide recommends, and demonstrably obeyed.
- **20 steps, `res_multistep` / `simple`, denoise 1.0, non-Turbo, 24 fps, the frame-count rule.** Nothing in the guide touches these, and they are project invariants.

1. **Raise the resolution and measure.** One clip, everything else held constant. This is a settings change, not a prompt change, and it plausibly dominates everything else on this list.

3. **Add a camera block and a visual shot list to every prompt.** The largest prompt-side gap, and it targets the cut and drift failures directly.

5. **State the exact cast count positively in every multi-person clip.**
6. **Investigate passing the character sheet as an identity reference** — but check the API graph supports it first.

chunks.heading: # Model Conversion & Profiling — PowerInfer preparation track
chunks.text:
# Model Conversion & Profiling — PowerInfer preparation track

## Purpose and current compatibility boundary

This track is the mandatory, offline preparation path for models proposed for
the PowerInfer control-plane endpoint. It covers base checkpoints, abliterated
derivatives, and post-LoRA merged checkpoints as candidate inputs. It does not
authorize a download, merge, profile, conversion, GPU load, or deployment.

The desired artifact layout is a model-specific bundle containing:

```text
<model-id>/<build-id>/
  source/                 # immutable source manifest + hash; not a duplicate model by default
  calibration/            # license-approved, sanitized, versioned calibration manifest
  activation/             # layer activation profiles; never mixed between model revisions
  predictor/              # predictor weights matched to the exact architecture/revision
  output/<model>.powerinfer.gguf
  output/<model>.q4.powerinfer.gguf
  validation/             # prompt set, raw measurements, report, hashes
  manifest.json           # lineage, tool commits, hashes, license, acceptance state
```

## Non-negotiable compatibility gate

The official PowerInfer conversion procedure takes **original compatible model
weights plus compatible predictor weights** and produces a `.powerinfer.gguf`.
PowerInfer lists a limited set of supported sparse families and says normal
llama.cpp-compatible weights receive no sparse performance gain. The inspected
documentation does not establish a maintained, general-purpose offline solver
that creates trustworthy predictor weights for every arbitrary dense,
abliterated, or post-LoRA checkpoint. See the [upstream PowerInfer README](https://github.com/Tiiny-AI/PowerInfer).

Therefore the pipeline has two routes:

1. **Supported sparse route:** exact architecture/revision with an upstream or
   independently validated predictor and activation-statistics source. Convert,
   quantize, and validate.
2. **Research route:** an otherwise unsupported model is catalogued and tested
   for a documented profiler/predictor-training method first. If no supported
   method, it remains an Ollama/llama.cpp candidate; it is not labeled or
   deployed as a PowerInfer model.

No predictor, activation profile, GPU index, calibration result, or final GGUF
may be reused across base revisions, quantizations, abliterated variants, or
post-LoRA merges without a documented evidence-backed compatibility result.

## Standard offline pipeline

No predictor, activation profile, GPU index, calibration result, or final GGUF
may be reused across base revisions, quantizations, abliterated variants, or
post-LoRA merges without a documented evidence-backed compatibility result.

## Standard offline pipeline

### Stage 0 — intake and eligibility

1. Assign immutable `model_id` and `build_id`; record source repository,
   revision/commit, architecture, license, model card, and SHA-256 for every
   input shard.
2. Classify input as `base`, `abliterated`, or `post_lora_merge`; record merge
   tool/version and adapter hashes for the last category.
3. Check the architecture against PowerInfer's supported sparse route and
   identify the exact predictor/activation provenance. Fail closed to the
   normal runtime when absent.
4. Reserve a controlled GPU-gateway window. The RTX 5080 must have no ComfyUI,
   VLM, render, or interactive-chat owner before profiling begins.

### Stage 1 — immutable staging and calibration contract

1. Keep source weights read-only after hashing. Never edit a source shard in
   place.
2. Create a calibration manifest, not an unreviewed data dump: source/license,
   redaction status, prompt IDs, expected language/domain mix, and hash.
3. Exclude personal chats, private creative work, credentials, protected story
   assets, and unlicensed corpora. Use a small approved calibration set first.
4. Pin the profiler/converter commit, Python environment lock, CUDA/driver
   version, and hardware inventory in `manifest.json`.

### Stage 2 — profile or obtain predictors

1. For the supported route, obtain matching predictor weights and activation
   files with hashes and license evidence.
2. For the research route, run only a separately approved, documented
   predictor-training/profiling implementation on the pinned calibration
   manifest. Treat its outputs as experimental until the validation gates pass.
3. Store activation files under the build-specific directory. Never overwrite
   prior profiles; a changed calibration manifest creates a new build ID.
4. Record wall time, peak VRAM, peak system RAM, disk I/O, tool output status,
   and any numerical errors. A failed profile is quarantined with metadata, not
   promoted or silently retried with different data.

### Stage 3 — convert, quantize, and package

1. Convert only the exact input/predictor pair to `<model>.powerinfer.gguf`.
2. Produce Q4_0 only where the pinned runtime supports it; retain source and
   conversion logs separately from the production artifact.
3. Generate an artifact manifest containing parent hashes, converter command
   fingerprint (arguments without secrets), output SHA-256, size, quantization,
   and expected runtime/version.
4. Keep generated GPU-index files and runtime caches in `runtime/`, not under
   the immutable output bundle; delete none automatically.

3. Generate an artifact manifest containing parent hashes, converter command
   fingerprint (arguments without secrets), output SHA-256, size, quantization,
   and expected runtime/version.
4. Keep generated GPU-index files and runtime caches in `runtime/`, not under
   the immutable output bundle; delete none automatically.

### Stage 4 — offline validation and release decision

1. Run deterministic smoke prompts and a fixed held-out coherence suite against
   both source baseline and converted candidate using equivalent sampling. The
   initial local implementation is `tools/powerinfer/quality_comparison.py`:
   it prepares ten benign reviewer-scored cases without starting either model,
   and verifies the completed score record separately.
2. Measure cold start, warm start, prompt throughput, decode throughput,
   peak VRAM, peak RAM, GPU/CPU utilization, and error/restart rate.
3. Inspect tool-call JSON, multilingual/long-context outputs where relevant,
   refusal behavior, and character/LoRA regression prompts where relevant.
4. Promote only an accepted manifest to the loopback PowerInfer registry. The
   proxy remains unlaunched until the GPU gateway is approved for the specific
   test.

## Storage and lifecycle policy

| Class | Location | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Source checkpoints | dedicated model vault outside the repository | hashed, read-only, no duplicate copies unless explicitly needed |
| Calibration manifests | repository metadata | sanitized, licensed, no private raw text |
| Private calibration/result content | encrypted artifact store outside repository | AES-256-GCM; access logged; never commit |
| Activation/predictor outputs | model vault per `model_id/build_id` | immutable once validation begins |
| Final GGUFs + manifests | model vault `production/` or `quarantine/` | only manifest-accepted builds may enter production |
| Logs/caches/GPU indexes | runtime scratch location | bounded retention, no automatic evidence deletion |

Budget before a run: free disk must cover source weights, profile/predictor
artifacts, final GGUF, temporary conversion workspace, and a 20% safety margin.
The staging process must refuse rather than overwriting an existing bundle.

`tools/powerinfer/init_vault.py` implements that layout. Preferred root is
`D:\PowerInferModels` (outside the git tree). It creates `production/`,
`quarantine/`, `scratch/`, `private/`, and `keys/`, plus per-build
`source/`, `calibration/`, `activation/`, `predictor/`, `output/`,
`validation/`, and `runtime/`. `preflight` refuses when free disk is below
need plus 20%. `protect-source` hashes then marks shards read-only.
Private calibration/results are AES-256-GCM envelopes under `private/` with
an append-only `access.log`. There is no delete path for conversion
evidence. The runner in `run_pipeline.ps1` is not yet required to call this
tool on every stage.

## Native runner (opt-in, unlaunched)

`tools/powerinfer/run_pipeline.ps1` is the Windows orchestrator for this track.
It parameterizes two targets in `tools/powerinfer/models.json`:

- `prosparse-7b` — supported-sparse proof of concept (`f=11008`, SentencePiece).
- `llama31-8b-abliterated-relu` — research route after ReLUfication (`f=14336`,
  `--vocabtype bpe`). SiLU abliterated Llama-3.1 checkpoints fail `relu-gate`.

Dump, train, convert, quantize, package, and the 20-turn acceptance gate are
shared. GPU/download/CMake work requires `-Execute`. The runner does not promote
a bundle to the interactive picker. Live compile and benchmark numbers are not
established until that execute path is run on an idle RTX 5080.

## Dependency links

### A. Real-time interactive Control Plane

No model may be listed in the PowerInfer proxy/model picker until its accepted
bundle manifest, sparse compatibility evidence, baseline comparison, and
GPU-gateway approval exist. Existing Ollama models remain unchanged.

### B. Harmon Town Nothing Forever character LoRA stage

After an approved LoRA merge: create a new candidate build ID and repeat
Stages 0–4. A base model's predictor/activation set cannot be assumed valid for
the merged character model. Until it passes, use the existing normal inference
route rather than blocking character work on experimental conversion.

### C. Judge evaluation loop

The Judge queue may reference only a registry-approved PowerInfer model by
immutable build ID. Batch workers do not perform conversion or profile a model
while handling user data. An unaccepted candidate stays out of the judge
fallback/routing table.

## Production acceptance checklist

- [ ] Source, adapter/merge (if any), calibration manifest, predictor,
  activation profile, converter, and final GGUF all have verified SHA-256
  lineage in one manifest.
- [ ] Architecture and runtime compatibility is evidenced; no unsupported dense
  checkpoint is represented as sparse PowerInfer-ready.
- [ ] License/provenance for weights, predictor, and calibration source is
  documented and acceptable.
- [ ] Conversion completed without numerical/converter errors; output loads in
  the exact pinned PowerInfer build.
- [ ] Baseline versus candidate held-out prompts meet the declared coherence,
  instruction following, tool-call, and character-consistency threshold.
- [ ] Cold/warm latency, decode rate, VRAM/RAM peak, GPU/CPU utilization, and
  failure rate are recorded under the same hardware conditions.
- [ ] Candidate does not interfere with ComfyUI, VLM, render, or active chat;
  the GPU gateway approved the controlled test and resources are released.
- [ ] Human reviewer accepts the evidence report; registry status changes from
  `candidate` to `accepted`. Otherwise it remains `quarantine` with its logs.

# Next-steps runbook — written for zero prior knowledge (2026-08-29)

This assumes you've never run a command in a terminal before. Every command
is something you type yourself on your Windows computer — nothing here runs
by itself, and nothing here happens just from reading this document.

## The basics you need before any of the sections below

**What's a "terminal" / "PowerShell window"?** It's a plain black or dark-blue
window where you type text commands instead of clicking icons. You'll open
one, type a line of text, press **Enter**, and it does something and prints
text back at you.

**Two different kinds of PowerShell window matter here:**
- **Ordinary PowerShell** — click the Start button, type `powershell`, press
  Enter. Fine for sections 2, 3, and 4 below.
- **"Developer PowerShell for VS 2022"** — a special version that also knows
  where your CUDA/compiler tools live. Required for section 1 (PowerInfer).
  Click Start, type `developer powershell`, and click the result called
  **"Developer PowerShell for VS 2022"** (not plain PowerShell, not "Developer
  Command Prompt"). If it's not there, Visual Studio 2022 with the Desktop
  C++ workload needs installing first — stop and say so if that's the case.
  Section 1 also needs CUDA Toolkit 12.8+ (`nvcc`, targeting `sm_120`)
  already installed; if that's missing, stop there too. This document does
  not walk through those installs.

**How to get to the right folder.** Every section below starts by pasting
this into whichever PowerShell window you just opened:

```powershell
cd "A:\Users\rhine\Documents\Codex\2026-08-07\referenced-chatgpt-conversation-this-is-an-2\COMFYUI_STORY_HANDOFF_2026-08-09"
```

Press Enter. Nothing dramatic happens — the prompt just changes to show
you're now "in" that folder. If you see a red error instead, the path is
wrong; double check it matches the folder on your machine exactly.

**How to copy a command from this document into the window.** Select the
text of the command in this document (click and drag over it, or triple-click
the line), press **Ctrl+C**, click inside the PowerShell window so it's the
active window, then press **Ctrl+V** (or right-click, which also pastes in
PowerShell). Then press **Enter** to actually run it — pasting alone does not
run it.

**How to tell if a command worked.** After it finishes, look at the last few
lines it printed:
- Red text starting with something like `Exception` or ending in
  `throw` usually means it failed. Read the message — the scripts in this
  project are written to explain in plain English *why* they refused, not
  just "error 1."
- If it just returns you to a normal prompt with no red text, it worked.
- Some steps also print their own "ok" / "done" / a summary — those are
  designed to be readable, not just log noise.

**If anything prints something you don't understand and it's not obviously
one of the "expected" messages below**, stop and paste the exact text back

## Section 1 — PowerInfer: prove the pipeline works on `relu-llama-7b`

This is the live, already-compatible sparse model to test with first
(`SparseLLM/ReluLLaMA-7B`, plain ReLU, `hidden_act` is `relu`) before ever
touching your actual Llama-3.1 model. It downloads several gigabytes and
uses your graphics card, so budget real time for this — the "train" step
especially can take a long while.

**Do not use `-ModelId prosparse-7b`.** That id is parked and retired.
The checkpoint already on disk at
`C:\PowerInferVault\prosparse-7b\20260829-prosparse` is FATReLU /
`SparseLlamaForCausalLM`, not plain ReLU. Running the relu-gate on that
vault is **expected to fail** with exit code 2. That is not a broken
download. Do not continue past a FATReLU fail. Do not bypass the gate.
Do not tell anyone (including another LLM session) to skip this check
or to treat ProSparse as the thing to compile and run.

### 1.0 — Before you type anything: two tools must already be installed,

2. **Visual Studio 2022** with the **Desktop C++** workload.

try to compile anyway. Tell the next session which one is missing.
This document does not walk through installing those — they are

You also must use **"Developer PowerShell for VS 2022"** (see the
basics at the top of this document), not ordinary PowerShell, for
every compile step in this section. Developer PowerShell is the window
that knows where the CUDA/compiler tools live.

Open that Developer PowerShell window, then type:

```powershell
nvcc --version
```

and press Enter. You want a version of **12.8 or higher**. If it says

window, or CUDA Toolkit isn't installed. **Stop.** If the version is

Then check the graphics card is free. In the same window, type:

```powershell
nvidia-smi
```

and press Enter. You'll see a table. Near the bottom is a list of
"Processes" — this shows anything currently using the graphics card. As long
as ComfyUI, a render, or anything you don't recognize isn't listed there,
you're clear to continue. If something IS using it, close that program first.

drive, and not inside this project's own folder. Setting
`$env:POWERINFER_VAULT` only lasts for this PowerShell window. If you close
the window or open a new one, paste both lines again before any other

### 1.3 — Download and build PowerInfer itself (this is the big one — expect
several minutes to tens of minutes depending on your internet and CPU)

Only do this after step 1.0 showed `nvcc` 12.8+ and Developer PowerShell
for VS 2022. If those were missing, you should have already stopped.

```powershell
.\tools\powerinfer\run_pipeline.ps1 -ModelId relu-llama-7b -Stage setup -Execute
```

What this does, in order: downloads the PowerInfer source code from GitHub,
creates a private Python environment just for this tool, installs a bunch of
Python packages (including a large one for CUDA — this is the slow download
part), then compiles the C++/CUDA program itself (the slow CPU part).

**If it stops early with `nvcc not on PATH`:** you opened plain PowerShell
instead of "Developer PowerShell for VS 2022," or CUDA Toolkit isn't
installed. Close this window. If Developer PowerShell + CUDA 12.8+ are
actually missing, **stop** (see step 1.0). If you just opened the wrong
window, reopen the correct one, repeat step 1.1, and start again from

## Section 1B — Actually talk to it: start the server and connect local_agent

This is what makes Section 1's work useful instead of just a file sitting on

## Section 3 — Add a second worker laptop (on hold for now)

Correction from earlier: the laptop is actually a **Mac**, not Windows — the
walkthrough below was written for Windows on both ends and is wrong for a
Mac (different WireGuard app, different install steps, different way of
finding the IP address). Since PowerInfer + local_agent (Sections 1 and 1B)
is the actual priority right now, this section is left as-is rather than
rewritten twice — say when you're ready to come back to it and it'll get
redone with correct Mac steps for the laptop side and Windows steps for the
workstation side.

This connects two machines over an encrypted private tunnel so the laptop
can safely reach the workstation's task queue. It has more moving parts than
the sections above — go slowly and confirm each piece before moving to the
next.

### 3.1 — Install WireGuard on both machines

On **both** the workstation and the laptop:

1. Open a browser, go to `https://www.wireguard.com/install/`.
2. Download and run the **Windows** installer.
3. Once installed, open the "WireGuard" app from the Start menu. It shows an
   empty list of tunnels.

### 3.2 — Find each machine's local network address

On **each** machine (workstation and laptop, separately), open plain
PowerShell and type:

```powershell
ipconfig
```

Look for a section called `Wireless LAN adapter Wi-Fi` (or `Ethernet
adapter` if it's wired) and find the line `IPv4 Address`. It'll look like
`192.168.1.XX`. Write down the workstation's number and the laptop's number
— you'll need both in the next step.

### 3.3 — Create the tunnel on the workstation

In the WireGuard app on the **workstation**, click **"Add Tunnel"** →
**"Add empty tunnel..."**. It creates a new tunnel and automatically fills
in a `PrivateKey` line for you — leave that alone. Replace the rest of the
text box so the whole thing reads:

```
[Interface]
PrivateKey = <leave whatever WireGuard already put here>
Address = 10.90.90.1/30
ListenPort = 51820

[Peer]
PublicKey = <you'll fill this in during step 3.5>
AllowedIPs = 10.90.90.2/32
Endpoint = <laptop's IPv4 address from step 3.2>:51820
PersistentKeepalive = 25
```

Name the tunnel something like `EqualSharesTunnel`. Don't click Activate
yet — you're missing the laptop's public key.

Click the tunnel name in the list; WireGuard shows its own **Public key**
for this tunnel near the top. Copy it somewhere safe (Notepad is fine) —
you'll paste it into the laptop's config in a moment.

### 3.5 — Finish the workstation side

Go back to the workstation's WireGuard window, edit the tunnel you made in

On both machines, click the toggle switch next to the tunnel name to
activate it. It should turn green / say "Active."

ping 10.90.90.2

## Section 4 — Decide where backups go

This section is a decision to make, not really a command to run yet. Before
anything is backed up, answer these for yourself (pen and paper, or a text
file — just don't put it in this project's folder where it could get
committed):

1. **Where's the main backup going?** A dedicated external hard drive you
   plug in, or an online storage service you already pay for? Either is
   fine — pick one you actually have access to.
2. **Where's the second copy?** Backups should exist in two places. If your
   main copy is a drive at your desk, the second should be somewhere else —
   a different physical location, or a different online service.
3. **Who remembers the password?** The backup tool encrypts everything with
   a password. If you forget it, the backup is unrecoverable — that's by
   design, for privacy. Decide now: a password manager you already use, plus
   a written copy stored somewhere physical (like a safe), is a solid
   answer.
4. **When will you actually test restoring a file?** Pick an actual date —
   "someday" means it never happens, and an untested backup might not work
   when you need it.

Once you've actually decided all four of those, `docs/ENCRYPTED_ARCHIVAL_RUNBOOK.md`
in this project has the exact command sequence to run — it was intentionally
left waiting on these decisions rather than guessing at them for you.

chunks.heading: # What the official ComfyUI H3 docs confirm, and what they change
chunks.text:
# What the official ComfyUI H3 docs confirm, and what they change

Source: <https://docs.comfy.org/tutorials/video/minimax/minimax-h3>
Read 2026-08-15.

---

## Confirmed — keep doing these

**Reference by tag, in connection order.** `<Picture 1>`, `<Video 1>`, `<Audio 1>`.
Tags follow the exact order the inputs were connected, which is why
`audio_pass_config.json` fixes the `ref_audio` index order per clip and why `09B`
and `09C` differ despite both being Kent and Avery.

**Give every reference an explicit job.** The docs put it plainly: *"State which
reference drives which part of the shot (identity, style, motion, camera, voice).
Explicit assignments tend to work much better."* This is the REFERENCE JOBS block,
and it is officially endorsed rather than a local invention.

**Frame count.** *"The duration input snaps to the model's 17-frame-per-block
(17k+5) grid at 24fps."* Exactly the mod-17 rule already in `CLAUDE.md`.

**R2V uses a different checkpoint from T2V/I2V.** ref2va for reference work,
fl2va for first/last-frame work. Already the project's three-path table.

**Reference limits: 9 images, 3 videos, 3 standalone audio clips.** The project's
worst case is 3 speakers in `27E`, so it fits, but there is no headroom for a
fourth speaking character in one shot.

---

## New — worth acting on

### 1. `ref_image_size: max` may be the face fix

> `match` scales references down to the generation resolution for speed; **`max`
> keeps up to a 2048px short edge for stronger identity fidelity** at the cost of
> speed.

Every render in this project has used `match`, which throws away reference
detail at exactly the moment identity is being decided. Reference sheets are
already 1672×941, so `max` has real detail to use.

This is a one-word change and a plausible answer to the face-drift problem that
drove the whole 0.9 MP investigation. **Test it on one clip.**

### 2. An int8 ref2va checkpoint exists

The docs name the R2V model as `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot`. This
project uses `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_nvfp4` — a more aggressively quantised
variant. The 00J audit already flagged nvfp4 as the reason to doubt ref2va at
0.9 MP.

If the int8 ref2va is on disk, it is worth a comparison. **If it is not, it is a
multi-GB download and stays blocked on the hotspot** — do not fetch it without
agreement.

  `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3/blob/main/docs/VIDEO_PROMPT_WRITING_GUIDE_base_en.md`
- **Reference mode (R2V)**:
  `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3/blob/main/docs/VIDEO_PROMPT_WRITING_GUIDE_ref_en.md`

The R2V guide covers *"the rewrite output structure, including subject
definitions, reference labels, and retention analysis, and how to assign each
reference a role."* "Retention analysis" is not a concept this project has been
using and may be directly relevant to the doubled-vocal problem — it is about
deciding what to keep from a reference and what to discard.

MiniMax also ships installable H3 skills including a prompt-writing skill.
Both guides are text files, so they are cheap to fetch.

### 4. Native canvas is ~1.0 MP, and this project deliberately runs below it

> *"For full-quality output, raise Megapixels to about `1.0` at 16:9, which
> yields roughly 1344×768: H3's native canvas."*

This project measured 1.0 MP breaking camera control on clip 11 and settled on
0.9 MP. **That empirical result stands** — it was observed directly. But it means
the project runs just under native, and the completion criteria in `CLAUDE.md`
still call for a 1344×768 master, so the film is upscaled slightly at assembly.

Worth knowing rather than changing. The camera failure was real.

### 5. Sage Attention warnings are expected

> *"MiniMax H3 runs some layers in other dtypes, so you may see 'Input tensors
> must be in dtype of torch.float16 or torch.bfloat16, using pytorch attention
> instead' messages. These are expected."*

If those appear in a render log, they are not a fault and not worth debugging.

---

## Nothing in the docs explains the doubled vocal layer

The docs do not mention voice duplication, echo, or reference leakage. So the
doubling remains unexplained by official guidance, and the live suspects are
unchanged:

1. the master reaching the model more than once (a second socket, or a reference
   video still carrying its audio track),
2. the master being long enough to supply material to replay, or
3. something the R2V "retention analysis" section addresses, which has not been
   read yet.

Reading `VIDEO_PROMPT_WRITING_GUIDE_ref_en.md` is the cheapest next step.

chunks.heading: # Opening sequence — rewritten shot lists
chunks.text:
# Opening sequence — rewritten shot lists

Scene 000, clips `00A` through `00O`. **Shot lists only.** Camera, cast, identity, lighting, dialogue timing, audio and prohibitions are unchanged — drop these blocks in place of the `SHOT LIST` section in column U.

Staging read from `boundary_narrator_close_v3.png` and `boundary_entry_start_v2.png`: bare walls, **one chair far screen-left**, **service window centre-right with the receptionist framed inside it, hands folded on the sill**, **open doorway far screen-right with a lit corridor behind it**. The receptionist's rest pose is hands folded, eyes level, mouth closed. Every beat below returns her to that pose so the model has something to come back to.

## Two rules applied to every beat

**Business is anchored to a phrase, not to a stopwatch.** Each block starts where a phrase of narration starts. A beat that begins mid-phrase reads as an accident; one that begins on a phrase reads as direction.

**Mouths are locked shut, explicitly, in every block.** The muttering is the model inventing speech for anyone whose face is visible while audio is playing. It will not stop because the prompt says it once at the bottom — it has to be denied in the same block that gives the person something to do, because that is where the model decides what their face is doing.

---

## `00A` — 15 s, narration 1–14 s

> "In a world of total equality, / fairness, kindness, and other generous human traits / get out of control."

```
SHOT LIST
[0-1 s] Held. The Narrator stands still in the left foreground, weight even, one breath before speaking. The receptionist sits framed in the service window at right, hands folded on the sill, eyes level, mouth closed. The public room is empty. No one is in the doorway.
[1-4.5 s] "In a world of total equality" - the Narrator speaks to camera, head still, hands at his sides. Behind him the receptionist unfolds her hands, squares a small stack of forms against the sill in two taps, and sets them down. She does not look at the Narrator. Her mouth stays closed.
[4.5-10 s] "fairness, kindness, and other generous human traits" - the Narrator's expression sobers slightly; he does not gesture. The receptionist takes the top form, lowers it into a slot below the sill, and refolds her hands into the rest pose. Her eyes stay down on her own work throughout. Her mouth stays closed.
[10-14 s] "get out of control" - the Narrator holds the camera. The receptionist lifts her chin and looks once along the empty room toward the doorway, as though expecting someone who has not arrived, then returns her eyes level and her hands folded. Her mouth stays closed.
[14-15 s] Held. The Narrator finishes and stays still. The receptionist is back in the exact rest pose she started in. Nothing else moves.

Only the Narrator speaks. The receptionist's mouth is completely closed in every frame: no muttering, no mouthed words, no lip movement, no chewing, no talking to herself, no speaking into the corridor behind her.
```

> "If all people feel that someone without should be helped so they are no longer without, / but in the process they become without, / how do people really help each other?"

```

[1-6 s] "If all people feel that someone without should be helped so they are no longer without" - the camera pushes in on the Narrator so slowly it is barely perceptible; it never changes angle or side. The receptionist opens a ledger on the sill and rules a single line across a page with a straight edge. Her mouth stays closed.
[6-9.5 s] "but in the process they become without" - the Narrator's delivery cools. The receptionist stops mid-stroke, lifts the straight edge, and looks at what she has drawn for a beat too long, as though the line came out wrong. She does not look up. Her mouth stays closed.
[9.5-14 s] "how do people really help each other?" - the Narrator holds the question on camera. The receptionist closes the ledger, sets it aside, and returns her hands to the folded rest pose on the sill. Her mouth stays closed.
[14-15 s] Held. Nobody moves. The room is still empty.

Only the Narrator speaks. The receptionist's mouth is completely closed in every frame: no muttering, no mouthed words, no lip movement, no counting under her breath.
```

[0.5-4 s] "When no one else feels that they are more important than the next person" - the camera begins moving past the Narrator into the room. He stays exactly where he is and does not turn to follow it; he continues addressing the lens he is leaving. The receptionist's hands stay folded and her eyes stay level. Her mouth stays closed.

## `00D` — 12 s, narration 1–5 s, dual anchor

Narration covers five seconds of a twelve-second clip. The remaining seven are pure action and were previously undirected — this is the clip where the men's business has to carry the shot on its own.

> "If there's one chair in a room and two people."

```
SHOT LIST
[0-1 s] Held on the empty public room. The receptionist is folded in the window. The doorway at screen-right is empty.
[1-2.5 s] "If there's one chair in a room" - Male Visitor One steps through the doorway at screen-right and walks into the public room. He does not hesitate or look around. The receptionist unfolds her hands as she registers him.
[2.5-3.5 s] Male Visitor One reaches the service window and stops squarely in front of it.
[3.5-5 s] "and two people" - Male Visitor Two steps through the same doorway, exactly one second behind, and stops a pace behind Visitor One, forming a short queue. He faces forward and waits. He does not tap the first man's shoulder or lean around him.
[5-7 s] Visitor One slides a form across the sill. The receptionist stamps it once, slides it back, and nods a single small nod. No words pass between them. Visitor One steps away from the window toward the chair at screen-left.
[7-9 s] Visitor Two takes his place at the window and repeats the exchange - form across, one stamp, form back, one nod. The receptionist returns her hands to the folded rest pose. Meanwhile Visitor One has reached the chair and stopped beside it without sitting.
[9-11 s] Visitor Two crosses to the chair and stops beside Visitor One. Both men now stand on the public side, the single chair between them, and turn to face each other for the first time.
[11-12 s] Held on both men beside the chair, looking at one another, neither moving toward the seat. This is the closing frame.

Nobody speaks in this shot. Every mouth in frame is completely closed at all times: no muttering, no mouthed words, no lip movement, no silent conversation between the two men, no talking to the receptionist. The check-in is transacted entirely through the form, the stamp and the nod.
```

## `00D2` — 10 s, narration 1–9 s, dual anchor

> "Both people insist that the other person takes the seat. / Even if one does take it, the other goes without."

The gesture loop needs a stated count. Left open, the model either does it once and stalls or loops until the bodies blur.

```
SHOT LIST
[0-1 s] Held. Both men stand facing each other beside the single chair. The receptionist watches from behind the window, hands folded, mouth closed.
[1-3 s] "Both people insist" - Visitor One extends an open palm toward the chair, offering it. Visitor Two answers by raising both hands slightly and shaking his head once.
[3-5 s] "that the other person takes the seat" - Visitor Two returns the offer, gesturing to the chair with an open palm. Visitor One declines with a small bow of the head and a hand to his own chest. Exactly two offers have now been made, one each.
[5-7 s] A third and final exchange, smaller and more tired than the first two: Visitor One gestures again, Visitor Two hesitates. Their shoulders drop. This is the moment the deadlock breaks.
[7-9 s] "Even if one does take it, the other goes without" - Visitor Two gestures once more toward the chair and holds it. Visitor One yields, steps in front of the chair, and sits. Visitor Two remains standing beside him, hands returning to his sides.
[9-10 s] Held. One man seated, one man standing beside him, the receptionist still folded behind the window. This is the closing frame.

There are exactly three offer-and-refusal exchanges in this shot, no more. Nobody speaks. Every mouth in frame is completely closed at all times: no muttering, no mouthed words, no lip movement, no polite conversation, no "after you" being mouthed. The entire negotiation is carried by hands, heads and shoulders.
```

> "The sitting now looks up at the standing, / and the standing looks down at the sitting. / Both people are now filled with debilitating anxiety."

The script asks for a shot-reverse-shot feeling inside one unbroken take. That means the focus shifts, not the camera.

```
SHOT LIST

[0.5-3 s] "The sitting now looks up at the standing" - focus rests on the seated man. He raises his eyes to the standing man's face. His head lifts only slightly; the movement is in the eyes.
[3-5.5 s] "and the standing looks down at the sitting" - focus shifts to the standing man without the camera moving. He lowers his eyes to the seated man. Their eyes meet.
[5.5-7.8 s] "Both people are now filled with debilitating anxiety" - neither breaks the look. The seated man's hands close on his knees. The standing man's hands close at his sides. Both hold the eye contact past the point of comfort.
[7.8-8 s] Held on the locked look. This is the closing frame.

The focus shifts between the two men; the camera does not move, cut, or change angle. Nobody speaks. Both mouths are completely closed at all times: no muttering, no mouthed words, no lip movement, no about-to-speak mouth openings.
```

## `00F` — 15 s, narration 1–14 s, single anchor

> "One wants to give their chair away so the other can be comfortable and sit. / They won't say anything, though, because they dare not be rude by gifting a gift back to the giver."

Fifteen seconds on a near-static close-up. The tension has to come from a suppressed impulse, timed — otherwise the model fills the time itself.

```
SHOT LIST
[0-1 s] Held on the seated man, filling the frame. The standing man's hip and hand are just visible at the frame edge. The seated man is still.
[1-5 s] "One wants to give their chair away so the other can be comfortable and sit" - the seated man's weight shifts forward a few degrees. His hands come off his knees and take the front edge of the seat, as though he is about to stand.
[5-8 s] He stops. The impulse dies before it becomes movement. His hands stay on the seat edge but his weight settles back down.
[8-14 s] "They won't say anything, though, because they dare not be rude by gifting a gift back to the giver" - his lips press together and stay pressed. His eyes drop from the standing man's face to somewhere on the floor between them. His hands return to his knees. He has decided to say nothing, and the decision is visible.
[14-15 s] Held. He is seated exactly as he began, but no longer looking up.

The seated man tries to stand exactly once and stops himself. He does not rise, and he does not try a second time. Only the Narrator speaks and he is off camera. The seated man's mouth is completely closed in every frame - the pressed lips are the point. No muttering, no mouthed words, no lip movement, no words he almost says.
```

## `00H` — 15 s, narration 1–14 s, single anchor

> "Of course they would never ask for the seat that they gave to another out of kindness. / But the consequence of inaction means more suffering and waiting - waiting to take the weight off their calloused and blistered feet."

Same anchor frame as `00G`, so the business must not repeat what `00G` already did or the two clips become one.

```
SHOT LIST
[0-1 s] Held on the standing man, same framing as before. He is still.
[1-6 s] "Of course they would never ask for the seat that they gave to another out of kindness" - his shoulders lower and settle. Whatever he was holding in reserve, he gives up. His hands go loose at his sides.
[6-10 s] "But the consequence of inaction means more suffering and waiting" - he lifts one heel slightly out of his shoe and sets it back down, the smallest possible relief. His eyes go to the middle distance, past the seated man, past the room.
[10-14 s] "waiting to take the weight off their calloused and blistered feet" - the other heel lifts and settles the same way. His face empties. He is no longer negotiating with himself; he is simply waiting, and expects to keep waiting.
[14-15 s] Held. Standing, loose, blank, still.

He does not shift his full weight from foot to foot in this shot - that already happened in the previous one. Here the relief is smaller and the resignation is larger. Only the Narrator speaks and he is off camera. The standing man's mouth is completely closed in every frame: no muttering, no mouthed words, no lip movement.

## `00I` — 12 s, narration 2–11 s, single anchor

> "Both people are frozen by their own anxieties, / wanting to make the world a better place - / but at what cost?"

The freeze, the light change and the pull-back are three separate events and need to land in order.

```
SHOT LIST
[0-2 s] Both men are visible in the room, mid-gesture, the seated man looking up and the standing man looking down. Then they stop. Not slowly - they simply cease moving, holding the exact positions they were in, like a photograph.
[2-5 s] "Both people are frozen by their own anxieties" - the camera begins pulling back. The practical room lights start to dim behind the two frozen men. The receptionist is frozen in the window too, hands folded, mouth closed.
[5-8 s] "wanting to make the world a better place" - the pull-back continues and the Narrator enters the foreground from the left, stepping into a single hard spotlight. The room behind him keeps dimming. The two men have not moved a millimetre.
[8-11 s] "but at what cost?" - the Narrator settles under the spotlight and delivers the question to camera. Behind him the waiting room is now dim, the three frozen figures barely lit.
[11-12 s] Held. The Narrator lit, the room dark behind him, everyone in it still frozen. The set begins to dissolve away at the very end of the shot.

The two men and the receptionist are completely motionless from 2 s onward - no breathing, no blinking, no drift, no swaying. Only the Narrator moves and only the Narrator speaks. Every frozen mouth is completely closed: no muttering, no mouthed words, no lip movement.
```

> "Kent is at an inflection point that some call midlife. / He's done everything he can in life to be a good person."

## `00L` — 15 s, narration 1–14 s, single anchor

> "He's taken care of his mom. / He's been a loving brother and uncle. / He's always worked hard, and has always paid his debts. / He has never hesitated to help someone he has seen in need."

Four clauses, so four small internal beats. The Narrator's performance is the only variable available.

```
SHOT LIST
[0-1 s] Held. Narrator under the spotlight in the foreground, Kent frozen and dim behind him. Both still.
[1-4.5 s] "He's taken care of his mom" - the Narrator begins the list. His delivery is plain, almost administrative.
[4.5-7.5 s] "He's been a loving brother and uncle" - a small warmth enters his face on this clause and leaves again.
[7.5-11 s] "He's always worked hard, and has always paid his debts" - the warmth is gone. He states it as fact.
[11-14 s] "He has never hesitated to help someone he has seen in need" - he holds a beat longer on this one than on the three before it, as though it is the one that matters.
[14-15 s] Held. Nothing behind him has moved for the entire shot.

The Narrator does not gesture, walk, or shift his stance at any point - the four beats are carried in the face and the timing alone. Kent and the street are completely motionless: no breathing, no blinking, no drift. Only the Narrator speaks. Every frozen mouth is completely closed: no muttering, no mouthed words, no lip movement.
```

## `00M` — 15 s, narration 1–14 s, single anchor

> "But always doing the right thing does not mean the right things happen. / Kent has gone in and out of debt his entire life. / He's about to be evicted. / His mother is sick."

Four sentences that get progressively worse. This is where the Narrator's sobering happens.

```
SHOT LIST
[0-1 s] Held. Same composition, same spotlight, Kent frozen behind.

chunks.heading: # Local Agent — sanitized architecture overview
chunks.text:
# Local Agent — sanitized architecture overview

This diagram is deliberately suitable for a portfolio draft. It omits local
paths, project media, credentials, paired identities, radio settings, and model
weight locations. It distinguishes verified interfaces from experimental work.

## System boundary

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Operator[Operator] --> Desktop[Desktop browser UI]
    Phone[Phone / Sideband] -. paired LXMF, experimental transport .-> Bridge[LXMF bridge]

    subgraph Workstation[Local workstation]
        Desktop --> HTTP[HTTP server\nlocalhost only]
        Bridge --> Agent[Transport-agnostic agent loop]
        HTTP --> Agent
        Agent --> Memory[Persistent memory + approved retrieval]
        Agent --> Tools[Schema-validated tool whitelist]
        Tools --> Files[Local files / URL fetch on request]
        Tools --> Media[Lazy media analysis queue]
        Tools --> Comfy[Guarded ComfyUI controls]
        Agent --> Route[GPU / CPU router]
        Route --> GPU[GPU reasoning model\nwhen resource is free]
        Route --> CPU[CPU reasoning model\nwhen render owns GPU]
        Media --> VLM[Exact lazy VLM\nloads only for media]
    end

    Comfy --> Render[ComfyUI render backend]
```

## GPU ownership and model lifecycle

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Request[New chat or media request] --> Check{Render owner, backend,\nor foreign GPU use?}
    Check -- yes --> CPU[Route chat to CPU tier]
    Check -- yes --> Queue[Keep media job queued]
    Check -- no --> Chat{General chat?}
    Chat -- yes --> GPUChat[Use full GPU reasoning model]
    Chat -- no --> Media[Start exact lazy VLM]
    GPUChat --> RenderStarts{Render claims GPU?}
    Media --> RenderStarts
    RenderStarts -- yes --> Evict[Release agent model/VLM safely]
    Evict --> Queue
    RenderStarts -- no --> Finish[Finish request]
    Finish --> Release[Release background media model]
```

## Remote permission decision

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Inbound[Inbound LXMF message] --> Paired{Paired identity?}
    Paired -- no --> Refuse[Refuse and log]
    Paired -- yes --> Answer[Run transport-agnostic agent loop]
    Answer --> Tool{Tool requested?}
    Tool -- no --> Reply[Chunked LXMF reply]
    Tool -- yes --> Permit{Allowed for this identity\nand whitelist validation passes?}
    Permit -- no --> Deny[Deny and audit log]
    Permit -- yes --> Execute[Run allowed tool]
    Execute --> Reply
```

## Portfolio claim labels

- **Verified local components:** localhost GUI, structured tool calling, tool
  validation, model routing, private-safe H3 evaluation, and a paired Sideband
  Tier A round trip.
- **Experimental:** LoRa/RNode mesh delivery and its reliability/latency
  measurements.
- **In progress:** custom Sideband Android packaging and direct phone media
  integrations.

chunks.heading: # Case study and résumé bullets (verified work only)
chunks.text:
# Case study and résumé bullets (verified work only)

Every sentence below is backed by a changelog or a recorded test. Unmeasured
or in-progress work is labeled as such. Do not paste private paths, names,
prompts, or media into a public application.

## One-paragraph case study

I designed and implemented a **localhost-only desktop agent** that talks to
local models through **native tool calling**, keeps a **fixed tool whitelist**,
and treats **GPU ownership as a first-class lock**: a ComfyUI render wins, media
analysis waits, and interactive chat can fall back to a CPU model instead of
layer-offloading onto a busy card. Visual analysis is a **lazy, exact-pair
VLM** that loads on demand and is released afterward. Remote phone access is a
**separate LXMF transport** with paired identities and default-deny privileges;
the HTTP server stays on loopback. The system includes a **privacy-safe
evaluation harness** that fingerprints a 124-prompt corpus and reports only
aggregates plus negative-control failures.

## What is not claimed

- The custom Android Sideband APK is **in progress**, not shipped.
- LoRa/RNode is an **experimental mesh transport**; Bluetooth pairing is not
  delivery proof; packet-loss numbers do not exist yet.
- Equal Shares picture/audio production is **paused** and is not a portfolio
  completion claim.
- No public source repository has been published yet.

## Résumé / LinkedIn bullets (safe)

- Built a local multimodal agent runtime with schema-validated tool calling,
  multi-call hops, and a legacy text-protocol fallback, covered by native-tool
  tests.
- Implemented GPU/CPU routing so an interactive chat yields to a local
  diffusion backend instead of contending for VRAM.
- Added a lazy visual-language path pinned to a specific GGUF + projector pair,
  with a live caption diagnostic that loaded, produced a result, and released
  the GPU.
- Designed remote access as paired LXMF over loopback HTTP rather than a
  public API; default-deny for privileged tools; 11/11 bridge tests on the
  last recorded run.
- Shipped a privacy-preserving evaluation harness: 124/124 valid prompts,
  synthetic negative controls, aggregate-only JSON (hashes, counts, timings).
- Wrote ADRs for localhost binding, tool calling, lazy VLM/render ownership,
  explicit-feedback-only learning, and CPU/GPU fallback.

## Evidence index

See `docs/portfolio/validation_matrix.md` and `docs/LOCAL_AGENT_CURRENT_HANDOFF_2026-08-30.md`.
Review those documents before publishing any numeric claim; rerun tests if the
tree has moved.

chunks.text:
# Experimental RNode inventory (portfolio-safe)

**Status:** experimental mesh transport layer. Not a product claim.
**Source:** existing changelog and diagnostic notes. No radios were probed,
flashed, or reconfigured for this document.

This inventory is for evidence tracking. It omits COM ports, node names,
passphrases, paired identities, and any network keys.

## Hardware class

| Role | Board class recorded | Radio | Host link |
|---|---|---|---|
| Workstation | Heltec LoRa32 v3 | Semtech SX1262 | USB serial + Bluetooth to the host |
| Phone companion | ESP32 LoRa V3 class (LilyGO/Heltec family; phone-side exact SKU not independently re-verified here) | LoRa in the 850–950 MHz capable class | Bluetooth to the phone |

A board is not an RNode until compatible **RNode firmware** is present and a
deliberate radio profile is applied. The workstation diagnostic found **no
stored TNC radio profile**, so the bridge must supply the agreed values.

## Recorded radio profile (workstation, after SF12 update)

Values below are operating assumptions already written into project changelogs.
They are **not** a regulatory determination.

| Parameter | Recorded value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 914.875 MHz | US 915 MHz ISM-class setting already in use |
| Bandwidth | 500 kHz | |
| Spreading factor | 12 | Updated 2026-08-25 from the earlier SF7 phone screenshot |
| Coding rate | 5 | |
| Transmit power | 10 dBm | Well below the SX1262 22 dBm maximum reported by `rnodeconf --info` |
| Wi-Fi on the radio | disabled | Host-controlled mode |
| Bluetooth on the radio | enabled | **Host-to-board cable replacement only** |

## What Bluetooth pairing is not

Bluetooth (or USB serial) only attaches the radio to its host. It does **not**
prove:

- Reticulum path establishment;
- LXMF delivery;
- encryption/identity pairing on the mesh;
- usable latency, loss, or range.

A stock-Sideband **LXMF round trip over the local Wi-Fi/TCP fallback** is a
separate, already-recorded desktop experiment. It is not LoRa mesh evidence.

## Legal / operating assumptions (unverified by counsel)

- Operate only on a frequency, bandwidth, and power the operator is allowed to
  use in their location.
- Do not raise TX power, change band, or flash firmware from an agent session
  without an explicit operator request.
- Treat all radio work as experimental until a controlled packet-delivery
  experiment exists. See `radio_packet_experiment.md`.

## Evidence links (private tree)

- `CHANGELOG/2026-08-23_rnode_remote_transport_plan.md`
- `CHANGELOG/2026-08-23_sideband_desktop_diagnostic.md`
- `CHANGELOG/2026-08-25_sideband_sf12_bridge_recovery.md`

chunks.heading: # Radio packet-delivery experiment (design only)
chunks.text:
# Radio packet-delivery experiment (design only)

**Status:** designed, **not executed**. No packets were sent for this document.
**Purpose:** make LoRa/RNode reliability measurable so portfolio language can
move from “experimental” to “measured prototype” later.

## Hypothesis

A paired RNode link at the recorded profile (914.875 MHz, 500 kHz, SF12, CR 5,
10 dBm) can carry LXMF payloads of known size with a measurable delivery rate
and latency. Bluetooth/USB attachment of the radios is a prerequisite, not the
result.

## What this experiment is not

- Not a Bluetooth pairing test.
- Not a Sideband UI test.
- Not a license to raise power, change band, or flash firmware.
- Not an Equal Shares, ComfyUI, or model-load task.

## Controlled variables

Hold constant across a session:

- both endpoints on the same frequency, bandwidth, SF, CR, and TX power;
- same payload schema (UTF-8, fixed byte sizes);
- same retry policy (zero retries for the raw-loss run; documented retries for
  the application-level run);
- operator notes environment class: indoor-same-room, indoor-through-wall,
  outdoor-line-of-sight.

## Payload sizes

Use synthetic, non-secret payloads only:

| Class | Target size | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Tiny | 32 bytes | Control / keepalive analogue |
| Chat | 256 bytes | Short assistant message |
| Tool | 1024 bytes | One compact tool result |
| Chunk | 2048 bytes | Upper bound before LXMF chunking is expected |

Never put paths, identities, prompts, or media into the payloads.

## Procedure (one environment class)

1. Confirm both radios share the recorded profile. Do not guess missing values.
2. Confirm the desktop HTTP server remains on localhost and is not the transport.
3. Send N=30 packets per size class from phone→workstation, then 30 the other way.
4. Log only: timestamp, direction, size class, sequence number, delivered
   (yes/no), one-way or RTT latency if available, failure mode enum.
5. Repeat on a second day for the same environment class (minimum two sessions
   before quoting a rate).

N=30 is a floor for a first measurement, not a publication-quality sample.

## Metrics to report (aggregates only)

- sample count per direction and size class;
- delivery rate;
- loss rate;
- median and p95 latency for delivered packets;
- failure-mode counts: no-ack, timeout, interface-down, identity-denied,
  payload-too-large, other;
- whether application retries were enabled.

Do not publish RSSI maps, GPS, street addresses, node IDs, or keys.

## Pass language

| Result | Allowed claim |
|---|---|
| Design only | “Experiment designed; not run.” |
| One session | “Preliminary; do not quote a reliability number.” |
| ≥2 sessions, same profile | “Measured prototype under stated conditions.” |
| Bluetooth paired, no packets | **Not** mesh evidence. |

# Sanitized portfolio demo runbook

This runbook prepares a future screen-recording demonstration without using any
private media, prompts, identities, project history, paths, network details, or
model files. It does not authorize a recording, download, model load, or render.

## Before recording

- [ ] Create a separate demo-only working directory with a generic name.
- [ ] Use only a benign asset with a documented reusable license, such as a
  public-domain train clip. Save source URL, license, and attribution in a
  separate release-evidence record.
- [ ] Start a new demo-only chat with synthetic requests and synthetic filenames.
- [ ] Disable or hide persistent-memory panels, existing chat history, media
  queues, downloaded-model lists, and project-specific tools.
- [ ] Confirm the browser UI shows no usernames, absolute paths, addresses,
  paired identities, credentials, private prompts, or uploads.
- [ ] Confirm ComfyUI is not rendering. Demonstrate guarded preflight only—do
  not create an image or video merely for the recording.

## Suggested three-minute flow

1. Show a new local chat and explain that the desktop HTTP service is local-only.
2. Ask one synthetic question that needs a read-only tool; show a structured
   action card and a sourced response.
3. Attach the benign media asset and show that media analysis is queued behind
   render ownership rather than competing for the GPU.
4. Demonstrate a synthetic preflight/refusal: an invalid or missing job folder
   must be refused with a clear reason, not fabricated or silently rendered.
5. Show the architecture diagram and the permission decision diagram.

## Frame-by-frame release check

- [ ] Inspect the recording at full resolution before export.
- [ ] Blur/redact any path, username, local host data, identity, key, source
  media title, project name, chat transcript, or model-file location.
- [ ] Verify every shown claim appears in `docs/portfolio/validation_matrix.md`
  or is explicitly labeled planned/experimental.
- [ ] Keep the original unredacted capture private; publish only the reviewed
  redacted export.
- [ ] Store public-asset attribution separately from the private project tree.

## Claims allowed in the narration

- “Implemented and locally tested” for structured tool calls, guarded tools,
  localhost-only HTTP, retrieval safeguards, and current source-test evidence.
- “Experimental” for mesh reliability and unmeasured radio delivery.
- “In progress” for custom Android packaging and direct mobile media features.

Never present an architecture diagram, static test, or UI mockup as a completed
performance or end-to-end device result.

chunks.text:
# Qwen2.5-VL lazy-load lifecycle benchmark (method only)

**Status:** three controlled lifecycle observations completed on 2026-08-26.
Their output hashes, VRAM peak, and release behavior match, but Windows cache
effects make their process-start figures unsuitable as a reproducible
cold-load metric. A cold-cache protocol and two repetitions are required before
publishing any aggregate performance claim.
See `CHANGELOG/2026-08-26_qwen25_vl_lifecycle_benchmark.md` and the private,
metadata-only report at
`artifacts/benchmarks/qwen25_vl_lifecycle_2026-08-26.json`.

This is the missing “controlled Qwen2.5-VL timing benchmark” from upgrade 20.
It must use only the approved exact pair:

- `Qwen2.5-VL-7B-NSFW-Caption-V4.Q4_K_M.local.gguf`
- matching `Qwen2.5-VL-7B-NSFW-Caption-V4.mmproj-Q8_0.local.gguf`

No substitute VLM. No Ollama vision model. No render. No Equal Shares job.

## Preconditions

1. Port 8188 is **not** listening.
2. No render-queue owner process is alive.
3. `nvidia-smi` (or the project GPU helper) shows the card idle enough that a
   lazy VLM load will not fight a sampler.
4. Operator has explicitly allowed a model load.

If any precondition fails, stop. Queuing this benchmark behind a render is
allowed; stealing the GPU is not.

## Measurements

Use a public-domain or synthetic still image, not project media. Record:

| Metric | How |
|---|---|
| Cold lazy-load time | watcher start → first successful model-ready log |
| First-analysis latency | model-ready → first caption return |
| Subsequent-analysis latency | second caption on a second benign image |
| VRAM before / during / after | nvidia-smi snapshots at those three points |
| VRAM release time | unload request → VRAM back to the before-load band |
| Text-chat negative control | send a text-only chat; assert the VLM process does not start |
| Render-yield negative control | if ComfyUI later owns 8188, a new media job stays queued |

The opt-in harness is `local_agent/measure_qwen25_vl_lifecycle.py`. Running it
without `--execute` is plan-only. The real measurement needs an explicit model
load approval and a benign input image:

```powershell
python local_agent/measure_qwen25_vl_lifecycle.py <benign-image> --execute --report artifacts/benchmarks/qwen25_vl_lifecycle.json
```

## Output

Write a metadata-only JSON next to the existing caption diagnostic pattern
under `artifacts/benchmarks/`. Allowed fields: timestamps, durations,
VRAM MB, model filenames (not paths), hashes of the diagnostic payload, pass
flags. Forbidden: caption text, file paths, usernames, image content.

Publish only redacted aggregates after **two** matching idle-GPU runs.

chunks.heading: # Mobile edge evaluation — Pixel 10 Pro / PowerInfer-2
chunks.text:
# Mobile edge evaluation — Pixel 10 Pro / PowerInfer-2

## Status and non-negotiable scope

This is an **unlaunched evaluation plan**, not a claim that PowerInfer-2 runs
on this phone today. It does not authorize a model download, Android rooting,
an NDK install, a public listener, Redis exposure, or a background service.
The Equal Shares renderer and ComfyUI stay outside this work.

The original PowerInfer-2 paper describes a heterogeneous NPU/CPU design with
I/O-aware caching. That paper is useful research context, but it is not itself
a reproducible Pixel build recipe. The currently documented upstream Android
path is the newer sparse **SmallThinker** runtime inside the PowerInfer
repository. It targets arm64 Android with the NDK, `libaio`, `liburing`, and a
sparse Q4_0 model. It does **not** document an NNAPI, Qualcomm QNN, or Hexagon
build flag. See the [PowerInfer-2 paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.06282) and
the upstream [SmallThinker Android guide](https://github.com/Tiiny-AI/PowerInfer/blob/main/smallthinker/README.md).

The Pixel 10 Pro uses Google Tensor G5 with a Google TPU, not a Qualcomm SoC.
Therefore a Qualcomm Hexagon/QNN delegate is not an available target on this
device. NNAPI is only a generic Android API; without an upstream PowerInfer
NNAPI backend and a Tensor-compatible driver path, enabling it would not prove
that inference left the CPU. Google lists Tensor G5 and 16 GB RAM in the
[official specifications](https://store.google.com/product/pixel_10_pro_specs?hl=en-US).

**Decision:** the intended Pixel deployment model is
`Tiiny/SmallThinker-21BA3B-Instruct-GGUF`'s exact
`SmallThinker-21B-A3B-Instruct.Q4_0.gguf` sparse artifact. It is the highest-
capacity upstream SmallThinker option that the runtime explicitly supports in
Q4_0, with a documented 8 GiB limited-memory configuration. The model file is
about 12.2 GB, while upstream reports 11.47 GiB for normal sparse 21B runtime;
that does **not** guarantee Pixel fit once Android and Termux overhead are
included. Its documented limited-memory path is therefore the planned operating
mode, subject to an actual thermal/throughput test and without rooting the phone.

`Tiiny/SmallThinker-4BA0.6B-Instruct-GGUF`'s exact Q4_0 artifact remains a
mandatory smoke-test model only. It validates the cross-built binary, Q4_0
format, UFS bundle, and thermal controls before the 21B artifact is copied.
It is not the selected final phone model.

**Superseded for the first benign phone test, 2026-09-05:** the TODO.md
step-2 test item now names `huihui-ai/SmallThinker-3B-Preview-abliterated`
instead of a generic "compatible 4B sparse model," chosen for
runtime-compatible provenance already used elsewhere in this stack. See
`CHANGELOG/2026-09-05c_pixel_edge_model_choice.md`. This does not change
the 21B deployment target above; it only changes which model runs the
first smoke test. A separate TODO item tracks abliterating the official
4BA0.6B checkpoint later to close the size gap.

carried over from this doc's original recipe and is still unproven optimal

Begin with a reproducible CPU-plus-UFS sparse-runtime benchmark. Treat NPU
usage as blocked until upstream publishes a Tensor/NNAPI backend and hardware
counters demonstrate accelerator execution. Do not root the phone to work
around the documented memory-efficient-mode limitation.

## Architecture boundary

```text
Pixel / Termux
  sparse runtime + small, approved model
          |
          |  mTLS or private-overlay HTTPS, per-phone token
          v
Workstation edge gateway (future, loopback/private overlay only)
  validates capability, size, lease, and result
          |
          |  local-only authenticated Redis/Celery
          v
Existing worker farm
```

The phone must **not** receive the farm Redis password, AES key, or direct
Celery access. A lost or compromised phone with those credentials could claim,
inspect, or poison workstation work. The initial phone allowlist is one small,
non-sensitive `edge_text_inference` job with a 12,000-character prompt and a
512-token cap. No historical chat exports, raw artifacts, rendering, commands,
file edits, model downloads, or decryption are phone jobs.

`local_agent/worker_farm/termux_powerinfer2_edge_worker.py` expresses this
gateway contract. It is disabled by default and its gateway endpoints do not
exist yet; it intentionally cannot connect to Redis.

## Phase A — phone inventory and thermal acceptance

Run these only from Termux after installing Termux:API if battery telemetry is
wanted. They are diagnostic, not build steps:

```sh
pkg update
pkg install python git curl coreutils openssl-tool
termux-battery-status
getprop ro.product.cpu.abi
getprop ro.build.version.sdk
df -h "$HOME"
```

Record: Android API level, free internal storage, battery state, and a
10-minute sustained CPU temperature/battery observation. Start with one model
and one process. Stop when charging is disconnected, battery is below 40%, or
the device reports thermal throttling.

## Phase B — supported Android compile path

Do the NDK cross-build on an **x86_64 Linux or WSL build host**, not inside
Termux. Android's documented NDK host tools are `linux-x86_64`; they cannot run
natively on the phone's arm64 userspace. A pure Termux/clang compile may be an
experiment, but it is CPU-only and is not the upstream sparse Android path.

Prerequisites on the build host:

```sh
sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y git cmake ninja-build clang-21 mold make python3 python3-venv
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/Tiiny-AI/PowerInfer.git
cd PowerInfer
python3 -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
cd smallthinker
export NDK="$HOME/Android/Sdk/ndk/27.3.13750724"  # r27d, locked 2026-09-05
export TOOLCHAIN="$NDK/toolchains/llvm/prebuilt/linux-x86_64"
export TARGET=aarch64-linux-android
export API=34
```

Build the two upstream dependencies into the NDK sysroot. Pin and record the
PowerInfer commit and NDK version before accepting a binary:

```sh
cd ../powerinfer/third_part/libaio
export HOST="$TARGET" AR="$TOOLCHAIN/bin/llvm-ar"
export CC="$TOOLCHAIN/bin/$TARGET$API-clang" AS="$CC"
export CXX="$TOOLCHAIN/bin/$TARGET$API-clang++"
export LD="$TOOLCHAIN/bin/ld" RANLIB="$TOOLCHAIN/bin/llvm-ranlib"
export STRIP="$TOOLCHAIN/bin/llvm-strip"
make prefix="$TOOLCHAIN/sysroot/usr" install

cd ../liburing
./configure --prefix="$TOOLCHAIN/sysroot/usr"
make install

cd ../../../../smallthinker
cmake -S . -B build_android -G Ninja \
  -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE="$NDK/build/cmake/android.toolchain.cmake" \
  -DANDROID_ABI=arm64-v8a -DANDROID_PLATFORM=android-34 \
  -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF \
  -DGGML_OPENMP=OFF -DLLAMA_CURL=OFF -DAZ_ENABLE_PERFETTO=ON \
  -DPOWERINFER_NO_FFN_REPACK=ON -DDISABLE_ARM_FEATURE_CHECK=ON \
  -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-march=armv8.6-a -D__USE_GNU -Ofast -flto" \
  -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="-march=armv8.6-a -D__USE_GNU -Ofast -flto"
cmake --build build_android --target llama-cli -j"$(nproc)"
```

Before deployment, calculate a SHA-256 of `llama-cli`, record the source
commit, and scan its dynamic dependencies. Copy only that known binary to
Termux with USB/ADB or an operator-approved immutable download:

```sh
adb push build_android/bin/llama-cli /data/local/tmp/llama-cli
adb shell chmod 700 /data/local/tmp/llama-cli
adb shell sha256sum /data/local/tmp/llama-cli
```

Do not claim `-march=armv8.6-a` is optimal for Tensor G5 until the phone binary
actually runs. If it fails an instruction check, rebuild with a lower proven
architecture level rather than disabling checks permanently.

Do not claim `-march=armv8.6-a` is optimal for Tensor G5 until the phone binary
actually runs. If it fails an instruction check, rebuild with a lower proven
architecture level rather than disabling checks permanently.

## Phase C — model and UFS layout

PowerInfer-2/SmallThinker needs a sparse-compatible model format; a normal
Ollama GGUF, arbitrary Qwen GGUF, or dense 70B model is not an upgrade path.
For the current documented runtime, use only an upstream-compatible sparse Q4_0
model. The deployment target is the selected SmallThinker 21B Q4_0 artifact;
the 4B Q4_0 artifact is used first only to validate the runtime. Do not replace
either with a normal Ollama GGUF, arbitrary Qwen GGUF, or dense 70B model. The
upstream conversion path is:

```sh
python3 convert_hf_to_gguf.py /path/to/safetensors_model \
  --outtype f16 --outfile /path/to/model_f16.gguf --transpose-down all
./build_android/bin/llama-quantize --pure /path/to/model_f16.gguf \
  /path/to/model_q4_0.gguf Q4_0 8
```

For constrained memory, first generate an immutable expert bundle, then create
a no-MoE-weight GGUF. Keep both files together and checksum them:

```sh
GENERATE_EXPERT_BUNDLE=/secure/path/expert.bundle ./build_android/bin/llama-cli \
  -m /secure/path/model_q4_0.gguf --no-cnv -t 2 -n 32 -p "health check"
python3 get_no_moe_weights_ffn.py /secure/path/model_q4_0.gguf \
  /secure/path/model_no_moe_q4_0.gguf
sha256sum /secure/path/model_q4_0.gguf /secure/path/model_no_moe_q4_0.gguf \
  /secure/path/expert.bundle > /secure/path/SHA256SUMS
```

On the phone, store only validated model, bundle, checksums, and short-lived
job scratch data under Termux private storage, for example
`$HOME/.local/share/powerinfer/`. Avoid shared `/sdcard` paths for model cache
or sensitive job output. Maintain at least 20% free UFS capacity, keep one
runtime process, use a 2–4 thread starting point, and benchmark only from a
cool, charging state. `MAX_N_CACHED=768` is the upstream SmallThinker 4B
starting example; it is a benchmark parameter, not a guaranteed Pixel value.

The upstream guide says the memory-efficient Termux route may require root.
That is a stop gate, not permission to root a personal phone. Test normal sparse
mode first; if it cannot fit or meet throughput at safe thermals, keep the
phone as a lightweight preprocessing edge node.

credential on the phone, no raw artifact content in logs, no model process

- Independently validate the upstream mobile binary and the 4B sparse smoke-test

- Identify a supported Tensor G5 accelerator backend only if upstream provides

chunks.heading: # PowerInfer chat-picker plug-in — design note
chunks.text:
# PowerInfer chat-picker plug-in — design note

Read before the code. This is how PowerInfer joins the existing local-agent
chat picker; it is not a new backend framework.

## What the router actually is today

`local_agent/router.py` is **not** a registry of inference engines. It is an
Ollama CPU/GPU handoff:

- Two Ollama hosts: GPU `127.0.0.1:11434`, CPU `127.0.0.1:11435`.
- `chat_models()` lists installed Ollama tags plus one opt-in GPU-only
  exception (`gpt-oss-20b-heretic`).
- `decide()` returns a `Decision(tier, host, model, …)` that `agent.py` always
  feeds to `ollama_client` (`/api/chat`).
- `llama_cpp_client.py` is a **vision** path (`capabilities.ensure_qwen25_vl_runtime`),
  not a chat-picker backend.
- There is no remote-chat backend. “Remote” in this tree is Sideband/phone
  transport, not a second LLM provider.

So the picker already chooses **which Ollama model** to pin. It does not
choose **which process** answers.

## Existing pattern for “this choice may be unusable”

The Heretic entry is the pattern to copy, not a new one:

- Always visible in `chat_models()`, including while the GPU is busy.
- `available: false` until the exact local artifact exists.
- GUI disables the option (`setup_hint` / `unavailable_reason`).
- New chats cannot pin it while unavailable (`server._valid_chat_model`).
- `decide()` returns `model is None` with an explicit reason. It never
  silently substitutes Huihui 8B / CPU Ollama.
- The router **does not start** the missing process. Setup is operator-side
  (`setup_gpt_oss_20b_heretic.py --create`).

PowerInfer is the same *product* shape (opt-in, GPU, may be down) but it is
**not** an Ollama tag. Treating it as one would send `/api/chat` to the
wrong server.

## How PowerInfer plugs in

1. **Picker.** A second Heretic-style row after the existing opt-in models:
   `name = POWERINFER_MODEL_ALIAS` (default `powerinfer-local`),
   `gpu_only: true`, `backend: "powerinfer"`. Always listed. `available`
   is true only when **both** the OpenAI proxy (`127.0.0.1:8091`) and
   PowerInfer `server.exe` (`POWERINFER_BACKEND_URL`, default
   `http://127.0.0.1:8080`) accept a short loopback probe. Timeouts match
   `up()` / `comfy_listening()` so a down backend cannot hang status polls.

2. **Routing.** `decide(model="powerinfer-local")` is a dedicated branch
   next to `is_gpu_only_opt_in_model`, **not** an extra Ollama preference.
   A runnable decision uses `host=127.0.0.1:8091`, `backend="powerinfer"`.
   A non-runnable decision keeps the chat pinned and explains:
   proxy down, `server.exe` down, or GPU owned by ComfyUI / a foreign
   compute process. No Ollama/CPU substitution.

3. **GPU ownership.** `gpu_busy()` today treats any non-Ollama compute
   process as a render. Live `server.exe` would otherwise make **every**
   PowerInfer turn look busy and refuse itself. Mirror the resident-Ollama
   exception: when the configured PowerInfer backend is the process on the
   card, Ollama auto-chat still yields to CPU, but a PowerInfer-pinned chat
   is allowed to talk to the already-running proxy. ComfyUI port 8188 and
   `render_queue_owner.json` still win.

4. **Transport.** `ollama_client.chat` / `chat_stream` dispatch on
   `host == POWERINFER_PROXY_HOST` to a small OpenAI-compat client that
   posts `/v1/chat/completions` (the proxy contract is unchanged). Native
   tool schemas are not sent (the proxy rejects tools). Legacy `TOOL:`
   parsing in `agent.py` remains. Tool-role history is flattened to
   alternating text roles so the Llama-2 renderer is not fed `role=tool`.

5. **GPU gateway.** A PowerInfer pin must not request an Ollama GPU load.
   If the proxy/`server.exe` pair is not up, the turn fails with a setup
   hint. That is the Heretic “not installed” path, not a new supervisor.
