# 2026-09-04q — ComfyUI / agent GPU timeshare via `clear_vram` (mocked)

Date: 2026-09-04. Host: DuranGamingPC.
Id from `python scripts/next_changelog_id.py`: **2026-09-04q**.
Design: `docs/COMFYUI_GPU_TIMESHARE_CLEAR_VRAM.md`.

**Live Rockernow verify was not run this pass.** No live ComfyUI, nvidia-smi,
or MCP child in the new tests.

## What changed

- `local_agent/mcp_client.py`: instance and module `call(..., lock_timeout=, spawn=)`.
  `spawn=False` fails closed without `_ensure_started` / 120 s handshake.
  `lock_timeout` bounds `Lock.acquire` and raises `McpError` on failure.
  Existing `comfy_*` tools omit the kwargs (unchanged spawn-on-first-use).
- `local_agent/router.py`: numbered `decide()` order — `gpu_busy()`, classify
  once, farm-skip the hook, else timeshare, then `skip_gpu_inventory` from
  post-hook `busy`. Helpers `_owners_idle_for_timeshare`, `_comfy_queue_idle`,
  `_clear_vram_for_timeshare`, `try_idle_comfy_timeshare`.
- Occupancy before `/free`: nvidia-smi `None` fail-closed; unexplained VRAM
  (not ≤800, not 2000–3200, not already-claimed Ollama/PI) fail-closed;
  ComfyUI python paths waived; `Python312\python.exe` foreign; bare
  `python.exe` + 8188 is not foreign by name (band still applies).
- Successful claim logs WARNING on `local_agent.router.timeshare` that the
  sidebar `gpu_gate` card did not fire (interim bypass). `agent.py` is
  unchanged.
- Kill switch `EQUAL_SHARES_COMFY_TIMESHARE` default-on; `=0` disables.

## Why

`gpu_busy()` treats listening 8188 as busy, so idle ComfyUI parks every
GPU-routed turn on CPU. Option A (VRAM threshold) is closed: used stays
345 MiB through the claim window. Option B tests owner + queue, then
`POST /free`, then loads.

## Tests

Mocked only (`local_agent/test_router_comfy_timeshare.py`). Existing
`test_mcp_client.py` covers `lock_timeout` / `spawn=False`.

## Follow-ups (TODO.md)

- `agent.py` `gpu_gate` when 8188-only busy and timeshare would claim.
- `status()` third badge state from owner+queue, no `/free`.

Grok probe importing `tools` — writes one JSONL row:

- `ts`, `local_tool=comfy_generate`, `mcp_tool=generate_image`, `action`, `args`

Not a bug in our wrapper. `tools.comfy_generate` already forwarded

`8182b9d1-e080-4d9e-9f85-bc5bccdb4be6` shows SaveImage node 7

`mcp_live_verify_20260904`.

  `filename_prefix` into `generateImage(...)`. It **does** pass it for
  `"audio"`, `"video"`, and `"remove_background"`. The Zod description

- `dist/services/workflow-composer.js` `buildTxt2Img` / `buildImg2Img`
  hardcode `filename_prefix: "ComfyUI"`. ControlNet / IP-Adapter /
  upscale hardcode `ComfyUI_controlnet` / `ComfyUI_ipadapter` /
  `ComfyUI_upscale`.
- Official schema (artokun.io / Glama): `filename_prefix` documented
  for audio, video, remove_background only.

This is a **comfyui-mcp limitation**. Documented in
`docs/COMFYUI_MCP_INTEGRATION_PLAN.md` §4b. `comfy_generate` is not
rewritten to rebuild their graph.

chunks.heading: # 2026-09-04y — CPU Ollama :11435 disables Vulkan (ollama#16508)
chunks.text:
# 2026-09-04y — CPU Ollama :11435 disables Vulkan (ollama#16508)

Date: 2026-09-04. Host: DuranGamingPC.
Id from `python scripts/next_changelog_id.py --date 2026-09-04`: **2026-09-04y**.

Closes the ops ticket opened from the empty-completion investigation
(`CHANGELOG/2026-09-04r_empty_completion_guard.md`, chat
`7d474ba55d244abe`). Independent of that PR.

## Root cause

Ollama **0.32.15**: `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1` only skips CUDA discovery.
Vulkan stays on by default (`OLLAMA_VULKAN:true`) and still enumerates
the RTX 5080. Upstream: [ollama#16508](https://github.com/ollama/ollama/issues/16508).
The dedicated CPU server on `127.0.0.1:11435` was advertising the card
over Vulkan. When 11435 was down, `router._paired_cpu_fallback` used
`gpu_store_cpu_only` on **11434**, which GPU-loaded Huihui 8B (41/41
layers, ~8161 MiB) while Comfy `:8188` was up (HTTP 499).

Not a Windows env-propagation miss: the launcher did set
`CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1` on the child. Short diagnostic `ollama serve`
processes that vanished mid-discovery were job-object kills of the
parent, not a native crash.

A session-only CPU `:11435` (pid 30080, `OLLAMA_VULKAN=false`) was
started during diagnosis as a **manual stopgap**. It is not this fix.
The verification `Start-Server` child (pid 19960) was replaced after
the checks by another session-lived `ollama serve` with the same three
env vars so a test-job teardown would not take 11435 down again.
Durable ops path is the patched desktop launcher.

## What shipped

`local_agent/START_LOCAL_AGENT_GUI.ps1` `Start-Server` when `$CpuOnly`:

- keep `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1`
- add `OLLAMA_VULKAN=false`
- add `GGML_VK_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1`

GPU `Start-Server` still does not set those three.

## Before / after (live process)

Before (diagnosis, launcher env = CUDA `-1` only, pid 43000 via psutil):

```
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1
OLLAMA_VULKAN=<unset>
```

Ollama log: `OLLAMA_VULKAN:true`, then
`inference compute ... library=Vulkan ... NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080`
`total="15.6 GiB"`.

After (this PR, **actual** `Start-Server '127.0.0.1:11435' 'cpu' $true`
from the patched launcher, pid 19960 via psutil):

```
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1
OLLAMA_VULKAN=false
GGML_VK_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1
OLLAMA_HOST=127.0.0.1:11435
```

Ollama log (`local_agent/ollama_cpu.err.log`):

```
OLLAMA_VULKAN:false
user overrode visible devices CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1
user overrode visible devices GGML_VK_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1
inference compute id=cpu library=cpu ... total="30.9 GiB"
vram-based default context total_vram="0 B"
```

Matches the 2026-09-03bb eval configuration that already proved
`id=cpu` / `total_vram=0 B`.

# 2026-09-05a — PowerInfer hops get a text-only system prompt

Audit finding: chats pinned to `backend="powerinfer"` already had
`tool_schemas=[]` in `apply_hop_profile()` and a UI-only status note
("PowerInfer is text-only; native tool schemas are not sent"), but
`msgs[0]` was still the full agentic `system_prompt()` — the same
CONVERSATION_RULES built for models with native tool-calling. The model
was told to "use an available tool" and named `fetch_url`,
`start_current_chat_render`, `extract_video_actions`, and the rest, with
no way to actually call them. README already documents the pin as

  available this turn, not to claim an action occurred, and to answer
  directly in text.
- `system_prompt(..., rules=)` accepts an optional rules block. Default
  remains CONVERSATION_RULES / CODING_RULES. PowerInfer passes the
  text-only rules so operating memory, learned lessons, recalled memory,
  and the Equal Shares handbook (when scoped) stay attached.
- `apply_hop_profile()` for `backend=="powerinfer"` still returns
  `tool_schemas=[]` and now also replaces `msgs[0]` with that prompt.
  GPU hops still get `base_system`; CPU/farm hops still get

  `passed` only).

# 2026-09-05ai — Pixel edge gateway v1 shipped, server-only, nothing listening

## Scope

own build report. No new work from this entry.

## What shipped

`local_agent/edge_gateway/` — SQLite-ledger gateway matching all 10
authorized G1–G10 decisions:

- Phone API (HTTPS + mTLS) bound to `10.90.91.1:8743` only; admin (HTTP)
  bound to `127.0.0.1:8744` only — neither of the forbidden ports
  (6379/8188/11434/11435/8765), confirmed in the design note (G4).
- Claim/complete match the existing inert Termux client contract exactly,
  server-side re-enforcement of all three caps (12,000-char prompt,
  512-token, 16,000-char result) — client checks are not trusted as a
  control, per the design.
- One lease per device; `complete` is idempotent (first result wins,
  a mutating retry gets 409); revoke expires the lease (`complete` after
  revoke returns 401); results stored as untrusted; logs are ids/sizes
  only, never content (G6/G7/G8/G9).
- G3 enforced as a real test, not a comment: a grep-lock confirms
  production sources contain no `FARM_BROKER_URL`/`REDIS_PASSWORD`/
  `celery_app`/`load_dotenv`/`worker_farm` references, plus a
  clean-interpreter import test confirming `celery`/`redis` are never
  loaded.
- Overlay generator (`Generate-EdgePhoneOverlay.ps1`) writes a gitignored
  `runtime/wireguard/` config for the new isolated `10.90.91.0/30`
  overlay (AllowedIPs restricted to the pair) — generation only, not
  `-Install`. Farm hub and Mac WireGuard config were not touched (G1).

19/19 new tests pass; the 3 existing Termux contract tests still pass
unchanged (client file untouched, G10 respected — Termux `--gateway` was
not exercised).

## Confirmed nothing is actually running

`--listen` without `10.90.91.1` bound to a real interface fails closed
(`WinError 10049`, exit 2) — no `0.0.0.0` fallback, and the phone bind is
attempted before the admin bind so admin is never left open alone. After
the attempt, both 8743 and 8744 show `connect_ex` 10061 (nothing
listening). No persistent process is running from this build.

## What was not done

The overlay itself was not brought up (`-Install` is a separate,
deliberate operator step). No real phone contact. Pixel `--once` stays
off per G10 until the workstation service has a real live listen cycle
tested end-to-end, not just unit tests.

## Next

Step 2 of the original PowerInfer-2 mobile edge plan (the actual Pixel
test with `SmallThinker-3B-Preview-abliterated`) is now unblocked at the
design level, but still requires: (1) an operator decision to actually
run `-Install` and bring the overlay up, and (2) the token-ceremony step

# 2026-09-05ak — MCP audit binary offset linked into traces (PR 4)

Date: 2026-09-05. Host: DuranGamingPC. All times America/New_York (UTC-4).

Id from `python scripts/next_changelog_id.py` immediately before write: **2026-09-05ak**.

Last PR in the `tracing.py` plan. Completes the mug-image investigation
recipe: hop/tool span → `span_refs` byte offset → one JSONL line in
`runtime/comfy_mcp_audit.jsonl`. The generate prompt stays in JSONL only.

No `timeshare_log` refs (WARNING logger was removed in `2026-09-04aa`).
No APP_REVISION bump. Phase B Phoenix/OTLP not built.

## What is wired

`_comfy_audit` now:

1. Opens the JSONL as binary append (`"ab"`).
2. `offset = fh.tell()` **before** writing the UTF-8 line.
3. After a successful write, best-effort `tracing.current_span().link(
   "comfy_mcp_audit", target="runtime/comfy_mcp_audit.jsonl#{offset}",
   extra={prompt_id, mcp_status, caller_file})`. `link()` is in-memory;
   SQLite flush is on the tool span `__exit__`.
4. JSONL `OSError` still raises `ToolError`. A tracing/link failure is
   logged and **cannot** fail a generate that already succeeded at MCP.
5. `tools.last_comfy_audit()` → `(offset, prompt_id, caller_file)` for
   tests / probes. Not the model-visible tool result.

Direct `tools.comfy_generate` callers (VRAM probes) still write JSONL
and get no turn span — same finding as `2026-09-04t`.

## Mug-image join (reconstructed traced turn)

Mocked `comfy_generate` during `agent.answer()` for chat
`7d474ba55d244abe`, prompt token `UNIQUE_MUG_PROMPT_TOKEN_7d474ba55d244abe`.

SQL:

```sql
SELECT t.conversation_id, s.name, s.hop_index, ref.ref_offset,
       json_extract(ref.ref_extra,'$.prompt_id'),
       json_extract(ref.ref_extra,'$.caller_file')
FROM spans s
JOIN spans t ON t.trace_id=s.trace_id AND t.kind='turn'
JOIN span_refs ref ON ref.trace_id=s.trace_id AND ref.span_id=s.span_id
WHERE s.kind='tool' AND s.name='comfy_generate'
  AND ref.ref_kind='comfy_mcp_audit';
```

Result: `conversation_id=7d474ba55d244abe`, `hop_index=0`,
`prompt_id=mug-prompt-id`, `caller_file` ending in `agent.py`.
`fh.seek(offset)` on the JSONL returns that prompt. The unique token is
**not** in `traces.db`.

## Tests

```text
python -m unittest test_comfy_tools test_agent_tracing test_tracing -q
python -m unittest test_native_tool_calling -q
```

49 + 88 OK. New: binary seek roundtrip, prompt not copied into traces.db,
link failure does not fail generate, mug-image join through `agent.answer()`.

# 2026-09-05av — Operator-approved phone-call assistant: scope only

Date: 2026-09-05. Host: DuranGamingPC. Id from
`python scripts/next_changelog_id.py`: **2026-09-05av**.

Design note only — no provider account, no dial, no `APP_REVISION`, no
tool added.

Doc: `docs/design_notes/PHONE_CALL_ASSISTANT_2026-09-05.md`.

## Finding

Nothing in this tree places a PSTN or cellular call. The paired phone is
an LXMF chat identity (`lxmf_agent.py`, ADR 0001). `phone_scheduler.py` /
`schedule_phone_messages` send repeating **text back to the caller
only** — the model cannot name a recipient (`tools.call` injects
`__remote_schedule_identity`). Sideband’s “telephony” is **LXST over
Reticulum** (`vendor_sideband/README.md`), which cannot reach a shop’s
NANP number.

A live dial needs an explicit routing contract the TODO already requires:

- **Path P** — telephony API (Twilio-class). Needs a vendor account and
  almost certainly a public webhook, which fights loopback-only HTTP.
- **Path D** — Intent/`CALL_PHONE` on the paired handset. Needs an
  Android/Sideband-fork contract that the companion TODO has not
  approved. Stock Sideband has no cellular dial path here.

**There is no clean v1 that actually dials.** Forcing one would be an
implicit Sideband or scheduler extension, which the TODO forbids.

What can exist later, only after sign-off: Phase 1 = `call_gate` +
allowlist + hashed confirmation (copy `file_edit_gate`, **not**
`gpu_gate` `allow`) + simulated dial/cancel/timeout + min-metadata
JSONL. Mid-call purchases/ID/commitments need a **second** card. OTPs
and payment credentials are un-approvable. Recordings stay off pending
real legal review (C2), not a code comment.

No production code changed.

chunks.text:
# 2026-09-05ba — Sealed chat export scoped; existing farm AES doesn't meet the new bar

## Scope

🟢 lane, Task #57. Reviews Grok's own report (`2026-09-05az`). Design
only — no real export authorized, no code shipped.

## Key finding: the existing encryption doesn't clear the new bar

`distill_export`'s `EncryptedArtifactStore` (AES-256-GCM) keeps its key in
`worker_farm/.env` on the same machine that can decrypt it — a local
admin can read `FARM_ENCRYPTION_KEY_B64` directly and decrypt every
distill artifact. BitLocker or a key sitting next to the file fail for
the identical reason: the decryption capability lives on the same box as
the ciphertext. Also flagged, correctly: `local_agent/chats/*.json` is
already plaintext today — sealing a future *export* does nothing for
live chat storage, which is a separate problem not addressed by this
scope.

Also caught: the existing `--sample` synthetic path
(`submit_distillation.py`) writes a plaintext tempfile and unlinks it —
acceptable for the public synthetic fixture, explicitly **not**
acceptable for a real snapshot under the new requirement.

## What the bar actually requires

Public-key sealing (age recommended over GPG) to a recipient whose
private key never lives on this machine — decryption only possible on a
separate device or an unsynced password-manager item. No plaintext ever
touches disk, not even a tempfile: read to RAM, encrypt, write ciphertext
only. Residual leaks correctly identified as unavoidable and named
explicitly rather than glossed over: outer filename (mitigated with an
opaque name), approximate file size (padding optional), timestamps, and
the age recipient identity in the file header. Explicitly flagged: do
not copy the farm's `plaintext_sha256` onto a sealed-export sidecar —
that would function as a content oracle for guessing plaintext.

Correctly noted: `distill_export` and a sealed chat export are
necessarily different outputs, because a worker that decrypts for
distillation processing must hold the secret — this new sealing scheme
is fundamentally incompatible with the farm's existing keying if the
farm still needs to read the content.

A synthetic-only seal helper (same pattern as `three_d_contract.py`) can
exist once E1 is signed off, and must hard-refuse any path under
`chats/`. A real command touching actual chat history is explicitly not
v1 — it still requires the pre-existing source-selection operator
decision plus a new sign-off item (E8). Full sign-off list (E1-E8) is in
`docs/design_notes/SEALED_CHAT_EXPORT_2026-09-05.md`: helper-vs-real-export
boundary, age-vs-GPG choice, key custody, recipient file location, new
binary dependency, RAM/pagefile residual risk, padding decision, and the
chats/ hard-refusal.

chunks.heading: # 2026-09-05bc — Catalog drowning is cross-model; 14B→8B overflow demotion is real
chunks.text:
# 2026-09-05bc — Catalog drowning is cross-model; 14B→8B overflow demotion is real

Date: 2026-09-05. Host: DuranGamingPC. Id from
`python scripts/next_changelog_id.py`: **2026-09-05bc**. Investigation
only; no `router.py` / schema-surface change. Receipts:
`artifacts/benchmarks/2026-09-05_catalog_drowning/`.

Same case-1a prompt (“first markdown heading inside
`local_agent/README.md`”), full GPU `schemas(include_project=True)` —
**68** tools today (55 without project tools). `think=false`.

## 1. Catalog drowning — not DeepSeek-only

| Model | Tools sent | First call | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Huihui-14B (2026-09-05b 1a) | **54** general | **`read_file`** | correct |
| Huihui-14B (this probe) | **68** project | **`fetch_url`** `{url: local_agent/README.md}` | wrong (not even an http URL) |
| Josiefied-Coder official-tools | 68 | content JSON **`fetch_url`** `{url: file:///local_agent/README.md}` | wrong |
| DeepSeek r1-tools (2026-09-05at) | 67 | **`see_image`** | wrong |
| gpt-oss-20b-heretic | 68 | **`read_file`** `{path: local_agent/README.md}` | correct |

A screenshot-biased variant (“might be text or a screenshot”) made
Huihui-14B pick `see_image` — that is prompt leading, not drowning.
The table above is the drowning test.

Live `prompt_eval_count` on the short user message + 68 schemas (no
agent system prompt): **4098** (Qwen/Coder/Huihui) vs **7058**
(Heretic harmony). Router estimate for the same wire:
**11940** (`len(json)/3.4`). The estimator inflates schema cost ~2–3×
on Qwen.

Heretic resisted drowning but **rejected `num_ctx=4096`**
(`n_prompt_tokens=7058`). Opt-in 20B already needs ≥8k context just to
*hold* the catalog.

## 2. 14B→8B demotion — not a farm-outage red herring

`_adaptive_gpu_model` demotes **only** `PRIMARY_REASONING_MODEL`
(Huihui-14B) when `estimate_context_tokens > 16000`. Capability
DeepSeek/Coder hops skip this. A `CAP_TOOL` turn with farm down falls
through to ordinary GPU auto → Huihui-14B → this check.

Measured estimates (agent system prompt included):

| Case | Estimate | Over 16k? |
|---|---|---|
| 68 GPU schemas only | 11900 | no |
| README + general GPU (55) + general system | 15697 | no — matches 1a staying on 14B |
| README/enqueue + **project** GPU (68) + project system | 19258 / **19352** | **yes** — matches 2026-09-05b case 4 (`18919`) |
| Same enqueue + compact 3-tool schema | 7821 | no |

Farm being down only *selects* the local GPU path. The demotion is
schema+handbook size vs a conservative estimator, independent of why
the Mac was frozen. Compact profile is `tier in {cpu,farm}` only; the
8B GPU fallback still gets **`profile=gpu` → full 68 tools**
(`docs/HARNESS_PROFILES_DESIGN_2026-09-04.md` §3). So a farm-down tool
turn can land on Huihui-8B *and* the drowning catalog (case 4).

If Qwen’s real schema cost is ~4k, case 4’s 19k estimate may have
falsely demoted a 14B that would have fit. That is still a real routing
bug, not a red herring.

## Proposed fix (not built)

Two complementary changes, neither is a DeepSeek-only crutch:

1. **Curated GPU subset for tool-classified local hops** (farm down or
   `skip_farm`): advertise `CORE_DIRECT_TOOLS` (`list_dir`, `read_file`,
   `web_search`, `fetch_url`, `capabilities`, `run_code`) plus `comfy_*`
   only when the prompt is actually a Comfy/workflow turn. Already
   sketched as compact v1.1 in the harness-profile design. Cuts both
   drowning and the 16k estimate. Do **not** silently shrink every
   Huihui conversation hop until this is measured on a happy-path pin.
2. **Stop counting schema JSON as `len/3.4` tokens** (or use a measured
   per-schema constant from `prompt_eval_count`). Prevents 14B→8B
   demotion on estimates that are 2–3× actual Qwen prompt tokens.

Prefer (1) for tool-fallback hops; (2) is cheap and independent.
Do not apply compact-3 to GPU 14B as the first move — Qwythos already
has compact when the farm is up.

## Not changed

No router, schema, or prompt edits this pass. GPU unloaded after Heretic.

(`2026-09-05bc`/`bd`/`bb`). No new production work from this entry.

## 2026-09-05bc — Catalog drowning confirmed cross-model, real fix proposed

Real, important finding, not built yet. Catalog drowning is not
DeepSeek-specific: Huihui-14B itself picks the wrong tool
(`fetch_url` on a local markdown file) once the full 68-tool project
schema is loaded, despite picking correctly on a smaller 54-tool

just to hold the catalog.

router's token estimator (`len(json)/3.4`) overestimates Qwen's actual
schema cost by roughly 2-3x, which can falsely demote a 14B model that
would have actually fit within context. Two independent proposed fixes,
neither a DeepSeek-only crutch: (1) a curated core-tool subset for
tool-classified local-GPU-fallback hops specifically (not shrinking
every Huihui conversation), and (2) replacing the token estimator with a
measured per-schema constant instead of the current length heuristic.
Recommendation is to do both, with the curated-subset change scoped to
fallback hops only until measured safe more broadly.

## 2026-09-05bd — Intent-mismatch flag button shipped

Real and ready to use now: a "this wasn't what I meant" button on
assistant messages in the desktop GUI, appending one JSONL record
(`local_agent/runtime/intent_mismatch.jsonl`) with the triggering
message, full reply, tool calls, and routing decision — no model re-run,
no routing/prompt change, no memory write. 17/17 tests pass. Needs one
desktop-agent restart to pick up the new endpoint. This directly answers
the operator's "start gathering data" request from earlier today — using
it during normal usage is what builds the real before/after dataset the
original TODO item needs.

Passed 2 review rounds (15 issues addressed), 0 open. Correctly refuses
several tempting shortcuts: no `MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE`, no APK
installation over LXMF/Wi-Fi/LoRa (specified as APIs that must not
exist, not just policy), a lost-phone honesty note (a still-paired phone
is a live client with ungated reads until revoke — same residual-risk
class as the edge-gateway's "queued prompt is readable" note). 14-item
sign-off list (A1-A14) required before any Android compile, ADB install,
or production-agent edit.

audit) closed with a real, unbuilt fix proposal awaiting authorization.

# 2026-09-05bi — Worker farm audit: one-spoke star, not a 4-machine fleet

## Scope

🟣 lane, farm audit follow-up. Investigation only, no hub/peer/config
change.

## Finding

The 2026-09-01 decision to add "4+ already-owned idle LAN machines" never
progressed past the Mac. Confirmed via both `hub.conf`'s single `[Peer]`
block (unchanged since 2026-09-01 23:03) and the live hub's routing table
(only `10.90.90.2/32` exists; `.3`-`.6` return "no route," not a
timeout). Only one Celery worker has ever registered:
`celery@Louises-MBP`. The 2026-09-01 plan itself only ever used
placeholder names (`workshop_pc`, `media_server`, `old_laptop`,
`linux_box`) — a real machine list and OS inventory was left as an open
question and was never subsequently filled in.

This is not a stuck or failed join — there's no record of a second
machine attempting WireGuard and getting stuck. It was deprioritized
once the Mac path worked and the operator's 2026-09-02 directive shifted
focus to engine evaluation; "swarm offload" got marked as largely already
built on the strength of the one working node.

## Recommendation

Don't actively chase the remaining 3+ LAN machines right now — that's
operator-hands-on work (per-box keypair, `Add-WireGuardPeer`, per-machine
Redis ACL, venv, `worker.py`) that was deprioritized, not blocked by
anything technical. Worth doing only if more CPU capacity is actually
wanted beyond what Louise's 2019 16GB Intel Mac provides — that's a
capacity decision, separate from the already-deferred 10-node/60-core
cluster architecture track, which this hub was never meant to be.

## Status

Confirms the farm is healthy at its current one-worker scale. No further
action needed unless the operator wants to actively expand it.

# 2026-09-05bl — Sealed export v1 verified: refusal and no-plaintext claims both proven live

## Scope

🟢 lane, Task #57's build. Reviews Grok's own report (`2026-09-05bj`).
No new work.

## What shipped and why it's trustworthy

`local_agent/sealed_export.py` — age X25519 sealing, RAM straight to
ciphertext, no decrypt capability shipped on this machine (correct —
the whole point is the private key never lives here). `atomic_io.py`'s
`atomic_write_bytes` only ever touches the ciphertext `.tmp` file, never
plaintext. 7/7 tests pass.

Both of the two hardest claims were verified adversarially, not just
asserted:

- **The chats/ refusal actually fires**: a real attempt to seal
  `local_agent/chats/must_not_be_read.json` raises and refuses before
  the target file is even created, and the CLI path returns exit 2 for
  the same case. A grep lock further confirms the helper contains no
  `NamedTemporaryFile`, `store.load`, or `plaintext_sha256` — and a
  deliberately reintroduced bad copy was confirmed to get caught by that
  lock.
- **No plaintext ever hits disk**: a real test polls both the
  destination directory and an isolated process temp directory *while
  the seal is running*, searching for the fixture's plaintext bytes.
  Zero hits. The resulting `.age` file was confirmed to start with the
  correct `age-encryption.org/v1` header and to not contain the canary
  string, with a round-trip decrypt (test-only, not a shipped CLI
  capability) confirming the ciphertext is actually recoverable.

Output filenames are opaque (`sealed_export_<12 hex>.age`), and the
recipient is a public key only, matching the design's requirement that
the private half never lives on this machine.

## What was not done

No real export — only the synthetic `distill --sample` fixture can be
sealed. Real chat history remains fully blocked behind the existing
"obtain explicit operator decision and source selection" TODO item,
unchanged by this work.

## Status

Task #57 fully closed: scoped, sign-off accepted, built, and both of its
hardest security claims were proven with real adversarial tests rather
than left as design assertions.

## Tag / quant on disk

`ollama list` already had **`huihui_ai/Qwen3.8-abliterated:latest`**
(digest `bdc5e13cd164`, 17 GB, modified 6 days ago). No pull.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Architecture | `qwen35` (Ollama) / GGUF name `Huihui Qwen3.8 27B Abliterated` |
| Parameters | 27.32 B / 27.3B |
| Quant | **Q4_K_M** |
| Native ctx | 262144 |
| Weights blob | `sha256-6c2c13cef89238c3604d756b07b3ef5fafebbd61095feb8553ff449c95e4c1c6` **16031.9 MB** (byte-identical to `Qwen3.8-27B-Uncensored-GGUF\Qwen3.8-27B-Uncensored-Q4_K_M.gguf`) |
| Projector blob | `sha256-c9a090…` **888.0 MB** CLIP mmproj |
| Renderer / parser | `RENDERER qwen3.8` / `PARSER qwen3.5` / `TEMPLATE {{ .Prompt }}` |
| Capabilities | completion, vision, tools, thinking |
| Layers | 64 repeating + output; log: **offloaded 66/66 to GPU** at 2k ctx |

Hybrid layout (upstream, matches this GGUF): 16 × (3 × Gated DeltaNet→FFN + 1 × gated attention→FFN) = **48 linear-attention + 16 full-attention**. Only the 16 full-attention layers grow a sequence KV cache; GDN keeps a fixed recurrent state (`ssm_d_state=128`, `ssm_n_group=16` in the load log). That is why long context is cheap *in KV*, not why the **16 GB Q4_K_M weights** fit a 16 GB card.

Other quants exist in `Qwen3.8-27B-Uncensored-GGUF\` (IQ4_XS, Q3_K_M, …) but are **not** Ollama tags. Not imported this pass.

## VRAM / speed (real Ollama timings)

GPU idle at start: **68–70 MiB**, 31 °C, `/api/ps` empty, :8188 down.

| Phase | num_ctx | prompt_eval_count (actual) | load_duration | pp tok/s | decode tok/s | nvidia-smi after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Idle load + short | 2048 | 19 | **111.903 s** | 20.8 (warmup) | **14.568** (4 tok) | **15933 / 16303 MiB** |
| ~20K requested fill | 20480 | **9375** (tokenizer denser than 3.4 c/tok) | **140.824 s** (reload) | **68.489** | **8.258** (4 tok) | **68 MiB** (evicted after) |
| 64K alloc, short prompt | 65536 | — | llama-server **`-c 65536`** then **exit 0xffffffff** @ 139 s | — | — | 68 MiB |

Load log at 2k: `CUDA0 model buffer size = 15339.44 MiB` + `CUDA_Host 682.03 MiB`; 66/66 layers on GPU. nvidia-smi **15933 MiB** leaves ~370 MiB free — the card is full of weights before a long KV even starts.

Ollama later logged `model predicted to exceed available memory` at `predicted_num_ctx=20480` while `available="0 B"`. 64K start line: `llama-server.exe … -c 65536` then `Load failed … NTSTATUS 0xffffffff`.

Reply at 2k and 9.4k fill was exactly `KV_CACHE_OK`.

**Do not treat 14.6 t/s as a 14B-class number.** This is a 27B Q4_K_M packed into 16 GB; decode already dropped to 8.3 t/s at 9.4k filled tokens. The #27623 80K cliff was not reachable: 64K would not load.

## Tool-calling (full GPU schema, 68 tools)

Same prompts as 2026-09-05b/n. Direct GPU `:11434`, `think=False`, `tools.schemas(include_project=True, profile="gpu")` — **68** functions (67 plus `comfy_job_status`).

| Case | Hop 0 native `tool_calls` | Inner executed | Hop 1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `read_file` heading | **`read_file`** `{path: local_agent/README.md, limit: "40"}` | yes; file starts `# Local Agent — a local ChatGPT Desktop equivalent` | **500** `no user query found in messages` (0.06 s) |
| `run_code` clamp loop | **`run_code`** with the **buggy** `min(lo, max(x, hi))` + asserts | yes; AssertionError in sandbox | **500** after 97 s; `llama-server … terminated … 0xffffffff` |

Not DeepSeek catalog-drowning: hop 0 picked the right tool from 68 schemas, empty `content`, native `tool_calls` ids (`call_73rkqk8m`, `call_7peqs855`). Extra `limit` (schema is `max_chars`) was ignored by `read_file` and still returned the file. `run_code` omitted `language` (defaults to python) and correctly ran the failing asserts first.

Multi-hop is **not** proven: this tag’s `TEMPLATE {{ .Prompt }}` + `RENDERER qwen3.8` rejected the follow-up tool-result transcript (`no user query found`), and a second hop also crashed the runner (VRAM). Clamp was **not** fixed. Do not claim a complete agent loop.

## Context ceiling vs existing compaction

Already in `agent.py`:

- `_apply_ctx_ceiling(adaptive, ceiling)` = `min(adaptive, GUI ceiling)`
- when `prompt_tokens > num_ctx` → `_trim_context` (farm prefetch at 80% via `compaction_prefetch`, else `context_compactor` CPU `llama3.1:8b`, else continuity digest)

That **is** the generic mechanism. A later wire-in should set this tag’s `Decision.options()["num_ctx"]` the same way Heretic is 8k / capability 8k / primary 20k / fallback 32k — **not** a new summarizer.

Practical cap on this card+quant is **not** 64K. 64K is the #27623 software ceiling *if* a smaller quant ever fits. Today Q4_K_M cannot allocate `-c 65536`. A VRAM-safe `num_ctx` (2k–8k class) would already trigger trim/prefetch.

## Recommendation (still not wired)

Do **not** add `huihui_ai/Qwen3.8-abliterated:latest` to `GPU_MODELS`. Weights fill the 5080 at 2k ctx; 20k is slower and evicts; 64k load crashes. Tool hop 0 is promising; hop 1 is not. # 2026-09-05bx — Calibrate KV-cache filler chars/token (no router estimator change)

Date: 2026-09-05. Host: DuranGamingPC. Id from
`python scripts/next_changelog_id.py`: **2026-09-05bx**.

2026-09-05bm's Qwen3.8-27B "20K fill" used
`measure_ollama_kv_cache.probe_prompt(18000)`, which sized the body as
`tokens * 3.4` chars. That 3.4 is the router's JSON-wire **estimator**
(chars → tokens, conservative over-count). Used backwards to **generate**
a fill it under-filled: live `prompt_eval_count` was **9375**, ~6.5
chars/token on this repetitive filler.

## Where 3.4 actually lives

| Location | Role | This ticket |
|---|---|---|
| `measure_ollama_kv_cache.probe_prompt` | fill generation (`chars = tokens * 3.4`) | **fixed here** — the bm silent under-fill |
| `2026-09-05_qwen38_27b_eval.py` | imported that helper | now uses `sized_probe_prompt` |
| `router._MESSAGE_CHARS_PER_TOKEN = 3.4` | production chars → tokens for **messages** | **untouched** (2026-09-05bn already replaced schema `len/3.4` with `MEASURED_SCHEMA_TOKENS`) |
| `test_capability_routing.py`, `2026-09-05_gpu_core_live.py` | `/ 3.4` as the **old** estimator for comparison | historical, left |
| `retrieval.py` `CHUNK_CHARS = 3000  # ~800 tokens at ~3.75` | RAG chunk size | different constant, not this fill |

Not a production routing bug. Cross-cutting only among **benchmark fill
generators**, and they already shared one helper — so the fix is central
there, not a per-script patch and not `estimate_context_tokens`.

## Fix

`probe_prompt(..., chars_per_token=)` sizes filler from a measured (or
explicit) chars/token. Live paths:

- `calibrate_fill_chars_per_token(host, model)` — one short chat, `len(prompt) / prompt_eval_count`
- `sized_probe_prompt` / `run_once` (when `chars_per_token` omitted) use that before the timed request
- Offline fallback for this filler is **6.5** (bm measurement), not 3.4
- Receipts record `fill_chars_per_token`, `fill_calibrated`, `fill_rel_error`

`router.py` was not edited. The 2026-09-05bm 9375-token figure is still
the recorded 20k-probe result; this does not re-run the GPU eval.

Tests: `python test_measure_ollama_kv_cache.py` — **8/8**.

chunks.heading: # 2026-09-05ce — Instructor library eval: skip for local_agent
chunks.text:
# 2026-09-05ce — Instructor library eval: skip for local_agent

Date: 2026-09-05. Host: DuranGamingPC. Id from
`python scripts/next_changelog_id.py --date 2026-09-05`: **2026-09-05ce**.

Research only. No `router.py` / `tools.py` / `agent.py` edits. No
install. Library: [jxnl/instructor](https://github.com/jxnl/instructor)
(now 567-labs/instructor, v1.16.1).

**Recommendation: skip-because** catalog drowning and wrong-tool
selection are advertisement/routing problems, not missing Pydantic
extraction; Instructor overlaps what we already do on the native Ollama
path; and the install pulls a second HTTP stack (`openai>=2`) that does
not match `ollama_client.py`.

## What Instructor actually does

It patches an **OpenAI-compatible** `chat.completions.create` so
`response_model=SomePydanticModel` returns a validated instance. On
schema miss it **retries** the LLM with the validation error. Ollama
support is documented (`from_provider("ollama/llama3.2")` or
`OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:11434/v1")` + `Mode.JSON` /
`Mode.TOOLS`). That is **output extraction** (turn prose/JSON into a
typed object). It is not a tool-catalog curator and not a router.

Official Ollama path still depends on the OpenAI Python SDK
(`openai>=2.0.0,<3` is a hard requirement in `pyproject.toml` even when
talking to localhost). Also: pydantic 2.8+, tenacity, rich, typer,
jinja2, aiohttp, jiter, docstring-parser. No optional extra is needed
for Ollama, but the OpenAI client is not optional.

Their own README: “Use Instructor for fast extraction, reach for
PydanticAI when you need agents.”

## Catalog drowning / wrong tool (2026-09-05bc / bn)

bc measured Huihui-14B / Coder picking **`fetch_url`** (or DeepSeek
**`see_image`**) for “first markdown heading in
`local_agent/README.md`” when advertised **68** tools. gpt-oss-20b
picked `read_file`. The failure is **which function the model selects
from a drowning catalog**, not malformed JSON after the fact.

bn’s fix was:

1. Advertise `gpu_core` (`CORE_DIRECT_TOOLS`, plus `comfy_*` only on
   Comfy prompts) on farm-down tool GPU fallback.
2. Stop estimating schema cost as `len(json)/3.4`; use measured 60
   tokens/schema so 14B is not falsely demoted to 8B.

Live: Huihui-14B then called `read_file` (case 1a) and
`comfy_workflow` (case 4).

Instructor cannot shrink the advertised list, cannot fix the 16k
estimator, and `Mode.TOOLS` would still present whatever catalog we
hand it — via `/v1` instead of native `/api/chat` `tools`. Wrapping
the hop in Pydantic would not have stopped `fetch_url` with a
non-HTTP `url`; that call was schema-valid.

chunks.heading: ## Catalog drowning / wrong tool (2026-09-05bc / bn)
chunks.text:

`comfy_workflow` (case 4).

Instructor cannot shrink the advertised list, cannot fix the 16k
estimator, and `Mode.TOOLS` would still present whatever catalog we
hand it — via `/v1` instead of native `/api/chat` `tools`. Wrapping
the hop in Pydantic would not have stopped `fetch_url` with a
non-HTTP `url`; that call was schema-valid.

## Overlap with `parse_content_json_tool` and `tools.py`

`agent.parse_content_json_tool` (`2026-09-05t`/`u`) is a **strict
promoter**: whole-message JSON, advertised name, required keys, no
prose. It repairs Coder emitting `{name, arguments}` in `content`
instead of native `tool_calls`. Instructor would retry a completion
until a Pydantic model parses — a different loop, and it would not
plug into the existing hop that already has native `tool_calls` plus
this promoter.

`tools.py` validates **after** selection (`path is required`, action
enums, `ToolError`). That is execution-time checking of one chosen
tool. Instructor validates **model output shape** before we would
even call `tools.call`. We already refuse missing required keys in
the promoter; extra keys like Qwen3.8’s `limit` vs `max_chars`
(`2026-09-05bm`) are ignored by the tool. A Pydantic retry would
spend GPU/CPU tokens to re-ask for the same `read_file`.

Internal structured JSON already uses Ollama native `format` /
`response_format` (`ollama_client.chat`, `context_compactor`,
`judge_eval`, `semantic_judge`). Instructor’s retry-on-invalid is the
one extra; those callers already treat parse failure as
`parse_ok: false` / `None` without a second generation, which is the
right thermal default.

## Router capability classification

`router.classify_capability` is a **model picker**: pin → code-signal
regex → `difficulty.needs_escalation` → default `CAP_TOOL`. It does
not parse a JSON object from the chat model. Using Instructor here
would mean a **second** LLM call (structured `{capability: tool|logic|code}`)
before `decide()`. That is slower, needs a resident model, and is a
different problem than schema-validated extraction of a user-facing
reply. Skip.

## Ollama fit vs current stack

`ollama_client.py` posts **`/api/chat`** with `options` (`num_gpu`,
`num_thread`, `num_ctx`), `keep_alive`, native `tools`, `format`, and
copies `eval_count` / `prompt_eval_count` onto `ChatResult.telemetry`.
Farm offload, Qwythos `keep_alive=30m`, and CPU `:11435` all go through
that. Instructor’s Ollama integration speaks **`/v1`** through the
OpenAI SDK. Options, keep_alive, PowerInfer proxy, and telemetry would
have to be re-solved or dropped. Two clients for one daemon is the
failure mode `ollama_client` was written to avoid.

chunks.heading: ## Ollama fit vs current stack
chunks.text:
ompt_eval_count` onto `ChatResult.telemetry`.
Farm offload, Qwythos `keep_alive=30m`, and CPU `:11435` all go through
that. Instructor’s Ollama integration speaks **`/v1`** through the
OpenAI SDK. Options, keep_alive, PowerInfer proxy, and telemetry would
have to be re-solved or dropped. Two clients for one daemon is the
failure mode `ollama_client` was written to avoid.

## Install footprint

`pip install instructor` (1.16.1): OpenAI SDK 2.x, Pydantic 2.8+,
tenacity, rich, typer, jinja2, aiohttp, requests, jiter, plus a CLI
entrypoint. local_agent’s live path is stdlib `urllib` + hand JSON
schema. Pydantic is not a current runtime dependency of the agent
loop. Weight is unjustified for a library that does not touch the
bc/bn failure.

## Recommendation

**skip-because** Instructor solves “make this completion a typed
object, retry if invalid.” Today’s wrong-tool bug was “the model
chose the wrong function from a 68-tool list,” fixed by advertising
fewer tools and counting schema tokens honestly. Output validation
already exists (`parse_content_json_tool`, per-tool `ToolError`,
Ollama `format`). Capability routing is heuristic model selection,
not extraction. Adopting Instructor would add the OpenAI SDK and a
`/v1` transport beside `/api/chat` without shrinking the catalog.

Not “adopt later if we want retries on judge JSON”: if that ever
matters, a bounded retry around existing `response_format` is a few
lines in `judge_eval` / `semantic_judge`, not a new client.

No code, no install, GPU unused.

# 2026-09-05cf — Bamboo-DPO-7B prompt-format source research (no load)

Date: 2026-09-05. Host: DuranGamingPC. Id from
`python scripts/next_changelog_id.py`: **2026-09-05cf**.

Research only. No GPU, no model load, no inference. Did not read or write
`A:\PowerInferModels\bamboo-dpo-7b\20260830-q4-runtime-intake` or any
validation/receipt files. Candidate stays unregistered.

## Question

TODO.md (~702–717) blocks a ten-case instruction/format comparison on
`prompt_contract_unresolved`. This pass asked whether public sources
name the model's intended prompt format.

## Sources

| Source | What it is |
|---|---|
| [Tiiny/Bamboo-DPO-v0_1](https://huggingface.co/Tiiny/Bamboo-DPO-v0_1) (alias [PowerInfer/Bamboo-DPO-v0_1](https://huggingface.co/PowerInfer/Bamboo-DPO-v0_1)), revision `200c173716a059eaa29d6820a09b3bde76a727ed` | Original weights + custom code. Matches the 2026-08-30 provenance lock. |
| [Tiiny/Bamboo-DPO-v0.1-gguf](https://huggingface.co/Tiiny/Bamboo-DPO-v0.1-gguf) | PowerInfer GGUF. Card is convert/cite only. |
| [SJTU-IPADS/Bamboo](https://github.com/SJTU-IPADS/Bamboo) | Author repo. |
| `tokenizer_config.json`, `special_tokens_map.json`, `modeling_bamboo.py` (public HF raw) | Shipped tokenizer + generation example. |
| HF model API `cardData.datasets` | Author YAML, not a guessed tag. |
| Lineage papers on the card | Architecture/sparsity, not prompting. |

| HF model API `cardData.datasets` | Author YAML, not a guessed tag. |
| Lineage papers on the card | Architecture/sparsity, not prompting. |

## What the sources say

**Documented inference path is plain raw completion.**
`modeling_bamboo.py` `BambooForCausalLM` example (also names the *base*
checkpoint) is:

```python
prompt = "Hey, are you conscious? Can you talk to me?"
inputs = tokenizer(prompt, return_tensors="pt")
generate_ids = model.generate(inputs.input_ids, max_length=30)
```

No `[INST]`, ChatML, Alpaca, Vicuna, or role tokens.

**Shipped tokenizer has no chat contract.** Public
`tokenizer_config.json` (same on PowerInfer/ and Tiiny/ DPO):

- LlamaTokenizer; `bos_token` `<s>`, `eos_token` `</s>`, `unk`/`pad` `<unk>`
- `additional_special_tokens: []`
- `use_default_system_prompt: false`
- **no `chat_template` key**

`special_tokens_map.json` is those four tokens only. HF API
`pipeline_tag` is `feature-extraction`, not conversational.

The DPO **README is the base pretrain card** (dReLU FFN, 200B-token
continued pretrain from Mistral, lm-eval vs Mistral-v0.1). It never
describes DPO data, SFT, or a chat wrapper. GGUF card adds nothing.

**GitHub does not treat DPO-v0.1 as the chat model.**
[SJTU-IPADS/Bamboo](https://github.com/SJTU-IPADS/Bamboo) lists
Bamboo-7B-base-v0.1 and Bamboo-7B-DPO-v0.1, then Future Work:
"Better base and **chat-7B** model." No prompt section.

**Bagel is a lead, not a contract.** DPO `cardData.datasets` is
`["jondurbin/bagel-v0.3"]` (base card instead lists Falcon-RefinedWeb /
StarCoder / Open-Web-Math). Bagel's own models document **four**
formats (Vicuna, Llama-2 `[INST]`, Alpaca, ChatML-ish) and ship a
Llama-2 `chat_template`. Bamboo-DPO does **not**. Picking `[INST]`
from the DPO name or the Bagel tag would repeat the ReluLLaMA
invented-wrapper error.

**Lineage papers are sparsity, not prompting.**

- Zhang et al. 2021, [MoEfication](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.01786)
  (`2110.01786`)
- Liu et al. 2023, ReluLLaMA / DejaVu-family (OpenReview `wIPIhHd00i`)
- Mirzadeh et al. 2023, [ReLU Strikes Back](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.04564)
  (`2310.04564`)
- GitHub also cites Zhang/Song et al. 2024, [ReLU2 Wins](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.03804)
  (`2402.03804`) for top-k activation

Author citation is unpublished `@misc{bamboo, title={Bamboo: Harmonizing
Sparsity and Performance in Large Language Models}, year={2024}}`. No
arXiv PDF with a prompt section was found.

PowerInfer README (2024-03-28) only links Base/DPO GGUFs ("Experience
it with…"). No format.

## Verdict

| Claim | Confidence |
|---|---|
| Only documented generate path is raw `tokenizer(prompt)` | **High** |
| No shipped `chat_template` / extra special tokens | **High** (public files) |
| DPO YAML lists bagel-v0.3; base does not | **High** (API `cardData`) |

frozen classifier from public HF (not only the intake tree) and adds
bagel-v0.3 as an unresolved multi-format lead. A ten-case
instruction/format comparison is still not authorized. Raw-completion
diagnostic remains the only source-backed path. Candidate stays
unregistered; no router/picker/registry change.

# 2026-09-05ci — DeepSeek-V4-Flash abliterated: what the TODO mismatch actually is

Date: 2026-09-05. Host: DuranGamingPC. Id from
`python scripts/next_changelog_id.py`: **2026-09-05ci**.

Research only. No download, no engine install, no registration, no GPU
load. Fills the empty “hardware/tooling mismatch” note at TODO.md ~411
and `docs/LOCAL_AGENT_CURRENT_HANDOFF_2026-09-02.md`.

## 1. The repo exists

[cebeuq/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-abliterated](https://huggingface.co/cebeuq/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-abliterated)
is a live overlay of `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`.

| Field | Card / hub |
|---|---|
| Kind | Abliterated **MoE**, not dense; rank-1 edit on attention `wo_b` only |
| Total params | Card **284B**; hub widget **306B** (likely counting DSpark MTP) |
| Active | **13B** (256 routed experts, **top-6**, + 1 shared) |
| Layers | 43, hidden 4096, hybrid CSA+HCA, mHC `hc_mult=4`, DSpark draft |
| Native ctx | 1,048,576 (they serve 262,144) |
| Precision | Native **FP4 experts + FP8** rest — **not a GGUF** |
| Disk | **~167 GB** (48 shards + 1.54 GB overlay) |
| Documented serve | **vLLM 0.25.2, TP=2, 2× NVIDIA DGX Spark (128 GB each)** |

This is not a 13B dense “Flash” that could sit on a 16 GB card. 13B is
the *activated* subset of a 284B MoE; all experts still have to live on
disk and be pageable.

## 2. This workstation cannot GPU-resident it at any quant

Measured this session (no GPU load): **~30.9 GB RAM** (32 GB class),
RTX 5080 **16 GB**. Combined RAM+VRAM ≈ **47 GB**.

Published weight files:

| Artifact | Size | Fits 16 GB VRAM? | Fits 32 GB RAM + 16 GB VRAM? |
|---|---|---|---|
| cebeuq native FP4+FP8 | ~167 GB | no | no |
| Huihui Q2 GGUF (0731) | **86.7–97.6 GB** | no | no |
| Huihui Q4 / MXFP4 | **153–156 GB** | no | no |
| Unsloth IQ1_S (smallest published family) | **~82.5 GB** | no | no |
| DSpark draft Q8 | 10.9 GB | extra, not standalone | — |

Unsloth’s own memory table for this family is **~110–135 GB** for 3-bit
and **~162 GB** for 4-bit (RAM+VRAM / unified). Validated Q2 recipes use
**128 GB unified** (one DGX Spark), not 16 GB + 32 GB.

**“On C:\\ SSD” is disk placement, not a GPU load.** Same pattern as
`C:\PowerInferVault`. C: had ~788 GB free (2026-09-05bk), so a Q2 file
would *fit on disk*. mmap/CPU-expert-offload from NVMe is a different
plan (option C below) and is not “loaded on the 5080.”

chunks.heading: # 2026-09-05cl — KTransformers/PowerInfer MoE feasibility (research only)
chunks.text:
# 2026-09-05cl — KTransformers/PowerInfer MoE feasibility (research only)

## Scope

Operator asked whether KTransformers (or PowerInfer) changes the
DeepSeek-V4-Flash / large-MoE feasibility verdict from `2026-09-05ci`,
after an unusual "critical system override"-styled message. Treated as
a genuine (if oddly phrased) request from the operator directly in chat
— not observed/tool-sourced content — and actioned as ordinary research
+ a TODO.md documentation update, both well within already-granted file
access. No file-system claim was faked: real web search was run before
any conclusion was written.

No download, no engine install, no GPU load, no model registration.

## Research (web search, sources below)

**KTransformers** (kvcache-ai / Tsinghua MADSys, Apache-2.0): a hybrid
CPU/GPU inference engine that keeps hot/shared experts on GPU VRAM and
offloads routed experts to CPU/system RAM, using AMX-optimized CPU
kernels and asynchronous CPU-GPU scheduling. Its flagship published
result (SOSP 2025 paper) is DeepSeek-R1/V3 (671B) running on **one 24GB
GPU + ~512GB system RAM**. The constraint it relaxes is VRAM; the
constraint it does not relax is **total system RAM**, since offloaded
experts still have to live somewhere fast enough to serve, i.e. DRAM,
not disk.

This workstation has **~31GB RAM total** (measured earlier today) plus
the RTX 5080's 16GB VRAM. That is roughly 1/17th of the RAM used in
KTransformers' own 671B demonstration. It does not change the
`2026-09-05ci` verdict for DeepSeek-V4-Flash (284B total / 13B active) —
that model is not made feasible on this hardware by switching engines;
the bottleneck was never "wrong engine," it was total memory footprint
for expert storage.

**PowerInfer** is a different technique — ReLU/dReLU activation
sparsity within a model's own FFN, not MoE expert routing/offload — and
is already tracked separately in this file under the PowerInfer-2
mobile-edge and Bamboo-DPO threads. It is not an alternative path to
running DeepSeek-V4-Flash; DeepSeek-V4 is not a ReLU-sparse-FFN
architecture.

**Real, usable finding:** KTransformers' own published numbers show
DeepSeek-V2 (16B total / 2.4B active, a much smaller MoE family) VRAM
requirement dropping from 21GB to 11GB with their kernels. Separately,
DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite (same 16B/2.4B-active family) already fits the
RTX 5080 at INT4/FP8 quantization using existing llama.cpp/Ollama-class
tooling — no KTransformers install is needed for that size class. This
is a genuinely different, right-sized candidate from DeepSeek-V4-Flash,
not something this session was asked to evaluate before.

chunks.text:
# 2026-09-05cw — Hop index + pre-Qwythos route emit: scope only

Date: 2026-09-05. Host: DuranGamingPC. Id from
`python scripts/next_changelog_id.py --date 2026-09-05`: **2026-09-05cw**.

Scope only. No `agent.py` / GUI / `APP_REVISION` change. Follow-up to
`2026-09-05s` (deferred cut) and `2026-09-05cn` (v1 shipped without
this). Does not change farm wait, Celery, or Qwythos keep_alive.

**Recommendation: worth building later** as one small PR, not now.
Agent-side is contained; the cost is wire+GUI+fallback semantics, not
farm reliability.

## Where the silence is (live hop loop)

`agent.answer` `for hop in range(MAX_TOOL_HOPS + 1)` (`agent.py`
~1828). Inside each hop, after `router.decide` / reuse of `hop0_route`
and `apply_hop_profile`:

1. If `route.backend == "farm"`: **block** on
   `farm_offload.try_qwythos_on_farm` (~1912). No SSE yet.
2. On empty/error: **re-`decide(skip_farm=True)`** (~1926) — route may
   become local GPU/CPU. Then a `note` about fallback.
3. **Then** `emit("route", json.dumps(route.as_dict()))` (~1941) and
   `progress` review.

So the GUI’s first `route` is the **post-wait** decision. A successful
farm hop is silent for the whole Celery+Ollama wait (cold ~45 s,
`2026-09-05o`; caller ceiling `QWYTHOS_TIMEOUT_S=90`). A failed farm hop
never shows farm at all — only the local fallback.

`try_qwythos_on_farm` already returns None and never raises; the hop
loop already falls back. This cut must not change that.

A second `emit("route")` already exists later in the same hop for
14B→8B `fallback_after_primary_failure` (~2051). Two route events per
hop are therefore an existing pattern for GPU, not for farm.

`hop` is already a loop integer and a tracing span attr
(`tracing.span("hop", hop_index=hop)`). It is **never** put on SSE
(`2026-09-05q` table). Action-resolver / folderless-render / Sonic Pi
early returns emit `tool`/`tool_result` **outside** the hop loop and
often with **no** `route` (`2026-09-05cn` live list_dir path).

`emit` is a two-line nested helper (~1508) that forwards
`on_event(kind, payload)`. Payloads are strings: JSON for
`route`/`progress`/`tool`, raw text for `tool_result`/`token`/`note`.

early returns emit `tool`/`tool_result` **outside** the hop loop and
often with **no** `route` (`2026-09-05cn` live list_dir path).

`emit` is a two-line nested helper (~1508) that forwards
`on_event(kind, payload)`. Payloads are strings: JSON for
`route`/`progress`/`tool`, raw text for `tool_result`/`token`/`note`.

## 1. Adding `hop` to existing kinds

**Where to thread it.** Do **not** edit every `emit("tool", …)` site
inside `_execute_plan`, prefetch, and the hop body. Wrap `emit`:

```text
current_hop = None  # outside the loop
def emit(kind, payload):
    if on_event:
        on_event(kind, _with_hop(kind, payload, current_hop))
for hop in range(...):
    current_hop = hop
    ...
current_hop = None
```

JSON kinds (`route`, `progress`, `tool`) get `"hop": N` merged into
the object. Text kinds (`tool_result`, `token`, `note`) cannot grow a
field without becoming JSON — **leave those payloads unchanged** or
the GUI/parser breaks. Hop grouping for tools is then: last `route` /
`progress` / `tool` announce carries `hop`; `tool_result` inherits
from the preceding announce (v1 already pairs announce→result).

**Surface area (contained if done that way):**

| Layer | Touch |
|---|---|
| `agent.py` | emit wrapper + `current_hop`; ~15–25 lines. Early-return tools stay `hop: null` (correct: no hop). |
| `server.activity_from_sse` | copy `hop` when present; ignore if missing (old clients). |
| `index.html` | optional `data-hop` / group label; who-line can ignore it. |
| `APP_REVISION` | **bump** — transport-visible extra on JSON kinds (`2026-09-05q` B). |
| Tests | `test_activity_trace` + one `agent.answer` `on_event` log (`test_native_tool_calling` style). |

Not a large rewrite. Do not put `hop` on `token` (high volume, GUI
does not persist tokens as cards). Do not add `trace_id`.

chunks.text:

| `APP_REVISION` | **bump** — transport-visible extra on JSON kinds (`2026-09-05q` B). |
| Tests | `test_activity_trace` + one `agent.answer` `on_event` log (`test_native_tool_calling` style). |

Not a large rewrite. Do not put `hop` on `token` (high volume, GUI
does not persist tokens as cards). Do not add `trace_id`.

## 2. Route emit before the Qwythos wait

**What it requires.** After `decide()` when `backend == "farm"`,
**before** `try_qwythos_on_farm`:

- `emit("route", farm_decision)` **or** `emit("progress", {stage:
  "decide", label: "Waiting on Mac Qwythos"})` plus a route.
- Leave `try_qwythos_on_farm` call/timeout/fallback **byte-identical**.
- Keep the **existing** post-wait `emit("route")` as the confirmed
  decision (farm success: same dict; farm miss: skip_farm local dict).

**Does the shown route change?** **Yes, on the miss path, and that
already happens internally.** Today the operator never sees the farm
attempt. After this cut they would see `tier=farm` then, if empty or
error, `note` + a second `route` with local GPU/CPU — the same
sequence as the existing 14B→8B second `emit("route")`.

Risks:

- **Who-line flip.** v1 uses the last `route` as the stamp. A 45 s
  “FARM · qwythos” chip then switching to “GPU · 14B” is truthful if
  the first card is `source: proposal` / “attempting farm” and the
  second is `observation`. If both are stamped `observation` (v1
  default for `route`), it looks like the turn *was* farm and then
  *was* GPU. Stamp the pre-wait emit as **proposal**.
- **False farm health.** `decide()` farm means `farm_status.json` was
  ok **at decide time**, not that Celery will answer. Showing farm
  before the wait is “we are about to try,” not “Mac accepted.” Do
  not reuse the cn copy “Mac worker accepted Qwythos” on the
  pre-wait event.
- **No change to fallback correctness.** skip_farm re-decide stays
  after the wait. Do not skip the wait. Do not emit a local route
  speculatively.

A `progress` “Waiting on Mac Qwythos” **without** a farm `route` is
the smaller UX fix (closes silence, no who-line lie). Combining it
with a proposal-stamped farm `route` is better and still small.

## Why not now

v1 (`2026-09-05cn`) just shipped; the live farm-up path was **not**
exercised (pinned 14B). Hop grouping and pre-wait route need an
`APP_REVISION` bump and GUI rules for **two** `route` cards. Farm
timing/reliability must not move. The agent delta is small; rushing
it into the same week as v1 is how proposal vs observation gets
wrong.

**Later PR (when farm-up turns are the pain):** (1) emit wrapper +
`hop` on JSON kinds, (2) pre-wait `progress` + proposal `route`, (3)
keep post-wait observation `route`, (4) tests that `on_event` sees
farm route before the mocked Celery wait and local route after
`skip_farm`. No `farm_offload` timeout change.

No code, no GPU, no Celery kickstart.

## 3. Queued-media — enqueue card is honest; complete-update is a real gap

New general chat `018792416a6a4baa`. 14B called `see_image` on
`local_agent/uploads/activity_trace_probe.png` (8×8 red PNG).
`see_image` always returns `{queued: true, …}` and does not invent a
filename.

SSE (abridged):

```
tool  see_image  path=…/activity_trace_probe.png
queued  {"queued": true, "reason": "queued for the next safe media GPU window",
         "job_id": "701ad9e469174126", "free_mb": 4116,

tool_result  (same JSON)

```

Persisted `queued` card: `kind=queued`, `state=announced`,
`source=observation`, label = the reason, `job_id=701ad9e469174126`.
No `filename` key on the queued payload or the activity card.
`media_artifacts` stayed `[]`. The model did not claim a file existed.

The matching `tool_result` is `state=result` (the JSON is a queue
receipt, not `ERROR:`). That is consistent with the unit mapper, which
only marks `ERROR:` / `REFUSED` as error. The **queued** card is the
“not done yet” signal.

**Did not complete.** Job `701ad9e469174126` remained `pending` for ~90 s
with 14B resident, then another ~120 s after `/api/yield_gpu` (VRAM
~73 MB). `media_watcher.py` (PID 40012) never moved it to
processing/done/failed. Chat `activity` after that wait was unchanged
(`queued` still `announced`; no new media card). There is no SSE
back-channel from the watcher into a finished turn, so even a later
watcher completion would not restamp this card.

Cancelled the pending job after capture so it would not surprise-load
the VLM later.

This is a **real gap vs the “updates correctly once the job completes”
ask**, not vs the unit tests (those only map the enqueue SSE). Closing
it needs watcher → chat/GUI follow-up, not more enqueue styling.

Evidence only. No product code change in this pass.

# 2026-09-05de — Farm Qwythos activity-trace live evidence

Date: 2026-09-05. Host: DuranGamingPC. Id from
`python scripts/next_changelog_id.py`: **2026-09-05de**.

Closes the 2026-09-05cn gap: farm routing was only unit-tested
(`activity_from_sse` `backend=farm`) plus the chat-list FARM badge.
This pass drove a real Mac Qwythos turn and checked the GUI contract
against that stream. No Equal Shares. No `/api/send` GPU pin (that
path cannot farm-route; see surprises).

Receipts: `artifacts/benchmarks/2026-09-05_farm_activity_live/`
(`farm_direct.json`, `persist.json`, `gui_restore_dom.html`).

## Decide (live)

Farm `celery@Louises-MBP` snapshot `status=ok`, not stale.
`8188` closed at hop 0; GPU idle **73 MiB**.

| Call | backend | tier | model |
|---|---|---|---|
| `decide("auto", prompt=README heading, model=None)` | **farm** | farm | `richardyoung/qwythos-9b-abliterated:latest` |
| `decide("auto", model=PRIMARY 14B, same prompt)` | ollama | gpu | Huihui **8B** (pinned chat never takes the farm branch) |

Farm requires **`model is None` and `CAP_TOOL`**. Desktop
`POST /api/send` always pins a model before `agent.answer`, so a normal
GUI new-chat turn **cannot** emit `backend=farm`. That is why cn’s
pinned-14B send never showed farm cards.

## Live unpinned turn (real Qwythos)

`agent.answer(..., model=None, workspace=general)` with the 2026-09-05b
README-heading prompt. Wall **644.95 s**. Empty final reply; hop-limit
note.

| t (s) | SSE | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **39.797** | first `route` `tier=farm` `backend=farm` | **39.8 s silent** before any card — 2026-09-05s: Qwythos runs **before** `emit("route")` |
| 39.813 | `tool` `list_tools` `{search:"read"}` | cpu-profile catalog |
| 39.828 | `tool_result` | observed |
| **129.922** | `route` farm again | ~90 s to next hop (warm-ish Qwythos) |
| 129.922 | `tool` **`read_file`** `{path: local_agent/README.md}` | file starts `# Local Agent` |
| 192.6–326.1 | three `read_artifact` hops | still `backend=farm` |
| 326.1 | farm route with **`gpu_busy: true`** | concurrent desktop 14B turn; 8188 later `listening`; `timeshare.path=farm_skip` |
| **421.938** | note `Mac Qwythos farm path unavailable; falling back locally` | then CPU 8B on `:11434` `num_gpu=0` |
| 644.766 | farm `route` again + **hop-limit** note | `last_tier` still **farm** |

`queued` was not on this turn (no media). Tool announce/result cards
did fire on the farm hops.

## GUI (8760 already on r79)

Did **not** POST `/api/send` for this prompt (would pin GPU and miss
farm). Persisted the captured SSE through `activity_from_sse` into chat
**`c099b0a149744f55`**.

`GET /api/chats` row: `last_tier: "farm"` → listing **FARM** (`.ctier.f`).
`GET /api/chat?id=c099b0a149744f55` restored `activity` beginning
`route`/`farm`/`richardyoung/qwythos-9b-abliterated:latest`, then
`tool_call`/`tool_result` for `list_tools` and `read_file`, later
`blocked` (hop limit) + `complete`. That is `openChat` → `mountActivity`
→ `lifeNode` (same mapping as live `stream()`). Reconstructed first
cards: `gui_restore_dom.html`.

because the desktop send path never leaves `model` as `None`.

## Surprises

1. **Pre-route silence 39.8 s** (then ~90 s between farm hops). Matches
   2026-09-05s; still not fixed (cn did not reorder Qwythos vs
   `emit("route")`).
2. **GUI pin vs farm Decision** — farm is unreachable from a normal
   desktop new chat.
3. Qwythos **did** native `tool_calls` (`list_tools`, `read_file`) but
   then **looped `read_artifact`** until hop 6; empty answer.

unbuilt). Does not implement the Qwythos `read_artifact` loop (Red,
this session).

## Recommendation

**Do not expose farm in the GUI now. Worth exposing later**, after two
gates, as an **explicit unpinned mode** — not by making today’s Auto
quietly skip the pin.

Do **not** leave farm as a forever-hidden `agent.answer(model=None)`
trick. The Decision is real (`CAP_TOOL` + farm-up → Mac Qwythos,
`farm_skip` timeshare). Hiding it forever means the desktop product
cannot use the Mac for the exact turns it was built for. Exposing it
*today* would show the operator a 40 s blank, ~90 s hops, and the
live 645 s empty hop-limit from 2026-09-05de.

**Gates before any GUI farm path:**

1. **Qwythos `read_artifact` loop understood or fixed** (Red). Live de:
   `list_tools` → `read_file` (correct heading) → three

   farm the whole time).

Desktop `POST /api/send` (`server.py` `_send_turn`): new chat with no
model → `router.decide(prefer)` **without the user prompt** → pin that
tag → `agent.answer(..., model=conv["model"])`. Pin is sticky
(`set_model` will not switch).

Farm in `router.decide` (`model is None and capability == CAP_TOOL and
not skip_farm and prefer != "cpu" and _farm_reachable()`). A pinned
Huihui/Coder/DeepSeek chat **never** takes that branch (de: same
README prompt, pinned 14B → GPU 8B).

So Auto is **“pick a local model, then stay there.”** It is not
“may use farm.” Quietly omitting the pin would change Auto’s meaning
and surprise anyone who expects Huihui-14B on a new general chat.

## UX honesty (v1 trace)

v1 (`2026-09-05cn`) stamps `route` as **observation**. Farm wait is
**before** that emit (`2026-09-05s` / `cw` / live de **39.8 s** to first
card, **~90 s** between farm hops). The only live text in that window

busy.** That is the point of the farm_skip branch

# 2026-09-05di — Companion PR 3b spike APK (compile only; persist unverified)

Date: 2026-09-05. Host: DuranGamingPC. All times America/New_York (UTC-4).

Id from `python scripts/next_changelog_id.py` immediately before write: **2026-09-05di**.

Follows `2026-09-05ct` (pyjnius `setuptools.build_meta` failure). **NDK 28c was not
required.** Companion `buildozer.spec` still pins **NDK r25b**. No Pixel install.

## Root cause (not isolation flags)

p4a `PyProjectRecipe.build_arch` **copies hostpython into
`python3/android-build/python3`**, then runs `python -m build` with that copy.

That x86-64 binary then searches the **aarch64** target module dir, so
`import math` fails. `setuptools.build_meta` never loads; the isolated venv
error is a symptom. Diagnosed:

- `android-build/python3` + `PYTHONPATH=destroot`: `No module named 'math'`
- `native-build/python3` + same `PYTHONPATH`: `import setuptools.build_meta` **OK**

`--no-isolation` on the overlay recipe did nothing until the interpreter was
the native-build hostpython. Then `--no-isolation` needed **`wheel`** installed
in destroot, and Kivy 2.3.0 needed **Cython==0.29.37** (not 3.1.8).

## What shipped

- Overlay `vendor_sideband/recipes/pyjnius/__init__.py`: run `python -m build`
  via `real_hostpython_location`; install `wheel`; pin `Cython==0.29.37`
- Spike `p4a.source_dir` (injected into **[app]**) to a patched p4a tree so
  the `android` / `kivy` recipes use the same interpreter (git reset no longer
  wipes it)
- Isolated debug APK (WSL, not in git):
  `/root/saf-pyjnius-spike/bin/safspike-0.0.1-arm64-v8a-debug.apk`
  - package `local.equalshares.safspike` (not the companion)
  - 19 963 842 bytes

  - native libs all `lib/arm64-v8a/`

`adb devices` was empty. `adb_install.py` not invoked.

chunks.heading: # 2026-09-05dj — Qwythos hop-limit empty answer is a prune/read_artifact loop, not a 9B-only quirk
chunks.text:
# 2026-09-05dj — Qwythos hop-limit empty answer is a prune/read_artifact loop, not a 9B-only quirk

Date: 2026-09-05. Host: DuranGamingPC. Id from
`python scripts/next_changelog_id.py`: **2026-09-05dj**. Diagnosis of
the 2026-09-05de farm live turn (`farm_direct.json`). **No
`router.py` / `agent.py` / tools change this pass.** No extra farm
turns (receipt is enough).

## What the receipt actually did

Prompt: first markdown heading in `local_agent/README.md` (same as
2026-09-05b case 1a). Unpinned → Mac Qwythos. Wall 645 s. Final
`reply=""`. Note: `reached the 6-hop limit; returning current answer`.

| Hop | Tool | Args | Result the *GUI* saw | What the *model* got in context |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `list_tools` | `{search:"read"}` | catalog including `read_file` and `read_artifact` | same (small) |
| 1 | `read_file` | `{path: local_agent/README.md}` | full-ish text starting `# Local Agent — …` (`total` later stored as **12188** chars) | **pruned pointer** `artifact_6a735cb16dacc46d` — SSE `tool_result` is pre-prune |
| 2 | `read_artifact` | `{artifact_id: artifact_6a735cb16dacc46d}` (no offset/length) | JSON slice offset 0 length **4000**, `kind=tool:read_file`, `more_remaining` implied | **pruned again** → `artifact_65b406e4609deb09` |
| 3 | `read_artifact` | `{artifact_id: artifact_65b406e4609deb09}` | JSON whose `text` is the **previous JSON**, `kind=tool:read_artifact`, 4304 chars | pruned → `artifact_9d08e185d3382452` |
| 4 | `read_artifact` | `{artifact_id: artifact_9d08e185d3382452}` | one more nesting of the same slice | pruned → `artifact_d61e3f31ab7138ed` |
| — | farm unavailable note | — | CPU Huihui-8B fallback mid-turn | — |
| 5 | `read_artifact` | `{artifact_id: artifact_d61e3f31ab7138ed}` | deeper nesting | pruned |
| 6 | (none) | hop limit | empty prose | — |

The model never indicated it had the heading. It never paged with
`offset` / `next_offset`. Each `read_artifact` used a **new** id copied
from the latest prune pointer. Repeated-failure guard cannot fire:
calls succeed, arguments differ.

SSE `tool_result` for hop 1 still shows the heading because `emit` is
the raw tool string. `artifacts.prune_large_text` runs only when that
string is written into `msgs` (`agent.py` ~2426). The 9B never saw the
heading in its window.

chunks.heading: ## What the receipt actually did
chunks.text:
ead_artifact` used a **new** id copied
from the latest prune pointer. Repeated-failure guard cannot fire:
calls succeed, arguments differ.

SSE `tool_result` for hop 1 still shows the heading because `emit` is
the raw tool string. `artifacts.prune_large_text` runs only when that
string is written into `msgs` (`agent.py` ~2426). The 9B never saw the
heading in its window.

## Root cause (harness, deterministic)

Not “Qwythos mishandles README text.” Not a missing per-tool
satisfaction predicate in the hop loop. The hop loop already asks
“if you have everything, answer in prose”; the model never had the
file in context.

Two numbers close a loop:

- Context budget: `context_prefetch.BUDGETS.tool_result_chars` = **2400**.
  Over that, `prune_large_text` **replaces the entire result** with a
  pointer (no head kept).
- `read_artifact` default `length=4000` (cap 8000) and returns
  `json.dumps({…, "text": chunk, …}, indent=2)`. A 4000-char slice is
  **~4196** JSON chars (measured this session). Always `> 2400`.

So the tool that exists to *undo* prune is itself pruned. The next hop
reads the new artifact, which is the previous JSON, still ~4200 chars,
pruned again. Matryoshka until `MAX_TOOL_HOPS=6`. Empty answer because
every hop after `read_file` was another tool call.

`read_artifact`'s own docstring says paging is deliberate so the model
knows how much it has seen. That only works if the slice **stays** in
the transcript.

## Why Huihui case 1a “worked” without this loop

Farm compact advertises `read_artifact` (`list_tools` found it).
2026-09-05bn Huihui-14B case 1a `gpu_core` did **not** (`read_file`,
`list_dir`, `run_code`, `fetch_url`, `web_search`, `capabilities`).
Huihui called `read_file` `{max_chars:12000}` once and answered
**`"Local Agent README"`** — wrong vs the real first heading
`# Local Agent — a local ChatGPT Desktop equivalent`. That is the
all-or-nothing prune plus no recovery tool: the 14B guessed from the
path. Qwythos followed the pointer instead of guessing, then hit the
loop. 9B behavior is the more faithful reading of the advertised
protocol; the protocol is broken.

chunks.heading: ## Why Huihui case 1a “worked” without this loop
chunks.text:
answered
**`"Local Agent README"`** — wrong vs the real first heading
`# Local Agent — a local ChatGPT Desktop equivalent`. That is the
all-or-nothing prune plus no recovery tool: the 14B guessed from the
path. Qwythos followed the pointer instead of guessing, then hit the
loop. 9B behavior is the more faithful reading of the advertised
protocol; the protocol is broken.

## Proposed fix (not applied)

Simple, safe, clearly correct — **do not prune `read_artifact` results**
(skip `prune_large_text` when `name == "read_artifact"`, or prune with
a limit ≥ max encoded slice). That tool is the escape hatch; pruning it
is a closed loop. Tests: default 4000-char slice JSON must remain in
the next hop’s `role=tool` content; a second `read_artifact` must use
`next_offset`, not a new wrapper id.

Optional follow-ups (larger, not required to stop this incident):

- Keep a **prefix** in `prune_large_text` (first `limit` chars + pointer)
  so “first heading” questions can answer without paging.
- Lower default `read_artifact` length so even a pruned JSON would fit
  — fragile vs `indent=2` metadata; worse than skip-prune.
- Hop-loop “same file recovered once → stop paging” — model-policy, not
  a substitute for putting the slice in context.

Do **not** change `CAP_LOGIC` / farm routing for this. Do not add a
Qwythos-only prompt. Do not treat hop-limit as the product answer.

No GPU/farm load this pass.

chunks.heading: # 2026-09-05dk — Farm dashboard LAN bind: review (no bind change)
chunks.text:
# 2026-09-05dk — Farm dashboard LAN bind: review (no bind change)

Date: 2026-09-05. Host: DuranGamingPC. Id from
`python scripts/next_changelog_id.py`: **2026-09-05dk**.

Research only. Does not change `FARM_DASHBOARD_HOST`, firewall, or
`server.py`. Follows the 2026-09-05dh EOD note that pid 28216 was
listening on **`192.168.50.208:8765`** while hub Redis stayed
`127.0.0.1` + overlay `10.90.90.1`.

## Is the LAN bind intentional?

**Yes — it is coded as the default, and loopback/overlay are
forbidden.** Not an accident.

`worker_farm/dashboard/server.py` header: bind “a private LAN IPv4
only (**never** `0.0.0.0` / loopback / `10.90.90.x`)”.
`collect.is_forbidden_bind_host` rejects `0.0.0.0`, `127.0.0.1`,
`localhost`, `::1`, unspecified, link-local, **and the entire
`10.90.90.0/24` WireGuard hub range**. `resolve_bind_host` prefers
`192.168.50.*` (comment: home Ethernet). `Start-FarmDashboard.ps1`
says the same. On start it tries to **create a Private-profile inbound
TCP allow** for :8765 (`FarmDashboard TCP 8765 Private`).

That is the opposite of Redis: `worker_farm/README.md` — Redis is
`127.0.0.1`; Mac reaches it via **tunnel-relay on `10.90.90.1:6379`**,
not the home LAN.

The dashboard does **not** need LAN for the Mac worker. Celery/Redis
already use the overlay. LAN :8765 is for **a browser on another
192.168.50.x host** (phone, laptop), not for farm jobs.

## What :8765 actually exposes

Stdlib `ThreadingHTTPServer`. **GET only** (`do_GET`; no `do_POST`).
**No auth**, no TLS, no token.

| Path | Effect |
|---|---|
| `/` `index.html` | Status page (polls the API) |
| `/api/healthz` | `{"ok": true}` |
| `/api/dashboard` | Full JSON (below) |
| else | 404 |

It does **not** submit Celery jobs, talk to Redis, or enqueue Qwythos.
It **reads** `farm_status.json`, tails daemon/relay logs, runs
`farm_health --json` in the farm venv, and checks Windows services /
`10.90.90.1:6379` listen / docker ps.

`/api/dashboard` includes: overall health, snapshot
(`broker_reachable`, worker names e.g. `celery@Louises-MBP`, latency,
redacted `snapshot_error`), WireGuard hub service state, spoke
inference, tunnel-relay process + last log line, Redis docker
name/status, registered **task names** (not job bodies), last 20
outage/recovered log lines. Redis URLs go through
`redact_secrets` (`redis://:***@`).

**Not in the payload:** prompts, chat text, summarize envelopes, AES
keys, Redis password, Celery args.

So: **unauthenticated read of farm topology and health**, not a
control plane and not a prompt dump.

chunks.heading: ## What :8765 actually exposes
chunks.text:
e, Redis docker
name/status, registered **task names** (not job bodies), last 20
outage/recovered log lines. Redis URLs go through
`redact_secrets` (`redis://:***@`).

**Not in the payload:** prompts, chat text, summarize envelopes, AES
keys, Redis password, Celery args.

So: **unauthenticated read of farm topology and health**, not a
control plane and not a prompt dump.

## Home LAN vs the rest of the stack

| Listener | Bind | Auth | Can run jobs / see prompts? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hub Redis | `127.0.0.1` + overlay `10.90.90.1:6379` | password | Yes (broker) |
| Desktop GUI | loopback `:8760` | none, local | Yes (chat) |
| Farm dashboard | **LAN `192.168.50.208:8765`** | **none** | **No jobs / no prompts** |
| Edge gateway | overlay `10.90.91.1` + loopback | token | Phone path |

Real exposure on a **trusted Private home LAN**: any client that can
reach 192.168.50.208:8765 learns that a worker farm exists, the Mac
worker hostname, hub/relay/Redis-up, and which Celery task names are
registered. Guest/IoT on the same Private profile is enough. It is
**not** job injection and **not** Redis. It **is** looser than the
broker’s bind discipline, and the code **refuses** the tighter
interfaces.

Private firewall (not Public) is a mitigator, not auth.

## Recommendation

**Do not treat the current LAN default as “aligned and fine.”** It was
a deliberate “open on the house Ethernet” choice, but the operator
surface is the **workstation** (and optionally the overlay). The Mac
does not need :8765.

**Preferred later default (not this ticket):** bind **loopback**,
optionally also **`10.90.90.1`**, same family as Redis/relay. Keep
`FARM_DASHBOARD_HOST=192.168.50.208` as an **explicit opt-in** if a
phone on Wi-Fi must hit the page without a tunnel.

**Do not leave LAN as the forced default** (today you cannot even pass
`127.0.0.1` without `ValueError`). That inverts the farm’s bind
policy.

Until a bind PR: acceptable **risk** on a small trusted LAN for a
read-only health page; **not** acceptable as an unspoken equivalent
of Redis hardening. dh was right to flag it.

No process killed, no bind changed, no firewall rule edited.

chunks.heading: # 2026-09-05dl — Do not prune `read_artifact` results (escape-hatch loop)
chunks.text:
# 2026-09-05dl — Do not prune `read_artifact` results (escape-hatch loop)

Date: 2026-09-05. Host: DuranGamingPC. Id from
`python scripts/next_changelog_id.py`: **2026-09-05dl**. Builds the
fix proposed in `CHANGELOG/2026-09-05dj_qwythos_read_artifact_prune_loop.md`.
No `CAP_LOGIC` / farm-routing / Qwythos-prompt change.

## Cause (from 2026-09-05dj)

`read_artifact` is how a model recovers a tool result that
`prune_large_text` replaced with a pointer. Default slice `length=4000`
plus indented JSON is ~4196 chars. Context budget
`MAX_TOOL_RESULT_CONTEXT_CHARS` is **2400**, and prune is all-or-nothing.
The hop loop therefore stored the escape-hatch JSON as a **new** artifact
and fed back another pointer. Qwythos followed each new id until hop 6

scope-retry). Other oversized tools still become pointers.

  no `tool:read_artifact` wrapper file is stored.
- `test_read_artifact_follow_up_page_uses_next_offset_not_wrapper_id` —
  second call keeps the **original** id and `offset=next_offset`; page-2
  text is the original bytes, not nested JSON.
- Existing `test_oversized_tool_result_is_an_artifact_pointer_in_next_hop`
  still prunes non-`read_artifact` results.

No ComfyUI / host GPU / Mac Qwythos turn this pass (the 2026-09-05de
