empty living room with no actor. The earlier manifest `image_62e576a9-….json`
(03:53:51Z) had the full prompt.

## Where the truncation happened — the model, primed by our own tool output

Evidence, all read-only:

- `knowledge/traces.db`, trace `54751f9e…`, tool span `render_story_image_batch`
  at 04:08:10Z: `arg_sha256=5448b458…`, `arg_json_bytes=360`. The span is
  recorded in `agent._trace_tool_call`, whose args are the Ollama native
  `tool_calls` arguments plus only the server-injected `__conversation_id`.
- **The hash reproduces exactly** from
  `{"__conversation_id":"1d4a42d3b5834081","flux":true,"jobs":[{"model_profile":"realpro_flux","prompt":"<first sentence>","story":"Backrooms Sitcom Audition Prompt Pack"}],"model_profile":"realpro_flux","stop_on_failure":true,"timeout_s":900}`
  (`json.dumps(sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False)`, as `tracing.summarize_tool_args`).
  The 03:41:46Z call's hash `3eef75f4…` (751 bytes) reproduces from the same
  dict with the **full** prompt. So the two calls are identical except the prompt.
- The turn went through the native tool-call path (review → decide → tool_call),
  not `action_resolver` (which short-circuits the turn), not the managed prompt-pack
  plans, and not the Backrooms adapters. `ollama_client.chat_stream` and
  `tools.parse_call_tool_args` do not alter string values. `tools._normalize_batch_job`
  only `.strip()`s, and it runs after the span was hashed anyway.
- Why the model sent that string: `tools.render_story_image_batch` labels
  each job `"prompt_preview": job["prompt"][:120]`. For this prompt, 120 chars
  ends **exactly** at the first period, so the preview reads as a whole
  prompt. `agentic_state.observe_tool` keeps the first 520 chars of each result
  as trusted task-state evidence. All three prior batch observations for this
  chat (`runtime/agentic_tasks/1d4a42d3b5834081.json`) contain that exact
  120-char preview. The 8B model (`huihui_ai/qwen3-abliterated:8b`) copied it
  back as the job prompt.

Also noted (already fixed earlier, not changed here): the 04:08 call returned
`completed` after 2.5 s with the *previous* 03:53 manifest. That was the stale
manifest bug fixed in `2026-09-24b` (launch-time manifest filter), which landed
after this incident (the `tools.py.bak_inlinemedia_20260924T002509` backup lacks
`_story_job_started_at`). The invented "QA passed / SELECTED" replies in this chat
are covered by `test_native_tool_calling.test_fabricated_qa_selected_claim_after_batch_render_is_corrected`.

chunks.text:
# 2026-09-24f — local_agent GUI: inline cards for failed and not-started batch stills

## Why

After 2026-09-24b, `render_story_image_batch` got one ready card per completed
still. `failures[]` and `pending[]` produced nothing, so in a half-failed batch
the operator saw the frames that rendered and no sign of the ones that didn't.

## What changed

`local_agent/server.py`
- `collect_story_media_artifacts()` now adds `_batch_status_cards()` after
  the ready cards of a batch result:
  - **one error card per `failures[i]`** (`status: "error"`, no filename),
    in the same locator shape as the `poll_render_watches()` error cards.
    `label` = `batch item <index>: <prompt_preview>`. `note` is the
    `blocked_by` summary when present (e.g. `foreign_backend: port 8188 is
    held by pid …`). Otherwise it is the error (`finished_without_manifest` /
    `timed_out` / the launch error), plus `(pid N)` and the last `log_tail`
    line. Capped at 240 chars. Also carries `batch_index` and `phase`.
  - **one summary card for all of `pending[]`** (`status: "not_started"`),
    labelled `N batch items (i, j, …)` and noted `not started after failure —
    story <s>`. Decision: one card, not one per entry. With
    `stop_on_failure` (the default), every job after the first failure lands
    in `pending[]`. Twenty identical "not started" cards would bury the one
    real failure. The label still lists every missing index.
- These file-less cards carry a `card_key`. `media_artifact_key()` uses it,
  and `extend_unique_artifacts()` de-duplicates on it just as it does for
  files. Pending/error locators without a `card_key` (render-watch cards)
  still always pass. Real duplication path found: `agent._emit_tool_result`
  sends the clipped `tool_result` **and** the full internal media event, and a
  batch result under 4000 chars (e.g. an all-launch-failure batch) parses on
  both. Without the key every error card appeared twice. The key includes the
  pid, so a retry that fails again with a new pid is a new card. It is
  per-turn only: the turn's `_media_artifacts` list starts empty.

`local_agent/static/index.html` — `mountMediaArtifact()`
- The error branch also renders `status === "not_started"` with the headline
  "not started" instead of "generate failed".
- Error/not-started cards show `label` inline unless `art.late` (late cards
  already show it in their tag). The GUI's own `mediaKey` de-dup is unchanged
  (files only), so a retried batch that fails again in a *later* turn still
  shows its card.

chunks.heading: # 2026-09-24g — render watch extended to chat video batches (`start_current_chat_render`)
chunks.text:
# 2026-09-24g — render watch extended to chat video batches (`start_current_chat_render`)

## Why

`2026-09-24b` added `/api/render_watch` so a still (`render_story_image`) or a
`comfy_generate` job that lands after the agent's reply ends is announced and
saved onto the reply. Video batches started from a chat ("start render") were
not covered, and they are the renders most likely to finish long after the
turn ends.

## How a chat render job is identified and observed (read-only)

Established from `local_agent/chat_render_jobs.py`, `tools.start_batch_render`
and `work/batch_render_folder.py`. No runner code changed.

- **Identity:** `start_current_chat_render` returns
  `{"prepared": {...}, "launch": {"started", "pid", "job_folder", "planned_renders", "limit", "log"}}`.
  `job_folder` is `local_agent/render_jobs/<cid>/render_<stamp>[_NN]/`; `pid`
  is the runner process. The watch id is `chat_render:<pid>:<cid>/<job>`.
- **Progress / outputs:** the runner writes `<job>/batch_manifest.json`
  (`renders[<key>].status` = `done` / `failed` / `invalid` / `error`, with
  `output_path` for `done`) and moves each finished take to
  `<job>/renders/<key>[_attemptN].mp4`.
- **Completion:** the runner logs `Batch complete: N/M renders done` as its
  last line, *after* releasing `batch_render_queue_owner.json`. A crash
  (for example `RuntimeError: ComfyUI exited during startup rc=1`, seen in the
  real job `5b3352e81fdb4f08/render_20260824_184105`) leaves only a traceback
  in `<job>/batch_runtime/logs/agent_batch_*.log`.
- The watch treats the job as finished when the log shows the marker or the
  PID is no longer live (`tools._pid_is_live`, the same tasklist check the
  launch preflight uses). It reads the manifest and log only. It does not touch
  the queue lock, the ports, ComfyUI or the runner.

- New media root id **`chat_render`** → `CHAT_RENDER_JOBS_ROOT`
  (`local_agent/render_jobs`). It serves **video only**, and only files at
  exactly `<cid>/<job>/renders/<file>`. The job folder also holds copies of the
  chat's uploads (`img0/`, `img1/`, `video_refs/`) and the Comfy scratch
  (`batch_runtime/`). None of those are servable. `forbidden_media_roots()` is
  unchanged: `outputs/equal_shares`, chats, uploads and Shared input are still
  refused for every root.
- `media_kinds_for_root()` replaces the duplicated
  `"media" if shared_output else "image"` choice in `generated_media_payload`
  and `reveal_generated_media`.
- `chat_render_job_dir()` and `collect_chat_render_media_artifacts(job, manifest)`
  turn `done` manifest entries into ready video locators through
  `resolve_generated_media` + `media_artifact_for`.
- `register_render_watch` accepts `start_current_chat_render` (nested `launch`)
  and a bare `start_batch_render`, but only when `job_folder` is a chat job
  folder. An operator-supplied folder elsewhere is not watched, because its
  files could not be served.
- New watch kind `chat_render`:
  - Still running → keep waiting.
  - At least one video, all planned renders done → `complete`.
  - Some videos plus failed/invalid entries, or fewer than `min(planned, limit)`
    → `complete` with the videos plus one summary error card
    (`card_key chat_render_partial|<id>`), e.g.
    `1 of 3 renders done; 0002 failed: …`.
  - No videos → `failed`, with the manifest error or the log's last line.
- Expiry for this kind is 72 h, because each attempt may run 120 min. It only
  ends a watch whose PID Windows reused. Failure cards for this kind are
  `kind: video`.

- `MEDIA_SOURCE_TOOLS` += `start_current_chat_render`, `start_batch_render`.

  4000-char clip.
- The deterministic "start render" path (`_explicit_folderless_render_request`)
  now calls `_emit_tool_result(...)` instead of `emit("tool_result", result[:4000])`,
  so it registers the watch the same way a native tool call does.

`static/index.html` is unchanged. `mountMediaArtifact` already renders
`<video controls>` and passes `art.root` through to `/api/generated_media`.

# 2026-09-24i — director mock metric and live-metric feedback read `start_prompt`/`video_prompt`

## Why

On 2026-09-16 the Generalized Video Director signature
(`generalized_video_director.director_signature_class`) moved from Wan's
`positive_prompt` to FLUX.1 `start_prompt` + MiniMax I2V `video_prompt`.
Earlier today the mock director LM (`build_mock_lm`) was updated to emit the
new fields. Two readers still only looked at `positive_prompt`:

1. `generalized_video_director.mock_vlm_scores()` scored alignment, motion and
   the Backrooms physics phrase against `positive_prompt`. For a
   current-signature prediction that field is empty, so every candidate got
   alignment 0.05 and temporal 0.42, and mock MIPRO compiles could not tell
   candidates apart.
2. `dspy_orchestrator._fail_result()` wrote
   `"positive_prompt": _field(pred, "positive_prompt")` into the failure
   feedback, so live-metric failure rows carried an empty prompt. The
   success-path feedback in `evaluate_live_candidate` recorded no prompt at all.

`mechanical_director_gate` was checked. It already resolves through
`_director_start_prompt`/`_director_motion_prompt` and reports
`start_prompt is empty` / `video_prompt is empty`, so it needed no change.
Tests were added to lock that in.

## What changed

- `local_agent/generalized_video_director.py` (CRLF preserved):
  - New `_mock_scoring_texts(pred) -> (scene_text, motion_text)`. When either
    `start_prompt` or `video_prompt` is set, the scene text is
    `start_prompt + video_prompt` and the motion text is `video_prompt` alone.
    Otherwise both fall back to legacy `positive_prompt`.
  - `mock_vlm_scores`: intent-token alignment, the `stylized_2d` style lock and
    the Backrooms `yellow`/`backrooms` look bonus read the scene text. Motion
    cues, the length bonus and the Backrooms `handheld walking momentum`
    phrase read the motion text. The local `positive` was renamed to
    `scene_text`. Legacy-only predictions score exactly as before.
- `local_agent/dspy_orchestrator.py`:
  - `_fail_result` feedback: `positive_prompt` key replaced with
    `start_prompt` and `video_prompt`, each resolved through
    `_director_start_prompt(example, pred)` / `_director_motion_prompt(pred)`
    and capped at 500 chars. Those resolvers already fall back to
    `positive_prompt`, so legacy rows still carry their prompt.
  - `evaluate_live_candidate` success feedback now also records the resolved
    `start_prompt` and `video_prompt` (500-char cap).
  - No other code reads a `positive_prompt` key out of the feedback JSON.
    Checked with a scoped grep of `local_agent/*.py`, excluding vendor dirs.

chunks.heading: # 2026-09-24n — tracing: WAL first-open race no longer disables tracing
chunks.text:
# 2026-09-24n — tracing: WAL first-open race no longer disables tracing

Found while verifying `2026-09-24l`. `test_tracing.TracingTests.test_concurrency_two_threads`
failed intermittently (`AssertionError: 6 != 1`): in two consecutive full
non-live suite runs, and 1 in 6 runs of `python -m unittest test_tracing` alone.

Backups: `local_agent/tracing.py.bak_wal_race_20260924T105158`,
`local_agent/test_tracing.py.bak_wal_race_20260924T105158`.

No ComfyUI, no GPU. Unit tests only.

## Cause (measured, not inferred)

A harness wrapped `tracing._mark_broken` to record its exception and ran the
two-thread turn→hop→reason scenario against a fresh DB each time:
**29 of 200 runs failed**. Every failure was
`sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked`, always raised at
`PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` in `tracing._connection()`.

On a brand-new DB that pragma converts rollback-journal mode to WAL. The
conversion needs an exclusive lock, and SQLite reports "locked" immediately
to the losing connection instead of waiting out the 10 s busy timeout.
`span()` caught it and `_mark_broken()` set `_BROKEN` (OperationalError is a
DatabaseError). After that, `enabled()` returned False for the rest of the
process and every later span was a dummy.

Production impact: the first time two threads opened a new `knowledge/traces.db`
at once, tracing could silently switch itself off until the process restarted.

## Change — `local_agent/tracing.py` (LF)

New `_enable_wal(conn)`, called from `_connection()` in place of the bare pragma:
- The pragma runs under a module-level `_WAL_LOCK` (`threading.Lock`), which
  serializes the conversion within the process. On an existing WAL DB it is a
  no-op read, so the lock is held only briefly.
- On `OperationalError` containing "locked"/"busy" it retries up to
  `_WAL_RETRIES = 50` times, `_WAL_RETRY_SLEEP = 0.02` s apart (~1 s). This
  covers a second process creating the DB at the same moment. Other errors, or
  the last failed attempt, raise as before, so a genuinely broken DB still
  marks tracing broken.
- "Tracing never raises into the caller" is unchanged.

## Verification

- Same harness after the fix: **0 of 1000** runs failed (before: 29/200).
- New `test_tracing.TracingTests.test_concurrent_first_open_never_marks_broken`:
  25 rounds, each on a fresh DB with 4 threads. It asserts `_BROKEN` stays
  False, 4 spans per DB, and journal mode `wal`. Against the pre-change
  `tracing.py` (temp copy) it fails in round 0 with `database is locked`.
- `python -m unittest test_tracing`: 16 OK, **30/30** consecutive runs clean.
- Full non-live suite from `local_agent/`:
  `python -m unittest $(ls test_*.py | grep -v _live | sed 's/\.py$//')` →
  **1466 tests OK (2 skipped)**. That is 1460 from `2026-09-24l` + this test
  + 5 tests another agent added in parallel (`bak_labelecho_20260924T105305`).

chunks.heading: # 2026-09-24p — partial chat video batch: card and toast wording
chunks.text:
# 2026-09-24p — partial chat video batch: card and toast wording

Follow-up to `2026-09-24g` (known limit 1). This change touches only
`local_agent/static/index.html`. Backup:
`static/index.html.bak_partialcard_20260924_153900`. CRLF line endings are
preserved.

## Why

When a chat video batch finished with some renders done and some failed, the
server's one summary card (`card_key` `chat_render_partial|<watch id>`) was
drawn by the generic error branch:
"RENDER ENDED AFTER THE REPLY · … / generate failed — 1 of 3 renders done; …".
That wording implied the whole job failed, even though the videos directly
above it were real and playable. The toast said "1 video ready for review"
and did not mention the failures.

## Change

- `mountMediaArtifact`: a card whose `card_key` starts with
  `chat_render_partial|` gets the tag "Batch finished after the reply · <label>"
  and the status "**some renders failed** — <note>". Every other error,
  not-started or late card renders exactly as before.
- `pollRenderWatch` toast: a `complete` watch that carries a note appends the
  note's first clause, e.g. "1 video ready for review — video job
  render_… (1 of 3 renders done)". Only a partial chat video batch completes
  with a note. Story-still and comfy watches always complete with `note: ""`,
  so their toasts are unchanged.

## Evidence

- `node --check` on the extracted page script: syntax OK.
- `mountMediaArtifact` was evaluated in isolation in the browser pane (the
  page's own startup needs the live server) with three cards:
  - partial batch → "BATCH FINISHED AFTER THE REPLY · VIDEO JOB … / some
    renders failed — 1 of 3 renders done; 0002 failed: …"
  - whole-job crash → unchanged "RENDER ENDED AFTER THE REPLY … / generate
    failed — RuntimeError: …"
  - story batch failure card → unchanged "generate failed — batch item 2 —
    finished without manifest"
- **Not verified in the live GUI.** A real partial batch is needed for that;
  no render was started.

## Coordination

Another agent was working on the GVD VLM judge (score collapse / false
passes) in `generalized_video_director.py`, `dspy_orchestrator.py` and
`_recompile_gvd_director_20260924.py`. None of those files were touched here.
`index.html` has no judge/VLM/GVD code, and it had not been modified since
01:30 when this edit started.

chunks.heading: # 2026-09-24q — GVD live-metric judge: labeled eval set, fault checks, hard-cut detector
chunks.text:
# 2026-09-24q — GVD live-metric judge: labeled eval set, fault checks, hard-cut detector

Follows 2026-09-24o (score collapse; false passes on GVD-M03 and GVD-D01).
Existing renders only: no ComfyUI start, no renders. VLM (Qwen2.5-VL Caption V4,
llama.cpp) loaded only after port 8188 closed, all render owners idle, and GPU
≤ 70 °C. The queue owner was held and `check_running_ceiling` checked before
every clip; the VLM was released after every run (peak 72 °C).

Backups: `local_agent/{dspy_orchestrator.py,media_accuracy_gate.py,test_dspy_orchestrator.py}.bak_judgefix_20260924T155503`
(`test_dspy_orchestrator.py` ended up unchanged).

## 1. Measure first: labeled set + runner

- `local_agent/runtime/dspy_opt/judge_eval/gvd_judge_labels.json`: **50 existing
  renders** from `ComfyUI-Shared\output\dspy_opt`, labeled by Claude from 2 fps
  contact sheets plus native-resolution frames for every good/partial
  candidate (sheets in `runtime/dspy_opt/judge_eval_20260924/{sheets,strips}/`).
  **8 good, 7 partial, 35 reject**, each with confidence, fault tags and a
  reason. Labels are against the Beta brief (`user_intent` + `constraints`);
  for the Backrooms batch clips (`gvd_c0xx`) against their rendered prompt pair.
  Partial = no hard fault but a requested action missing; excluded from
  false-pass/false-fail.
- `local_agent/gvd_judge_eval.py`: `run --variant baseline|production`,
  `report`. `baseline` is a verbatim copy of the pre-fix judging block. The
  runner starts the owned llama-server itself with its output logged
  (`results_*.llama_server.log`), retries a clip once on a connection reset,
  and resumes from the results file (`--retry-errors`).

Baseline (pre-fix judge) on the 50 clips, `results_baseline.jsonl`:
- Deterministic: it reproduced the history scores (temperature 0.0, JSON mode).
- Collapse: 13 distinct triples in 50; (0.85, 0.95, 0.90) ×12, (0.95, 0.98, 0.92) ×7.
- @0.60: **false pass 28/35 (80%)**, high-confidence 20/27; false fail 2/8.
- @0.85: false pass 20/35, false fail 5/8.
- **AUC good vs reject 0.414**: a random good clip outscores a random reject
  less than half the time.
- Passed at 0.60: style violations 4/4, wrong viewpoint 3/3, hard cuts 8/10,
  requested subject absent 10/13. Includes text logos ("Deithess" 0.95/0.98/0.90,
  "iye" 0.95/0.98/0.92), a salamander in the creek brief, a clip that opens on a
  studio camera on a tripod, a brown blur with no bee, and three
  instruction-echo renders of abstract glowing shapes (1.0/1.0/0.95).

chunks.text:
Passed at 0.60: style violations 4/4, wrong viewpoint 3/3, hard cuts 8/10,
  requested subject absent 10/13. Includes text logos ("Deithess" 0.95/0.98/0.90,
  "iye" 0.95/0.98/0.92), a salamander in the creek brief, a clip that opens on a
  studio camera on a tripod, a brown blur with no bee, and three
  instruction-echo renders of abstract glowing shapes (1.0/1.0/0.95).

## 2. Causes found

1. **The judge never saw the brief.** It got only the student's FLUX/MiniMax
   prompts. GVD-M03's MiniMax prompt never mentions water ("pans across the
   moss-covered rocks"), so a waterless clip "matched". The brief's
   constraints ("single skater, no crowd") were never sent, so D04 failed for
   the wrong reason. The echo renders scored 1.0 against their own echoed
   field descriptions.
2. **Anchoring on the prompt text.** The M03 rationale restates the MiniMax
   prompt almost word for word.
3. **Scores before reasoning.** The schema had the three numbers first and the
   rationale after, so the model committed to a default triple first.
4. **Not frame coverage.** `extract_eval_frames(count=3)` is clamped to 8
   uniform frames at 2%..98% (0.16 … 7.84 s for 8 s). The failing late regions
   of D01 (drift from ~5 s) and M03 (cut at 4.7 s) are inside the sample. More
   or re-placed frames were **not** tested.
5. **Not temperature.** Decoding was already 0.0 (only temperature and max_tokens
   reach llama.cpp; `repeat_penalty` is set but not forwarded).

   of D01 (drift from ~5 s) and M03 (cut at 4.7 s) are inside the sample. More
   or re-placed frames were **not** tested.
5. **Not temperature.** Decoding was already 0.0 (only temperature and max_tokens
   reach llama.cpp; `repeat_penalty` is set but not forwarded).

## 3. Fix

- New `local_agent/video_judge.py`:
  - CPU detector over every decoded frame (64×36). A hard cut is a colour-histogram
    step ≥ 0.20, ≥ 8× the local median, grayscale correlation < 0.70, not in
    the first two steps (the I2V conditioning pop), not a flash (the picture
    returns within 12 frames, forward or backward), and not a step into or out
    of a near-black frame. Near-black fraction = frames with mean luma < 16.
    On the set: cuts flagged in D01 `8358` (0.88 s), M03 `371a` (4.71 s),
    D03 `5c73` (1.08 s), D03 `ffd4` (0.92 s); near-black ≥ 25% in 5 rejects;
    **no good or partial clip flagged.** Only 4 of 10 labeled cuts; gradual
    (morph) cuts are left to the VLM. Narrow margin: c017's lights-off frame is
    14.7 luma, M03's post-cut frame 17.2.
  - VLM prompt judged against **BRIEF + CONSTRAINTS** (student prompts no
    longer sent). Order: one line per frame with timestamps, then 7 yes/no
    checks plus `constraint_broken`, then the three scores and rationale.
  - Python caps: subject not visible → alignment ≤ 0.20; medium mismatch
    (only when the brief names a stylized medium) → ≤ 0.30; wrong subject count
    or a real constraint quote → ≤ 0.40; unrequested text/logo → alignment
    ≤ 0.30 and aesthetic ≤ 0.40; location change or cut → temporal ≤ 0.30;
    time-of-day change → ≤ 0.40; detected hard cut → ≤ 0.25; near-black → aesthetic ≤ 0.20.
- `dspy_orchestrator.py`: new `judge_rendered_clip()`; `evaluate_live_candidate`
  uses it (new optional `signals_fn` hook). Output keeps the
  `parse_video_director_scores` shape, so `_fail_penalty`, the curriculum and
  the 0.7·min + 0.3·mean MIPRO scalar are unchanged. Feedback rows add
  `scores_vlm`, `checks`, `caps`, `signals`; `vlm_raw` kept to 4000 chars.
  `run_qwen_director_scores` `num_predict` 1024 → 1536.
- `media_accuracy_gate.py` (CRLF kept): literal-mode override factored into
  `literal_override_block()` and shared by both judges. Old builder output is
  byte-identical in all three modes (verified against the backup).

Two rules were added after the first run (`results_v2a.jsonl`) showed the VLM
misusing checks. Both are general, not per-clip:
(a) `constraint_broken` counts only if the brief has constraints and the text
isn't a dump of check answers; (b) medium mismatch binds only for stylized
briefs (it called clean Backrooms hallways "3D renders"), plus one prompt line
saying a brief that names no medium accepts any realistic look.

## 4. Re-measured on the same 50 clips, final code (`results_v2b.jsonl`)

| | baseline | fixed |
|---|---|---|
| false pass @0.60 | 28/35 (80%) | **10/35 (29%)** |
| … high-confidence labels | 20/27 | **4/27** |
| false fail @0.60 | 2/8 | **0/8** |
| false pass / fail @0.85 | 20/35 / 5/8 | 8/35 / 3/8 |
| AUC good vs reject | 0.414 | **0.821** |
| distinct triples / top share | 13 / 0.24 | 17 / 0.18 |
| hard cuts passed @0.60 | 8/10 | 1/10 |

Still passed: wrong viewpoint 3/3 (drone visible in frame: D02 `614e`,
D01 `3032`; camera operator in shot: c036), late location drift (D01 `086a`,
D01 `3032`, c030), style (S01 photographed print, S05 full colour instead of
B&W ink), M04 dry-adult "teleports" (`15e7`, `cfa7`), B01 wall wobble.
@0.85 the three failed good clips are Backrooms clips at aesthetic 0.80.

Caveats:
- Small set (8 goods), labeled by one reviewer.
- The detector thresholds and rules (a)/(b) were tuned on this same set, so
  these numbers flatter the judge. A held-out set is needed before trusting
  the absolute rates.
- The VLM is prompt-sensitive: between v2a and v2b individual verdicts flipped
  both ways (M05 caught, M04 `15e7` lost).
- Scores are now bimodal (checks fire together: a halo). Collapse is reduced,
  not solved.

The VLM score ranks clips; it does not accept them.

## Runtime notes

- v2a: 4 clips lost to `ConnectionResetError` (llama-server died mid-request and
  the owned-runtime check relaunched it). The same 4 requests replayed with
  server logging (`judge_eval_20260924/repro_vlm_crash.py`,
  `repro_llama_server.log`) all succeeded in ~7 s, about 10.6k tokens, no
  truncation. The media watcher (log idle since 09:57) and the unit tests
  (Comfy `/free` only) were ruled out. **Cause unknown.** The production launch
  sends llama-server output to DEVNULL; the eval runner now logs it. v2b: 0 resets.
- `run_qwen_director_scores` appended 150 rows (3 runs × 50) to
  `runtime/dspy_opt/gvd_vlm_raw.jsonl` (debug dump).
  `gvd_live_metric_history.jsonl` untouched (261 rows).

## Tests

`test_video_judge.py` (25): detector (cut, pan, I2V pop, flash, lights
off/on, black), check parsing, every cap, medium and constraint rules,
orchestrator wiring (brief not student prompt, literal override, legacy
two-arg judge, signals), feedback fields, report maths. Full non-live suite:
**1496 OK (2 skipped)**, was 1471. Run again on the final files, after the
line-ending fix below: 1496 OK (2 skipped)
(`runtime/dspy_opt/judge_eval/full_suite_20260924_final.log`).

Line endings: a scripted `write_text` edit on Windows briefly turned
`dspy_orchestrator.py` (LF) into CRLF on all lines. Caught while diffing
against the backup, and restored to LF. The diff against
`.bak_judgefix_20260924T155503` is now exactly the five intended hunks, with
no edits from other sessions. `media_accuracy_gate.py` is still pure CRLF. The
new files are LF.

## Open

- Future MIPRO scores are not comparable with history rows ≤ 260 (different
  judge, now against the brief).
- Pre-existing, unchanged: a judged clip with all-zero scores gets MIPRO 0.0,
  **below** a render timeout (0.05) or mechanical fail (0.02). The fixed judge
  gives 0.0 more often, so this now matters more. Operator decision.
- Not tried: more or better-placed frames, pairwise first/last-frame questions,

# 2026-09-24r — GVD judge: held-out check and frame-count experiment

Follows 2026-09-24q. Operator asked for both a held-out set and a test of
more frames. Existing renders only: no ComfyUI, no renders. The VLM ran under
the same guards as 24q (port 8188 closed, owners idle, GPU ≤ 70 °C at start,
owner held, 82 °C check before every clip, release plus wait for ≤ 58 °C after
each run). Six runs, 0 server crashes, GPU idle afterwards (37 °C).

**Outcome: production stays at 8 uniform frames.** No production code change
in this entry (`dspy_orchestrator.py` untouched).

## Held-out set (labels frozen before any fixed-judge run)

`local_agent/runtime/dspy_opt/judge_eval/gvd_judge_labels_heldout.json`,
sha256 `c915d3adef4dd12b2665a3aaff344a025472030cb676e0058e23f859c88821d9`.
29 clips not used in 24q tuning: **12 good, 12 reject, 5 partial**. Sheets are
in `runtime/dspy_opt/judge_eval_20260924/heldout/`. Excluded as ambiguous, with
reasons in the file: c015, c027, c012 (their prompts ask for, or contradict,
the "fault"), the br_c002/c008/c009 boilerplate prompts, and c031 (a
duplicate).

Bias: every good clip is a Backrooms-batch clip, and 6 of 12 rejects are GVD
Beta clips. Old-judge history scores were visible for the GVD clips while I
scanned; no fixed-judge score was seen before freezing.

## Results (@0.60 unless noted; hc = high-confidence labels only)

| set | judge | false pass | false fail | hc FP | hc FF | FP / FF @0.85 | AUC |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| tuning (50) | baseline | 28/35 | 2/8 | 20/27 | 0/4 | 20/35 / 5/8 | 0.414 |
| tuning | fixed, 8 frames | 10/35 | 0/8 | 4/27 | 0/4 | 8/35 / 3/8 | 0.821 |
| tuning | f12 | 10/35 | 1/8 | 5/27 | 1/4 | 6/35 / 4/8 | 0.809 |
| tuning | f8c | 9/35 | 2/8 | 3/27 | 0/4 | 6/35 / 5/8 | 0.784 |
| **held-out (29)** | baseline | 8/12 | 3/12 | 4/7 | 0/5 | 3/12 / 9/12 | 0.587 |
| **held-out** | **fixed, 8 frames** | **2/12** | **3/12** | 1/7 | 2/5 | 1/12 / 8/12 | **0.809** |
| held-out | f12 | 4/12 | 4/12 | 2/7 | 2/5 | 1/12 / 11/12 | 0.649 |
| held-out | f8c | 4/12 | 4/12 | 3/7 | 2/5 | 1/12 / 11/12 | 0.691 |

- f12 = 12 uniform frames. f8c = 8 uniform frames plus up to 4 frames just
  after the largest colour-histogram steps. Both have the same 12-frame budget.
- On held-out the fixed judge's false-pass reduction holds (8/12 → 2/12, AUC
  0.587 → 0.809). **False fails do not improve (3/12).**
- More frames made things worse on held-out and doubled the time (about 18–20 s
  per clip vs 7–10 s). They also produced 2 parse failures in 158 scorings: the
  output ran away ("no text, no watermark, no people on the cliff edge, …")
  until `num_predict` ran out. The 8-frame judge had 0 in 79.
- Change-placed frames did not rescue late drift. D01 `086a` still scores 0.95
  with extra frames at its largest changes, so the VLM sees the drift but
  does not call it a fault.
- Strict bar: at 0.85, 8 of the 12 good held-out clips fail (Backrooms clips
  sit at aesthetic 0.80–0.85). The later curriculum steps would reject most
  good clips.

## Held-out false fails of the fixed judge (8 frames)

- **c004** (good, high): the requested fluorescent flicker gives one dark frame;
  the VLM answered "different dark hallway" and capped temporal at 0.30.
- **c018** (good, high): CPU cut-detector false positive at 1.83 s. Lights dim to
  luma ~20 (not near-black, so the exposure guard misses it) and come back to
  ~80 within two frames. A before/after layout-correlation rule does not
  separate it: 0.55 vs 0.57 for D01 `8358`'s real cut. **Detector left unchanged.**
- **c035** (good, medium): the prompts contradict each other (FLUX "no body in
  frame"; MiniMax "actor freezes…" and a man is visible), and the requested
  lights-fade trips the near-black aesthetic cap (51% of frames). The label is
  disputed; left as frozen.
- CPU detector on held-out: 2 true cuts (c008 3.33 s, D04 `5ac6` 3.04 s),
  1 false (c018).

# 2026-09-24t — Qwen2.5-VL llama-server output logged instead of DEVNULL

This closes the open item from `2026-09-24q`: "Production llama-server output
still goes to DEVNULL." In the 24q v2a run, four judge requests died with
`ConnectionResetError` when the server crashed mid-request. The cause is still
unknown, because the production launch discarded the server's output.

## Change

Both production launches of the Caption V4 server (`127.0.0.1:11436`) now
append stdout and stderr to
**`local_agent/runtime/logs/qwen25_vl_llama_server.log`**:

- `capabilities.ensure_qwen25_vl_runtime` (media watcher / vision batches)
- `dspy_optimizer._ensure_owned_qwen25_vl_runtime` (GVD live-metric judge,
  also the relaunch path in `gvd_judge_eval.py` after a connection reset)

New helpers in `capabilities.py`:
- `open_qwen25_vl_server_log(caller)`: returns an append handle and writes a
  `===== <time> llama-server launch by <caller> =====` header.
  - **Rotation:** once the log exceeds 20 MB
    (`QWEN25_VL_SERVER_LOG_MAX_BYTES`) it is rotated once to `.prev`. At most
    the current and previous logs are kept, and nothing else is deleted.
  - **Fallback:** if the log can't be opened, it returns `subprocess.DEVNULL`,
    so logging can never block the VLM.
- `close_qwen25_vl_server_log(handle, pid)` writes `===== pid N =====` and
  closes this process's copy of the handle. The server keeps its inherited
  handle.

`dspy_optimizer`'s "exited before becoming healthy" `HandoffError` now names
the log path. Launch arguments, ownership/state handling and teardown are
unchanged.

**Not changed:** `gvd_judge_eval.py`'s own `_launch_logged_vlm` (per-run
`results_*.llama_server.log`), the judge files `video_judge.py` and
`dspy_orchestrator.py`, and `media_accuracy_gate.py`. A separate agent was
actively working on the GVD judge (`2026-09-24q`, `2026-09-24r`), so its files

chunks.heading: # 2026-09-24u — render_story_image: face_detail + realpro_flux fails fast; found (not fixed) a separate still-QA file-lookup regression
chunks.text:
# 2026-09-24u — render_story_image: face_detail + realpro_flux fails fast; found (not fixed) a separate still-QA file-lookup regression

Operator reported a live batch failure: job 0 ("Wide interior view of a
modest apartment living room converted into a makeshift audition space...")
— `generate failed — batch item 0 — finished_without_manifest (pid 55888) —
ERROR: realpro_flux face_detail is not available until the isolated
custom-node startup is repaired`. The other 5 batch items (Scene Start
Images 2-5) never started (`stop_on_failure`, correct by design — see
`2026-09-23g`).

## Root cause

`work/image_render.py:736` has always hard-refused `face_detail=True` with
`model_profile=realpro_flux` (Flux) — this is a real, standing limitation,
not new. The chat agent chose that combination anyway: the `face_detail`
tool description ("Opt in to an automatic detected-face repair pass...")
never mentioned the Flux incompatibility, and this job's prompt describes a
person (an actor auditioning), so a face-repair pass was a reasonable-sounding
choice for a model that had no way to know it always fails with Flux — the
same tool-description-gap pattern as the earlier `reference_name`/mode
confusion (`2026-09-23`).

Worse than a wrong choice: `render_story_image` didn't validate the
combination until deep inside `image_render.py`'s own graph builder, which
only runs *after* `_start_owned_backend()` has already spawned a real
ComfyUI process and spent its startup time. So the mistake cost a full
backend-start cycle (pid 55888) before failing, and then blocked 5 unrelated,
valid Scene Start Image jobs behind it.

## Fix

`local_agent/tools.py`:
- `render_story_image()`: reject `face_detail=True` + `model_profile=realpro_flux`
  immediately after parsing args — before `router.gpu_busy()`, `gpu_gate.request()`,
  or `subprocess.Popen` are ever touched. `render_story_image_batch()` calls
  `render_story_image()` per job (confirmed by reading the loop), so this is
  covered for both the single-render and batch paths without a second change.
- Both `face_detail` tool-description strings (`render_story_image` and
  `render_story_image_batch`'s per-job schema) now say plainly: not available
  with `model_profile=realpro_flux`, use `realvisxl` if face repair is needed.

Backups: `local_agent/tools.py.bak_facedetailflux_20260924220404`,
`local_agent/test_render_story_image.py.bak_facedetailflux_20260924220506`.
Both files are LF; no line-ending changes.

## Tests

`test_render_story_image.py`: 2 new —
`test_refuses_face_detail_with_realpro_flux_before_spawning_backend` (asserts
`router.gpu_busy`, `gpu_gate.request`, and `subprocess.Popen` are never
called) and `test_face_detail_with_realvisxl_is_unaffected` (negative
control). Verified fail-then-pass: reverted `tools.py` to the pre-fix backup,
confirmed the new test fails for the right reason (execution reaches
`router.gpu_busy()`, which the test hadn't configured a return value for),
restored the fix, confirmed 24/24 pass.

`test_render_story_image.py` full file: 24 OK.

## Found, not fixed: `test_story_stills_batch_review.py` — 4 failing, unrelated to this change

While checking for regressions, `StoryStillQATests` (4 tests) failed with
`'fail' != 'not_run'` / `error: no rendered output file was found on disk to
check` — the still-QA wiring from `2026-09-24a` cannot find the rendered PNG
its own test fixture lays down. **Confirmed unrelated to this entry**: reverted
`tools.py` to the pre-face_detail-fix backup and reran — identical 4 failures,
byte-for-byte same output. So this regressed sometime between `2026-09-24a`
(when this test suite was presumably passing) and now, most likely from one
of the same-day sessions that also touched `tools.py`'s output-path handling
(`24e` truncated-prompt guard, `24f` batch-failure cards, `24g` chat-video
watch, `24p` card wording) without rerunning this specific suite.

This matters beyond test hygiene: if the QA lookup is broken the same way in
production, the still-QA safety net wired in this morning could currently be
silently returning `not_run` instead of a real verdict on real renders — the
opposite of fail-closed. **Did not investigate further or fix** — multiple
sessions are actively editing `tools.py` today (see `24t`'s note on leaving
another session's in-progress files alone), and this needs someone who can
diff the manifest/output-path handling across today's `tools.py` changes
without racing a concurrent edit. Failing tests:
`test_batch_carries_qa_into_completed_review_payload_and_summary`,
`test_completed_status_runs_creative_approve_with_manifest_prompt`,
`test_qa_crash_is_reported_as_error_never_as_pass`,
`test_regression_operator_empty_room_fails_real_qa_and_reaches_review`.

chunks.heading: # 2026-09-24w — image_render: tolerate transient /history poll failures
chunks.text:
# 2026-09-24w — image_render: tolerate transient /history poll failures

## Problem

`work/image_render.py` `_wait_for_outputs` polled `/history/<prompt_id>` via
`_get_json` (8 s timeout). `_get_json` wraps URLError/OSError/timeouts in
`ImageRenderError`, and the loop's `except ImageRenderError: raise` re-raised it
at once, so the `except Exception: pass` meant for transient polling failures
never saw transport errors. One slow `/history` response killed the job.

Evidence: `work/runtime/agent_image_jobs/startup-deadline-fix-verify_run2_20260924_185909.log`
exited 2 with `ComfyUI API unavailable at .../history/09a1f706-...: timed out`,
while ComfyUI (`work/runtime/image_render_runtime/logs/comfy_20260924_185910_757374.stderr.log`)
logged `Prompt executed in 00:12:16` and wrote
`outputs/stories/_comfy_output/stories/startup-deadline-fix-verify/renders/bfa0d801c89941669f1a1586a6195c7b_00001_.png`
at 19:14:32. No manifest was written; that PNG is orphaned and was left untouched.

## Change

- The `_get_json` call now has its own `try`: an `ImageRenderError` from it is
  recorded and printed (`history poll failed, retrying: ...`), followed by the
  existing 2 s sleep, and polling continues within `timeout_s`. The final
  timeout message appends the last poll error.
- Unchanged and still immediate: the owned-process-exited check, the
  `status_str == "error"` graph-failure raise, and the
  `thermal_guard.check_running_ceiling` call and its 15 s cadence.

## Tests

Added to `local_agent/test_production_integrity.py` `IntegrityTests`:
`test_wait_for_outputs_tolerates_history_timeout` (one "timed out" then outputs
→ images returned), `test_wait_for_outputs_graph_error_still_raises`,
`test_wait_for_outputs_backend_exit_still_raises`.
`python -m unittest test_production_integrity` from `local_agent/`: 51 tests OK.

## Verification status

Live run 19:21–19:35 local, story `history-poll-fix-verify`, same args as the
failed verify run except seed 2
(`work/runtime/agent_image_jobs/history-poll-fix-verify_20260924_192136.log`):
exit 0, `Prompt executed in 00:11:41`, manifest
`outputs/stories/history-poll-fix-verify/manifests/image_2d2834d6-6dec-437a-8460-82c9c70d6f2f.json`
status `complete`, PNG exists (1,346,575 bytes) and its sha256 matches the
manifest. Backend stopped, owner released, port 8188 free afterwards.

**The retry path itself was not exercised live**: the log has no
`history poll failed` line, so no `/history` poll timed out this time. That path
is covered only by the unit test. The run confirms the normal completion path
still works after the change. The orphaned verify-run PNG from run 2 has not
been adopted into a manifest at the time of this entry; it was adopted later in `2026-09-24z`.

chunks.heading: # 2026-09-24y — image_render: final readiness probe at the startup deadline; default 240 s → 300 s
chunks.text:
# 2026-09-24y — image_render: final readiness probe at the startup deadline; default 240 s → 300 s

## Problem

`work/image_render.py` `_start_owned_backend` polled `/object_info` only while
`time.monotonic() < deadline`, then raised `"startup deadline exceeded"`
unconditionally. The last in-loop probe's timeout is clamped to the time left
(down to 0.1 s), so a backend that starts listening in that final window is
torn down.

Evidence: `work/runtime/agent_image_jobs/Scene-Start-Image-1_20260924_181712.log`
failed `alive_not_listening`, `elapsed_seconds: 240.016`. The health snapshot
taken at the deadline ends at `No OpenGL_accelerate`; the full stderr
(`work/runtime/image_render_runtime/logs/comfy_20260924_181714_618110.stderr.log`,
last written 18:21:16 local vs. deadline 18:21:14.6) then shows `Starting server`,
`To see the GUI go to: http://127.0.0.1:8188`, and `Global interrupt` — the last
being `_stop_owned_backend`'s own `/interrupt` reaching a now-listening server.
The backend became ready ~0.5–1.5 s **after** the deadline, not at it.

Startup history (413 `server_ready` health records in that logs dir): median
51 s, but 225.8 s, 228.2 s and 239.1 s had already come within seconds of 240;
verification run 2 below took 185.2 s. So the budget, not only the race, was
too tight.

## Change

- After the loop exits: if the process has exited → `process_exited` as before;
  otherwise one `thermal_guard.check_running_ceiling` (same order as the loop)
  and exactly one `/object_info` probe with a full 2 s timeout. Success returns
  the process with a `server_ready` health record carrying
  `ready_on_final_check: true`; failure raises `"startup deadline exceeded"`
  unchanged. Not a retry loop.
- `startup_timeout` default 240 → 300. `verify_prompt_pack_startup.py` still
  passes its own `--seconds`.
- In-loop cadence and thermal-guard behaviour unchanged. `router.gpu_busy()`
  unaffected (owner file + port 8188 already mark the GPU busy during startup).

## Tests

`local_agent/test_production_integrity.py::IntegrityTests::test_startup_final_check_at_deadline`
(fake monotonic clock): ready exactly at the deadline → returns proc, health
`server_ready` + `ready_on_final_check`; never ready → still raises
`startup deadline exceeded`, stops the backend, health `alive_not_listening`.
Against the pre-fix code the ready case fails with the production error.
Full file: 55 tests OK (includes 2026-09-24w's history-poll tests).

# 2026-09-25a — free-text VLM callers measured at repeat_penalty 1.0 vs 1.08; action extractor pinned to 1.0

Follows 2026-09-24ae, which made `repeat_penalty` actually reach llama-server
and left the free-text callers running at the intended 1.08 "unmeasured
beyond the probe". The operator asked for the same measurement the judge got.
There is no labeled set for these callers, so this is an A/B on the same
inputs: every output at 1.0 (what the callers ran at until 24ae) and at 1.08
(what they run at now), compared for truncation, format compliance,
repetition and required-field presence, with a repeat run at 1.0 as the
determinism control.

VLM only, one owned llama-server launch under `gvd_judge_eval.preflight`
(8188 closed, owners idle, GPU 29 °C at start, 82 °C check before every call,
release and cool-down after). 75 calls, 0 errors, server alive throughout,
GPU 35 °C afterwards. No ComfyUI, no renders.

Harness and data: `local_agent/runtime/dspy_opt/judge_eval_20260924/freetext_penalty_ab.py`,
rows `freetext_penalty_ab.jsonl` (full texts), `freetext_penalty_ab_summary.json`,
log `freetext_penalty_ab_run.log`, server log `freetext_ab_llama_server.log`.

## Inputs

8 labeled clips (c005, c017, D03 `1adb`, M01 `4f74`, S05 `361f`, D01 `6609`,
M04 `15e7`, c036: Backrooms hallways, drone, macro, stylized, black/logo,
butterfly, operator-in-frame). Per clip, the exact prompt builders production
uses:

| caller | production path | frames | budget |
|---|---|---|---|
| `see_image` | watcher vision job, default `_build_prompt` | 1 (judge frame 4) | 512 |
| `tl_observe` | `analyze_video` → `_timeline_observation_instruction` | 1 | 512 |
| `tl_change` | `analyze_video` → `_timeline_change_instruction` | 2 | 512 |
| `actions` | `extract_video_actions` → `_action_frame_instruction` (ffmpeg `fps=2,scale=768:-1`) | 16–20 | 2048 |

`Frame N | t=… | …` (0 non-conforming of 196, both ways); no run of identical

| see_image (8) | 171 → 185 | 1.5 → 1.5 | 0.64 → 0.67 | 0/8 | 0.23 |

28 in `tl_change`), which is the direction the instructions ask for. Nothing
in the metrics or a read of the pairs (e.g. M01 web caption, `jsonl`) says

get rarer. Lines carrying a camera-motion term (`static`, `push-in`, …,

- The 16–20-frame batch call is **not deterministic** at temperature 0: the

## Decision

- `see_image` / watcher vision jobs and `analyze_video`'s timeline calls

# 2026-09-25b — action log: mandatory cam= slot; camera field now on every line (but always "static")

Follows 2026-09-25a, which found the `extract_video_actions` camera-motion
field present on only about half of all lines even with the repeat penalty
off, and flipping per clip between identical runs. Operator asked for the
compliance fix. Done and measured; one honest limit found on the way.

VLM only, one owned llama-server launch under `gvd_judge_eval.preflight`
(8188 closed, owners idle, GPU ≤ 70 °C at start, 82 °C check before every
call, release and cool-down after). 33 calls, 0 errors, server alive
throughout, GPU 37 °C afterwards. No ComfyUI, no renders.

Backups: `local_agent/{media_tools.py,test_media_analysis.py}.bak_camslot_20260925T004500`.
The edit itself was applied by
`local_agent/runtime/dspy_opt/judge_eval_20260924/_edit_camslot.py` (kept as
the record of the exact replacement; its asserts refuse a second run).

## Change (`local_agent/media_tools.py`, LF)

- `_action_frame_instruction`: the line template gains a mandatory third
  slot, `Frame N | t=… | cam=<camera motion> | <visible state …>`, in both
  the plain and the H3-beats format. New rule text: the slot takes exactly
  one of `static | push-in | pull-back | pan-left | pan-right | tilt-up |
  tilt-down | uncertain`, is mandatory even when the camera is still and
  even when the rest of the line is "no visible change", and is never left
  blank. The camera list moved out of the free-text state list.
- `_action_coverage`: parses `cam=` per line (`_CAMERA_SLOT_RE`, position
  in the line does not matter) against `_CAMERA_MOTION_VALUES`. New fields:
  `camera_labels` (frame → value), `invalid_camera_labels` (a `cam=` value
  outside the vocabulary), `missing_camera_labels`, `camera_complete`. A
  missing or invalid slot is reported, never inferred. `complete` keeps its
  old meaning (frame labels); `warning` now concatenates both problems.
- `extract_video_actions` result `note`: says what `camera_labels` are and
  what `static` does and does not mean (below).
- Tests: `test_action_instruction_…` asserts the slot in both formats;
  new `test_action_coverage_reports_camera_slot_without_inferring_one`
  (valid, case-insensitive, invalid vocabulary, missing slot, all-present).
  Downstream: nothing parses the line format (`lxmf_agent` passes the text
  through), so the template change breaks no consumer.

- **Every one of the 196 values is `static`.** That includes D03 (aerial

chunks.heading: # 2026-09-25c — deterministic camera-motion estimator beside the action log's cam= claim
chunks.text:
# 2026-09-25c — deterministic camera-motion estimator beside the action log's cam= claim

Follows 2026-09-25b: the action-log VLM writes `cam=static` for every frame
of every clip, so the field carries no information. Operator asked for the
deterministic estimator. Built, unit-tested on synthetic motion, run over all
79 labeled clips (CPU only, no VLM, no ComfyUI, no renders), and wired into
`extract_video_actions` as a separate measured field next to the model's
claim.

Backups: `local_agent/{media_tools.py,test_media_analysis.py}.bak_cammotion_20260925T013000`.
The wiring edit was applied by
`local_agent/runtime/dspy_opt/judge_eval_20260924/_edit_cammotion.py` (kept
as the record; its asserts refuse a second run).

## New module `local_agent/camera_motion.py` (LF, numpy only)

- `decode_gray(video)`: every frame via ffmpeg, 256×144 grey. `video_fps`.
- `phase_shift(a, b)`: Hann-windowed phase correlation, sub-pixel by
  parabolic fit, returns `(dx, dy, response)`. Response is the normalised
  cross-power peak: ~0.95 for a pure shift, 0.06–0.09 across a real cut.
- `pair_motion(a, b)`: 3×3 block grid, one shift per block, weighted by its
  response, fitted to `v_i = t + s·c_i` (translation plus isotropic scale
  about the frame centre). Blank frames (mean luma < 16, the judge's value)
  and block shifts over a quarter of the block are discarded.
- `estimate_from_frames(frames, fps, windows)` /
  `estimate_camera_motion(video, windows)`: pairs are summed per
  observation window (`start < t(i+1) ≤ end`), pairs with response < 0.10
  are excluded and counted; a window with more than half its pairs unusable
  is `uncertain`. `classify` picks the dominant axis against thresholds of
  2% of frame width/height (pan/tilt) or 2% summed scale (push/pull),
  otherwise `static`. Vocabulary is exactly the `cam=` slot's.
- `compare_with_claims(estimates, camera_labels)`: agree count and a
  disagree list; `uncertain` windows and unclaimed frames are skipped.
- Sign convention, pinned by tests: content moving right = `pan-left`;
  content moving down = `tilt-up`; content moving outward = `push-in`.
- Stated limits (module docstring): this is global image motion, not camera
  motion. A subject filling the frame or flowing water registers as a move;
  dolly and zoom both read as scale; rotation is not modelled.

`test_camera_motion.py` (11): signed roll recovery, unrelated pictures low
response, pan/push/pull/blank pair motion, a five-window synthetic clip
(static → pan-left → tilt-up → push-in → cut), a mostly-cuts window is
`uncertain`, a black clip is `uncertain`, threshold and vocabulary table,
claim comparison. Two things the tests taught: smooth synthetic textures
correlate spuriously in small blocks (the cut test uses white-noise frames),
and gradient pre-filtering was tried and bought nothing on real footage
(adjacent-frame response 0.47–0.78 either way, cut 0.06–0.09), so it is not
used.

## Real footage: all 79 labeled clips, one-second windows

`runtime/dspy_opt/judge_eval_20260924/camera_motion_labeled_clips.{txt,json}`;
67 s for 656 windows (ffmpeg decode dominates; ~0.85 s per clip).

| label | windows |
|---|---|
| push-in | 293 |
| static | 169 |
| pan-left / pan-right | 43 / 28 |
| pull-back | 38 |
| tilt-up / tilt-down | 26 / 16 |
| uncertain | 43 |

Against the briefs (no ground truth beyond them):
- Forward flight and walks read as push-in on every window: D01 `8358`
  (drone toward cliffs), D02 `614e` (FPV through pines), D03 `1adb`
  (tracking beside a motorcycle), every B01 handheld camcorder walk, and the
  good Backrooms hallway walks (c005, c017, c028, c029, c033). The VLM had
  called all of these `static`.
- Locked macros read as static on every window: M01 `4f74` (dew on silk,
  good), M04 `cfa7`/`4c83` (butterfly), M02 `9562`/`9405`.
- Black/logo clips read as uncertain: D01 `6609` (7/8 windows), M01 `5329`
  (8/8), br_c007 (7/8).
- Drift and multi-shot rejects show it: c030 (location drift) `PR PR PR PL
  PL PL Z+ …`, D01 `086a` (late drift) `PL PL TD PR Z- Z- Z- Z-`, c036
  (operator in frame, lighting swings) mixed labels.
- The stated limit shows too: M03 `1216` (creek, good) reads `tilt-up` on
  all 8 windows, which is the water flowing down the frame, not the camera.
  D01 `8358`'s cut at 0.88 s is one excluded pair inside a push-in window,
  so a single cut does not flip a window; sustained cuts do.

## Wiring (`media_tools.extract_video_actions`)

After the VLM batches: `camera_motion = estimate_camera_motion(video,
observation_windows)` and `camera_motion_vs_model = compare_with_claims(…,
coverage.camera_labels)` are added to the result; an estimator failure is
recorded in `camera_motion_error` and never fails the tool. The `note` now
says to prefer the measured field over the model's claim and what the
measurement cannot tell apart. The model's `cam=` slot is unchanged and is
**not** overwritten by the measurement: the two are reported side by side so

chunks.heading: # 2026-09-25e — camera-motion estimator: border-ring fit and subject-motion flag; coherence gate tried and rejected
chunks.text:
# 2026-09-25e — camera-motion estimator: border-ring fit and subject-motion flag; coherence gate tried and rejected

Follows 2026-09-25c/d. Operator asked for the border-only-blocks refinement
that 25c listed as the next step for the creek-style confounder (subject
motion filling the frame read as a camera move). Built, unit-tested, and
measured on the same 79 labeled clips. Result, plainly: the refinement is a
sound estimator and adds a real subject-motion signal, but it does **not**
fix the creek or the butterfly, and the coherence gate I built alongside it
turned out to be wrong in both directions and was removed before shipping.
CPU only, no VLM, no ComfyUI, no renders.

Backups: `local_agent/{camera_motion.py,test_camera_motion.py}.bak_border_20260925T030000`.
Edits applied by `local_agent/runtime/dspy_opt/judge_eval_20260924/_edit_border.py`
then `_edit_border2.py` (kept as the record; asserts refuse a second run).

## Change (`local_agent/camera_motion.py`, LF)

- Grid 3×3 → 4×4 (64×36 px blocks, the judge's own frame size). The
  translation+scale fit now uses the **outer ring** (12 blocks) and gives
  `dx`, `dy`, `scale`, `response`; the four centre blocks are compared
  against that fit and their mean excess motion is `subject_excess_px`.
  The all-blocks fit is still computed as `full_dx/dy/scale` and, per
  window, `full_frame_camera`, so the two can be compared.
- `_fit_similarity` handles a non-centred block set (the ring's centroid is
  the frame centre, the inner set's is too, but the code no longer assumes
  it).
- Per window: `coherence` (weighted fraction of ring blocks within
  1.0 px + 25 % of the fitted shift), `subject_excess_px`, and
  `subject_motion` (excess ≥ 1.0 px per pair). `camera` is classified from
  the ring sums exactly as before; **coherence does not relabel anything**.
- Public API unchanged for callers: `estimate_camera_motion`,
  `compare_with_claims`, `classify`, `CAMERA_VALUES`. The 25d feed to the
  VLM therefore now carries ring-based labels.
- `test_camera_motion.py` +3 (14): a textured subject sliding across a
  still background is `static` with `subject_motion` true; a field where
  every block slides by its own amount has lower coherence than a clean pan
  but keeps its summed label; a clean pan agrees between ring and full
  frame with coherence ≥ 0.9. The earlier 11 pass unchanged (pan, tilt,
  zoom, cut, blank, thresholds, sign convention).

chunks.heading: ## Change (`local_agent/camera_motion.py`, LF)
chunks.text:
xtured subject sliding across a
  still background is `static` with `subject_motion` true; a field where
  every block slides by its own amount has lower coherence than a clean pan
  but keeps its summed label; a clean pan agrees between ring and full
  frame with coherence ≥ 0.9. The earlier 11 pass unchanged (pan, tilt,
  zoom, cut, blank, thresholds, sign convention).

## What the coherence gate would have done, and why it is not in

The first build relabelled any above-threshold window with mean coherence
below 0.6 as `uncertain` ("incoherent"). Measured on 12 clips at three
tolerances (`camera_motion_border_vs_full.txt` companion run, and the
transcript of this session):

| clip | what the pixels are | coherence (1.0 px + 25 %) |
|---|---|---|
| M03 `1216` creek, good | water filling the frame | **1.00** |
| M03 `2b3d` creek | still water | 1.00 |
| c005 hallway walk | corridor push-in | 1.00 |
| M04 butterfly | wings spanning the frame | 0.99 |
| B01 handheld walk | corridor push-in | 0.92 |
| D01 `8358` drone | forward flight over cliffs | 0.87 |
| c036 handheld | operator in frame, lighting swings | 0.76 |
| D03 `1adb` drone | tracking beside a motorcycle | **0.68** |
| synthetic per-block random slide | not a camera | 0.79 |

Uniform flow is perfectly coherent; a real camera move over a 3D scene is
incoherent because near and far blocks shift by different amounts
(parallax). Tightening the tolerance to 0.75 px + 15 % made 7 of 8 D03
windows `uncertain` and left the creek at 1.00. So the gate would have
thrown away real drone moves and kept the confounder. Removed; `coherence`
stays in the output as a diagnostic with that caveat in the docstring.

## Ring vs full frame on the 79 clips (656 one-second windows)

`runtime/dspy_opt/judge_eval_20260924/camera_motion_border_vs_full.txt`,
refreshed `camera_motion_labeled_clips.{txt,json}`.

- Ring label == full-frame label on the same 4×4 grid: **636/656**.
- Ring label == 25c's 3×3 full-frame label: 608/656; the 48 differences are
  on the chaotic clips (D04 skateboard, c036, c030 drift, M02 bee, D04
  `2d86`), one window at a time, with no way to say which is right without
  labeled camera moves.
- Label distribution is unchanged in shape: push-in 300, static 169,
  pull-back 42, pan-left 35, pan-right 27, tilt-up 24, tilt-down 16,
  uncertain 43.
- `subject_motion` fired on 91 windows. Where it fires hardest it is right:
  D04 skateboard `3f0c` (excess 5.7 px on the flip), c009 (5.1), c030
  (4.3), c036 (3.0), D03 `5c73` (2.7 on the motorcycle). Where the operator
  cared it does not fire: M03 creek 0.1 px (the flow reaches the ring, so
  the ring moves with it), M04 butterfly 0.6 px (wings reach the ring).

chunks.text:
n 43.
- `subject_motion` fired on 91 windows. Where it fires hardest it is right:
  D04 skateboard `3f0c` (excess 5.7 px on the flip), c009 (5.1), c030

## Bottom line

The ring fit is at parity with the full-frame fit on real footage and
strictly better on the synthetic case it was designed for (subject confined
to the centre). It adds a subject-motion flag that fires on genuine
subject action. It does not resolve a subject that spans the whole picture,
and no geometric split of one frame can; that needs either depth (parallax
between far-apart frames) or a labeled camera-motion set to learn against.
Both stay open.

## Change (`local_agent/video_judge.py`)

- `CHECK_KEYS` gains `camera_or_operator_visible` (eighth, after
  `text_or_logo_visible`). `normalize_checks`, the "fault checks unanswered"
  reason and rule (a) from 24q (a `constraint_broken` that names a check key
  is a dump, not a quote) pick it up automatically.
- `VIDEO_JUDGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT`: the failure list names "showing the recording
  rig itself (a camera, a tripod, the drone that should be carrying the
  camera, or the operator) in the picture"; the per-frame line asks for "any
  camera, drone, tripod or person holding a camera that is itself an object
  in the picture"; and the question reads (final wording, v3):

  > answer from the pictures only, not from the BRIEF: is any recording
  > equipment or its operator IN the picture in any frame: a camera or
  > camcorder body, a lens, a tripod or light stand, a drone / quadcopter /
  > aircraft seen from outside (from behind, beside, above or below it, flying
  > ahead of the camera), a boom, a monitor, or a person holding, carrying or
  > looking through a camera or camcorder? If a drone is an object in the
  > picture, the camera is not on that drone, whatever the BRIEF calls the
  > shot: "yes". If a person is holding a camcorder in the picture, that
  > person is the operator: "yes". A view seen THROUGH a camera or drone with
  > none of this in the picture is "no", and a still, locked-off framing is
  > "no": the fault is the rig or operator appearing in the image, not the
  > shot being static

  Deliberately **not** in the question: the task's suggested "a viewpoint that
  looks unusually static or shake-less while the brief implies handheld
  footage also counts". From eight stills this VLM cannot judge shake, the
  measured camera-motion estimator (25c) is the instrument for that, and
  locked-off framings are legitimate in this pack (br_c003 "static reference
  framing", the Mode A audition briefs). Putting it in the same yes/no would
  create exactly the false-fail mode this entry has to avoid.
- `fault_caps`: `camera_or_operator_visible == "yes"` caps
  `text_video_alignment` at **0.25**, unless `_GEAR_REQUESTED` matches the
  brief. 0.25 sits between "subject absent" (0.20: nothing requested is
  there) and "wrong medium" (0.30: the scene is there in the wrong form): the
  scene is usually there, seen from the wrong side. Any cap ≤ 0.40 already
  fails both curriculum bars (0.60 / 0.80), so the value only orders rejects
  among themselves.
- `_GEAR_REQUESTED`: a brief that has the actor handle or inspect the gear

## 1. What c018 actually is (measured before changing anything)

Mean luma per frame (64×36 decode): frames 0–12 lit at 76, 13–23 dimmed to
29, 24–34 **near-black at 3**, 35–43 **dim at 20**, 44 at 56, 45+ lit at 80.
So the flagged step at 1.83 s is dim → lit at the *end* of a 1.3 s dip, not
a two-frame blink. Every existing rule misses it for a stated reason: the
dark side (19 luma) is above the 16 near-black guard; the histogram never
"returns" because a lights-off frame never histogram-matches a lights-on
frame; and the adjacent-frame layout correlation is 0.63 because the panels
themselves are off (the lighting pattern changed, not just the gain), which
is why 24r's before/after correlation "did not separate it".

What does separate it: the lit picture **on the far side of the dip**. Frame
45 (luma 79) correlates with frames 0–12 (luma 76) at **0.86–0.91**. The same
comparison across every labeled real cut: D01 `8358` 0.56, c008 0.36, D04
`5ac6` −0.25, M03 `371a` 0.16–0.21 (a cut *into* a dark scene that brightens),
D03 `5c73` −0.12, D03 `ffd4` 0.03–0.10. Prototype run over all 79 clips
before touching the file: exactly one cut list changed (c018), all six
detected real cuts unchanged.

## 2. Change (`local_agent/video_judge.py`)

- **CPU detector, dip rule** (`_dip_returns_same_picture`, constants
  `CUT_DIP_FRACTION = 0.5`, `CUT_DIP_MAX_FRAMES = 48`): for a candidate step
  that survived every older test, take the brighter frame as the lit side;
  walk away from the step on the dark side over frames at least 2× darker
  than the lit frame (at most 2 s); the first frame beyond that stretch is
  the far reference. If its layout correlation with the lit frame is ≥
  `CUT_MAX_CORR` (0.70, the same threshold the adjacent-frame test uses),
  the step is one edge of a lighting dip on an unchanged picture and is not
  a cut. With no dip the reference is the adjacent frame, which already
  failed the correlation test, so a plain cut is never rescued; a cut into a
  dark scene that brightens (M03) walks 2 frames and finds a different
  picture (0.18). Exposure-invariant, so it covers dim stretches that the
  near-black guard cannot, without raising that guard (M03's post-cut frame
  at 17.2 luma is still a cut).
- Re-measured on the real file, all 79 clips: **1 change (c018: [1.83] →
  []), the six real cuts and every `blank_fraction` unchanged**
  (`judge_eval_20260925/frame_signals_v3b.json`).
- **Dark-frame annotation** (second iteration, after the prompt rule alone
  did not fix c004): `frame_signals` now returns `dark_spans_s`
  (`[[start_s, end_s, "near-black"|"dim"], …]`: runs below 16 luma, and runs
  below `DIM_FRACTION = 0.5` × the median lit luma), and
  `build_judge_user_prompt(..., signals=)` marks each sampled frame that
  falls in a span: `F2=1.6s (near-black: lights down in this frame,
  measured)`, followed by one line: a near-black or dim frame is a lighting
  dip in the same shot, not a new place and not a cut; judge place, cuts and
  the subject from the lit frames. Without a dip the user prompt is byte-
  identical to before. `dspy_orchestrator.judge_rendered_clip` passes its
  `signals` into the user prompt (three-line change). This is the 25d
  pattern: an instrument reading fed to the VLM instead of asking it to
  infer exposure from a JPEG. On the labeled sets it marks 62 sampled frames
  in 19 of 79 clips (c004 F2 near-black, c018 F2 dim, c017/c019/c033 flicker
  frames, and the all-black rejects, which the 25 % near-black aesthetic cap
  still holds at 0.20 whatever the VLM answers).
- **Prompt rule** (`VIDEO_JUDGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT`, "Lighting and camera moves"):
  a requested flicker / strobe / lights-out / dead tube / lighting change
  makes a merely darker or brighter frame with the same layout that effect,

## 5. The judge is not bit-deterministic (measured here, matters for 24q's claim)

Between v3b and v3c only the 19 annotated clips received a different prompt.
Of the 60 clips whose system and user prompts were **byte-identical**, 4
came back different: tuning D01 `3032` (constraint_broken text only), D01
`b028` (alignment 0.0 → 0.2, a reject either way), D03 `ffd4` (two checks
flipped, scores identical), and held-out **c028** (aesthetic 0.80 → 0.75,
checks identical, raw text differs). 25a found the same on the action log's
batched image calls and attributed it to the server's batched decode /
flash-attn; the 8-image judge call is evidently not exempt, only less
affected (56 of 60 identical). Consequences: single-clip flips between runs
of ±0.05 or one check are within noise; 24ae's "13 re-judged clips
identical" was luck-compatible, not proof of determinism; and a good clip
sitting exactly at 0.80 (most Backrooms clips, 24ac) can land at 0.75 on a
re-run and fail the strict bar. Not fixed here; noted for the curriculum.

## The three questions

**(a) Do good Backrooms clips clear the 0.80 bar?** Yes, at the edge. The
only good B01 render (`644b`) was never judged live (next section); judged
offline it scores 1.00 / 1.00 / 0.80 and passes at exactly 0.80, which is
where 24ac showed every correct Backrooms clip sits. The live-judged B01
(`d959`) failed at 0.30 for a real text overlay, correctly. Two non-Backrooms
good rows cleared the bar live (D02 0.90, M03 0.95). Caveat from 25h: the
judge's run-to-run noise is ±0.05 on the aesthetic axis, so a clip at 0.80
can land at 0.75 on another run; the bar has no margin for Backrooms clips.

**(b) Does a judged reject outrank a timeout / mechanical fail?** Yes, by
construction and now in a real row: row 266's raw scalar is **0.050**, which
is exactly the timeout penalty and would have tied it (and sat below it with
one fewer frame), and the floor made it 0.100; row 265's mechanical fail is
0.02; row 262's judged reject is 0.175. Ordering in the history: 0.960 >
0.920 > 0.375 > 0.350 > 0.315 > 0.175 > 0.100 (judged) > 0.02 (mechanical).

**(c) Are Phase A / B visible in real rankings?** Partly.
- 25g rig check: fired once, on row 268, where a human hand reaches into
  frame; the verdict is right (the constraints forbid it) and the category
  is a stretch (a hand is "operator" only if it is the operator's). It
  correctly stayed "no" on the true FPV row 263. It **missed** row 267's
  F1, where the VLM's own frame line says "a black object (likely drone)"
  and the check still answered "no": the 614e anchoring miss, seen live.
- 25h: the CPU dip rule had nothing to suppress (no false cuts on eight
  renders); the two real cuts in row 266 were detected and capped. Only row
  267 had a sampled frame inside a measured dip (F2, dim) and it was
  annotated. No flicker Backrooms clip reached the judge live because `644b`
  was gated, and `644b` has no dark span anyway, so the flicker rules were
  **not exercised** by this pass. A negative result, not a failure.

## Problems this pass surfaced (outside A/B scope; documented, not fixed)

1. **The mechanical gate runs after the render and rejects on prompt text.**
   Row 265: 757 s of GPU for a clip the review calls good, then
   `_fail_result` 0.02 because the student's `video_prompt` said
   "gradually moves … panning" instead of walk / push in / tracking / dolly.
   `mechanical_director_gate` is called after `generate_minimax_clip` in
   `evaluate_live_candidate`; its keyword test needs only `pred` and could
   run before the GPU like 24o's `instruction_echo` check. Pre-existing
   (15l saw it), but it is why the Backrooms bar question needed the offline
   re-judge. Operator decision: move the keyword test pre-render, or relax
   it (the prompt it rejected rendered a good clip).
2. **Runaway repetition in the judge.** Two in 87 scorings this session:
   D03 `5c73` (25h) and row 263's clip offline ("more motion blur,
   approaching a break in the canopy, slight upward tilt, …" until the
   budget). `repeat_penalty=1.0` (24ae) is what permits the loop; 24ae
   measured 1.08 as harmful to the checklist. In production a runaway is
   `VLM scores rejected` → 0.01, below the floor and below a mechanical
   fail, for a clip the same judge scored 0.92 live. A retry on
   `missing or invalid float score` (with the penalty on for the retry only,
   or a smaller value) is the obvious fix; not done here.
3. **Non-determinism confirmed on live renders** (25h §5): row 267 is a
   reject at 0.315 live and a clean 0.80 pass on the byte-identical offline
   prompt; row 263 parsed live and looped offline. Chaotic clips are a coin

# 2026-09-25j — GVD live metric: the mechanical gate runs before the render

Follows 2026-09-25i, which found it in the live pass: history row 265 spent
757 s of GPU rendering GVD-B01 `644b` (a clip the sheet review calls good),
then `mechanical_director_gate` rejected the student's `video_prompt` for
lacking a motion keyword ("gradually moves … panning" instead of walk / push
in / tracking / dolly) and the row scored 0.02 without the clip ever reaching
the judge. Operator decision: move the check before the render. The keyword
tables are not relaxed here; that is a separate decision.

No GPU, no VLM, no renders: code and unit tests only.

Backups: `local_agent/{dspy_orchestrator.py,test_dspy_orchestrator.py}.bak_pregate_20260925T094303`.
Edit applied by `local_agent/runtime/dspy_opt/judge_eval_20260925/_edit_pregate.py`
(kept as the record; asserts refuse a second run). `dspy_orchestrator.py`
LF (0 CR before and after); `test_dspy_orchestrator.py` CRLF (0 bare LF
before and after).

## Why it can move

`mechanical_director_gate(example, pred, video_path=None)` reads only the
resolved `start_prompt` / `video_prompt`, the instruction-echo shingles, the
example's `duration_seconds` and category, and the Backrooms camera / motion
keyword tables. Its `video_path` argument was never read (checked line by
line; the docstring now says so). Nothing in it needs the file, so nothing
is lost by running it first.

## Change (`local_agent/dspy_orchestrator.py`, `evaluate_live_candidate`)

- After the existing pre-GPU checks (empty prompt → 0.02, instruction echo →
  0.02) and before `prepare_comfy`: when no `check_fn` is injected, run
  `mechanical_director_gate(example, pred)`; on failure return
  `_fail_result` with `error = "mechanical video check failed: [...]; skipped
  GPU"`. Same leading text as before, so `_fail_penalty` still gives 0.02 and
  history readers keyed on "mechanical video check failed" still match; the
  suffix "; skipped GPU" is the same convention the echo path uses. The row
  carries `video_path: None` and an empty `vram_trace`, as any pre-GPU fail
  does.
- After the render: only an injected `check_fn(video_path, prompt, clip_id)`
  is run now (the test hook, or a future check that actually needs the
  file), with the unchanged failure path (`video_path` set, `vram_trace`
  kept). The built-in gate is no longer called a second time.
- `passes_curriculum()` and `mechanical_director_gate()` themselves are
  unchanged.

What a gated candidate costs the optimizer now: the same 0.02, ~0 s instead
of ~13 min of GPU per occurrence. In the 24o and 25i passes that was 1 of 16
and 1 of 8 candidates respectively.

chunks.heading: # 2026-09-25k — GVD judge: one retry when the answer arrives without the three scores
chunks.text:
# 2026-09-25k — GVD judge: one retry when the answer arrives without the three scores

Follows 2026-09-25g/h/i, which each left the same item open: a judge answer
that never reaches the three float scores is a `_fail_result` in the live
metric, below every judged clip, for a clip that may be good. The fix named
in all three ("a retry on `missing or invalid float score`") is built here,
measured on the clips that failed, and its two obvious forms (a penalty on
the retry, an anti-repetition note) are rejected by that measurement.

VLM only, under `gvd_judge_eval.preflight` (8188 closed, owners idle, GPU
29–35 °C at start, 82 °C check before every clip, release and cool-down after
each run). No ComfyUI, no renders; existing files only.

Backups: `local_agent/{video_judge.py,test_video_judge.py,dspy_orchestrator.py,gvd_judge_eval.py}.bak_judgeretry_20260925T101616`.
Edits applied by `local_agent/runtime/dspy_opt/judge_eval_20260925/_edit_judgeretry.py`
(retry, tests) and `_edit_judgeretry_v2.py` (the measured note and penalty;
kept as the record, asserts refuse a second run). All four files LF, 0 CR
before and after.

## 1. What fails (measured in the result files before changing anything)

Two shapes, both `status: fail` from `parse_video_director_scores`:

- **Runaway.** A frame line loops ("more motion blur, slight upward tilt, …")
  until `num_predict=1536` and the JSON never closes → "VLM did not return a
  JSON object with float scores". Tuning D03 `5c73` (v3b and v3c, 8 frames);
  phase C D02 `53ae` offline (25i); and under the 12-frame variants D01
  `6609` (f12) and br_c005 `db78` (heldout_f8c).
- **Closed early.** Frames and checks are written, `constraint_broken` dumps
  the checks, the object closes before the scores → three "missing or invalid
  float score" reasons. Held-out br_c001 `32ce` (v3a, 1536 chars); and at
  `repeat_penalty=1.08` (24ae's results_v2c) D04 `2d86`, D01 `6609`, D04 `cc43`.

What production does with them today, from `_fail_penalty`: a runaway scores
**0.02** (its reason text contains "JSON"), an early close **0.01**. 25i and
TODO said 0.01 for both; 0.02 is the same scalar as a mechanical fail. Either
way the row sits below the 0.10 floor of every judged clip.

They are stochastic on a fixed prompt, which matters for the fix: D03 `5c73`
looped in v3b and v3c and parsed today; D02 `53ae` parsed live (0.92), looped
offline, parsed today (1.00 / 1.00 / 0.90) on the byte-identical prompt;
br_c001 `32ce` closed early once (v3a, 25g's prompt) and parsed in v3b, v3c
and today (25h's prompt). None of the three failed in this session, so the
retry never fired on its own during the measurement (section 3 forces it).

## 2. Change

- `local_agent/video_judge.py`: `JUDGE_RETRY_REPEAT_PENALTY`,

  verdict, which no retry can fix); `retry_user_prompt(prompt)` (the first
  attempt's user prompt plus the note).
- `local_agent/dspy_orchestrator.py`, `run_qwen_director_scores`: the call is
  an inner `_ask(user_prompt, num_predict, repeat_penalty, attempt)`; the first
  call is byte-identical to 24ae (1536, 1.0, `json_mode`); if

  `raw_chars` (true length; `raw` is still cut at 4000). Debug rows in
  `gvd_vlm_raw.jsonl` carry `attempt`. `apply_fault_caps` copies the dict, so
  `retry` reaches `judge_rendered_clip`'s caller.
- `evaluate_live_candidate`: feedback rows gain `judge_retry` (None unless the
  retry produced the verdict); a verdict still without scores after the
  retry fails with the same leading text, `VLM scores rejected: […]; after
  one retry`, so history readers keyed on "VLM scores rejected" still match
  and the penalty is unchanged.
- `local_agent/gvd_judge_eval.py`: result records carry `retry`; the per-clip

## 1. Measure first: what the estimator says over the judge's own gaps (CPU only)

For every labeled clip and the 8 phase C renders, the judge's 8 sampled frame
times (`extract_eval_frames`, cached) define 7 gaps; `estimate_camera_motion`
was run over those gaps and the per-gap label and summed pan / tilt
fraction recorded (`camera_gaps_v3e.txt`). Two things decided the gates:

- The bare label marks far too much: 32 of 87 clips (109 frames), among them
  the 25c creek confounder M03 `1216` (good: water flowing down the frame
  reads tilt-up on all 7 gaps at 0.13–0.15 of the frame) and 23 rejects,
  because cuts, morphs and drift are also large global shifts.
- c038's turn is large and rigid: pan-left at **0.46** (F3→F4) and **0.32**
  (F4→F5) of the frame width with the estimator's `subject_motion` flag off
  (centre excess 0.1–0.3 px). c030 (reject, a cut-and-return the brief also
  calls a turn) swings at 0.27 / 0.27 / 0.48 but **every swing carries the
  flag** (excess 2.4–4.4 px), as do both of D01 `086a`'s (late drift), both
  of D04 `3f0c`'s, and D02 `7d15`'s single pan (phase C).

Gates, both on the estimator's own output: the picture must have slid by at
least **`TURN_MIN_FRAC = 0.20`** of the frame across the gap (the creek's
0.15 stays under it), and **`subject_motion` must be off** (a rigid turn, not
a moving subject, a morph or a drift). Marked clips under both gates: **9 of
79 labeled, 0 of 8 phase C**: goods c038 (F4, F5) and br_c002 (F8, its "turn
toward the floor"); tuning rejects M05 `c6a5` (F3–F5, tilt-down), D01 `3032`
(F6, F7, tilt-up), c009 (F3, F5); held-out rejects c026 (F6), D04 `5ac6` (F5,
F6, the frames after its 3.04 s cut), D04 `cc43` (F8), M01 `d9e1` (F3). No
partial. Every marked reject except M05 was already held by a cap that no
temporal answer can lift (rig 0.25, text 0.30/0.40, subject absent 0.20, CPU
hard cut 0.25), and M05 was a false pass, so the worst case for the rejects
was "no change". The gates were chosen with c038's readings in view, so the
held-out numbers below are not a blind test of this change.
