## 2. Change

- `local_agent/video_judge.py`: `TURN_MIN_FRAC`, `TURN_LABELS`;
  `measured_camera_moves(video, frame_times)` (gap windows keyed by the later
  frame's 1-based index → `estimate_camera_motion`, one compact record per
  gap: frame, start, end, camera, dx_frac, dy_frac, scale, response, pairs,
  low_response_pairs, subject_motion); `turn_amount`; `measured_turns(moves)`
  (the two gates → `{later frame: "turned left" | "turned right" | "tilted up"
  | "tilted down"}`). `build_judge_user_prompt` marks the later frame of each
  rigid turn, `F4=4.4s (camera turned left between F3 and F4, measured)`, on
  the same line a dip mark would share (`dim: …; camera turned …`), and when
  any frame is marked appends one line, `TURN_RULE`: a measured turn is an
  instrument reading, the whole picture slid between those two frames as it
  does when the camera pans or tilts within one continuous shot; a wall,
  floor, ceiling or object of the same room or scene filling the later frame
  after a turn is that camera move, not a cut, not a new place, and still the
  BRIEF's setting; answer abrupt_cut "yes" or same_place "no" across a
  measured turn **only if the setting itself is somewhere else** (another
  room, landscape or set). With no rigid turn, or no measurement, the prompt
  is byte-identical to 25h's. The system prompt, checks, caps table and CPU
  detector are unchanged; a turn caps nothing.
- `local_agent/dspy_orchestrator.py`: `judge_rendered_clip` extracts the
  frames, then, on the production path (no injected `signals_fn`), calls
  `video_judge.measured_camera_moves` and stores the result as
  `signals["camera_moves"]`, so it reaches the user prompt, the feedback row
  and the eval records; a failed estimate is printed and skipped. New
  `camera_fn` hook on `judge_rendered_clip` and `evaluate_live_candidate`
  (an injected `signals_fn` gets no measurement unless `camera_fn` is
  injected too, so every existing test is unchanged and none runs ffmpeg).
- `gvd_judge_eval.py`: no change needed; result records already carry
  `signals`, now with `camera_moves`.

## 1. Free evidence first (no GPU)

- v3c (25h), v3d (25k) and v3e (25l) are three separate launches on
  byte-identical prompts for 69 clips (46 tuning + 23 held-out, the ones 25l
  did not mark): **raw text identical 69/69**, so the noise is not a steady
  per-request rate.
- 25h's v3b → v3c: recounted at raw-text level, **8 of 60** prompt-identical
  clips differed (25h counted the 4 with check or score changes). v3b is the
  one run with a mid-run server relaunch (the D05 connection reset at
  position 4); the six tuning differences sit at positions 5 (D05's own
  retry, the new server's first request), 29, 31, 32, 38, 46. The
  divergence in each pair is a single near-tie word deep in a frame line or
  rationale ("Distant view of cliffs" vs "View of cliffs"; "black lizard" vs
  "dark lizard"), after which the rest of the answer re-converges or not.
- The production launch (`dspy_optimizer._ensure_owned_qwen25_vl_runtime`)
  and the runner's launch use the same arguments (ctx 32768, all layers on
  GPU, `--image-min-tokens 1024`, `--flash-attn auto`), so launch flags are
  not a live-vs-offline difference.

## 2. What the server does (its own log)

For every request after the first in a launch: `selected slot by LCP
similarity, f_sim_best = 0.130, f_keep = 0.124` and `prompt eval … 9271
tokens` of ~11 200: the slot keeps the shared prefix (the system prompt's
KV, computed inside the **first** request's batch) and prefills only the
rest. The first request prefills everything (10 660 tokens). A prompt-cache
of finished slots is kept in host memory ("making room for prompt cache
entry, removing oldest entry, 1.5 GiB"), so a request identical to a recent
one is restored almost whole. Three conditions therefore exist, and each
live MIPRO judgement is the first of them (the VLM is launched per candidate
and released after it, 25i):

| condition | what is prefilled | where it occurs |
|---|---|---|
| **cold** | the whole prompt, in its own batch | the live metric, every time; clip 1 of every eval run |
| **warm-prefix** | everything but the system prompt, whose KV came from the launch's first request | every eval-runner clip after the first |
| **warm-full** | the generated tokens only, the prompt restored from the cache | back-to-back repeats of one clip (never production) |

## 6. The bar, from the data

Only one clip on either labeled set has a warm minimum axis in [0.60, 0.80):

Three goods sit at exactly 0.80 in every judgement, cold and warm (br_c002
8/8, br_c003 8/8, tuning c017 in both conditions) and c018 in 6 of 8: the
missing margin is a property of the judge's aesthetic scale on Backrooms
clips (24ac), not of noise.

From all 163 warm judgements collected (5–8 per clip, mixed histories):
single sample at 0.80: false pass 2.00/12, false fail 1.88/12; either-of-two
1.54; both-of-two 2.21; mean-of-two ≥ 0.80 2.21, ≥ 0.775 1.79;
majority-of-three 1.89; single at 0.75 1.12; at 0.60 1.12. From the cold
judgements: every rule gives false pass 2/12 (c021, M04 `4c83`), false fail
1/12 (c035, disputed label), because the two cold samples are identical.
Two-sample judging buys at most 0.35 expected false fails on 12 goods for
double the VLM time under warm, and nothing under cold.

## 8. Operator decision (not applied here)

Recommended: **judge cold everywhere.** Send `cache_prompt: false` on the
judge's request: one entry in `llama_cpp_client._SAMPLER_FIELDS`
(`("cache_prompt", bool)`), one keyword through `media_tools._run_vision_gpu`
from `dspy_orchestrator.run_qwen_director_scores` (first attempt and retry),
plus tests. Production is unchanged in effect (already cold, and protected
against any future warm-up call); the eval runner then measures the
production judge, deterministic and history-independent, at ~+0.3 s per
clip (a 10.6k-token prefill instead of 9.3k). Re-baseline on the cold
results already on disk (`nondet_tuning_nocache.jsonl`,
`nondet_heldout_nocache_a.jsonl`; section 4). Alternatives, for the record:
warming production with a fixed prefill would move it to the condition where

## Root cause (two halves)

1. **Detection.** `_requests_specialist_project_context(text)` is text-only by
   design ("Old chats and retrieved memories … are not authority to answer a new
   unrelated turn as if it were still that project"). Msg 10 has no Flux/Comfy
   keyword ("genration" is misspelled, so even `image generation` cannot match)
   and "regenerate that one" has no image noun, so it is False. "status" is
   False. `_pending_specialist_continuation(history)` covered three shapes:
   an offer / successful plan on the immediately-previous assistant turn, a
   confirmation after such an offer, and "finish the earlier prompt" over an
   unfinished `plan_story_image`. Msg 9 is a plain status explanation
   (no `_SPECIALIST_CONTINUATION_OFFER_RE` match), the chat had renders but no
   unfinished plan, so all three were False. `specialist_scope` came out False
   for a chat that had never been about anything else.
2. **Fallback honesty.** With `specialist_scope` False, `run_one()` refuses any
   `_SPECIALIST_PROJECT_TOOLS` call. When every call in the hop was refused and
   the one-shot retry was unused, the loop appended "Scope correction: … Do not
   retry any H3, ComfyUI, … tool. Use a tool relevant to the current request, or
   answer the current request directly" and gave the model another free-text
   turn. That turn is what the operator saw. The sibling guards in the same
   function (write_file ERROR, batch-folder refusal, batch-render refusal,
   current-chat-render refusal) all return a hardcoded truthful `final` for
   exactly this reason (their comments: "Do not give a small model a second turn
   in which it can turn a … denied … approval into a made-up claim"); the
   scope refusal did not.

## Change — `local_agent/agent.py`

Detection (fourth continuation shape, `_pending_specialist_continuation`,
docstring updated):

- `_SPECIALIST_REGENERATION_UTTERANCE_RE`: regenerate / re-render / redo / rerun /
  remake / retry, "try (it) again", "generate|render|make|run|do it|that one|
  this one|another one again", "one more time|try|attempt", "again without|with|
  but".
- `_SPECIALIST_STATUS_UTTERANCE_RE`: **whole-message only** — "status",
  "what's the status", "any update(s)?", "progress", "is it done|ready|finished
  (yet)?", "did it finish?", "how's it going", "still running?", "done?",
  "check on it", "where is it / the output" — with an optional "of|on|for it |
  that | the job|render|generation|regen|last one". "status of the powerinfer
  calibration" and "status of the download please" do not match.
- Both are gated by the existing `_SPECIALIST_CONTINUATION_OTHER_TOPIC_RE`
  (powerinfer / calibration / jsonl / sonic pi / wireguard / todo.md / farms):
  naming another topic never opens image scope
  (`_is_specialist_regeneration_or_status_utterance`).
- `_recent_specialist_tool_activity(history)`: walks back over at most
  `_RECENT_SPECIALIST_EVIDENCE_TURNS = 4` assistant turns, with the server's
  "Saved local tool evidence" system receipts attached to the turn they follow.
  The first turn carrying a tool row that actually ran decides: a successful
  `_SPECIALIST_PROJECT_TOOLS` row → True; any other successful tool (e.g.
  `validate_powerinfer_calibration`) → the chat has moved on → False. Rows with
  outcome `error` (including the guard's own refusals), `list_tools` /
  `describe_tool` / `call_tool` rows, and announce-only `kind: tool_call`
  activity rows are skipped and do not count toward the bound, so one misfire
  of the guard cannot lock the operator out of the chat's own work (live msg 12
  after the refused msg 11 still reaches msg 9). Tool-free replies count toward
  the bound; four of them and "status" is no longer a continuation. Only rows
  persisted on the history contribute — retrieved memories and other chats are
  not on it, which is the leak this guard exists to stop.
- `_requests_specialist_project_context` and `_SPECIALIST_CONTEXT_REQUEST_RE`

## Is msg 10's refusal correct as-is? (edge case considered)

No. "that one" has exactly one candidate in this chat's own evidence: msg 9's
`render_story_image` for `Scene-Start-Image-2`, whose PNG the operator had just
looked at ("i see a genration that was made yesterday" — msg 9 is 2026-09-24
evening local). Requiring the operator to restate the story name would guard
against a risk the scope guard does not own: which image to redo is a
target-selection question the model answers from the evidence in context (its
live hop-0 args carried `story`, `mode: i2i`, `reference_name`), and if a chat
held several recent stills the right move is for the model to ask, in scope,
not for the guard to refuse. The signal used here — this chat's most recent
real tool activity was specialist work, bounded to four turns, other-topic
words excluded — is the same first-party evidence the three existing
continuation shapes already trust. What stays refused: a regeneration or
status phrase in a chat whose last real activity was something else, one that
names another topic, or one four tool-free turns after the last render.

## 4. Root cause

The inversion appears **only when the DWPose map carries face and hand
keypoints together** (inverted 3/4 and 4/4). Removing either one (4/4
upright each), or both (8/8 upright), gives an upright scene that follows
the pose. Stick width makes no difference in either direction (pass9 vs
pass6, pass10 vs pass11). The union model reads depth correctly (4/4). So
this is an out-of-distribution control image for xinsir's union model
(trained body-only), not a model, loader, ComfyUI or AnimateDiff fault.
Scope of the evidence: one clip, one seed, 4 frames per condition (16 for
pass14). The rule for any template of this approach:
**`DWPreprocessor detect_face: disable`** (body-only is xinsir's documented
preparation; hands tested fine). Isolation (c), the non-union canny
baseline, was not run: (a) had already shown the union model is sound. The
runner supports it (`--control canny --cn-model canny`).

# 2026-09-26b — GVD tool router: MiniMax-first engine policy, Wan only by request or as an announced last resort

Offline code work in `local_agent/gvd_tool_router/` plus one whitelist
description string in `local_agent/tools.py`. No render was started, no
ComfyUI call was made, no registry or catalog JSON on disk was rewritten, no
model was downloaded. The only GPU-adjacent action was a read of the existing
`runtime/gvd_tool_router/registry/active.json` and
`inventory/environment_lock.json`.

Operator policy being enforced: **MiniMax is the default video engine. Wan may
be selected only when (a) the operator's own request explicitly names Wan, or
(b) no MiniMax implementation fits the shot and Wan is the only compatible
implementation left — and (b) must be surfaced to the operator, not just
logged.**

## 1. Legacy Backrooms pipeline — confirmed MiniMax-only, not touched

- `batch_run_backrooms_gvd.py` (repo root): the only "Wan" strings are two
  comments saying not to invent Wan/FLUX CFG for the distilled H3 path. No
  Wan graph builder, no Wan node, no fallback.
- `local_agent/dspy_orchestrator.py`: `build_wan_graph()` raises
  `RuntimeError("build_wan_graph is retired…")`; `generate_wan_clip()` is a
  deprecated alias that calls `generate_minimax_clip()`. The remaining "wan"
  hits are docstrings, the `GVD_WAN_TIMEOUT_S` env name (reused as the
  MiniMax track timeout), and a scoring heuristic on error text.
- `test_dspy_orchestrator.py::test_build_wan_graph_is_retired` already pins
  the retirement. Nothing in that path was changed.

## 2. Where MiniMax-vs-Wan is decided now

`gvd_tool_router/router.py::route()` → inner `consider()`:

1. `engine_family(impl)` classifies every catalog row as `"minimax"`,
   `"wan"` or `"other"` from `limits["engine_family"]` if stated, else from
   `implementation_id` + each stage `model_family_key` (MiniMax H3 and the
   FastH3 distillations are one family; `wan22_*`, `wan21_*`,
   `wan_tile_video`, `wan22_animate`, `wan21_vace` are the other; LTX,
   AnimateDiff, IP-Adapter, SDXL, LongCat are neutral).
2. `engine_tier(impl, manifest.requested_engine)` gives the sort tier.
   Default: MiniMax 0, other 1, Wan 2. With `requested_engine == "wan"`:
   Wan 0, everything else 1.
3. Viable candidates sort by `(tier, -score, implementation_id)`. Before this
   change they sorted by `(-score, implementation_id)` only — there was no
   engine concept anywhere in `route()`.
4. `engine_policy(winner)` annotates the `RouteDecision`:

   | winner | `requested_engine` | `engine_selection` | `reason_codes` | `operator_notice` |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | MiniMax / other | none | `default` | `()` | none |
   | Wan | `"wan"` | `explicit_request` | `ENGINE_EXPLICIT_WAN` | "Wan selected … because the operator's request explicitly named Wan" |
   | Wan | none | `fallback` | `ENGINE_FALLBACK_WAN` + `minimax_unfit:<id>:<reasons>` per rejected MiniMax row, or `minimax_absent` | "MiniMax didn't fit, used Wan instead (<id>), because … Wan was the only compatible implementation left … confirm before rendering." |
   | MiniMax / other | `"wan"` | `requested_engine_unavailable` | `REQUESTED_ENGINE_UNAVAILABLE:wan` + `wan_unfit:<id>:<reasons>` | "The operator requested Wan but it could not be used (…); selected <id> instead." |

   The fallback and explicit paths are therefore distinguishable by
   `engine_selection`, by reason code, and by notice text.

Manifest hook: a dedicated `ShotManifest.requested_engine: str | None` field
(schema.py), read by `shot_from_dict` (lower-cased, empty → None). It was
chosen over `hard_requirements` because `required_capabilities()` treats every
`hard_requirements` entry as a capability name, and over `priorities` because
those are numeric quality floors. An unknown value (e.g. `"sora"`) makes
`validate_manifest()` emit `unknown_requested_engine:<x>` and `route()`
returns `blocked` instead of guessing.

Planner path (planner.py): `requested_engine_from_text()` sets
`requested_engine = "wan"` only for a verb of choice next to the word
("use wan", "try wan", "switch to wan", "render it with wan", "on Wan 2.2",

("use wan", "try wan", "switch to wan", "render it with wan", "on Wan 2.2",
"wan for this one", "wan instead"). A bare "wan" (English word) is not a

never rescue an otherwise unreadable request — the `needs_manifest_review`
check runs first. `user_manifest["requested_engine"]` still overrides. The
planner's return now includes `requested_engine`.

- `route_shot()` → `to_plain(decision)` now carries `engine`,

  and `gvd_plan_shot` (via `plan_narrative`) return them unchanged.

  planned DAG **with the notice attached**; with `live=True` it is
  **blocked** (`ENGINE_FALLBACK_WAN`, `operator_acknowledgement_required`,

  still attaches on `blocked`.

## 3. `requires_operator_approval` — what it actually did before, and now

Traced before changing anything (the trace in the request was correct):

- `router._select_profile()` used it only as
  `if operator_approval and impl.limits.get("requires_operator_approval")`
  → headroom 512 MiB instead of 2,048. With `operator_approval=False` the
  flag was never read.
- `schema.can_activate()` does not reference it.
- `switch.switch_to()` lowers headroom on `operator_approval` alone and never
  reads the flag.
- `service.execute_tool()` called `route()` **without** passing
  `operator_approval` at all, so an approved manifest could route via
  `route_shot()` but the same approval was dropped on the execute path.

Net: the flag gated nothing. It only *widened* admission when approval was
already present; with enough free VRAM (not this 16 GiB card, but any larger
one) the row would have been selected with no approval. The name says
"requires"; the 2026-09-22i intent was "this row may only be admitted with an
explicit operator approval". It is kept, with that meaning made real:

- `router._compatible()` rejects a flagged row with
  `operator_approval_required` whenever `operator_approval` is False,
  regardless of free memory. With approval the existing 512 MiB headroom rule
  still applies.
- `execute_tool()` now reads `operator_approved_resource_override` from the
  raw dict and passes it to `route()`, matching `route_shot()`.
- `catalog_seed.py`: comment above the `fasth3_v2_unvalidated` row stating
  the enforced semantics. No data change; the on-disk registry digest
  `c495262e…` is unchanged.

Read-only check against the live registry (route() with a synthetic
15,831 MiB free inventory): `fasth3_v2_unvalidated` is rejected
`operator_approval_required` without approval and selected with it.

## 1. The gate before and after (`local_agent/dspy_orchestrator.py`, LF kept)

Before: `mechanical_director_gate` required, for a Backrooms example, a
substring hit from `_CAMERA_KEYWORDS` **and** from
`_MOTION_KEYWORDS = (walk, walking, momentum, push in, push-in, tracking
forward, track forward, dolly, glide, advance, move forward)`. History row
265 (GVD-B01 `644b`, CHANGELOG 2026-09-25i) — `video_prompt` "The handheld
camcorder gradually moves along the hallway, panning slowly." — has neither
"walk" nor any listed phrase, so it scored 0.02; the clip it produced is
reviewed good and judges 1.00 / 1.00 / 0.80 offline (min 0.80 = the bar).

After:

- `_MOTION_KEYWORDS` keeps every old entry and adds plain motion verbs and
  camera moves: move/moves/moving/movement, pan/pans/panning,
  tracking/tracks, drift(s/ing), creep(s/ing), step(s/stepping) forward,
  approach(es/ing), travel(s/ing/ling), wander(s/ing), tilt(s/ing),
  turn(s/ing), sway(s/ing).
- Matching is **word-bounded** (`_MOTION_RE`), not substring: "remove",
  "improvement", "span" no longer read as motion (the old substring test
  would have passed "remove" via "move" had "move" been in the table, which
  is why it was not).
- **The floor**: `_MOTION_NEGATION_RE` blanks a negated motion phrase before
  matching — "the camera does not move", "no panning", "never moving",
  "without any camera movement" — so a prompt that echoes motion vocabulary
  while describing a static shot still fails with the same
  `backrooms clip missing a motion keyword` reason (the message now lists
  pan/moves and says a negated phrase does not count). The camera-keyword
  requirement and the `instruction_echo` check are unchanged, so the three
  things the gate existed for — an empty/echoed prompt, a static shot, a
  prompt with no camera at all — are still rejected.
- New `has_motion_keyword(text)` is the single entry point; the gate calls
  it. `_is_drone_or_cinematic` bypass, duration checks: unchanged. The gate
  still runs pre-render (25j).

plus `_edit_gate_26e_fix.py`: the first script was fed through a shell

## 1. Trace: what reached the operator before

  `{"status": "needs_manifest_review", "reason_codes": ["NEEDS_MANIFEST_REVIEW"], "note": "unknown interpretation; refusing to pick the fastest tool"}`
  when no interpretation matches; `router.py::route` returns
  `needs_manifest_review` (low-confidence hard requirement) or `blocked`
  (validation reasons; `NO_COMPATIBLE_TOOL` + `UNAVAILABLE_CAPABILITY` with a
  `rejection_log` whose per-row reasons carry `RESOURCE_BLOCKED`,
  `PROFILE_REQUIRED`, `unknown_vram`, `operator_approval_required`,
  `missing_capabilities:…`); `service.py::route_shot` adds
  `missing_capabilities` / `blocked_candidates` (25q); `execute_tool` wraps
  the decision under `decision`, and adds its own `ENGINE_FALLBACK_WAN`
  (26b), `QA_GATE_BLOCKED`, and lease-contention `RESOURCE_BLOCKED` blocks.

## 1. `local_agent/motion_transfer_masks.py` (new, LF; PIL only)

- `load_pose_frames` / `frame_people`: parses controlnet_aux's POSE_KEYPOINT
  JSON (OpenPose body-18, `[x, y, c]` triples, pixel or normalised — both
  handled), drops skeletons under 15 % of the canvas height (the framed
  photo on the nightstand that DWPose read as a person, doc §6).
- `select_person(people, {"by": largest|leftmost|rightmost|index|nearest})`.
- `track_person`: nearest body centre frame to frame within 25 % of the
  canvas diagonal; a frame with no match carries the previous person and is
  counted as `carried`.
- `body_mask`: padded keypoint box (12 %) plus a head disc sized from the
  shoulder width, drawn at the render size (scaled from the DWPose canvas).
- `face_rule`: `{"mode": "ordered", "target": "x1"|"y1"|"area", "order":
  bool, "take_count": 1}` when the character's head is unambiguously the
  leftmost/rightmost/topmost/bottommost head (5 % margin) in every frame it
  shares with someone, `area`/descending when alone, else
  `{"mode": "union_mask"}`.
- `prepare(pose_json, out_dir, size=, selector=)`: writes `mask_00001.png…`
  directly in `out_dir` (so `VHS_LoadImagesPath` over it loads exactly the
  frame masks) and `union/union_mask.png`, returns a manifest record with
  sha256s, counts, people per frame and the face rule.

`2026-09-26g`. Id claimed once with `scripts/next_changelog_id.py`. Benign

reference copy in the owned input dir). Nothing downloaded or installed.

## 1. New files

- **`local_agent/motion_transfer_render.py`** (LF). Contents:
  - `prepare_request` validates a call (attestation, inputs, prompt, fps
    4–12, start/max seconds, target, frame cap) and probes both files with the

  the ComfyUI venv, CPU only; it refuses unless `buffalo_l` is on disk.

  - `faces`: faces per sampled frame.

## 2. What a job does

The graph is the 25t–26g recommended configuration:
- **Pose:** DWPose body + hands with face keypoints off, xinsir sticks;
  union-promax openpose through `ACN_AdvancedControlNetApply_v2`.
- **Motion model:** AnimateDiff `mm_sdxl_v10_beta`, 16/4 pyramid context,
  RealVisXL, 20 steps, cfg 6, 768×448.
- **Identity, main pass:** IP-Adapter PLUS FACE 0.8 on the automatic face
  crop, with an attention mask over the target's band when more than one
  person is present.
- **Identity, detail pass:** Impact video face-detail (denoise 0.5) on the
  target face (by left-to-right rank, or the largest face for one person)
  through FaceID Plus V2 (loader on the AnimateDiff model, detail pass only).
  PLUS FACE is used when the still has no detectable face or FaceID is absent.

Target analysis samples 8 reference frames (ffmpeg), detects faces, picks
`target` and follows it by nearest centre. The band is the median Voronoi
interval (at least 25% wide), mapped through the centre crop to output
pixels.

Order of operations:
1. Claim the shared image-render owner (`_write_owner`, which refuses a live
   owner) **before** the CPU analysis, so a still render cannot slip in.
2. Analyse the inputs.
3. `preflight_execute` (Equal Shares owner, port 8188, thermal wait).
4. Owned backend, 900 s start limit.
5. Validate the graph against live `object_info`; post.
6. Wait (timeout 1800 s + 60 s per frame; the thermal ceiling is checked
   throughout) while a passive nvidia-smi sampler records peak memory and
   temperature.
7. Collect outputs with sha256 and ffprobe.
8. `verified_outputs` is true only if source = pose = generated (= detailed)
   = planned frames and the final mp4's `nb_frames` equals the plan.
9. Always stop the backend and release the owner.
10. On CPU: the identity score.
11. Write `manifest.json` ("acceptance: not accepted …").

## Limits / not done

- At most **64 frames per job** until a longer run is measured. Sections
  rendered separately do not share a scene.
- Portrait 448×768 is unmeasured. Output is 8 fps with no audio or
  interpolation.
- Faces in pictures inflate the people count. People crossing paths can
  break the band or rank.
- Late-window identity drift; untargeted people are not controlled.
- No GVD VRAM profile or promotion (the router still reports
  `motion_reference` blocked), and the seed row stays disabled. Wan approaches
  not built.
- Content rule: the tool requires `likeness_attestation: true` and records it.
  It cannot verify it; the operator is responsible for inputs.

**This folder exists because things got lost in translation between the operator,
ChatGPT/Codex, and Claude, and a whole render pass was wasted.**

## The rule

> **Any agent that changes anything in this project writes an entry here in the
> same session it makes the change.** Not a summary afterwards. Not "I updated
> the docs." An entry, with the evidence.

An entry is only complete if it answers all five:

1. **What changed** â€” exact file and function or key
2. **Why** â€” the observed problem, not the theory
3. **The evidence** â€” a measurement, a diff, an extracted graph. Not a belief.
4. **What was verified after** â€” the command run and its output
5. **What is still unverified** â€” say it plainly

## What does NOT count as verification

- "the config and the docs agree"
- "the script reports no drift"
- "I regenerated the prompts and they look right"

**These all passed on 2026-08-16 while the renderer was sending a corrupted
prompt to every clip.** Document consistency proves nothing about what H3
receives.

## What DOES count

- the workflow extracted from a real render's PNG or MP4, diffed against
  `docs/GOLDEN_REFERENCE/PROVEN_GOOD_AUDIO_GRAPH.api.json`
- a measurement from `work/validate_audio_take.py` or `work/speech_density.py`
- the operator's ear

## Job 3 — the soundtrack pass

All 124 clips at **0.2 MP**, ref2va, non-Turbo, 20 steps, `res_multistep` /
`simple`, denoise 1.0, 24 fps, 8-bit, one clean backend per clip, **using the
shortened `frames` from the config**.

### Why the length matters more than anything else

**Length is the retry knob, not the seed.** The number of words is fixed by the
script and the window is fixed by the frame count, so the speech rate the model
must hit is words ÷ duration — and the seed cannot change it. When that rate is
unspeakable H3 does not slow down; it slurs, mispronounces, or invents syllables
to fill the bar. Re-rolling buys a different flavour of the same fault. Moving
one second changes the rate by about 10%.

Hence the operator's ladder: **base, +1, −1, +2, −2, +3, −3**, seed held fixed.

```
python work\duration_ladder.py --clip 00B      # that clip's rungs, in order
```

Correction you must not undo: this file used to say *"H3 fills whatever window it
is given with speech."* **That is false.** `4_`.mp4` in the good-audio set is 56%
silence and is clean. The `00B` failures had a corrupt prepended header as well
as a long duration, and the duration got the blame. Fitting the render to the
line is still right — it is cheaper and removes a variable — but it is a
precaution, not the cause of gibberish.

```
SOUNDTRACK   short   audio_pass_durations.json    00B  345 frames  14.38 s
PICTURE      full    story_config.json            00B  362 frames  15.00 s
ASSEMBLY     pad     +0.63 s digital silence    = 15.00 s
```

**Never write a shortened length into `story_config.json`.** Picture keeps the
film's pacing.

### Accepting a take — mechanically, then queue for ears

You cannot hear. Do not pretend to, and do not stall waiting for me.

```
python work\validate_audio_take.py <take.mp4> --clip <ID>
```

It measures three things and returns exit code 1 on a fault:

- **WRONG_LENGTH** — rendered longer than the config allows. If this take was a
  deliberate ladder retry, re-run the check with `--configured-seconds <its
  render_seconds>`; the checker is wrong, not the take. Otherwise the renderer
  used a stale frame count — re-render at the configured length. **Never re-roll
  the seed for this.**
- **INVENTED** — far more speech than the word count can account for.
- **SILENCE** — too little speech to be the line.

A take with no faults is **plausible, not accepted**. Record it
`pending_ear_review` in `audio_pass_manifest.json` and **move to the next clip**.
Whether the words are right, whether the voice matches, and whether a second
quieter vocal sits underneath are things only I can judge, and I will do it in
batches afterwards. **The audio gate reaching 124/124 accepted is my job, not
yours. Yours is 124/124 rendered and mechanically plausible.**

The speech recogniser cannot decode H3's synthetic voice. **An empty transcript
means unknown, never perfect.** Never mark anything on a transcript alone.

what is next. No log dumps, no questions.

## North star

This is a parity roadmap for a **local ChatGPT Desktop equivalent**. Equal Shares

assistant behavior and desktop UX take priority; project actions are added as
guarded tools without weakening evidence, render-queue or thermal protections.

## Why this order

Prompt 1 matters more than the model swap. The agent currently asks the model to
emit `TOOL: name {json}` on a line by itself and parses it with a regex. That is
why a model can silently "forget" to use a tool and answer from memory — the
exact failure you saw with `qwen3:8b`. Ollama supports structured function
calling; models trained for it comply far more reliably than any amount of
prompt nagging.

Prompt 4 is the trick that makes the internet wait bearable: every sensory tool
gets **built, tested and registered now**, returning a clear "model not installed"
message. When the downloads land, nothing needs rewiring — the tools start
working.

## Downloads for prompt 5, so you can plan

```

nomic-embed-text       ~275 MB   retrieval over the docs

```

Roughly **21 GB total.** Nothing before prompt 5 needs any of it.

## Where this is heading

`local_agent/ROADMAP.md` records the end goal: a **Reticulum mesh** linking phone
and workstation, so the same agent is reachable from an Android client with file
access — the phone as a thin terminal, all compute staying on the RTX 5080.

**Prompts 6a and 6 are the interim steps**, and 6a comes first for a reason:
`adb reverse` over a USB cable forwards the phone's own localhost to the
workstation's, so the server keeps binding `127.0.0.1` and nothing is exposed to
any network. It proves the entire mobile client — UI, streaming, auth, permission
tier — with the transport reduced to a physical cable. Prompt 6 then swaps the
cable for Tailscale.

`06b` is what makes it an *assistant on the phone* rather than a web page: a
Progressive Web App with a home-screen icon, Android share-sheet integration,
camera capture and voice. No Android development and no downloads.

**One dependency to know about:** PWA features need a secure context. Over 06a's
USB link the phone sees `http://127.0.0.1`, which qualifies — so build and test
06b there. Over Tailscale, `http://100.x.x.x` does **not** qualify, and 06 will
need `tailscale cert` / `tailscale serve` for real HTTPS before the installed app
works remotely.

All three build the same seam the mesh needs: **one predicate that decides whether
a session is remote.** USB answers it by token, Tailscale by source address,
Reticulum by cryptographic identity. Three transports, one function.

That end state is not built in these prompts, but it constrains them. Two rules to
preserve throughout: the HTTP server stays bound to **127.0.0.1**, and
`agent.answer()` stays **transport-agnostic** — it is the seam the mesh plugs
into. Read the roadmap before making an architectural decision.

chunks.heading: # Upgrade 1 — native function calling. No internet needed.
chunks.text:
# Upgrade 1 — native function calling. No internet needed.

Paste everything below the line into Claude Code.

---

Replace the local agent's hand-rolled text tool protocol with **Ollama's native
function calling**. No downloads. Work straight through; do not stop to check in.

```
A:\Users\rhine\Documents\Codex\2026-08-07\referenced-chatgpt-conversation-this-is-an-2\COMFYUI_STORY_HANDOFF_2026-08-09
```

Read `local_agent/README.md` and `local_agent/agent.py` first.

## The problem

`agent.py` asks the model to emit `TOOL: name {json}` on a line of its own and
parses it with `TOOL_RE`. That is fragile by construction:

- a model that ignores the convention silently answers from memory instead —
  observed with `qwen3:8b`, and the reason the current prompt is full of shouty
  `NEVER answer from memory` rules
- only **one** tool per hop, so multi-step questions burn the whole hop budget
- malformed JSON degrades to `{}` and the tool runs with no arguments
- the protocol string eats context in every single request

Ollama's `/api/chat` accepts a `tools` array of JSON schemas and returns
structured `message.tool_calls`. Models trained for it comply far more reliably
than prompt instructions can achieve.

## Job 1 — schemas in `tools.py`

Every entry in `TOOLS` currently carries a human description string. Add a proper
**JSON Schema** for each of the 14: parameter names, types, which are required,
and enums where the value set is fixed (`run_build.action`, `propose_gpu.action`,
`read_doc.name`).

Keep the existing description text — it becomes the schema's `description`.

Add `tools.schemas()` returning the OpenAI-style array Ollama expects:

```python
[{"type": "function", "function": {"name": ..., "description": ...,
  "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {...}, "required": [...]}}}]
```

**Do not change what any tool does, and do not relax any guard.** The clip-id
regex, the doc whitelist, the build-action whitelist and the protected-file check
in `write_file` all stay exactly as they are. A JSON schema is a hint to the
model, never a substitute for validation.

## Job 2 — native calls in `ollama_client.py`

Add `tools=` to `chat()` and `chat_stream()`, passed through to the request body.

Streaming plus tool calls needs care: Ollama emits tool calls in the message
object, sometimes with no content tokens at all. Make sure a turn that is purely
a tool call does not render as an empty reply.

chunks.text:

## Job 2 — native calls in `ollama_client.py`

Add `tools=` to `chat()` and `chat_stream()`, passed through to the request body.

Streaming plus tool calls needs care: Ollama emits tool calls in the message
object, sometimes with no content tokens at all. Make sure a turn that is purely

## Job 3 — rewrite the loop in `agent.py`

- Pass `tools.schemas()` on every request.
- Read `message.tool_calls` instead of regex-parsing the text.
- **Support multiple tool calls per turn.** Run them all, append one
  `{"role": "tool", "name": ..., "content": ...}` message per result, and
  continue. This is the main capability gain — "compare 00B and 27E" becomes one
  hop instead of two.
- Raise `MAX_TOOL_HOPS` to 6 now that hops are not wasted one-per-tool.
- **Keep a fallback.** If a model returns no `tool_calls` but its text matches
  the old `TOOL:` pattern, honour it. Some models will not support the native
  path and must still work. Log which path was used.
- Delete the now-redundant nagging from `CONVERSATION_RULES` — the whole
  "NEVER answer from memory / NEVER describe what a tool would return" block
  exists only because the text protocol was unreliable. Keep the short version:
  prefer tools for state, counts, clips and files. Reclaimed context is the point.

## Job 4 — the GUI keeps working

`server.py` streams `tool` and `tool_result` events and `static/index.html`
renders them as action cards. Preserve that. With several calls in one turn,
emit one card per call.

## Verify — all of it, no shortcuts

```powershell
python local_agent\tools.py
python -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'local_agent');import tools,json;print(json.dumps(tools.schemas(),indent=2)[:1500])"
```

- [ ] all 14 tools have a valid schema; every enum matches the real whitelist
- [ ] a live question through the GUI produces a real `tool_calls` response
- [ ] a two-part question ("compare the ladders for 00B and 00A") triggers **two
      tool calls in one turn** and both results reach the answer
- [ ] the legacy `TOOL:` fallback still fires for a model that does not support
      native calling — test by stubbing a reply
- [ ] **the guard rails still refuse**: unknown tool, clip id `../etc`, doc name
      `/etc/passwd`, build action `rm -rf /`, and `write_file` onto a protected
      manifest
- [ ] Stop, Regenerate, attachments and persistence all still work
- [ ] `python local_agent\validate_h3_prompt.py --dir outputs\equal_shares\prompts_native_r2v`
      still reports **124/124 valid**

Then measure and report: how many tokens the system prompt lost, and whether the
model called tools on questions where it previously answered from memory. Give
the numbers.

## Do not stop

A failing test is a task, not a stopping point. Stop only when every box above is
ticked and you have written the `CHANGELOG/` entry.

chunks.heading: # Claude Code prompt — retrieval over the whole doc tree (refreshed 2026-08-23)
chunks.text:
# Claude Code prompt — retrieval over the whole doc tree (refreshed 2026-08-23)

Paste into your coding agent. Run from the repo root
(`COMFYUI_STORY_HANDOFF_2026-08-09/`). Read `local_agent/README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`,
`local_agent/agent.py`, and `local_agent/router.py` first.

## What this is (and what already changed since the original 02)

The original upgrade 2 had two halves. **Half one — raising `num_ctx` — is already
done** and must NOT be redone: the adaptive reasoning pair now sets context
per-model in `router.Decision.options()` (primary 14B → 20480, fallback 8B → 32768)
with predictive routing at ~16K tokens. **Do not blanket-edit `GPU_OPTIONS`
num_ctx** — that would fight the adaptive logic.

This prompt is the **half that was never built: retrieval.** Today the agent only
knows `knowledge/SYSTEM_PROMPT.md`, a compiled ~9.5 KB digest of a ~200 KB tree.
Ask about a specific CHANGELOG measurement or a paragraph of `H3_PROMPT_RULES.md`
and it either reads a whole file or guesses. Give it lexical search over the tree.

## Job 1 — a retrieval index, no model required

New file `local_agent/retrieval.py`. Index, chunked to ~800 tokens with ~100-token
overlap, chunk boundaries on headings where possible:

    docs/**/*.md      CLAUDE.md      README.md
    CHANGELOG/*.md    START_*.md     FINISH_LOCAL_AGENT.md
    local_agent/UPGRADE/*.md
    outputs/equal_shares/runtime/agent_questions.md

**Skip** `archive/`, `_QUARANTINE_*`, `*.BACKUP*`, and anything bannered SUPERSEDED
— those are deliberately not current and must never be retrieved as fact.

- **Scoring: BM25 in plain Python** (~40 lines). No `rank_bm25`, no `sklearn`,
  nothing to install — offline forever.
- Make the scorer swappable: `score(query, chunks)` behind a small interface with
  `LexicalScorer` as default, so upgrade 5's `EmbeddingScorer` drops in later
  without touching callers.
- Persist the index as JSON next to the code, keyed by each file's mtime + size;
  rebuild only changed files. Startup stays under a second.

## Job 2 — expose it as a tool

Add `search_docs` to `tools.py` (registry + schema), `{"query": "...",
"max_results": 5}`, returning the top chunks each with its **source file and
heading** so the agent can cite where a claim came from — a claim without a source
is not evidence in this project. It is a read-only tool; it never writes.

Update `CONVERSATION_RULES` in `agent.py`: for any question about a rule, a
decision, why something is the way it is, or project history — **search the docs
first**; `read_doc` stays for reading a whole named file.

## Job 3 — shrink the compiled brief

Now that retrieval exists, `build_knowledge_pack.py` should compile a **smaller**

## Job 4 — a context-trim guard that respects the adaptive window

Add a guard: if a request's estimated tokens would exceed the **effective** window
for the chosen model (use `router.Decision.options()["num_ctx"]` /
`router.estimate_context_tokens`, which already exist), trim the **oldest**
conversation turns — never the system prompt, never the current turn — and emit a
`note` event when trimming happens. This complements the predictive 14B→8B switch;
it does not replace it.

- Index builds over the real tree — report file count, chunk count, index size.
- Touching one file re-indexes only that file.
- `search_docs "why was the pace corrected to 2.5"` returns the 2026-08-17b
  CHANGELOG chunk in the top 3; `search_docs "duration ladder"` returns the right
  `H3_PROMPT_RULES` section.
- Archived / superseded docs never appear in results (add a test asserting this).
- `test_native_tool_calling.py` still green; `search_docs` schema registered.
- Brief is under 6 KB.
- `validate_h3_prompt.py` still **124/124**.

chunks.heading: # Upgrade 6 — reach the agent from your phone over cellular. Before the mesh.
chunks.text:
# Upgrade 6 — reach the agent from your phone over cellular. Before the mesh.

Paste everything below the line into Claude Code. Run **after** upgrade 3.

Needs internet **once**, to install Tailscale. After that it works on cellular.

---

Make the local agent reachable from the operator's phone over the cellular
network, as an interim step before the Reticulum mesh in `local_agent/ROADMAP.md`.

```
A:\Users\rhine\Documents\Codex\2026-08-07\referenced-chatgpt-conversation-this-is-an-2\COMFYUI_STORY_HANDOFF_2026-08-09
```

## Read this before writing any code

**The agent currently has NO authentication.** None. Zero. Its entire security
model is the single line binding it to `127.0.0.1` — the assumption that only a
process on this machine can reach it.

That assumption is about to be removed. And this agent can:

- write files anywhere not on the protected list
- run build actions that regenerate project state
- read any file on the machine
- (if upgrade 3 added it) execute Python

So **transport alone is not enough.** Even on a private network, the app itself
needs authentication. A phone left on a table is now a key to the workstation.
Both layers, or neither.

## Job 1 — the transport: Tailscale, not port forwarding

**Do not port-forward. Do not use ngrok or a public tunnel.**

Cellular carriers put phones behind CGNAT, so nothing can connect *in* to the
phone, and many home ISPs now do the same. Tailscale solves this: it is a
WireGuard mesh with NAT traversal and a relay fallback, so both devices dial out
and meet in the middle. Traffic is end-to-end encrypted between devices.

The free Personal plan covers this comfortably — as of August 2026 it allows six
users and **unlimited user devices**, with no expiry.

Install on the workstation and on the phone, sign both into the same tailnet.
Verify the phone can ping the workstation's `100.x.x.x` address over cellular
with Wi-Fi **off** — that is the actual test, not Wi-Fi.

**Alternatives, if a third-party coordination server is unacceptable:**
`headscale` is a self-hosted control plane but needs a VPS with a public IP;
plain WireGuard is free and fully self-hosted but requires a reachable endpoint
at home, which CGNAT may prevent. Tailscale is the pragmatic choice here.
Record which was chosen and why.

chunks.text:

## Job 2 — bind to the tailnet interface only, never 0.0.0.0

This is the important line of code.

`server.py` currently binds `127.0.0.1`. Change it to bind **the Tailscale
interface address specifically** — not `0.0.0.0`.

The difference matters: `0.0.0.0` exposes the agent on every network the machine
joins, including hotel Wi-Fi and coffee shops. Binding the tailnet IP exposes it
only on the encrypted overlay, which no other network can route to.

Implement as `--bind` with a default of `127.0.0.1`, plus `--tailscale` which
discovers the tailnet address and binds that **in addition to** loopback. If the
address cannot be found, **fail loudly and stay on loopback** — never silently
fall back to a wider bind.

Update `ROADMAP.md`: the "never bind 0.0.0.0" rule stands unchanged; this is a
narrower exception, not a repeal.

## Job 3 — real authentication on the app

Add a token layer to `server.py`:

- a long random token generated on first run, stored in
  `local_agent/remote_token.txt` with a note that it is a secret
- every `/api/*` request requires it, via `Authorization: Bearer` header or a
  cookie set once from a `?token=` URL
- **loopback requests are exempt** so the desktop experience is unchanged
- constant-time comparison; never log the token
- a `--rotate-token` flag

Also add basic rate limiting on `/api/send` — a phone reconnecting in a loop
should not be able to queue fifty generations.

## Job 4 — remote gets fewer powers than the desk

A request arriving over the tailnet is not the same as one from the keyboard.
Add a permission tier keyed on whether the connection is loopback:

| | desktop (loopback) | remote (tailnet) |
|---|---|---|
| read tools — `project_state`, `clip_info`, `read_prompt`, `duration_ladder`, `search_docs`, `read_file`, `list_dir` | yes | **yes** |
| `run_build` — regenerates derived files | yes | **no by default** |
| `write_file` | yes | **no by default** |
| `run_python` if it exists | yes | **no** |
| `propose_gpu` — proposes only, starts nothing | yes | yes |

Make it configurable in one obvious place, defaulting to the table above. The
operator can widen it deliberately; it must not be wide by accident.

This is also the groundwork for Reticulum, where permissions will key on
cryptographic identity instead of loopback. Structure it so that swap is easy.

## Job 5 — make the UI usable on a phone

`static/index.html` is a fixed desktop layout with a 262 px sidebar. On a phone
it will be unusable.

- responsive breakpoint: below ~700 px the sidebar becomes a slide-over drawer
- touch targets at least 44 px
- the composer must not be hidden by the on-screen keyboard
- `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">`
- show a clear **REMOTE** indicator with the reduced permission set, so it is
  never ambiguous which mode you are in
- assume a slow, flaky link: if the SSE stream drops mid-generation, reconnect
  and recover the reply rather than losing it. The conversation is already
  persisted server-side, so the answer survives — make the client re-read it.

The agent cannot answer if the machine is asleep. Document, do not automate:

- how to disable sleep while allowing the monitor to turn off
- Wake-on-LAN over the tailnet if the operator wants it
- what happens if a render is mid-flight — the router already sends replies to
  CPU, so remote use during a render is fine and expected

- [ ] the server binds the tailnet address and loopback, and **not** `0.0.0.0` —

## Why this approach is better than it sounds

`adb reverse tcp:8760 tcp:8760` makes a port on the **phone's own localhost**
forward, over the USB cable, to the **workstation's localhost**.

From the phone's browser, `http://127.0.0.1:8760` *is* the workstation's agent.

That has a property nothing else does: **the server keeps binding `127.0.0.1`
and nothing changes.** No `0.0.0.0`, no tailnet address, no firewall rule, no
network exposure of any kind. The transport is a physical cable. `ROADMAP.md`'s
"never bind 0.0.0.0" rule is not bent — it is not even touched.

It also needs no internet, no account, and no coordination server, which suits an
operator currently on a hotspot.

## What this DOES prove

Everything except the network:

- the UI on a real phone screen, with a real on-screen keyboard
- SSE streaming into a mobile browser
- the token layer
- the remote-vs-desktop permission tier
- conversations shared between phone and desktop
- reconnect behaviour when the stream drops

## What it does NOT prove

Be honest about this in the CHANGELOG — do not let it be mistaken for a
completed 06:

- NAT traversal and CGNAT, the actual hard part of remote access
- real latency and packet loss over cellular
- behaviour when the link drops for minutes rather than seconds
- whether the workstation is reachable at all when the operator is out

## Job 1 — the cable path

Install Android platform-tools on the workstation (~10 MB — state the exact size
before downloading). Then:

1. Phone: Settings → About → tap Build Number seven times → Developer Options →
   **USB debugging on**
2. Connect by cable, accept the RSA fingerprint prompt on the phone
3. `adb devices` — the device must show as `device`, not `unauthorized`
4. `adb reverse tcp:8760 tcp:8760`
5. Phone browser → `http://127.0.0.1:8760`

Write `local_agent/START_PHONE_USB.ps1` doing all of it: check adb is present,
wait for a device, set up the reverse, start the server if it is not running,
print the URL, and tell the operator plainly what to do if the device shows
`unauthorized` or `offline` — those two are the failures they will actually hit.

`adb reverse` does not survive unplugging. Have the script re-establish it if the
device reconnects.

## Job 2 — the parts that are NOT transport

These are the real work, and they are identical whether the bytes arrive over USB
or Tailscale. Do them now, so 06 becomes almost nothing.

**Authentication.** The agent has none today; its whole security model is the
loopback bind. Over `adb reverse` the requests *arrive* as loopback, so an exempt-
loopback rule would exempt the phone too. So:

- generate a token into `local_agent/remote_token.txt` on first run
- treat a request as **remote** if it carries the token, or if a
  `X-Client: phone` header is set by the phone UI — not merely by source address
- desktop browser on the same machine stays token-free
- constant-time comparison, never logged, `--rotate-token` provided

**Permission tier.** A remote session gets fewer powers, same table as 06:

| | desktop | remote |
|---|---|---|
| reads — `project_state`, `clip_info`, `read_prompt`, `duration_ladder`, `search_docs`, `read_file`, `list_dir` | yes | **yes** |
| `run_build` | yes | **no by default** |
| `write_file` | yes | **no by default** |
| `run_python` if present | yes | **no** |
| `propose_gpu` — proposes only | yes | yes |

Configurable in one obvious place. Wide only on purpose, never by accident.

**Mobile UI.** `static/index.html` is a fixed desktop layout with a 262 px
sidebar; on a phone it is unusable.

- responsive breakpoint below ~700 px — sidebar becomes a slide-over drawer
- touch targets ≥ 44 px
- the composer must stay visible above the on-screen keyboard
- `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">`
- a clear **REMOTE** badge showing the reduced permissions
- if the SSE stream drops, reconnect and re-read the conversation rather than
  losing the reply — it is already persisted server-side

## Job 3 — leave 06 a short walk

Structure the permission check so the "is this remote" decision is **one
function**. USB answers it by header/token; Tailscale will answer it by source
address; Reticulum will answer it by cryptographic identity. Three transports,
one predicate, changed in one place.

Note in the CHANGELOG that this is the seam.

chunks.heading: # Upgrade 6b — make it a real phone app. Run after 06a.
chunks.text:
# Upgrade 6b — make it a real phone app. Run after 06a.

Paste everything below the line into Claude Code. **No downloads.**

---

Turn the mobile web page from 06a into something that behaves like the ChatGPT
app: installed on the home screen, able to take files from the phone, able to use
the camera and voice. **No Android development, no app store, no downloads** —
this is a Progressive Web App, which Android treats as a real installed app.

```
A:\Users\rhine\Documents\Codex\2026-08-07\referenced-chatgpt-conversation-this-is-an-2\COMFYUI_STORY_HANDOFF_2026-08-09
```

## Read this first — the constraint that shapes everything

**A browser cannot browse the phone's filesystem.** Android does not permit it,
and no amount of web code changes that. What a browser *can* do is receive files
the operator hands it: through a file picker, through the camera, or through the
Android share sheet.

So "file access on the phone" here means **push, not pull.** The operator shares
or picks a file and it goes to the workstation as an attachment. The agent cannot
go looking through the phone on its own.

Genuine filesystem access needs the native Android app in `ROADMAP.md`. Say so
plainly in the CHANGELOG rather than letting this be mistaken for it. What is
below covers most of what the ChatGPT app actually gets used for.

## The HTTPS catch — read before you start

PWA features (installability, service worker, share target) require a **secure
context**: `https://`, or `http://` on `localhost` / `127.0.0.1`.

- **Over 06a's USB `adb reverse`** the phone connects to `http://127.0.0.1:8760`,
  which **counts as secure**. Everything in this prompt works.
- **Over 06's Tailscale** the address is `http://100.x.x.x`, which does **not**
  count. Service workers and install will be blocked.

The fix for that case is Tailscale's own HTTPS — `tailscale cert` / `tailscale
serve` issues a real certificate for the machine's `*.ts.net` name. Note this in
06 as a dependency, but **build and test everything here over USB first**, where
it just works.

## Job 1 — installable app

Add `local_agent/static/manifest.webmanifest`:

- `name`, `short_name`, `start_url`, `display: "standalone"` so it opens without
  browser chrome
- `theme_color` and `background_color` matching the existing dark palette
- icons at 192 and 512 px, **generated as plain SVG/PNG in the repo** — no
  external asset, nothing fetched

Add a service worker that caches the app shell — HTML, CSS, the icons — so it
opens instantly and shows a clear "workstation unreachable" screen instead of a
browser error when the cable is out or the machine is asleep.

**Never cache API responses.** Conversation state lives on the workstation and
must never be served stale from a phone cache.

Verify Chrome on Android offers "Install app" / "Add to Home screen", and that
launching from the icon opens standalone.

- **images go to the vision tool**, once a model exists (upgrade 4 built the

original name preserved, and pass the **path** to the tools. Do not put binary
into the conversation JSON — store the path and a description.

This is the feature that makes it feel like an app rather than a bookmark.

Add `share_target` to the manifest so the agent appears in Android's share menu.
Then, from any app on the phone — gallery, browser, file manager — the operator
can share a photo, a link or text straight into a conversation.

Add a `POST /api/share` endpoint that receives it, creates or appends to a
conversation, and opens the app on that conversation.

Test all three: shared text, a shared URL, and a shared image.

## Job 4 — camera and voice

**Camera** — an input with `accept="image/*" capture="environment"` opens the
camera directly. One tap, photo, straight into the conversation. That is how a
frame gets from the real world to the vision tool.

**Voice** — record on the phone with `MediaRecorder`, upload the audio, and
transcribe it **on the workstation with whisper**. Do not use the Web Speech API:
it usually sends audio to a cloud service, which defeats the point of this whole
project. Whisper is already on the upgrade-5 download list and runs locally.

Until whisper is installed, the record button must say what is missing and its
size — same honesty rule as upgrade 4. Do not hide the button; a disabled control
that explains itself is better than a missing feature.

- **notify on completion** — a long generation started on the phone should raise

- **keep the screen awake during generation** via the Wake Lock API, released

- **safe-area insets** so the composer clears the home indicator and notch

Everything above is additive. The desktop browser experience must not change: no
install prompt nagging, no service worker interfering with development, no layout
shift. Verify by using it on the desktop after the changes.

      conversation JSON
- [ ] the **desktop** experience is unchanged

chunks.heading: # Upgrade 7 — point it at folders, get renders. The automated ComfyUI maker.
chunks.text:
# Upgrade 7 — point it at folders, get renders. The automated ComfyUI maker.

Paste everything below the line into Claude Code. **No downloads.**

---

Build a **generic batch renderer**: the operator points the agent at a job folder
of prompts and reference assets, and it renders the whole sequence through
MiniMax H3 unattended.

```
A:\Users\rhine\Documents\Codex\2026-08-07\referenced-chatgpt-conversation-this-is-an-2\COMFYUI_STORY_HANDOFF_2026-08-09
```

This is **not** Equal Shares. It must never read or write
`outputs/equal_shares/**` state — no touching `audio_pass_manifest.json`,
`story_config.json`, or `voice_requirements.json`. It is a second, general
pipeline that happens to reuse the same proven render infrastructure.

## Read first

- `docs/reference/MINIMAX_PROMPT_GUIDE_ref.md` §2.1–2.5 and §4.1 — the reference
  label and marker rules. **Quoted below where they matter; verify them.**
- `docs/GOLDEN_REFERENCE/PROVEN_FACTS.md` §1 — the settings that must not change
- `work/render_single_pass.py` — `build_ref2va_workflow`, `build_fl2va_workflow`,
  `start_comfy`, `stop_comfy`, `submit_workflow`, `wait_for_completion`. **Reuse
  these. Do not rewrite the render path.**
- `work/thermal_guard.py`, `work/duration_ladder.py`

## THE MOST IMPORTANT THING IN THIS DOCUMENT

**Socket numbers are zero-based. Prompt tags are one-based.** They are not the
same number and confusing them is the single most likely way this ships broken.

| Operator's name | ComfyUI socket | Prompt tag | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| img 0 | `ref_images.ref_image_0` | **`<Picture 1>`** | character reference |
| img 1 | `ref_images.ref_image_1` | **`<Picture 2>`** | setting — stays the same |
| img 2 | `ref_images.ref_image_2` | **`<Picture 3>`** | second character, when present |
| video ref | first video socket | **`<Video 1>`** | motion only |

Tags follow **connection order**, so if a slot is empty the later tags shift down.
Three images wired means `<Picture 1>`, `<Picture 2>`, `<Picture 3>`. Two images
wired means `<Picture 1>` and `<Picture 2>` — never `<Picture 3>`.

This project already has a scar from exactly this class of bug: a prompt declared
`<Audio 2>` while the reference was wired into `ref_audio_0`, so every voice in
the clip was mis-attributed. Four clips were affected. See
`CHANGELOG/2026-08-18c_one_off_speaker_rule.md`.

**Also: the operator's existing hand-made renders used `<Video 0>`.** That is
non-conforming — the guide is one-based throughout. A tag of `<Video 0>` likely
bound to nothing, which would explain why those prompts needed heavy prose to
compensate. Emit `<Video 1>`.

**Also: the operator's existing hand-made renders used `<Video 0>`.** That is

## Job 1 — verify the video socket before building anything

**Do not assume `MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo` accepts a video reference.** The
project's 15 proven-good graphs use image and audio references only; a video
reference socket has never been exercised here.

Establish the truth, in this order:

1. Query the running ComfyUI at `/object_info` for the node's real input schema
2. If a video socket exists, record its exact name
3. If it does not, **stop and report that** — the motion-reference feature cannot
   be built on a socket that is not there, and the operator needs to know rather
   than receive something that silently ignores the video

Write what you find into the CHANGELOG. This is the one genuine unknown.

## Job 2 — the job folder layout

The operator points at one folder. Detect this structure:

```
<job>/
  prompts/       0001.txt, 0002.txt, ...      one per render, sorted
  video_refs/    00.mp4, 01.mp4, ...          motion reference per render
  img0/          character reference
  img1/          setting reference
  img2/          second character (optional)
  renders/       created by you — output goes here
```

**Slot filling rule — auto-detect, do not ask:**

- a slot folder holding **one** file → that file is used for **every** render
- a slot folder holding **numbered** files → matched **sequentially** to the
  prompt index

So `img1/` with a single `setting.png` stays fixed across the whole batch, while
`img0/` with `00.png, 01.png, …` advances per render. That covers both cases the
operator described without any configuration.

Accept flat layouts too — files named `prompt_001.txt`, `video_001.mp4`,
`img0_001.png` in one folder. Sort **naturally**, so `2` comes before `10`.

**Report the plan before rendering anything.** A dry run that prints, per render:
prompt file, video ref, each image slot, resolved tags, duration, output path.
The operator must be able to see the whole batch is correctly paired before a
single frame is generated. Mismatched counts are reported as a warning with the
pairing shown, not silently truncated.

prompt file, video ref, each image slot, resolved tags, duration, output path.
The operator must be able to see the whole batch is correctly paired before a
single frame is generated. Mismatched counts are reported as a warning with the
pairing shown, not silently truncated.

## Job 3 — the motion-only lock, done properly

The operator's rule: **the video reference supplies motion only. The model must
never copy imagery from it.**

The guide has a canonical construction for exactly this. From §2.1:

```text
<Subject 1> is the woman whose appearance comes from <Picture 1> and whose
walking motion comes from <Video 1>.
```

That is the correct way to say it — appearance sourced from the image, motion
sourced from the video, in the subject definition where the model expects it.

And `retention_analysis` gets the matching marker. From §4.1 the visible-content
markers are `fully_preserved`, `partially_preserved`, `attribute_transfer`,
`weak_reference`, and the guide's own example for a structural video reference is:

```text
<Video 1> (cut and pacing structure): weak_reference - ...
```

So emit, for a motion-only video:

```text
<Video 1> (motion and camera structure only): weak_reference - only the movement,
timing, and camera behaviour are taken from <Video 1>. None of its people,
faces, bodies, clothing, setting, or lighting appear in the target video.
```

Plus the identity line pinning appearance to `<Picture 1>`.

**This is stronger than prose alone** because `retention_analysis` is the section
this project already proved the model actually acts on — adding it is what
removed the doubled voice after weeks of prose failing to.

Build all three pieces automatically: the subject definition, the retention line,
and a short confirming sentence in `detailed_description`. The operator's prompt
files should not have to contain any of it.

## Job 4 — the renderer

New `work/batch_render_folder.py`. Reuse the existing infrastructure; do not
reimplement it.

Non-negotiable, from `PROVEN_FACTS.md` §1:

```
ref2va      minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_nvfp4.safetensors
fl2va       minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors
encoder     qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors
VAEs        minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16 + minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32
sampler     res_multistep / simple, denoise 1.0, 20 steps
fps/depth   24 / 8-bit
frames      congruent to 5 modulo 17
```

Megapixels is a **CLI argument**, defaulting to 0.9 for picture work. Turbo
checkpoints, nodes and LoRAs stay prohibited.

Operational rules, all reusing what exists:

- **one backend per render**, stopped after, `thermal_guard` before and after
- claim `render_queue_owner.json` — never run beside the Equal Shares pass
- resume: skip renders whose output already exists, unless `--force`
- **never overwrite.** Attempt N goes to a new file; nothing is replaced
- per-job manifest inside the job folder, recording for every render: prompt
  file, every reference path, resolved tags, seed, duration, frames, megapixels,
  output path, status
- `--limit N` so the operator can try three before committing to eighty
- on VRAM failure, drop 0.1 MP and record it; floor at 0.4 MP for picture

If a prompt has dialogue, reuse `duration_ladder.py` for retries — same rule,
duration not seed. If it has none, a failed render retries once then reports.

## Job 5 — validate before spending GPU time

Every assembled prompt goes through `local_agent/validate_h3_prompt.py` **before**
it is submitted. A prompt that fails is reported with its faults and **skipped**,
not rendered.

Eighty renders at several minutes each is hours. Catching a malformed prompt
beforehand costs milliseconds.

Note honestly in the CHANGELOG: that validator was written for this project's
six-section dialogue prompts and passes 124/124 of them. Behaviour on
motion-reference prompts is **unproven** — if it produces false positives on
valid batch prompts, fix the validator with a recorded measurement, do not
disable the check.

## Job 6 — expose it to the agent

Two tools in `local_agent/tools.py`:

- **`batch_plan`** — `{"folder": "..."}`. Scans, pairs, resolves tags, validates
  every prompt, returns the plan. **Read-only, renders nothing.**
- **`batch_render`** — proposal only, exactly like `propose_gpu`. Returns the
  command for the operator to approve. **The agent must never start a batch.**

Then the operator can say *"look at D:\jobs\scene12 and tell me if it's ready"*
and get a real answer, followed by a command they run themselves.

## Verify

Build a synthetic job folder with 3 prompts, 3 video refs, a sequential `img0/`,
a single fixed `img1/`, and a two-file `img2/`. Then:

- [ ] pairing is correct and reported before anything renders
- [ ] the fixed slot repeats; the sequential slots advance
- [ ] natural sort puts `2` before `10`
- [ ] tags are **one-based and contiguous**, and match the sockets actually wired
- [ ] a render with only two images emits `<Picture 1>`/`<Picture 2>` and **no**
      `<Picture 3>`
- [ ] the motion lock appears in all three places: subject definition, retention
      line with `weak_reference`, and detailed description
- [ ] mismatched counts warn and show the pairing rather than truncating silently
- [ ] an invalid prompt is skipped with its faults listed, not rendered
- [ ] `--limit 1` renders exactly one
- [ ] re-running skips completed renders; `--force` redoes them
- [ ] nothing under `outputs/equal_shares/**` is read or written — verify by
      timestamp
- [ ] the queue owner is claimed and released
- [ ] `batch_render` refuses to execute and returns a command instead
- [ ] guard rails still refuse; `validate_h3_prompt.py` still **124/124** on the
      Equal Shares set

## Do not stop

Work through. The one legitimate stop is Job 1 finding that no video reference
socket exists — report that clearly and continue building everything else, with
the motion reference disabled and the reason recorded.

Finish with a `CHANGELOG/` entry: the real socket name you found, the tag mapping
as implemented, and whether the validator needed adjusting for this prompt shape.

chunks.heading: # Claude Code prompt — GUI context ceiling + "Yield GPU" button (refreshed 2026-08-23)
chunks.text:
# Claude Code prompt — GUI context ceiling + "Yield GPU" button (refreshed 2026-08-23)

Paste into your coding agent. Run from the repo root
(`COMFYUI_STORY_HANDOFF_2026-08-09/`). Read `local_agent/README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`,
`local_agent/router.py`, `local_agent/agent.py`, and `local_agent/server.py` first.
**Do not touch the render pipeline, the busy-detection signals, or
`outputs/equal_shares/**`.**

## What changed since the original 08 — read this first

`num_ctx` is no longer a single hard-coded value. The adaptive reasoning pair now
sets it **per model** in `router.Decision.options()`: the 14B primary gets 20480,
the 8B fallback gets 32768, and there is predictive 14B→8B routing at ~16K
estimated tokens. So the GUI control must be a **ceiling that coordinates with**
that logic — never a blanket override that fights it.

## Feature 1 — a GUI context ceiling (num_ctx)

The operator wants to cap how much context the agent uses, live, from the chat
interface, without editing code or restarting.

1. **Control in `local_agent/static/index.html`** — a select of presets
   (`8192 / 16384 / 24576 / 32768`) plus an "Auto" default, labelled "Context
   (tokens)". Persist the choice in `localStorage`, restore on load, show the value
   actually in effect.
2. **Send it each turn** (match how `server.py` already receives `message`/`prefer`).
3. **Apply as a CEILING, after the adaptive value is computed.** Thread the value
   into `agent.answer(...)`. The effective num_ctx for a turn is
   `min(adaptive_value_from_Decision.options(), gui_ceiling)` when the operator set
   one, else the adaptive value unchanged. Never raise num_ctx above what the
   chosen model/tier already allows. "Auto" means: don't cap — use the adaptive
   value as-is.
4. **Clamp** the incoming value to `[4096, 32768]`; a bogus value never crashes a

chunks.heading: # Claude Code prompt — tiered vision load, "GPU Busy" queue, and a GPU watcher
chunks.text:
# Claude Code prompt — tiered vision load, "GPU Busy" queue, and a GPU watcher

> **Source preserved from Google Drive (2026-08-24):**
> [`09_media_gpu_queue.md`](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Z3Wdu3Xcj1AAUdEjSQPepQsy7WKvZKbJ5GoC59KmzQU/edit?usp=drivesdk).

Paste into Claude Code, run from the repo root
(`COMFYUI_STORY_HANDOFF_2026-08-09/`). Self-contained. Read `local_agent/README.md`
and `CLAUDE.md` first — they are binding. Internet **is** available now, so
`ollama pull` is allowed. Do not touch the render pipeline or `outputs/equal_shares/**`.

## The behaviour to build

When the operator asks the agent to look at an image/video or listen to audio, the
sensory model must load on the **GPU**, but the GPU is often occupied by a render.
The required policy, in order:

1. **Primary model, full GPU load.** If the GPU has enough free VRAM to hold the
   primary abliterated Qwen vision model *fully*, load it there and process now.
2. **Smaller model, full GPU load.** If the primary will not fully fit, try a
   smaller vision model that needs less VRAM. If *it* fully fits, use it now.
3. **Queue + "GPU Busy".** If even the smaller model will not fully fit, do **not**
   run it half-offloaded to CPU. Emit **`GPU Busy`** to the GUI and enqueue the
   file(s) in a persistent watch queue, telling the operator it will be processed
   when the GPU frees.
4. **Watcher drains the queue.** A background watcher polls the GPU; the moment
   enough VRAM is free to fully load a model (and no render owns the card), it
   loads the best-fitting model and processes the queued items in order, writing
   results back so the GUI shows them. Then it idles until more work or more VRAM.

This is a deliberate change from today's behaviour in `media_tools._vision`, which
falls back to the **CPU** Ollama server when the GPU is busy. A Qwen-VL model on
four CPU threads is unusably slow, so **remove the CPU fallback for vision** and
replace it with the tiered-GPU + queue policy above. (Whisper transcription stays
CPU-side as it is — see "Audio" below.)

chunks.text:

This is a deliberate change from today's behaviour in `media_tools._vision`, which
falls back to the **CPU** Ollama server when the GPU is busy. A Qwen-VL model on
four CPU threads is unusably slow, so **remove the CPU fallback for vision** and
replace it with the tiered-GPU + queue policy above. (Whisper transcription stays
CPU-side as it is — see "Audio" below.)

## What "fully fits" means — detect it deterministically

Ollama will silently offload layers to system RAM when a model does not fit,
producing a slow "partial" load. Detect fit **before** loading, by free VRAM:

1. Add `router.gpu_free_mb() -> int | None` next to `router.gpu_memory()`, reading
   `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.free --format=csv,noheader,nounits` (same
   subprocess/except pattern; `None` when nvidia-smi is unavailable).
2. Define per-tier VRAM requirements (weights + KV headroom), as named constants,
   e.g. in `capabilities.py`:
   - primary `qwen3-vl-abliterated:8b-q8_0` → ~11500 MB
   - smaller `qwen3-vl-abliterated:4b`      → ~7000 MB
   Add a safety margin constant (e.g. `VRAM_SAFETY_MB = 1024`) on top.
   Tune the numbers with a comment citing the model file sizes (8B Q8_0 = 8.71 GB
   + f16 mmproj 1.16 GB; 4B ≈ 6.1 GB).
3. A tier "fully fits" iff `gpu_free_mb() is not None and free >= need + margin`
   **and** `router.gpu_busy()` reports no render owning the card (queue owner /
   port 8188 / foreign compute process). **Fail safe:** if `gpu_free_mb()` is
   `None` (nvidia-smi missing), treat as *does not fit* → queue. An unknown GPU is
   never permission to load.

## The smaller model

Add the smaller tier to `capabilities.VISION_PREFERENCES` (created in the
2026-08-22 vision-watcher change) so selection stays deterministic. Pull it (net is
allowed):

    ollama pull huihui_ai/qwen3-vl-abliterated:4b

or import a local 4B GGUF if the operator prefers. Give `capabilities.py` a way to
report, per tier, `(model_name, vram_need_mb)` so both `media_tools` and the
watcher choose the same tiers from one source of truth — e.g.
`capabilities.vision_tiers() -> list[dict]` returning the installed, vision-capable
tiers largest-first with their VRAM needs.

## The queue (persistent, stdlib, atomic)

- Store under `local_agent/media_queue/` — `pending/`, `processing/`, `done/`,
  `failed/` subdirs, one JSON job file per item. No database, no deps.
- A job records: `id`, `created` (pass a timestamp in; do not rely on wall-clock
  inside any workflow), `media_type` (`image`|`video`|`audio`), `path`(s),
  `question`, `crop`/frame args, `status`, and on completion `model`, `tier`,
  `result`, or `error`.
- Writes must be atomic (write temp, `os.replace`) so a crash never leaves a
  half-written job. Move the file between dirs to change state.
- A single module `local_agent/media_queue.py` owns enqueue / claim-next / complete
  / fail / list, transport-agnostic (no HTTP knowledge), so the server, the tools,
  and the watcher all use it.

## Where the tiering plugs in

- `media_tools._vision(...)`: replace the CPU-fallback block. Compute the best
  tier that fully fits (via `capabilities.vision_tiers()` + `router.gpu_free_mb()`).
  If one fits, load that model on the GPU and return the analysis as today. If none
  fits, **enqueue** the item(s) and return a structured
  `{"queued": true, "reason": "GPU Busy", "queue_id": ...,
    "position": N}` result — the tool result the model/GUI shows.
- `see_image` / `analyze_video`: unchanged entry points; they still call `_vision`,
  which now either analyses or queues. `analyze_video` already extracts frames
  first — enqueue the extracted frame paths so the watcher needs no ffmpeg re-run.
- **Audio** (`transcribe`): Whisper runs on CPU, so it does not need GPU VRAM. But
  the operator wants audio queued too when the machine is busy. Enqueue audio jobs
  with `media_type:"audio"`; the watcher processes them through the existing CPU
  Whisper path, gated on "no render active and the CPU chat model can be evicted"
  rather than on VRAM. Keep the existing one-CPU-model-at-a-time eviction.

## The watcher

`local_agent/media_watcher.py`, mirroring the project's watchdog conventions:

- Single-instance (own owner/lock file under `local_agent/media_queue/`), bound to
  nothing (no network server); pure local loop. `--once` does one drain pass and
  exits (for tests/cron); default loops every ~15 s.
- Each pass: if `pending/` is empty, idle. Else pick the largest tier that fully
  fits right now (`gpu_free_mb` + not `gpu_busy`); if none fits and there are only
  vision jobs, stay idle and log "waiting for GPU". For each processable job:
  claim → move to `processing/` → run the same code path as the live tool →
  move to `done/` with the result (or `failed/` with the error). Never delete a
  source file.
- It loads the model once and processes as many queued items as fit that window,
  then optionally `router.unload(GPU_HOST, model)` when the queue drains so it does
  not hold VRAM against the next render. Respect the one-owner rule: never load
  while `gpu_busy()` says a render owns the card.
- Start it from `START_LOCAL_AGENT_GUI.ps1` alongside the server (or document a
  separate launch). Log to `local_agent/media_queue/watcher.log`.

## GUI (`server.py` + `static/index.html`)

- New SSE event kind `queued` emitted when `_vision` queues: data
  `{count, reason:"GPU Busy", position}`. In `index.html`'s EventSource switch
  (alongside `route`/`tool`/`note`/`error`/`done`), render a clear inline
  card: **"GPU Busy — N item(s) queued; the agent will watch them once the GPU is
  free."**
- Add `GET /api/media_queue` returning `{pending, processing, done, failed}` counts
  and recent completed results. Add a small queue indicator in the GUI (near the
  existing GPU-status pill that already shows "GPU busy — render has it") that shows
  the pending count and lets the operator see a completed result when the watcher
  finishes. Poll it on the same cadence as the status pill.
- When the watcher completes an item, its result must be retrievable in the GUI via
  `/api/media_queue` (surfacing it into the originating conversation is a bonus, not
  required).

## Constraints (do not violate)

- Standard library only (PIL is already a dep; no new pip deps beyond the Ollama
  model pull). Server stays on `127.0.0.1`.
- `router.gpu_busy()` semantics and the "unknown GPU = busy / does-not-fit"
  fail-safe rule are preserved everywhere.
- One GPU owner ever. The watcher must never load a model while a render owns the
  card. Never delete a raw generation, reference, source media, or evidence.
- `media_queue.py` and `media_watcher.py` stay transport-agnostic; only `server.py`
  knows HTTP.

     `reason:"GPU Busy"` and never calls the CPU host.
