chunks.heading: # Claude Code / Codex prompt — coding mode (Qwen2.5-Coder) + a safe run-and-test sandbox
chunks.text:
# Claude Code / Codex prompt — coding mode (Qwen2.5-Coder) + a safe run-and-test sandbox

Paste into your coding agent. Work in `COMFYUI_STORY_HANDOFF_2026-08-09/local_agent/`.
Read `router.py`, `agent.py`, `tools.py` (esp. `write_candidate_tool`,
`run_safe_check`, `write_file`/`read_file`, the `_TOOLS`/`_SCHEMAS` registry),
`server.py`, `static/index.html`, and `START_LOCAL_AGENT_GUI.ps1` first.
**Constraints:** stdlib only; server on `127.0.0.1`; `tools.py` stays a whitelist;
never start a render/ComfyUI; never touch `outputs/equal_shares/**` or project files
from the sandbox; phone identities stay default-denied for code execution.

## Goal

Make the local agent genuinely useful for writing and **debugging** programs, within
the 16 GB card. Two parts: (1) a **coding mode** that uses a code-specialist model and
a coding system prompt; (2) a **sandboxed run-and-test loop** so the model can execute
code, read the real error, and fix it — the thing that actually makes it debug.

## Part 1 — coding mode

- Add `CODING_MODEL = os.environ.get("EQUAL_SHARES_CODING_MODEL",
  "huihui_ai/qwen2.5-coder-abliterate:14b")` in `router.py`. It is already in the
  GPU/CPU fallback lists; make it explicitly selectable, not just a fallback.
- Ensure it's installed: extend `START_LOCAL_AGENT_GUI.ps1` to optionally ensure the
  coding model on the GPU server (same `Ensure-GpuChatModel` pattern, pulled only by the
  launcher, only if a flag/env asks for it — do not force a ~9 GB pull on every start).
- Expose "coding mode" in the GUI: the model picker already supports model-per-chat, so
  add a clear **Coding mode** choice that (a) selects `CODING_MODEL` and (b) swaps in a
  **coding system prompt** — concise, test-driven, "write the code, then run it in the
  sandbox and fix failures before answering", cite exact errors, no invented APIs, prefer
  stdlib, state assumptions. Keep the general assistant prompt for normal chats.
- Routing unchanged: coding mode still goes through `router` (GPU 14B-coder when the card
  is idle, CPU fallback when a render owns it). A 14B coder on CPU is slow — surface that
  in the UI so the operator knows to free the GPU for heavy coding.

chunks.text:

  stdlib, state assumptions. Keep the general assistant prompt for normal chats.
- Routing unchanged: coding mode still goes through `router` (GPU 14B-coder when the card
  is idle, CPU fallback when a render owns it). A 14B coder on CPU is slow — surface that
  in the UI so the operator knows to free the GPU for heavy coding.

## Part 2 — the sandbox (`run_code` tool)

Add a `run_code` tool to `tools.py` that executes code in an **isolated, bounded**
environment so the agent can iterate:

- **Isolation:** a dedicated dir `local_agent/sandbox/run_<id>/` (created per run). The
  sandbox may read/write only inside its own run dir. It must NOT see the project tree,
  `outputs/`, uploads, or any model/render file. Set the subprocess `cwd` to the run dir.
- **Interpreters:** start with Python (the repo's Python); optionally Node if `node` is on
  PATH. A fixed allowlist of interpreters — never an arbitrary shell string.
- **Bounds:** hard `timeout` (e.g. 30 s default, cap 120 s), capture stdout+stderr+exit
  code, cap captured output size. Kill the process group on timeout. Limit what one run
  can spawn.
- **No network by default:** run with a flag/env that disables network (and document that
  the guarantee is best-effort on Windows). A `allow_network:true` arg exists but is
  off by default and logged.
- **Input:** `{"language":"python","code":"...","stdin":"...","timeout":30}` OR
  `{"language":"python","path":"sandbox/run_x/main.py"}` to run a file the agent wrote
  there with `write_file`. Return `{stdout, stderr, exit_code, timed_out, duration}`.
- **Never** executes anything under the project tree; refuse a `path` outside the sandbox.
  Never runs while a render owns the GPU is NOT required (CPU code execution doesn't need
  the GPU) — but a `run_code` that itself tries to use the GPU is out of scope; keep it CPU.

Then wire the **debug loop** into coding mode's guidance: write file → `run_code` → read
stderr → edit → re-run, with a capped number of iterations per turn so it can't loop
forever. This is the core capability that makes local debugging work.

## Part 3 — keep the existing dev-workspace tools coherent

`write_candidate_tool` (isolated dev workspace, cannot run/replace project code) already
exists. `run_code` complements it: candidate helpers can be *tried* in the sandbox, but
still can never run against or replace project code. Make the boundary explicit in both
tool descriptions. `write_file`/`propose_file_diff` continue to gate protected project
files; the sandbox is the only place code actually executes.

files; the sandbox is the only place code actually executes.

## Security recap (do not weaken)

- The sandbox is the ONLY code-execution surface, and it is walled to its run dir, CPU,
  bounded time/output, network-off by default, no project/outputs/render access.
- `run_code` is **desktop-only** and **default-denied for phone/remote identities** (reuse
  the Sideband per-identity permission gate).
- Never delete project evidence; sandbox run dirs may be cleaned on a size/age policy, but
  nothing outside `local_agent/sandbox/` is ever touched.

## Verify (show commands + output)

- `python local_agent/test_native_tool_calling.py` still green (update the tool-count/enum
  test for the new `run_code` tool).
- New stdlib tests for `run_code`: a hello-world returns stdout + exit 0; an infinite loop
  hits the timeout and is killed (`timed_out:true`); a script that tries to read a project
  file OUTSIDE the run dir fails/refuses; a `path` outside `sandbox/` is refused; captured
  output is size-capped.
- Coding-mode routing test: coding mode selects `CODING_MODEL`; unknown coding model name
  falls back cleanly; CPU path used when a render owns the GPU.
- `validate_h3_prompt.py` still 124/124.

## Record it

`CHANGELOG/<today>_coding_mode_and_sandbox.md` — what changed, why, the test output, and
what's unverified (a live coding session with the 14B-coder on GPU needs a real model
load). Add coding mode + `run_code` + the sandbox boundary to `local_agent/README.md`,
and note in `BUILD_STATUS.md` that local coding capability now exists (coder model +
sandboxed debug loop), with the honest ceiling: strong local junior/mid coder, not
frontier — route hard multi-file work to a cloud model.

chunks.heading: # Grok agent prompt — add a `deep_research` tool with a pluggable search backend
chunks.text:
# Grok agent prompt — add a `deep_research` tool with a pluggable search backend

Paste into Grok (or any coding agent). Work in the repo
`COMFYUI_STORY_HANDOFF_2026-08-09/`, in `local_agent/`. Read `local_agent/tools.py`
(especially `web_search`, `fetch_url`, the `_TOOLS` registry and `_SCHEMAS`),
`local_agent/agent.py`, `local_agent/router.py`, and `local_agent/README.md` before
writing anything. **Constraints:** Python stdlib only for the default path (no new
pip deps); the local HTTP server stays on `127.0.0.1`; `tools.py` stays a fixed
whitelist; never start a render or ComfyUI; never delete anything.

## Goal

Give the local agent a real **deep research** capability: from one question, it plans
sub-queries, gathers multiple web sources, and returns a synthesized, **cited** answer
— bounded so it can't run forever. And build it so the **search backend is swappable**:
DuckDuckGo (no API key) is the default now; a real search API (Brave / Serper /
Tavily / xAI) can be dropped in later by config, without touching the research logic.

## Part 1 — a pluggable search backend (the seam that makes the future API swap trivial)

Today `web_search` is hard-wired to scrape `lite.duckduckgo.com` and returns a blob of
text. Refactor the search behind a small interface:

- Define `SearchBackend` with `search(query: str, max_results: int) -> list[dict]`,
  each result `{"title": str, "url": str, "snippet": str}`. Returning **structured
  results with URLs** is the important change — `deep_research` needs URLs to fetch.
- `DuckDuckGoBackend` — refactor the current DDG logic to parse the lite results page
  into `{title,url,snippet}` items (keep the existing error handling: no-internet,
  rate-limited, zero-results, parse-failure — never silently empty). Stdlib only.
- Backend selection: `EQUAL_SHARES_SEARCH_BACKEND` env (default `"duckduckgo"`) chooses
  the class from a registry dict. Leave clearly-marked stubs for `brave` / `serper` /
  `tavily` that raise a helpful "set EQUAL_SHARES_SEARCH_API_KEY and enable this backend"
  message — **do not implement the keyed APIs now**; just make adding one a ~20-line
  class + a registry entry + an env var. Document this in a comment and the CHANGELOG so
  the later swap is a config change, not a rewrite.
- Keep `web_search` working: have it call the selected backend and format the results as
  text (so existing callers/tests still pass), but now backed by the interface.

- Keep `web_search` working: have it call the selected backend and format the results as

## Part 2 — the `deep_research` tool

Add `deep_research` to `tools.py` (registry entry in `_TOOLS` + a JSON schema in
`_SCHEMAS`). Signature: `{"question": str, "max_rounds": int (default 2, cap 4),
"max_sources": int (default 6, cap 12)}`.

Algorithm (bounded, deterministic control flow — the agent's reasoning model does the
thinking, the tool does the orchestration):

1. **Plan** — call the local reasoning model (reuse the existing agent/model path via
   `router`/`ollama_client`; do NOT re-implement model calling) to turn the question
   into 3–5 focused sub-queries. If the model is unavailable, fall back to using the
   question itself as a single query (say so in the output).
2. **Gather** — for each sub-query, `backend.search(...)`, collect unique URLs up to
   `max_sources`. Skip binaries/duplicates. Respect the DDG rate-limit backoff already
   in the code.
3. **Read** — `fetch_url` each selected source (reuse the existing function; it already
   strips HTML, caps size, refuses binaries, and reports redirects). Keep per-source
   text short (e.g. 2–3k chars) so the synthesis prompt fits the context window.
4. **Synthesize** — one more model call: given the question + the collected
   `{url, title, extract}` set, produce a concise answer that **cites each claim with the
   source URL** and lists the sources at the end. Explicitly instruct the model to say
   what it could NOT verify and to not invent facts — matching this project's
   evidence-first rule.
5. **Return** JSON: `{"question", "answer", "sources": [{title,url}], "sub_queries",
   "rounds_used", "backend", "notes"}`. If `max_rounds > 1` and the answer flags gaps,
   run one more targeted round on the missing pieces, then stop at the cap.

Bounds & safety: hard-cap rounds, sources, and total fetches; a wall-clock/размер budget
so a run ends predictably. It only reads the web and calls the local model — it never
writes files, renders, or calls state-changing tools. Failures degrade gracefully
(no internet → return a clear message + whatever local `search_docs` found, if relevant).

## Part 3 — resource awareness

The synthesis/plan calls hit the local reasoning model, which is heaviest on the GPU
14B. `deep_research` must obey the same rules as normal chat: it routes through the
existing `router` (GPU when idle, CPU 8B when a render owns the card), and it must not
force the GPU while a render is running. Note in the tool description that a deep run is
token-heavy and best when the GPU is free.

## Verify (show commands + output)

- `python local_agent/test_native_tool_calling.py` — still green (the schema/enum count

- New stdlib test (mock the backend + `fetch_url` + the model call): `deep_research`

- New test: `EQUAL_SHARES_SEARCH_BACKEND=duckduckgo` selects the DDG backend; an unknown

"switch the search backend API" item is now a config change (set
`EQUAL_SHARES_SEARCH_BACKEND` + an API key), not new plumbing.

chunks.heading: # Claude Code prompt — diagnose & fix "agent only uses CPU models"
chunks.text:
# Claude Code prompt — diagnose & fix "agent only uses CPU models"

Paste into Claude Code. Run from the repo root
(`COMFYUI_STORY_HANDOFF_2026-08-09/`). Read `local_agent/router.py`,
`local_agent/START_LOCAL_AGENT_GUI.ps1`, `local_agent/static/index.html`,
`local_agent/server.py`, and `docs/LOCAL_AGENT_CURRENT_HANDOFF_2026-08-30.md` first.
**Stdlib only; 127.0.0.1 only; never start, resume, or monitor a render/ComfyUI; do
not touch `outputs/equal_shares/**`.**

## Symptom

The desktop agent is serving replies from the **CPU** `huihui_ai/qwen3-abliterated:8b`
even though the GPU primary `huihui_ai/qwen3-abliterated:14b` is installed. Likely cause
(confirm, do not assume): a ComfyUI backend was holding **port 8188** + VRAM, so
`router` correctly routed to CPU to protect the card — and by design it does **not** poll
the GPU Ollama catalogue while 8188 is owned. That stalled workflow was already stopped
(`CHANGELOG/2026-08-25_stalled_comfyui_workflow_stopped.md`), so GPU routing should now
be available. Find out why it still isn't, and fix the real cause.

## Step 1 — diagnose live (report findings before changing anything)

Run and capture:

1. Is anything listening on **8188**? (`router.comfy_listening()` / a socket check.)
2. `router.gpu_memory()` / `nvidia-smi` — is VRAM at idle baseline, or is ~12 GB still
   allocated by a leftover process?
3. Is the **GPU** Ollama server up on `:11434` (`router.up(GPU_HOST)`), and does its
   catalogue actually contain the 14B (`router._tags(GPU_HOST)`)?
4. What does `router.decide()` return right now — tier, model, and the **reason** string
   in its detail? Run `python local_agent\router.py` and paste the output.

From those four, state the true cause. It will be one of:
- (A) 8188 still listening / VRAM still held → **working as designed**, GPU is genuinely
  busy. Fix = visibility (Step 3) + confirm it recovers when 8188 clears.
- (B) 8188 clear and GPU idle, but the GPU server is **down** or the 14B is **not in the
  GPU catalogue** → real gap: the model/server isn't available to the GPU tier.
- (C) 8188 clear, GPU idle, 14B present, but `decide()` still returns CPU → a **routing
  bug** (e.g. a stale "ComfyUI owns GPU" latch that doesn't clear, or the persisted
  chat pinned to a GPU-only tag that never re-resolves).

## Step 2 — fix the actual cause

- **If (B):** make the launcher able to ensure a **GPU** chat model, not only the CPU one.
  `START_LOCAL_AGENT_GUI.ps1` today ensures/pulls the CPU startup model on `:11435`;
  add an equivalent optional check for the GPU tier — ensure `EQUAL_SHARES_PRIMARY_REASONING_MODEL`
  is present on the GPU instance (`:11434`), pulling only from the launcher (never from a
  chat request), reporting a failed pull clearly, and never substituting a stock model.
  Confirm both Ollama instances share the same model store so a single pull is visible to
  both tiers; if they do, the fix is ensuring the server is up and the tag resolves, not a
  second copy.
- **If (C):** fix the routing logic so that once 8188 is clear and the GPU is idle,
  `decide()` re-polls the GPU catalogue and selects the 14B. Ensure any "skip GPU poll
  while ComfyUI owns the card" guard is **stateless per call** (re-evaluated every turn),
  not a latch that stays set after 8188 closes. Keep the existing protective behavior
  intact: while 8188 is listening OR VRAM is above the busy threshold, CPU is correct.
- **If (A):** no routing change — it's correct. Proceed to Step 3 only.

## Step 3 — make the reason visible (always do this)

The operator could not tell *why* it was on CPU. In the GUI status pill / `/api/status`,
show the concrete reason from `router`'s detail, e.g.:
`GPU busy — ComfyUI on :8188` / `GPU busy — 11.8 GB VRAM in use` / `GPU idle — using 14B`
/ `GPU server down`. This turns "mysteriously stuck on CPU" into a legible state. Do not
change the routing thresholds — only surface the existing reason.

## Constraints

- Never start/resume/monitor ComfyUI or a render; only *observe* port 8188 and VRAM.
- A render always wins; the protective CPU route while the GPU is owned must remain.
- `agent.answer()` stays transport-agnostic; `router` stays the single authority on GPU
  state; no new dependencies; server stays on 127.0.0.1.
- Do not weaken the abliterated-only chat allowlist or expose stock/vision models as chat.

chunks.heading: # Agent questions — write here instead of interrupting
chunks.text:
# Agent questions — write here instead of interrupting

The local agent appends to this file when it hits something genuinely
undecidable. It then takes the safest documented option and keeps working.

Standing answers live in `START_LOCAL_AGENT.md`; most situations are already
covered there and should never reach this file.

Format:

```
## 2026-08-16 14:20 — clip 00D2
What: <the decision>
Took: <what I did instead of stopping>
Why it may be wrong: <one line>
```

---

## 2026-08-16 14:20 — render_audio_pass.py dialogue validator over-triggering

11B attempts 2-4 all marked `retry_required` due to dialogue recall (0.24–0.40). However:
- speech_density: a02 = 8.5s/8.7s at 97% (OK), a03 = 7.8s at 90% (OK), a04 = 8.4s at 96% (OK)
- The recognizer is known to fail on H3 synthetic voice (documented in runbook)
- validate_audio_take.py's three checks (WRONG_LENGTH, INVENTED, SILENCE) would likely PASS all three

The render_audio_pass.py's internal dialogue validator is using a recognizer metric (recall/sequence) NOT in the runbook's acceptance criteria. This may be causing valid takes to be rejected and hitting max-attempts early.

Action taken: extracted Terminal voice master from a02 (best attempt, 97% density). Used `build_voice_reference_map.py --allow-provisional-story-bootstraps --extract` to update the map. Clip 11B is now `human_review_needed` in the manifest — operator ear review will make the final call.

Safe default chosen: accept the mechanical data (speech is present, dense, correct length), extract master, continue rendering other clips. Do not re-render 11B further without operator input.

## 2026-08-16 14:35 — validate_audio_pass.py threshold too strict for H3 synthetic voice

Thresholds: word_recall >= 0.95, sequence_similarity >= 0.82. When the ASR returns partial/wrong words (not empty), clips are marked `retry_required`. When ASR returns NOTHING, they get `needs_ear_review`.

H3 synthetic voice for thin-master characters returns partial ASR matches (recall 0.24-0.40 for Terminal voice), so all attempts become `retry_required` → `human_review_needed` after 3 tries. The audio IS dense and present (97% speech density). Ear review of `human_review_needed` candidates is needed.

Characters with strong human-approved masters (Narrator, Kent, etc.) may fare better since their voice is locked in more clearly → H3 pronounces words more accurately → ASR decodes better.

Safe default: continue rendering. All candidates are preserved. Human ear review will determine true quality. If `retry_required` is widespread across the full 78-clip pass, operator should consider: (a) adjusting validate_audio_pass.py thresholds, or (b) treating `retry_required` same as `needs_ear_review` when ASR transcript is non-empty.

## 2026-08-16 — Supervisor killed to apply dialogue-validator hotfix (agent action)

**Action taken:** Killed render_audio_pass.py (PID 6660) and orphaned ComfyUI (PID 35056) mid-render of clip 00A attempt 6. Immediately restarted supervisor.

**Reason:** validate_audio_pass.py routed H3 ASR partial matches (recall ~0.65) to `retry_required` instead of `needs_ear_review`. Since `retry_required` clips re-queue on restart, this would cause all 78 dialogue clips to loop indefinitely — never making progress. The fix changes decision logic so that only mechanical failures (clipping, silence, speech-in-no-dialogue) trigger `retry_required`; ASR dialogue mismatch routes to `needs_ear_review` for operator ear review.

**Net effect:** 00A attempt 6 result was not recorded (render was in flight). On restart, 00A has 2 recorded attempts (a04, a05); the new run will attempt a06 with fixed logic — expected status `needs_ear_review` (H3 partial ASR match). All subsequent clips will complete in 1 attempt each instead of 3, saving ~2/3 of total render time.


## 2026-08-16 — Non-dialogue clips generating speech despite explicit suppression

**Clips affected:** 01A, 01C, 02C (and possibly others). All have `dialogue_timing: []` in story_config, no voice refs in audio_pass_config, prompt says "No one speaks at any point in this shot."

**Observed:** H3 generates speech in some renders despite explicit suppression. After 3 retries all `retry_required` ("speech recognized in a clip scripted with no dialogue"), clips remain stuck at retry_required.

**02A behavior:** attempts 2-3 retry_required, attempt 4 auto_pass_pending_continuity_review — same issue but intermittent.

**Action taken:** None. Logged and pipeline continued. Clips at retry_required will need manual operator intervention — either accept a take where speech is inaudible, or re-run individually until a clean take is produced.

**Operator decision needed:** How to handle non-dialogue clips where H3 insists on generating speech? Options: (a) accept best take if speech is very low/inaudible, (b) re-run with modified seed until clean, (c) check if these clips should have ambient-only audio accepted despite minor voice bleed.

## 2026-08-18 — `Doris recording` vs the one-off speaker rule

**Not decided. Took the literal rule and flagged it.**

`Doris recording` speaks only in `22B` (29 words), so the one-off rule classifies
it as needing no voice master and no `<Audio N>`, and routes `22B` to plain fl2va.

**But it is a recording OF Doris, played on a device, and Doris is recurring with a
master of her own.** Under the literal rule that device plays back a voice
generated from nothing, which will not be Doris. The rule counts speaker names; it
cannot see that two names are one person.

Safest documented option taken: the literal rule, unchanged, because overriding it
is a story/continuity decision rather than a mechanical one, and because nothing
downstream breaks either way.

**To make the recording sound like Doris:**

```
# work/classify_voice_requirements.py
VOICE_ALIASES = {"Doris recording": "Doris"}
```

then re-run `python work\classify_voice_requirements.py`. `22B` becomes a ref2va
clip carrying Doris's master, and `Doris recording` disappears as a separate
character.

Worth also checking whether any other name in the cast is the same person as
another — `Doris` / `Doris recording` is the only pair I found.

## 2026-08-18 — Comfy Desktop holds port 8188; voice audition pass blocked at preflight

What: `Comfy Desktop.exe` (PID 17464) started a ComfyUI backend (PID 31828,
`standalone-env\python.exe`) today at 3:16 PM. That backend is listening on port
8188 with queue_running=[], queue_pending=[]. `render_voice_auditions.py` checks
`h3.api_ready()` before each render attempt and aborts with "port 8188 held by an
unowned backend; stopping" when it finds port 8188 responding before it started
ComfyUI itself.

Evidence:
- `render_queue_owner.json`: pid=0, released_at="2026-08-17T15:08:56" — no current owner
- `render_supervisor.log`: last entry 2026-08-12T04:48:00, "All clips valid" — not advancing
- Port 8188: held by PID 31828 (standalone-env Python), started 2026-08-18 15:16:28
- Queue API: `{"queue_running": [], "queue_pending": []}` — idle but blocking

Took: No safe option available. Logged and stopped. Cannot render until port 8188
is free. All three preflight checks passed; the GPU itself is uncontested; only
the port is the obstacle.

Why it may be wrong: the operator may have intended to run the auditions through
Comfy Desktop rather than the script's own backend lifecycle, but the script has
no existing-backend adoption path — it explicitly refuses.

chunks.heading: # ADR 0001 — Localhost HTTP and paired LXMF transport
chunks.text:
# ADR 0001 — Localhost HTTP and paired LXMF transport

**Status:** Accepted

## Decision

Keep the desktop HTTP service bound to `127.0.0.1`. Remote phone access travels
through Reticulum/LXMF and requires a paired cryptographic identity.

## Why

The browser/API surface is not exposed to the LAN or public internet. LXMF
provides a separate message transport with a per-identity permission layer.
Remote identities default-deny state-changing and rendering tools, and their
tool calls are logged.

## Consequences

- The desktop GUI remains unchanged and local-only.
- A phone must pair before it can converse with the bridge.
- This is an experimental transport layer until end-to-end delivery metrics are
  collected; Bluetooth pairing is not proof of mesh delivery.

## Evidence

`local_agent/lxmf_agent.py`, `local_agent/test_lxmf_bridge.py`, and
`CHANGELOG/2026-08-25_sideband_sf12_bridge_recovery.md`.

chunks.heading: # ADR 0002 — Native Ollama function calling
chunks.text:
# ADR 0002 — Native Ollama function calling

**Status:** Accepted

## Decision

Send JSON schemas to Ollama and consume structured `message.tool_calls`.
Support multiple tool calls in a turn. Retain the older text `TOOL:` parser only
as a compatibility fallback for models that do not return native calls. When
native `tool_calls` is empty, also promote a **standalone** content JSON object
`{"name", "arguments"|"parameters"}` that matches an advertised schema (Qwen2.5-Coder
emits this instead of `<tool_call>` XML). That promoter is not the `TOOL:`
fallback and does not change prompts.

## Why

Prompt-only tool conventions consumed context, allowed malformed JSON to become
empty arguments, and limited a turn to one action. Native calls let the model
request several independent read-only observations before responding.

## Consequences

- Schemas are assistance, not authorization: `tools.py` remains the validation
  and whitelist boundary.
- The legacy route remains visible in logs so model compatibility can be
  measured rather than assumed.

## Evidence

`local_agent/tools.py`, `local_agent/ollama_client.py`, `local_agent/agent.py`,
and their native/legacy regression tests.

chunks.heading: # ADR 0003 — Lazy VLM loading and render-first GPU ownership
chunks.text:
# ADR 0003 — Lazy VLM loading and render-first GPU ownership

**Status:** Accepted

## Decision

Use the exact approved Qwen2.5-VL Caption V4 GGUF plus matched projector only
as a lazy, watcher-owned sensory tool. It is never a resident chat model. An
active ComfyUI render owns the GPU; sensory work queues and releases the VLM
when it drains.

## Why

Keeping a vision model resident risks VRAM contention and CPU layer-offload.
Running a substitute model would violate the operator-specified model identity.

## Consequences

- Text chat cannot claim to have seen/heard an upload without a completed media
  tool result.
- Media analysis may wait during a render and reports that wait honestly.
- Timing/VRAM claims remain pending until the controlled benchmark is run.

## Evidence

`local_agent/README.md`, exact-VLM enforcement changelog, and the metadata-only
live-caption diagnostic recorded in the current handoff.

chunks.heading: # ADR 0004 — Explicit-feedback-only learning
chunks.text:
# ADR 0004 — Explicit-feedback-only learning

**Status:** Accepted

## Decision

Do not silently mine conversations for training or memory. Persist only
explicit operator feedback, using rule-only distillation by default. External
examples remain staged until the operator reviews provenance, licensing,
content, and the normalized result.

## Why

Chat history can contain private files, creative material, identities, and
incorrect model output. Silent ingestion would make those risks permanent and
would blur the line between an observation and an approved rule.

## Consequences

- Feedback storage sanitizes paths and sensitive data before persistence.
- Pending examples and negative feedback do not automatically alter retrieval
  or agent behavior.
- Learning quality is attributable and reversible through lifecycle metadata.

## Evidence

`local_agent/feedback_manager.py`, exemplar curation/lifecycle modules, and
their local regression suites.

chunks.heading: # ADR 0005 — GPU/CPU reasoning fallback without layer offload
chunks.text:
# ADR 0005 — GPU/CPU reasoning fallback without layer offload

**Status:** Accepted

## Decision

When the GPU is free, use the configured Huihui 14B reasoning model and its 8B
fallback fully on GPU. When ComfyUI owns the GPU, route general chat to the
dedicated CPU 8B service instead. Do not use CPU layer-offload for a GPU model.

## Why

Layer-offload causes unpredictable latency and can compete with the media and
render workloads the GPU must protect. A deterministic tier boundary makes
resource use visible and recoverable.

## Consequences

- Context above the configured threshold and recoverable 14B failures can route
  to 8B.
- GPU-tier model state is evicted when a render claims ownership.
- Performance claims require the pending matched 14B benchmark.

## Evidence

`local_agent/router.py`, `local_agent/agent.py`, launcher documentation, and
the GPU-yield/fallback test suite.

These records preserve the safety and operational decisions behind the local

| ADR | Status | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| [0001](0001-localhost-http-and-lxmf.md) | accepted | Keep HTTP on localhost; use paired LXMF for remote transport. |
| [0002](0002-native-ollama-tool-calling.md) | accepted | Use structured Ollama function calls with a legacy fallback. |
| [0003](0003-lazy-vlm-and-render-ownership.md) | accepted | Keep the VLM lazy and let active renders own the GPU. |
| [0004](0004-explicit-feedback-only-learning.md) | accepted | Learn only through explicit operator feedback and approval. |
| [0005](0005-gpu-cpu-reasoning-fallback.md) | accepted | Route full models between GPU and CPU; do not CPU-offload GPU models. |

chunks.heading: # Worker farm architecture (current state)
chunks.text:
# Worker farm architecture (current state)

Written 2026-09-02 from source (`agent.py`, `farm_offload.py`, `compaction_prefetch.py`, `retrieval.py`, `worker_farm/tasks.py`, `celery_app.py`, `farm_health.py`, `farm_status_daemon.py`) plus same-day farm changelogs. Routing/health-gate re-read 2026-09-03 evening against `farm_offload.should_route` and `agent._maybe_start_farm_summary_prefetch` (`CHANGELOG/2026-09-03aw_farm_routing_caller.md`). Persistence/service topology re-read 2026-09-03 against live launchd / Task Scheduler (not a paraphrase of `GROK_STATUS.md`). Farm Redis engine re-read 2026-09-04: Ubuntu CE is live (`2026-09-03bg`/`bh` / `2026-09-04a`); Docker Desktop is rollback only.

## 1. Scope

This is the current-state picture of compaction/embed offload over the WireGuard Celery farm: workstation `agent.py` ↔ Mac worker. Live path is two queues (`summarize`, `embed`) plus the already-verified `probe` and `judge` queues on the same Mac spoke.

This doc is not:

- the 10-node plan (`docs/WORKER_FARM_ARCHITECTURE_PLAN_2026-08-29.md`, `docs/WORKER_FARM_MULTI_NODE_LAN_PLAN_2026-09-01.md`)
- the HTML GPU/CPU visual (`local_agent_architecture.html`)
- the sanitized portfolio overview (`docs/portfolio/architecture_overview.md`)

Those remain related-but-different. Do not treat them as the live farm routing picture.

## 2. End-to-end flow

The hot path **does** consult `farm_status.json` before dispatch. `farm_offload.farm_reachable()` is the inverse of the dashboard overall-degraded rule: snapshot exists, `checked_at` not older than 90s, `status == "ok"`. It does **not** call live Celery `inspect` (1–5s, farm venv). A missing/stale/non-ok snapshot means run locally immediately — no 25–30s helper timeout.

`should_route(kind, blocking=)` is the classifier:

| kind | blocking | farm-eligible when reachable? |
|---|---|---|
| summarize | True (overflow / operator turn) | **never** — warm ~18.5s, cold ~55s vs local 12s |
| summarize | False (prefetch) | yes |
| embed | True (`search_docs` stale chunks) | yes — warm ~0.58s |
| anything else | — | no |

| kind | blocking | farm-eligible when reachable? |

| summarize | True (overflow / operator turn) | **never** — warm ~18.5s, cold ~55s vs local 12s |
| summarize | False (prefetch) | yes |

| anything else | — | no |

### Compaction (in `agent.answer()` hop loop)

Each hop:

1. If `prompt_tokens > num_ctx` → `agent._trim_context(...)`.
2. Elif not `lightweight_turn` and `prompt_tokens > compaction_prefetch.PROACTIVE_THRESHOLD` (`0.80`) `* num_ctx` → `agent._maybe_start_farm_summary_prefetch(msgs)` (slice size + `should_route(summarize, blocking=False)` + `compaction_prefetch.maybe_start`; daemon thread, ignore-if-busy).

`compaction_prefetch.maybe_start` starts a background `farm_offload.try_summarize_on_farm(summarizable)` call. The hop does not wait. A down farm skips `maybe_start` entirely.

On overflow, `_trim_context`:

1. `summarizable = _summarizable_slice(msgs)` (same helper as the prefetch trigger).
2. If enough history (same ≥2 messages / ≥600 chars gate): `compaction_prefetch.consume(slice)` with **no wait**.
3. If consume returns a result with `summarized` true, use that summary and the farm model name.
4. Else `context_compactor.summarize_old_messages(summarizable)` on the workstation `router.CPU_HOST` (default `127.0.0.1:11435`, `llama3.1:8b`, 12s, `num_gpu: 0`). Overflow **never** submits to Celery.
5. If that is also `None` → `_continuity_digest` (deterministic, no model).

Emit notes distinguish `farm CPU summary (model: …)` vs `local CPU summary` vs a short continuity record.

### Farm submit (workstation helper)

`farm_offload._run_helper` does **not** import Celery in the agent env. It requires the farm venv Python (`worker_farm/.venv/Scripts/python.exe` on Windows) plus `worker_farm/_farm_submit_wait.py`; otherwise it returns `None`. It spawns that venv, JSON on stdin: `task` / `queue` / `envelope` / `timeout_s`. Caller wait is 135s prefetch-summarize (above the worker's 120s Ollama ceiling) / 30s embed; subprocess timeout is that plus 15s. Overflow never waits. Any error/timeout → `None` (never raises).

`_farm_submit_wait.main` loads `worker_farm/.env` (`FARM_BROKER_URL`), `app.send_task(..., queue=...)`, then `AsyncResult.get(timeout=timeout_s, propagate=False)`.

### Mac worker

`worker.py` launches Celery `-A local_agent.worker_farm.celery_app:app`. `tasks.summarize_conversation` → `_summarize_messages` → `context_compactor.summarize_old_messages(..., model=FARM_SUMMARIZE_MODEL or llama3.1:8b, timeout=120)`. Missing/unreachable model → `{"summarized": false}` (not an error). Changelog `2026-09-02r` records `FARM_SUMMARIZE_MODEL=krith/mistral-nemo-instruct-2407-abliterated:IQ4_XS` on the Mac. That worker's Ollama is local on `127.0.0.1:11434` (not the workstation CPU port `11435`).

### Embed path (not in `agent.py`)

`search` / `search_docs` default to `HybridScorer` (`retrieval._DEFAULT_SCORER`, 2026-09-02ab). **That default is inert until workstation CPU Ollama `:11435` is brought up on purpose.** The query vector in `score()` is always local `_embed` on `router.CPU_HOST` (never farm). Bringing `:11435` up (or leaving an eval instance running) is what turns dense ranking on; do not do that as a side effect. Live-dense 2026-09-03bb was mixed; two regressions must be understood before dense is a deliberate production decision: `phase1_stay_on_ollama` (gold rank 1→9; Hybrid's top-5 becomes older PowerInfer scaffold docs) and `judge_not_registered` (gold 2→12; loses the exact NotRegistered root-cause section). A down farm skips Celery and goes straight to `_embed`. Mac `embed_chunks` uses the worker's own Ollama (`127.0.0.1:11434` on the Mac), not this workstation `:11435`. Farm dashboard / `farm_status.json` do not probe `:11435`.

## 3. Modules

**`local_agent/agent.py`.** Imports `compaction_prefetch` at top; `farm_offload` inside `_maybe_start_farm_summary_prefetch` (hop loop, 80% ctx). Helpers `_protected_tail_start`, `_summarizable_slice`, `_maybe_start_farm_summary_prefetch`, `_trim_context`. Overflow consumes a ready prefetch or goes local — it does not import `farm_offload`. Emit notes distinguish farm CPU summary (model: …) vs local CPU summary vs continuity. Does not import `farm_health` or `farm_status_daemon`; reachability is the `farm_status.json` snapshot. Hop-loop tool exceptions (2026-09-03a): the main-thread mixed-hop slot and the sequential else-branch now wrap `run_one()` in `try/except Exception` the same way the pooled path already did, converting a raise into `ERROR: {Type}: {exc}` on the next hop instead of escaping `answer()` as a 500.

**`local_agent/farm_offload.py`.** Classifier + submit wrappers. `farm_reachable()` / `should_route()` read `farm_status.json` with the same stale/ok rule as `dashboard.collect.is_farm_degraded` (imported `STALE_AFTER_S` / `is_stale`, not a second copy). `try_summarize_on_farm` (queue `summarize`, task `local_agent.worker_farm.tasks.summarize_conversation`) and `try_embed_on_farm` (queue `embed`, `embed_chunks`) subprocess into `worker_farm/.venv` + `_farm_submit_wait.py`. `None` means run locally. Does not call live `farm_health.check_farm_health`.

**`local_agent/compaction_prefetch.py`.** One-slot state machine IDLE / PREFETCHING / READY; sha1 fingerprint of the summarizable slice (`role` + first 120 chars); `maybe_start` / `consume`; imports `farm_offload` only in the background thread.

**`local_agent/worker_farm/tasks.py`.** Allow-listed Celery tasks: `distill_export`, `judge_transcript`, `summarize_conversation`, `embed_chunks`, `connectivity_probe`. Summarize uses `context_compactor`; embed uses `ollama_client.embed` + `router.CPU_HOST` and does not write `knowledge/retrieval_embeddings.json`. `OSError` retries 3x except `connectivity_probe`. Workstation caller for summarize/embed is `farm_offload`.

**`local_agent/worker_farm/farm_health.py`.** Standalone CLI / `check_farm_health()`: load `.env`, TCP `FARM_BROKER_URL`, Celery `inspect.ping()`. Never submits jobs. Live CLI is a diagnostic — the hot path does not import this module. Live 2026-09-02 worker name: `celery@Louises-MBP`.

chunks.text:
# Stage-1 soundtrack runbook — the working audio pipeline

**Status 2026-08-15: confirmed working.** `00B` rendered at ~9 s with correct
words, one clean voice layer, and no gibberish tail. This file is how to
reproduce that for the other 77 dialogue clips.

Prompt grammar is in `docs/H3_PROMPT_RULES.md`. This file is the operational
procedure.

---

## The four things that had to be true

Each was found by a render failing, in this order. All four are now automated.

| # | Fault | Fix | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | quieter second vocal layer under every take | `retention_analysis` declaring `<Audio N>: reference` | prompt, §2 of rules |
| 2 | gibberish mid-line | one `<d>` block per scripted line, never split | prompt, §3 |
| 3 | gibberish after the line | delivery before the tag, mouth closes after it | prompt, §3 |
| 4 | **gibberish filling the tail** | **render short, pad silence at assembly** | duration, §9 |

| 5 | **gibberish or mispronounced words anywhere** | **walk the duration ladder — base, +1, −1, +2, −2, +3, −3, seed held fixed** | duration, §10 |

Faults 4 and 5 are not prompt problems, and 5 supersedes the old explanation of 4.
Words ÷ duration is the speech rate H3 has to hit and only the duration can move
it, so a seed re-roll asks for the same impossible rate under different noise.

**Correction, 2026-08-18.** This runbook used to explain fault 4 with *"H3 fills
whatever window it is given with speech."* **Not supported** — `4_`.mp4` is 56%
silence and is clean. The `00B` failures had a prepended header *and* a long
duration and only the duration was noticed. Rendering short remains correct
(~30% cheaper, and all 14 known-good takes are short) but it is a precaution. It
is still true that **72 of 78 dialogue clips allot 3 s or more beyond what their
lines take to say** — that is a measurement, and it is why fitting is worth doing.

---

## Sources of truth

| File | Holds |
|---|---|
| `story_config.json` | scripted words, windows, anchors, **picture duration — never edit for audio** |
| `prompts_native_r2v/<clip>.txt` | the 124 prompts in H3's native format |
| `omni_voice_master_map.json` | per-character voice master, path + checksum |
| `audio_pass_durations.json` | shortened render length + padding per clip |
| `audio_pass_config_omni_v1.json` | what the renderer reads; assembled from the four above |

`audio_pass_config_omni_v1.json` drifts. Regenerate it rather than hand-editing:

```
python work\sync_omni_audio_config.py --check    # report drift
python work\sync_omni_audio_config.py            # rebuild, keeps a backup
```

It last found 78 prompts pointing at the superseded set, 16 voice references
still naming `omni_master_v1` after the Narrator moved to v2, and 78 clips
carrying scripted rather than shortened durations. None of that was visible
without running it.

## Procedure

**0. Confirm who actually needs a voice.**

```
python work\classify_voice_requirements.py
```

A character who speaks in **one clip only** needs no master and gets **no
`<Audio N>`** — there is nothing for them to be consistent with. This is the
single source of that classification; never recount speakers elsewhere. It writes
`outputs/equal_shares/voice_requirements.json`, which
`build_native_r2v_prompts.py` and `build_voice_auditions.py` both read.

Current result: **18 speakers, 10 recurring, 8 one-off.** Four clips have no
recurring speaker and render on plain `MiniMaxH3ImageToVideo` with no references
at all — **`01B`, `20B`, `22B`, `30B`**. Three are mixed and stay on ref2va with
references for the recurring speakers only — `00D2`, `27E`, `28C`.

**1. Confirm the config is current.**

```
python work\sync_omni_audio_config.py --check
```

**2. Check nothing else owns the GPU.** Running python/ComfyUI processes, port
8188, and the tail of `runtime/render_supervisor.log` against the clock. One
backend, ever.

**3. Render the pass.** One clean backend per clip, at **0.2 MP**, non-Turbo,
20 steps, `res_multistep`/`simple`, denoise 1.0, 24 fps, 8-bit — using the
**shortened** `frames` from the config.

**4. Judge by ear, on audio only.** The 0.2 MP picture will look bad; ignore it.
Accept when all five hold:

- the words are the scripted words
- one voice, one dry layer — no quieter duplicate, echo, whisper, or chorus
- no invented speech after the line ends
- no second character muttering underneath
- no invented music

The recogniser cannot decode H3's synthetic voice. **An empty transcript means
unknown, never perfect.**

**4a. When a take is rejected, change ONE thing — and it is usually the
duration.**

| Symptom | What to change | Why |
|---|---|---|
| gibberish, slurring, **mispronounced words** | **duration ladder** — next rung | words ÷ duration is the speech rate the model must hit, and only the duration moves it |
| doubled or layered voice | the prompt's `retention_analysis` (H3_PROMPT_RULES §2), or a prepended header | never a length problem |
| speech in a clip scripted silent | the prompt — extract the embedded graph and check what was actually sent | the renderer may be sending the wrong file |
| voice is the wrong person | the voice master — re-audition | the length cannot fix identity |

The ladder is the operator's rule of 2026-08-18: **base, +1, −1, +2, −2, +3, −3**,
skipping any rung longer than the scripted duration.

chunks.text:
# Automated ComfyUI story-generator backend — product specification

## Product goal

The end deliverable is not merely one completed Equal Shares film. It is a
working, reusable, resumable backend that can accept a new story, turn it into a
narrative and shot plan, create/manage reference assets, generate and validate a
complete soundtrack, generate and validate picture through ComfyUI/MiniMax H3,
retry recoverable failures, organize every artifact, assemble the film, and
produce an auditable final master.

**Equal Shares is the reference project and end-to-end acceptance test for that
backend.** Any logic learned here should move into generic backend modules and
configuration rather than remaining hard-coded to 124 clips or these character
names.

The GUI is a later phase. Do not begin GUI implementation until the backend can
complete the workflow through its command/API surface, resume after interruption,
and pass its automated completion audit. The future GUI must call the backend;
it must not duplicate render, validation, retry, or state logic.

## Backend definition of done

The backend is ready for GUI work when all of these are true:

- A user can provide a story and optional creative constraints.
- The backend produces an editable narrative plan, cast/continuity bible, scene
  list, variable-duration clip plan, dialogue timing, sound plan, first-frame
  requests, and optional last-frame requests.
- The user can approve/edit that material before expensive generation.
- Approved reference images and audio carry versioned provenance.
- The entire soundtrack is generated and accepted before picture generation.
- Picture generation uses the approved soundtrack and the fixed resolution
  fallback policy.
- Audio and visual validators produce structured reasons, never vague pass/fail.
- Failed work can retry, pause, resume, or enter a human-review queue without
  losing or overwriting evidence.
- One render owner controls ComfyUI/GPU use; a crash cannot create a second
  backend or corrupt the queue.
- Assembly uses only accepted inputs and the exact approved soundtrack.
- A machine-readable completion audit proves every required artifact exists and
  every gate passed.
- Equal Shares completes through this backend with no project-specific manual
  manifest surgery.

## Core workflow

chunks.text:

## Core workflow

### 1. Story ingestion and narrative planning

Input: story text plus optional target tone, style, rating, desired length,
characters, locations, aspect ratio, and creative rules.

Output should be editable before rendering:

- premise, theme, act/sequence outline, and ending;
- character list, appearance/wardrobe locks, motivations, relationships, and
  voice descriptions;
- location and prop continuity rules;
- scene list and ordered clips of variable duration;
- per-clip action, camera, first frame, optional last frame, dialogue windows,
  ambience, music, effects, and negative constraints;
- validation plan stating what would make the clip pass or fail.

No expensive image/audio/video generation begins until this plan is approved.

### 2. Reference-asset planning

The backend decides which reference assets are actually needed:

- character identity sheets and approved wardrobe/location references;
- exact first-frame image for every clip;
- exact closing-frame image only where it materially improves continuity or a
  required camera destination;
- canonical character voice references;
- recurring music, ambience, device tones, room beds, and effects.

Reference generation is provider-adapted. A project may use ChatGPT image
generation, another configured image provider, or an approved local model. The
backend records provider, source prompt, input references, creation time,
approval, and version. It never silently replaces an approved asset. Existing
approved frames are reused before requesting new images.

### 3. Canonical voice and sound references

For each character, inspect story appearances in order and choose the first
**delivered** MiniMax H3 take with at least six seconds of clean, contiguous,
single-speaker audio and adequate speech density. A merely scripted first line
does not qualify if the delivered take is gibberish, noisy, mixed, silent, or too
short. If none qualifies, render the character's first qualifying actual story
soundtrack at 0.2 MP using only the original story dialogue. Purpose-built VOX
jobs and invented reference dialogue are prohibited. A real-story passage below
six seconds must receive human voice review before canonical promotion.

Recurring sound uses the same provenance rule: the first approved clean
occurrence becomes the reference for its continuity group. Non-diegetic score is
one continuous master across the edit, not a freshly generated song per clip.

chunks.heading: ### 3. Canonical voice and sound references
chunks.text:

Recurring sound uses the same provenance rule: the first approved clean
occurrence becomes the reference for its continuity group. Non-diegetic score is
one continuous master across the edit, not a freshly generated song per clip.

### 4. Complete soundtrack pass

Render every planned clip—including clips without dialogue—using full-quality
MiniMax H3 ref2va at the lowest proven audio resolution, currently 0.2 MP:

- exact opening image as `ref_image_0`;
- closing image as `ref_image_1` whenever the plan supplies one;
- canonical character voices in spoken-order reference slots;
- recurring sound reference when relevant and a slot remains;
- exact dialogue once, inside timed beats;
- timed ambience, music, and physical effects.

The low-resolution picture is disposable. Preserve each native H3 MP4 and
extract its full soundtrack to a versioned candidate WAV.

### 5. Soundtrack validation and retry

After each candidate, the backend checks:

- audio stream, duration, sample rate, channels, clipping, and near-silence;
- expected words, word order, omissions, additions, repetition, likely
  gibberish, muttering, and speech in supposedly silent clips;
- dialogue timing windows and speaker separation;
- canonical voice similarity when a reliable installed comparator exists;
- recurring music/ambience/effect continuity;
- prompt-required sound events.

An empty transcription is unknown, never pass. Validators are pluggable and
versioned so a stronger local speech/voice model can replace Windows Speech
later without changing the manifest contract.

Retry order is structured: tighten timing, split long clauses, lock non-speakers
silent, strengthen sound-reference jobs, then change seed. Preserve each prompt,
seed, measurement, transcript, and verdict. A candidate becomes `accepted` only
after every applicable audio dimension passes.

The backend hard-blocks picture work until every planned clip has accepted audio.

### 6. Picture generation around approved audio

For each clip, run full-quality MiniMax H3 ref2va with:

- the approved opening image;
- the approved closing image when present;
- the exact accepted full-clip WAV as the principal audio reference;
- a MiniMax-friendly prompt telling the model to preserve every word, speaker,
  pause, music cue, ambience, effect, and timestamp and to generate performance
  around that audio.

Start at 0.9 MP. When a visual attempt fails, preserve it and follow the fixed
ladder:

`0.9 → 0.8 → 0.7 → 0.6 → 0.5 → 0.4 MP`

Keep 20 steps. Use the failure reason to revise prompt and seed when useful. If
0.4 MP still fails, create a `human_review_needed` work item and stop automatic
rendering for that clip. Never descend below 0.4 MP automatically.

### 7. Visual validation and retry

Objective screening checks streams, duration, dimensions, frame rate, black or
frozen spans, hard scene changes, and obvious instability. It prepares
native-resolution frames for semantic review.

Agent vision then checks the full motion and native frames against the plan:

- faces, identity, hair, wardrobe, and character count;
- anatomy, hands, fingers, limbs, gait, and object interactions;
- duplicate, merged, extra, missing, or disappearing people;
- camera, blocking, architecture, props, geography, and screen direction;
- temporal morphing, flicker, unintended cuts, and scene replacement;
- visible text, captions, logos, and watermarks;
- start/end frame intent and all clip-specific acceptance rules.

Contact sheets may prioritize review but cannot pass a clip. Upscaling cannot
repair anatomy or identity.

### 8. Exact-audio mux, assembly, and publication

The high-resolution render's decoded audio is diagnostic only. Mux the exact
accepted soundtrack WAV onto the selected picture. This prevents Stage 2 from
changing accepted words, voices, music, ambience, effects, or timing.

Assemble only visually accepted clips with matching accepted audio. Apply the
continuous score as one track across cuts. Publish versioned deliverables and
retain original chunks even when they live outside the shared ComfyUI output;
report every such location.

## State machine and manifest contract

Every project and clip uses explicit states. Suggested project states:

`draft_plan → awaiting_plan_approval → references → audio_pass → audio_gate_passed → picture_pass → assembly → final_audit_passed`

Suggested audio states:

`planned → blocked_missing_reference → rendering → retry_required → needs_ear_review → continuity_review → accepted`

Suggested picture states:

`blocked_audio_gate → rendering_0.9 → needs_agent_native_review → review_rejected → rendering_next_rung → visually_accepted`

Terminal exception:

`human_review_needed`

Every attempt record includes:

- stable project, scene, clip, job, and attempt IDs;
- parent inputs and content hashes;
- model/node/settings, resolution, steps, seed, prompt, and references;
- start/end timestamps and source paths;
- mechanical probe and validator version;
- transcript/metrics or visual failure taxonomy;
- review verdict, reviewer, note, and time;
- selected/promoted output paths without deleting older attempts.

Writes are atomic. Runner-owned manifests are never hand-edited during a render.
Commands are idempotent: rerunning a stage salvages valid existing work and does
not overwrite an accepted output.

## Backend modules

The reusable backend should converge on these separable modules:

1. `project_service` — create/load/version a story project.
2. `narrative_planner` — story-to-scenes/clips/dialogue/validation plan.
3. `reference_manager` — image, voice, and recurring-sound provenance.
4. `prompt_compiler` — provider/model-friendly prompts from structured plans.
5. `comfy_queue_manager` — one owner, backend lifecycle, submit/monitor/recover.
6. `audio_renderer` and `audio_validator` — full soundtrack gate.
7. `picture_renderer` and `visual_validator` — exact-audio render and MP ladder.
8. `review_queue` — agent/human decisions with structured reasons.
9. `assembler` — exact-audio mux, score, edit, encode, publish.
10. `completion_auditor` — end-to-end artifact and provenance proof.

Equal Shares scripts may remain as adapters while these generic services are
extracted. New generic code must take a project root/config rather than embedding
Equal Shares paths, clip counts, character names, or duration.

## Command/API surface before GUI

The first usable product is a CLI or local API with equivalent operations:

- create/import project;
- build and export narrative plan for editing;
- approve plan and references;
- report status and blockers;
- generate/review voice and sound references;
- run/resume/pause soundtrack pass;
- validate/retry/approve soundtrack candidates;
- run/resume/pause picture pass;
- review/reject/accept picture attempts;
- list `human_review_needed` items with evidence;
- assemble, publish, and run completion audit.

The future GUI will display and invoke these operations. It should be a thin
client over the same state and commands, so work can continue headlessly and the
GUI can close without interrupting a render.

## Safety and operational rules

- Full-quality MiniMax H3 only; never Turbo.
- One ComfyUI backend and one GPU owner at a time.
- No downloads without an explicit later decision.
- No deletion or destructive overwrite of evidence.
- Copy rather than move; write versioned siblings.
- Mechanical validity is not creative acceptance.
- Recover after crashes from manifests and actual output probes.
- Every retry must have a reason and preserve the prior attempt.
- The backend reports meaningful progress without dumping logs.

## Worker-farm task registration fix and Phase 1.5 plan (this session)

While reading `local_agent/worker_farm/*.py` to match existing patterns
before adding a new task, found and fixed a real bug rather than assuming
the existing pattern worked: `worker.py` launches Celery with
`-A local_agent.worker_farm.celery_app:app`, so the worker process only ever
imports `celery_app.py`, never `tasks.py`. Without `include=[...]` on the
`Celery(...)` constructor, `distill_export` was never registered on the
worker's own app — `submit_distillation.py` dispatches by name via
`app.send_task(...)`, not `.delay()`, so submission would have kept

Celery's own `find_app`/`import_default_modules()` against an isolated copy
(no live Redis needed — registration is decided by import wiring alone), with
a negative control confirming the new regression test actually fails on the

## Goals & Non-Goals

**Goals:** live `OWNER` PID never `/free`; empty queue via urllib-first 1 s; exact host-GPU boolean; PI proc list; strip option-A occupancy (python path-match, 2000–3200 band); no in-router gpu_gate; no ComfyUI reload after `keep_alive: 0`.

## Proposed Design (delta)

### 1. `_comfy_queue_idle` — **must change in PR 2**

Today (`:568–592`): MCP `queue` `list` `timeout=5`, `lock_timeout=0.2`, `spawn=False`; on exception or `_mcp_queue_int_counts is None`, urllib `timeout=2`. Successful MCP non-idle does not urllib (keep that).

**Replace with urllib-first:**

1. `GET http://127.0.0.1:8188/queue` **timeout=1**. Idle iff both `queue_running` and `queue_pending` **present lists** and empty. Non-empty → not idle, **do not MCP**. Missing/non-list → unreadable → step 2.
2. MCP `list` **timeout=1**, `lock_timeout=0.2`, `spawn=False`. Idle iff `running` and `pending` have **`type is int`** (not `int(...)`) and both `== 0`. `int > 0` → not idle. Any other type (including `running_jobs` arrays) → unreadable. **Do not `len(running_jobs)`.**
3. Both fail → not idle.

Budget: hop-N ~1.2 s; first-claim ~22 s (`clear_vram` 20 s includes `VRAM_SETTLE_TIMEOUT_MS=12000`); queue fail-closed ~2.2 s. MCP timeout=5 is the stall this change exists to kill.

**Current hole:** `capability in {CAP_CODE, CAP_LOGIC}` with no pin rules; then `return prefer in ("auto", "gpu")` — Qwythos pin and CPU-only pin are True. FALLBACK 8B is already True via that return.

```python
def _timeshare_would_load_host_gpu(prefer, model, capability) -> bool:
    if prefer == "cpu":
        return False
    if is_powerinfer_model(model) or is_gpu_only_opt_in_model(model):
        return True
    if (capability in {CAP_CODE, CAP_LOGIC}
            and (model is None
                 or _is_configured_variant(model, DEEPSEEK_MODEL)
                 or _is_configured_variant(model, JOSIEFIED_CODER_MODEL)
                 or is_coding_model(model))):
        return True  # same as want_capability_gpu :1488–1493
    if model is None:
        return True
    if _is_configured_variant(model, QWYTHOS_MODEL):
        return False
    if any(_is_configured_variant(model, name) for name in GPU_MODELS):
        return True
    if is_coding_model(model):
        return True
    return False  # CPU-only / unknown pin
```

def _timeshare_powerinfer_procs(procs: list[str]) -> list[str]:

# comfyui-mcp integration plan for local_agent — 2026-09-04

## Decision record

Operator asked to install `https://github.com/artokun/comfyui-mcp` and
integrate it with **the custom Ollama-based `local_agent` project**
(`agent.py`/`tools.py`), not just as a Claude Code MCP config entry. Given
two options for scope, operator chose **full access** — generation, model
management (including deletion), custom-node install (git clone + pip
install), and ComfyUI process control (start/stop/restart) all wired in, not
scoped down to generation-only and not pointed at an isolated instance.

This is recorded explicitly because it's a real tension with standing rules
in `CLAUDE.md`: "One ComfyUI, ever," the stage supervisor owning process
lifecycle, `work/thermal_guard.py` gating GPU jobs, and "never destroy
evidence." Full access was still the operator's explicit choice after that
tension was raised — this doc is where that decision lives, not a place to
silently relitigate it. The design below keeps the letter of `tools.py`'s
"fixed whitelist, not a shell" model even while wiring in comfyui-mcp's full
surface: every comfyui-mcp action gets an explicitly named, individually
whitelisted `local_agent` tool. There is no raw "call any MCP tool"
passthrough — that would turn `tools.py` into an actual shell, which is the
one thing `CLAUDE.md` says not to do "for convenience."

## What comfyui-mcp actually is

A Node.js (>=22) MCP **stdio server** — not a Python library, not a REST
service by default. It talks to a locally running ComfyUI over ComfyUI's own
REST/WebSocket API, and exposes ~38 MCP tools: image/video/audio generation,
workflow authoring/validation/visualization, model search/download/delete,
custom-node search/install (registry + git clone + pip install), VRAM
control (`/free`), and **process control** (`restart_comfyui`
start/stop/restart, which finds and manages the ComfyUI process directly —
this is a second, independent lifecycle owner alongside this project's own
stage supervisor and `thermal_guard.py`).

`npx -y comfyui-mcp` is the normal invocation — no repo clone is required
for use, only for building from source. It speaks MCP (JSON-RPC over
stdio), which `local_agent` has never spoken before; `tools.py` is a flat
Python dict of `def foo(args: dict) -> str` functions dispatched by
`tools.call(name, args, ...)` — completely synchronous, no MCP client
exists anywhere in this codebase today (confirmed: no `asyncio` in
`agent.py`, concurrency is `ThreadPoolExecutor`-based).

## Architecture

## Architecture

### 1. `local_agent/mcp_client.py` (new)

A minimal, synchronous MCP stdio client — not a general-purpose MCP SDK,
just enough to drive this one server, matching the project's preference for
small dependency-free modules over heavy frameworks (see `context_compactor`,
`ollama_client` for the existing style).

- Spawns `npx -y comfyui-mcp` (or a pinned local install — decide during
  implementation whether `npx` fetching a possibly-newer version on every
  restart is acceptable, or whether to pin an exact version / vendor a
  local `node_modules` install for reproducibility) as a subprocess once,
  lazily, on first use. Kept alive across calls; not respawned per call.
- Speaks MCP's JSON-RPC-over-stdio handshake (`initialize`, `tools/list`,
  `tools/call`), with a lock around request/response so concurrent
  `ThreadPoolExecutor` tool calls don't interleave on the same stdio pipe.
- Bounded timeout per call (comfyui-mcp's own generation calls can run long
  — match or exceed `COMFYUI_MCP_STALL_S` semantics, don't impose a tighter
  ceiling that kills a legitimately slow render).
- Environment for the child process sets `COMFYUI_PATH`/`COMFYUI_URL`
  explicitly (see "Which ComfyUI instance" below) rather than relying on
  comfyui-mcp's own auto-detection, so there is no ambiguity about which
  installation it's driving.
- Logs go to stderr on the child process side already (per comfyui-mcp's
  own design, "safe for stdio transport") — capture and surface that
  through `local_agent`'s existing logging, not silently discarded.

### 2. New whitelisted tools in `local_agent/tools.py`

One `local_agent` tool per comfyui-mcp tool group (not one giant passthrough),
each a thin `def comfy_<group>(args: dict) -> str` wrapper calling
`mcp_client.call("<comfyui-mcp tool name>", args)` and formatting the
result the way every other tool in this file already does (string return,
same error-handling conventions as `stop_all_comfyui`/`start_batch_render`
next to it). Suggested grouping, mirroring comfyui-mcp's own tool
consolidation:

| local_agent tool | wraps comfyui-mcp tool(s) |
|---|---|
| `comfy_generate` | `generate_image` (all actions: image/controlnet/ip_adapter/video/3d/upscale/remove_background/audio) |
| `comfy_workflow` | `enqueue_workflow`, `queue`, `create_workflow`, `visualize_workflow`, `get_workflow`, `save_workflow` |
| `comfy_assets` | `get_image`, `upload_image` |
| `comfy_models` | `download_model`, `list_local_models` (deletion capability lives here — see guardrail below) |
| `comfy_nodes` | `search_custom_nodes`, `install_custom_node`, `node_pack` |
| `comfy_system` | `get_system_stats`, `clear_vram`, `get_history`, `comfy_cli` |
| `comfy_process` | `restart_comfyui` (start/stop/restart — see guardrail below) |

Add all seven to `TOOLS`. Add `comfy_process` and `comfy_nodes` to
`PROJECT_ONLY_TOOLS` at minimum (process control and arbitrary node
install are not things a casual/general conversation turn should be able to
trigger incidentally) — decide during implementation whether the others
need the same treatment or are safe as general tools. None of the seven
belong in `CONCURRENCY_SAFE_TOOLS` — they all talk to a single shared
ComfyUI instance and the single shared MCP subprocess.

### 3. Which ComfyUI instance — the one open question that needs an explicit operator pick before writing code

The operator chose "full access," not "point it at a separate instance,"
but *which* ComfyUI install this targets was not asked as a separate
question and still needs a real answer, because this repo's ComfyUI-shared
tree includes Equal Shares' paused evidence:

- If `COMFYUI_PATH`/`COMFYUI_URL` points at the same install/data dir
  `local_agent`'s own `work/image_render.py` already renders story images
  against, `comfy_models`'s delete action and `comfy_nodes`'s install
  action can touch files in that shared tree, and `comfy_process`'s
  restart can race the stage supervisor for port 8188. `CLAUDE.md`'s "One
  ComfyUI, ever" becomes a real, not theoretical, collision risk the
  moment both `local_agent`'s existing render dispatch and a comfyui-mcp
  call are live at the same time.
- Concretely: `A:\Users\rhine\ComfyUI-Shared\output\...` is where Equal
  Shares evidence lives per `CLAUDE.md`. Confirm with the operator whether
  `COMFYUI_PATH` for this integration should point at that same shared
  install (accepting the collision risk, mitigated by never running both
  at once) or a distinct ComfyUI checkout/data directory reserved for
  general local_agent image work, keeping Equal Shares' tree completely
  out of reach of `comfy_models(remove)`/`comfy_nodes(install)` by
  construction.
**Decided, 2026-09-04: the same shared install** —
`A:\Users\rhine\ComfyUI-Shared\...`, the one Equal Shares' paused evidence
lives under and `local_agent`'s own `work/image_render.py` already renders
against. Operator explicitly accepted the collision risk described above on
the condition that comfyui-mcp and `local_agent`'s own render dispatch are
never run at once. `COMFYUI_PATH`/`COMFYUI_URL` should be set to that exact
path explicitly in the MCP subprocess environment (not left to comfyui-mcp's
own auto-detection) so there's no ambiguity about which installation is
targeted. Because this is the shared, evidence-bearing tree, the runtime
guardrails in the next section are not optional polish — they are the only
thing standing between "full access" and an accidental collision with the
stage supervisor or Equal Shares' evidence.

### 4. Runtime/lifecycle guardrails to build in regardless of "full access"

"Full access" was about *which tools get wired in*, not about removing
this project's own safety plumbing. Concretely:

- `comfy_process` (`restart_comfyui`) must check `work/thermal_guard.py`'s
  current state and the stage supervisor's own liveness (same checks
  `stop_all_comfyui`/`start_batch_render` in `tools.py` already do) before
  acting, and must refuse if the stage supervisor currently owns the
  process — two independent things starting/stopping the same ComfyUI is
  exactly the failure mode "One ComfyUI, ever" was written to prevent.
- `comfy_models` deletion and `comfy_nodes` install should log what they
  did somewhere durable (this project's existing pattern: a CHANGELOG
  entry per session, not silent) since both are effectively irreversible
  or code-execution-risk actions.
- `comfy_generate` also appends `local_agent/runtime/comfy_mcp_audit.jsonl`
  on every call (desktop agent or a Grok probe script): timestamp, caller
  (pid / script / function), args, `prompt_id`. Generate is not
  irreversible in the delete/install sense, but without this log a probe
  mug in the shared output folder cannot be distinguished from an
  operator job.
- None of this should be allowed to touch anything under the Equal Shares
  paused tree, however "Which ComfyUI instance" above gets answered.

### 4b. `filename_prefix` on `generate_image` — MCP limitation, not our wrapper

Live 2026-09-04 mug probes passed `filename_prefix` (`mcp_live_verify_20260904`,
`vram_phase_probe_20260904`). ComfyUI wrote `ComfyUI_00214_.png` /
`ComfyUI_00215_.png`. History for prompt_id `8182b9d1-…` shows SaveImage
node 7 with `"filename_prefix": "ComfyUI"`.

This is **comfyui-mcp 0.52.x**, not a drop in `tools.comfy_generate` and
not ComfyUI ignoring a correctly-set SaveImage widget:

- `dist/tools/generate-image.js` action `"image"` calls `generateImage({
  prompt, width, height, steps, cfg, sampler, scheduler, seed,
  checkpoint, batch_size })` — **`filename_prefix` is not passed**.
  The same file *does* pass `filename_prefix` for actions `"audio"`,
  `"video"`, and `"remove_background"`. The Zod field description names
  only those three actions.
- `dist/services/workflow-composer.js` `buildTxt2Img` / `buildImg2Img`
  hardcode `filename_prefix: "ComfyUI"`. ControlNet / IP-Adapter /
  upscale similarly hardcode `ComfyUI_controlnet` / `ComfyUI_ipadapter`
  / `ComfyUI_upscale`.
- Official docs (comfyui-mcp.artokun.io generate_image parameters):
  `filename_prefix` is documented as applying to audio, video, and
  remove_background only.

Do **not** work around this inside `comfy_generate` (rewriting the MCP
graph would fork their composer). Probe scripts that need isolated files
enqueue their own graph via `local_agent/mcp_test_output.py`
(`SaveImage` prefix `mcp_test/<stem>`). Operator generation is unchanged.

## Implementation steps (for whoever has real shell access — this plan was
written without it; see the handoff note below)

1. Confirm Node >=22 is installed on DuranGamingPC (`node --version`); install
   or update if not — do not assume.
2. Answer the "Which ComfyUI instance" question above with the operator
   before setting `COMFYUI_PATH`/`COMFYUI_URL` anywhere.
3. Write `local_agent/mcp_client.py` per the spec above. Unit-test it against
   a mocked stdio subprocess first (no live ComfyUI needed) — same pattern
   this project already uses for `ollama_client`/farm-task tests (mock the
   external process, don't require live infra for the base test suite).
4. Add the seven `comfy_*` tools to `tools.py`, `TOOLS`, and the appropriate
   whitelist sets.
5. Live-verify against a real running ComfyUI: at minimum `comfy_system`
   (read-only, lowest risk) first, then `comfy_generate` with one real
   render, before touching `comfy_models`/`comfy_nodes`/`comfy_process` live.
6. Update `local_agent/README.md`, `TODO.md`, and add a dated `CHANGELOG`
   entry per the standing pattern — cite the actual test run and the actual
   live verification, not just "should work."

It does not install anything, does not add `local_agent/mcp_client.py` or
the `comfy_*` tools yet, and does not answer the "Which ComfyUI instance"
question — that still needs the operator, and everything downstream in
"Implementation steps" needs real shell access this session doesn't have.

# local_agent/ — architecture audit

*2026-08-27. Static-code audit: every module below was read in full, not sampled or summarized from filenames. Every count is grep- or AST-verified against the current tree, not estimated. Where a claim could not be verified by reading code (e.g. concurrent-access behavior under real load), it is marked unverified rather than asserted — the project's own standard for evidence, applied here to the audit itself.*

*Scope note: an external architecture review already happened once, on 2026-08-24 (`docs/design_notes/architecture_review_response.md`). Its five accepted items became UPGRADE 12, which is still unbuilt. This audit does not repeat those five items; it looks at what that review missed, plus what has changed since.*

## System at a glance

`local_agent/` is no longer a small chat wrapper. Excluding the vendored Sideband/Reticulum source tree, it is **~50 top-level modules totaling 13,333 lines**, plus **51 test files totaling 4,753 lines**. It has grown across 23 sequential numbered upgrade prompts, most implemented by a different agent session than the one before it. That history is visible in the code: several of the findings below are exactly the shape you'd expect from independently-scoped upgrades landing in the same files without a shared abstraction being extracted afterward.

Two fan-in numbers matter for everything that follows: **13 modules import `router.py` directly**, and **3 import `tools.py`** (`agent.py`, `agentic_eval.py`, `server.py`). `router.py` is the de facto hub of the system; `tools.py` is not, because its role is a registry consumed almost entirely through one function, `call()`.

chunks.text:

Two fan-in numbers matter for everything that follows: **13 modules import `router.py` directly**, and **3 import `tools.py`** (`agent.py`, `agentic_eval.py`, `server.py`). `router.py` is the de facto hub of the system; `tools.py` is not, because its role is a registry consumed almost entirely through one function, `call()`.

## 1. Multimodal orchestration ↔ structured tool-calling pipeline

**What's solid.** `tools.call()` (tools.py:1787–1824) is a genuinely well-built chokepoint: it checks the tool exists, checks `ToolContext.permits()`, injects trusted fields the model can never forge (`__remote_render_identity`, `__remote_schedule_identity`) only from server-side context, audits every call through `remote_security.audit_tool()`, and converts every exception into a uniform `ERROR:` string rather than crashing the turn. `capabilities.py`'s gate-with-reason pattern (`{"available": bool, "reason": str, "install": str, "size": str}`) is applied consistently across every sensory tool. This part of the system is not the risk.

**The risk is `agent.answer()`.** It is one function, agent.py:671–1047, ~377 lines, and it is where every subsystem in the project actually meets: routing (`router.decide()`), GPU permission gating (`gpu_gate.request()`), task checkpointing (`agentic_state`), URL prefetch, project-doc retrieval prefetch, prior-chat retrieval prefetch, difficulty-based model escalation, exemplar prefetch, context trimming, the primary→fallback retry, legacy tool-call parsing, and the actual multi-hop tool loop — all interleaved by direct, sequential mutation of a shared `msgs` list and a shared `emit()` callback. There is no seam between "decide what context the model needs" and "run the model" and "enforce permissions." A change to any one of those eight concerns touches the same function.

A concrete symptom of the same pressure: **eight compiled regexes at module level** (`_START_CURRENT_RENDER_RE`, `_STOP_COMFYUI_RE`, `_ACCESS_BYPASS_RE`, `_UNVERIFIED_EXECUTION_RE`, `PROJECT_CONTEXT_RE`, `_PROJECT_MEMORY_LINE_RE`, `URL_RE`, `TOOL_RE`) implement a second, deterministic router that runs *before* the model ever sees the request, specifically for actions where the model's tool selection isn't trusted — starting a render, stopping ComfyUI, refusing an access-bypass request. This isn't a stylistic choice; it's evidenced necessity. `CHANGELOG/2026-08-27_optional_dep_guards_and_scheduler_live_pending.md` records the model choosing `start_current_chat_render` over `schedule_phone_messages` **for 26 consecutive messages** in one real conversation, because the tool description didn't say clearly enough "this is not rendering." The fix that day was a tool-description edit, not a structural one. That pattern — patch the description, add a regex escape hatch — doesn't scale linearly as more must-not-get-wrong tools are added; each one needs its own hand-authored classifier bolted onto `agent.py`.

## 2. Chroma DB memory persistence

**Correct the premise first.** Chroma is not the project's memory system; it's one of **four independent, non-communicating retrieval/memory subsystems**, each with its own storage format, its own relevance-scoring math, and its own dedup strategy:

| subsystem | file(s) | storage | scoring | gated by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| operator facts | `memory.py` (133 lines) | flat JSON, byte-capped | none (priority sort) | explicit "remember that…" |
| project docs | `retrieval.py` (360 lines) | JSON chunk index, mtime-keyed | BM25 (custom, ~35 lines) | none — read-only |
| prior chats | `chat_retrieval.py` (50 lines) | reads `store.py` JSON | term-overlap / √length (not BM25) | none — read-only |
| approved exemplars | `exemplar_embeddings.py` (200 lines) + curator/filter/lifecycle (334 lines) | Chroma `PersistentClient` | cosine similarity | human approval queue |

That's roughly 1,077 lines solving overlapping "find relevant context for this turn" problems four different ways, each independently reimplemented rather than sharing an interface. `retrieval.py` was in fact built with exactly this kind of extension in mind (`ScorerProtocol`, a stubbed `EmbeddingScorer` placeholder for a future embedding model) — but `chat_retrieval.py` and `exemplar_embeddings.py` didn't grow into that interface; they're separate code with separate math.

**The Chroma-specific code itself is careful.** Telemetry is explicitly disabled (`anonymized_telemetry=False`), the collection is created with the correct `hnsw:space: cosine` for normalized embeddings, writes to the JSON sidecar records use the same atomic tmp-then-replace pattern as the rest of the project, and — as of today, `CHANGELOG/2026-08-27_optional_dep_guards_and_scheduler_live_pending.md` — the two bare `import chromadb` statements are now guarded, with `agent.py`/`server.py` confirmed (by that entry's own test run) to still import when chromadb is absent. I re-read the current `exemplar_embeddings.py` directly rather than trusting the changelog claim: the guard is in place exactly as described.

chunks.text:
