### 7.3 Long-prompt limits

Audit token counts for every actual text encoder, including positive/negative branches. Many CLIP implementations have a 77-token context; model-specific encoders and ComfyUI chunking can behave differently. The verifier and generator may not see the same text if one truncates, errors, chunks, or uses another tokenizer. [TorchMetrics CLIP implementation](https://github.com/Lightning-AI/torchmetrics/blob/master/src/torchmetrics/functional/multimodal/clip_score.py)

Prefer short audit captions and per-criterion checks. For a long master prompt, log each encoder's actual tokenization and truncation behavior, test clause ordering, and keep a structured prompt compiler. YRIKKA's inspected CLIP scorer does not explicitly add a truncation option, so an overlong prompt can be an execution problem rather than a low alignment score.

### 7.4 Persistent evidence

Store immutable rows in GVD's SQLite state, keyed by job, attempt, image hash, workflow/model profile, rubric hash, and policy ID. Log raw scores with units; Qwen verdicts and evidence; WD14 tags; prompt text/hash; seed; timing; peak GPU/RAM; retry reason; and accepted/rejected/error status. Keep prompt-learning results in a separate experiments table with parent prompt revision and held-out outcome. The routing LLM reads these records but cannot rewrite earlier QA evidence or thresholds.

## 8. Strict VRAM strategy for 16GB

### 8.1 One GPU owner, not three competing model managers

Use GVD's machine-wide GPU lease across the entire transition. An in-process Python lock is insufficient if separate runners can launch GPU work. Use a Windows named mutex or a shared file-lock implementation with crash recovery and worker ownership records.

| Phase | Allowed GPU owner | Other model processes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Plan | Routing LLM, only if needed | Generation and GPU verifiers unloaded/stopped |
| Generate | Diffusion worker | Ollama unloaded; Qwen/ImageReward workers stopped; WD14 CPU-only |
| Fast QA | Prefer dedicated CPU QA worker | Diffusion released; no GPU LLM/verifier |
| Qwen QA | Isolated Qwen worker | Generation/ImageReward unloaded or stopped; routing LLM unloaded |
| Reward QA | Isolated ImageReward worker, or validated CPU worker | Qwen stopped; generation unloaded; routing LLM unloaded |
| Commit | CPU agent | No new GPU allocations |

Start with a 2GiB device headroom reserve, then adjust using measured transient peaks and display usage. Admission requires a locally measured profile that fits observed free VRAM plus its workspace, KV cache, image tokens, activations, and decode buffers. Also budget host RAM for offload and multiple CPU workers. Model file size is not peak memory.

### 8.2 Transition procedure

1. Stop dispatch. Wait for the owned ComfyUI queue and active job to finish. Confirm there are no foreign jobs that would invalidate exclusivity.
2. Ensure the candidate PNG and stage journal are durable. Do not hold CUDA tensors in the agent between jobs.
3. Unload each GVD-owned Ollama model, then check `/api/ps` and device memory. Use an empty generate request with its exact model name and `keep_alive: 0`. Do not unload another user's model without ownership. [Ollama API](https://docs.ollama.com/api/generate)
4. Request ComfyUI unloading only while idle: `POST /free` with `{"unload_models": true, "free_memory": true}`. Validate support against the installed backend.
5. Check device-level free-memory telemetry repeatedly until stable; a 200 response is not proof of release. This cannot free allocations in Ollama, ONNXRuntime, llama.cpp, or another process.
6. YRIKKA and other ordinary custom-node models may survive in caches. Stop the dedicated verifier worker at phase exit for a dependable process-level release. If a generation worker cannot release enough memory, restart only that owned idle worker, at most once before blocking.
7. Start/admit the next phase only after observed free GPU and host RAM satisfy its calibrated profile. If memory remains occupied, return `RESOURCE_BLOCKED` rather than relying on Windows shared GPU memory or forced paging.

    response = session.post(ollama_url + "/api/generate", json={

        "keep_alive": 0}, timeout=(5, 60))

    response = session.get(comfy_url + "/queue", timeout=(5, 15))
    response.raise_for_status()

    response = session.post(comfy_url + "/free", json={
        "unload_models": True, "free_memory": True}, timeout=(5, 30))

### 8.3 GGUF: separate diffusion and vision-language paths

**Diffusion GGUF:** Use an exact supported ComfyUI-GGUF model/loader combination and ComfyUI's validated offload settings. This is not llama.cpp's layer-offload mechanism. Quantized transformer weights can reduce residency, but dequantization and activations still require memory. Do not force all encoders/models onto `cuda:0`. [ComfyUI-GGUF](https://github.com/city96/ComfyUI-GGUF)

**Qwen GGUF:** YRIKKA's inspected Qwen loader uses Transformers/Outlines and FP16; it does not accept a GGUF path or `n_gpu_layers`. For GGUF, register a separate `qwen_gguf` implementation using a compatible vision-capable llama.cpp/Ollama backend and a matching vision projector. It must emit the same checklist report, with its own profile and calibration. Do not drop a GGUF file into the existing loader and assume it works.

For a compatible pinned llama.cpp build, the offload controls include `--n-gpu-layers` and `--no-mmproj-offload`. A conservative CPU-first launch profile has zero GPU layers and the projector on CPU; increase GPU layers only during the isolated QA phase after profiling. A matched model/projector and actual image-input smoke test are mandatory. [llama.cpp server options](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/tools/server/README.md)

## 10. Rollout and verification

1. Record backend commit, `/object_info`, custom-node versions, model hashes, Python/Torch/CUDA/Outlines versions, and device/RAM telemetry. Compare the actual local code with this blueprint.
2. Add the report adapters and history parser. Test synthetic pass/fail/error reports before loading any new GPU model.
3. Run the fast QA graph on approved sample images. Confirm units, single-image semantics, tag export, and CPU provider behavior.
4. Validate Qwen criterion accuracy, model loading, structured output, and process release on the RTX 5080. Test complex spatial scenes and trait-to-person binding.
5. Profile ImageReward separately. Calibrate thresholds and freeze profiles on held-out GVD images.
6. Enable bounded reroll in `master_batch_runner.py`, then enforce receipt/hash checks in `generate_video.py`.
7. Run PromptTester experiments separately and promote prompt revisions only after held-out evaluation.

Reference-code checks completed while preparing this blueprint: seven mocked tests pass for low-CLIP reroll, Qwen rejection reroll, uncertainty blocking, attempt-budget exhaustion, malformed/non-finite scores, stale/Boolean-invalid reports, and changed-image rejection. Tests use synthetic scores and mocked workers, not GPU inference. Custom nodes, ComfyUI history behavior on the installed backend, model accuracy, process eviction, and end-to-end I2V still require local tests.

Required local fault tests additionally include: unknown node class; missing model; overlong CLIP caption; API submission accepted but connection lost; worker crash after candidate save; `/free` returning while an unmanaged model remains resident; ONNX unexpectedly using CUDA; zero available VRAM headroom; and I2V attempting to bypass acceptance.

chunks.text:
# GVD Tool Router and Workflow Discovery Specification

Version: 1.0 · Research date: 2026-09-21 · Project: Local AI / Generalized Video Director

Target: Windows workstation, NVIDIA RTX 5080 with 16GB VRAM, ComfyUI 0.36.0, Ollama. Treat the installed ComfyUI version as user-reported until local inventory confirms its backend commit. Desktop, frontend, and backend versions are distinct.

Status: Architectural specification with Python reference contracts and discovery orchestration. No workflows, checkpoints, or custom nodes were installed on the workstation in preparing this document. Hardware compatibility and performance remain unmeasured locally. The names below are GVD interfaces, not claims that those exact nodes already exist in ComfyUI.

## 1. Architectural decision

GVD selects a **capability**, resolves it to an immutable, validated **workflow implementation**, and schedules its stages through a single GPU owner. A narrative scene can be a composition of still generation, image-to-video, lip-sync, repair, and assembly. Each GPU stage is a discrete ComfyUI API workflow; the scene-level tool orchestrates their dependency graph.

Separate four concerns:

1. **Planner:** Ollama converts narrative intent into a typed shot manifest and explicit constraints. It cannot invent installed node types, change security policy, or activate downloads.
2. **Registry and router:** Deterministic code filters implementations by capability, compatibility, resource measurements, and quality requirements before scoring candidates.
3. **Scheduler and executor:** A persistent dependency graph, GPU lease, ComfyUI API adapter, artifact store, and quality gates manage execution and recovery.
4. **Discovery and validation:** Web search proposes candidates. Quarantine, isolated validation, and a promotion controller determine whether candidates enter the executable registry.

Generation remains local. Search sends generic capability and hardware queries, never private scripts, reference faces, or media. Hosted-model workflows are ineligible under the default `local_only` policy.

| `execute_continuous_take` | Extend an unbroken take from accepted temporal context | LongCat-Video continuation; MiniMax H3 FL2VA; Ref2VA only where its exact graph supplies required continuation controls | Reference conditioning alone does not guarantee exact first/last frames or motion continuation. |
| `execute_montage_morph` | Deliberate visual transformations across a prompt schedule | AnimateDiff-Evolved plus FizzNodes prompt scheduling | Prompt embedding interpolation is not a guarantee of geometry-preserving latent morphing. |
| `execute_fast_action` | Drafts, B-roll, establishing shots, action candidates | LTX-2.3; FastH3 with exact version and supported input mode | Short inference time does not establish superior physical accuracy. Test action fidelity separately. |

All four interfaces exist in the initial catalog even when no implementation is active. If every implementation is disabled, return `UNAVAILABLE_CAPABILITY` with reasons rather than pretending a workflow exists.

### 1.2 Research corrections that affect routing

**StoryDiffusion:** The upstream repository separates consistent image generation from its video motion predictor; its published low-memory demo describes testing on 24GB and expectations above 20GB. That does not prove the proposed compound workflow fits 16GB. Start with a candidate still-generation stage and measure it. [StoryDiffusion upstream](https://github.com/HVision-NKU/StoryDiffusion)

The ComfyUI wrapper combines several distinct identity methods. Its availability does not establish that arbitrary StoryDiffusion and IPAdapter attention patches compose correctly. Preserve separate implementation IDs for each tested combination. [ComfyUI StoryDiffusion](https://github.com/smthemex/ComfyUI_StoryDiffusion), [IPAdapter Plus](https://github.com/cubiq/ComfyUI_IPAdapter_plus)

**H3:** FL2VA and Ref2VA are separate model variants. The official integration catalog lists a 12–16GB quantized/offloaded path, but lists component sizes rather than an end-to-end RTX 5080 peak-memory measurement. Treat this as a promising candidate, not a validated profile. [MiniMax integration catalog](https://github.com/MiniMax-AI/awesome-minimax-h3-integration), [MiniMax H3 upstream](https://github.com/MiniMax-AI/MiniMax-H3)

**FastH3:** The Preview V1 announcement describes four-step, T2VA-only checkpoints. Current ComfyUI documentation instead describes an eight-step V2 checkpoint, T2V and first/last-frame I2V, no distilled Ref2VA, and ComfyUI 0.36.0 or later. These are different releases, not interchangeable settings. Pin the checkpoint, workflow, attention implementation, and step schedule together. The ComfyUI documentation also describes motion/audio quality tradeoffs, so speed cannot be used as a physics score. [FastH3 V1 announcement](https://haoailab.com/blogs/fasth3-preview/), [ComfyUI FastH3 guide](https://docs.comfy.org/tutorials/video/minimax/minimax-h3-fastvideo)

**LongCat and LTX:** Both are valid research targets. LTX-2.3 has official ComfyUI workflows; LongCat has upstream continuation support. Neither fact certifies a particular graph on this Windows installation. [LTX-2.3 guide](https://docs.comfy.org/tutorials/video/ltx/ltx-2-3), [LongCat-Video](https://github.com/meituan-longcat/LongCat-Video)

## 2. Files and runtime boundaries

Use configurable `GVD_ROOT`; do not assume the existing ComfyUI installation lives inside it.

| Relative path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `config/runtime.json` | Explicit ComfyUI/Ollama endpoints, GPU identity, approved environment paths |
| `registry/catalog.json` | Public tool names and all candidate implementation versions |
| `registry/active.json` | Atomic snapshot of executable implementations only |
| `registry/releases/<digest>/` | Immutable registry snapshots and rollback metadata |
| `workflows/approved/<digest>/` | API JSON, bindings, dependency lock, provenance |
| `quarantine/<sha256>/` | Downloaded bytes and discovery metadata; never a `custom_nodes` directory |
| `validation/<candidate>/<run>/` | Isolated-validation logs, measurements, outputs, verdicts |
| `assets/characters/<id>/<revision>/` | Reference images, wardrobe references, prop and appearance descriptions |
| `jobs/<project>/<shot>/<attempt>/` | Rendered API request, result manifest, media, quality report |
| `state/gvd.sqlite` | Job DAG, attempts, artifact hashes, leases, prompt IDs, discovery state |

Only the promotion service writes `active.json`. Only the GPU scheduler submits production jobs. Discovery has no production credentials or permission to install Python packages. Use a dedicated ComfyUI worker where practical; a shared GUI queue cannot provide an exclusive GPU guarantee unless its writers cooperate.

### 3.1 Load-time invariants

- The stage graph must be acyclic. Every input source, output binding, fallback ID, and asset reference must resolve. Detect fallback cycles separately.
- `active` requires policy and validation receipts, exact dependency hashes, a compatible runtime, and at least one local resource profile. Unknown memory is never interpreted as zero.
- Frame-count and dimension constraints belong to each workflow version. Do not apply one model's frame grid to another. Record requested and actual duration; reject rounding outside the manifest's tolerance.
- Model disk size, peak GPU allocation, and peak host RAM are separate measurements. Each model and custom node carries its own license record; open code does not imply unrestricted weights.
- Freeze each job to its registry digest. Promotion cannot change implementations underneath queued or running jobs.
- Separate identity reference support, first-frame support, last-frame support, video-context support, audio conditioning, and native audio output into individual capabilities.
- Use exact parameter binding into parsed JSON. Never interpolate a whole JSON file with string substitution, evaluate downloaded expressions, or let an LLM supply arbitrary node classes.

### 3.2 API JSON and template binding

A runnable API graph maps node IDs to objects containing `class_type` and `inputs`; visual-editor JSON commonly contains a node list and link/widget metadata. They are not interchangeable. UI-only candidates remain quarantined until exported through a compatible frontend or an explicitly tested converter. Do not guess widget positions.

The binder deep-copies an approved graph, checks its SHA-256, verifies each declared binding against `/object_info`, applies typed values, and validates the resulting graph. For an image parameter, resolve the approved asset, upload it if required, and bind the returned ComfyUI filename; do not pass an arbitrary Windows filesystem path supplied in a prompt.

The executor submits `{"prompt": graph, "client_id": client_id, "extra_data": {"gvd_attempt_id": attempt_id}}` to `/prompt`. Persist its `prompt_id`; use `/ws` for progress and `/history/{prompt_id}` for reconciliation and outputs. A successful queue response is not a successful render. Use only capabilities available in the installed backend. [ComfyUI server routes](https://docs.comfy.org/development/comfyui-server/comms_routes)

## 4. Scene-to-tool decision logic

### 4.1 Constraint precedence

Interpret the script once, then freeze its typed requirements. The classifier emits a confidence and evidence span for each inferred feature. User-specified manifest fields always outrank inferred ones. Unknown interpretation returns `NEEDS_MANIFEST_REVIEW`; it does not silently choose the fastest tool.

| Manifest signals | Route preference | Hard checks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Continuous camera movement, no cuts, accepted preceding clip | `execute_continuous_take` | Required start/context inputs, compatible duration, boundary-quality policy |
| Recurring cast across edits, fixed wardrobe/props | `execute_narrative_scene` | Character references and revision, composition, downstream I2V identity tests |
| Explicit dream/morph intent with keyframes | `execute_montage_morph` | Valid prompt schedule, matching timebase, constraints on intentional identity changes |
| Independent establishing/action/B-roll shot | `execute_fast_action` | Supported input mode and measured motion quality |
| Dialogue with visible mouth | Add `synthesize_dialogue` and `apply_lipsync`, or an audio-conditioned renderer | Audio precedes lip-sync; face track remains available and synchronized |
| Local artifact in an otherwise accepted clip | `repair_video` | Source clip, tracked mask, affected time interval, preservation requirements |

A continuous take featuring a named character must satisfy both constraints. Do not let a high motion score compensate for missing identity conditioning. If no implementation can satisfy the conjunction, return `NO_COMPATIBLE_TOOL` with the missing capabilities. Splitting a no-cut shot or turning a named character into anonymous B-roll requires an explicit manifest revision.

### 4.2 Routing flowchart

```mermaid

    A["Shot manifest"] --> B["Validate constraints and assets"]
    B --> C{"Complete and consistent?"}
    C -->|No| D["Manifest review"]

    F -->|No| G["Compatible fallback or discovery request"]

```

### 4.3 Router pseudocode

```text
route(manifest, registry_snapshot, inventory):
    validate manifest, references, timeline, and dependency graph
    required = explicit hard constraints + validated mode requirements
    candidates = active implementations compatible with preferred tool family
    for implementation in candidates:
        reject unless required is a subset of capabilities
        reject unless all stage inputs and dependencies resolve
        reject unless exact environment/model/node hashes match inventory
        reject unless local-only policy is satisfied
        select a locally measured profile covering this exact workload
        if none exists: emit PROFILE_REQUIRED; do not production-render
        reject unless every stage fits GPU, host RAM, and disk budgets
        reject unless profile meets manifest quality floors
    if candidates empty:
        evaluate declared fallback IDs with the SAME checks and a visited set
        enqueue generic discovery request if still empty
        return blocked decision with per-candidate rejection reasons
    rank by measured quality, latency, failure rate, and switching cost
    choose deterministic winner, breaking ties by implementation_id
    persist decision, registry digest, profile, and expanded stage DAG
```

Suggested initial scoring policy, applied only after hard filtering:

`score = 0.35*identity_fit + 0.30*motion_fit + 0.15*style_fit + 0.10*audio_fit + 0.10*reliability - 0.10*normalized_latency - 0.08*normalized_switch_cost`

These coefficients are design defaults, not research findings. Renormalize relevant quality weights from manifest priorities. A required dimension needs a measured minimum; missing measurements cannot receive an optimistic score. Calibrate on a small GVD evaluation set and retain the policy version with every decision.

### 4.4 Boundary verification and character continuity

For continuous extensions, store the accepted predecessor's final frame, a short tail window, audio tail, frame rate, color space, camera direction, and artifact hashes. Extract from the accepted intermediate, not a screenshot or preview. The next segment waits for predecessor acceptance.

Compare generated head/tail windows for cuts, flicker, color shift, motion direction and velocity, identity, wardrobe, and prop continuity. Use optical flow and image/identity metrics as signals; calibrated visual review remains necessary for ambiguous seams. No universal cosine or pixel threshold establishes continuity.

Deduplicate shared boundary frames only where the workflow contract says they overlap. Matching one endpoint does not establish matching velocity. A failed seam gets a bounded re-render with more context or a compatible model; a dissolve is allowed only if the manifest permits one.

For narrative scenes, maintain a character bible including full-body and clothing references. Face embeddings alone cannot verify clothing or objects. Generate and accept anchor stills before animation; then inspect first/middle/last frames and flagged intervals of each clip. Persist approved scene state at every cut so later shots cannot silently revert props or wardrobe.

## 5. Expanded workflow catalog

The following is a source-grounded shortlist, not a claim that every candidate is an industry standard or already production-ready. Every row begins disabled pending local validation. “Priority” is the proposed validation order.

| Area / priority | Source and integration | GVD role | Validation focus |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Narrative / P1 | [StoryDiffusion ComfyUI wrapper](https://github.com/smthemex/ComfyUI_StoryDiffusion) and [IPAdapter Plus](https://github.com/cubiq/ComfyUI_IPAdapter_plus) | Anchor stills, identity conditioning | Attention-patch compatibility; per-character masks; drift; 16GB feasibility |
| Stills / P1 | [FLUX upstream](https://github.com/black-forest-labs/flux) | Composition, image editing, Fill, depth/edge-guided stills | Match controls to exact model; measure quantized/offloaded configuration |
| Multi-character / P2 | [StoryDiffusion wrapper's MS-Diffusion and related identity modes](https://github.com/smthemex/ComfyUI_StoryDiffusion) | Multiple subjects with separate references | Identity swapping, clothing leakage, spatial placement; do not assume a single FLUX prompt solves identity |

For F5-TTS and ProPainter, upstream capability was verified but a deployable ComfyUI wrapper was not established by this research. Register them as `adapter_required`, not as existing executable API templates. If wrapped, the custom node calls an approved local service with typed inputs and a fixed endpoint, never a generic shell command. The service must participate in the same GPU lease.

### 5.1 Dialogue composition

Render dialogue first when the shot timing depends on speech. Store the original waveform, transcript, speaker ID, sample rate, and timing. Generate the shot from its audio where supported, or apply a dedicated lip-sync pass after video generation. Resample audio explicitly and preserve exact video timebase. Do not let both a native-audio model and a mux step produce competing dialogue tracks.

Benchmark lip-sync offline first. Live inference is a separate profile including preprocessing and output latency. A model capable of audio-driven mouth motion is not necessarily a complete real-time facial animation system.

### 5.2 Repair without full re-generation

The repair request identifies a source artifact, frame interval, mask track, desired change, and protected regions. Decode only the affected interval plus temporal handles. Track and refine masks, crop with spatial context where supported, inpaint the temporal window, and composite only inside the mask. Compare before/after boundaries and confirm that protected regions remain unchanged in the decoded intermediate.

Keep original lossless frames or a high-quality intermediate. Re-encoding a final compressed file can change pixels outside the mask even when the compositor preserves them. Distinguish “no full generative re-render” from “no final encoding.” ProPainter is an initial object-removal/repair candidate; arbitrary semantic replacement may need another temporally conditioned model. Independent per-frame image inpainting requires a flicker gate.

## 6. Autonomous web discovery

### 6.1 Search, evidence, and quarantine policy

Expose `discover_workflows(capability, hardware_profile, max_candidates)` to the local agent. Trigger it on a missing capability, an explicit upgrade request, or a configured maintenance interval. Do not discover/install during a render-critical section.

Use a configurable web-search adapter: a locally hosted SearXNG instance or an authenticated search API. Add GitHub repository/release/file API adapters for provenance. Civitai and Comfy workflow galleries are discovery sources; fetch assets only through supported, permitted download paths. Login failures, rate limits, or missing APIs yield `SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE`, not a browser/login bypass.

Example generic queries:

- `site:github.com ComfyUI video continuation RTX 5080 16GB workflow`
- `site:civitai.com ComfyUI LTX 2.3 16GB workflow`
- `site:comfyworkflows.com ComfyUI video inpainting workflow`
- `site:docs.comfy.org MiniMax H3 first last frame workflow`

Rate-limit searches, cache results for 24 hours, cap a run at 30 hits and 10 downloaded templates, and use bounded retry with backoff for HTTP 429/5xx. Record query, source URL, author, release/commit, publication time, retrieval time, file hash, and provenance chain. Dates and popularity affect ranking; they do not establish correctness.

Community benchmark records must contain GPU/VRAM, host RAM, OS, Torch/CUDA, attention kernel, exact model/quantization, resolution, frames/FPS, steps, reference count, offload/tiling, cold versus warm status, timing scope, peak memory, and output examples. Missing fields remain unknown. Separate author claims, independent reports, and GVD measurements. A 4090 or 5090 result may nominate a candidate but cannot validate the 5080 profile.

Treat fetched text as data, including README instructions and JSON metadata. Never execute installation instructions from a page. JSON can reference custom nodes with arbitrary behavior, so parsing it successfully does not make it safe.

Required adapter behavior:

- **SecureFetcher and SourceResolver:** HTTPS only; approved exact hosts/download CDNs; reject credentials in URLs; verify DNS results and the connected peer are public addresses; block private/link-local/loopback destinations and metadata services; recheck redirects and prevent DNS rebinding. Enforce connection/read/total timeouts, decompressed-byte limits, and JSON content expectations. No archives, executable downloads, or model downloads in discovery.
- **StaticValidator:** Bounded JSON depth/node count; distinguish UI/API format; check node structures, typed links, outputs, graph cycles, model references, and declared bindings. Unknown classes go to dependency review. Reject dynamic code/eval/shell nodes, unapproved network nodes, remote loaders, and arbitrary filesystem destinations. An approved node class must also resolve to a pinned, reviewed implementation.
- **QuarantineStore:** Hash-derived directory names only; no source-supplied paths. Atomic creation, unique digest constraint, immutable downloaded bytes, separate append-only metadata. A duplicate download may add provenance without replacing bytes. The store adds UTC timestamps itself.
- **ValidationQueue:** Durable jobs with unique candidate/profile keys. Reconcile `validation_pending` records periodically so a crash between marking and enqueueing does not lose work. Quarantine errors are not activation grants.

### 6.3 Local validation and automatic promotion

Candidate lifecycle: `discovered → quarantined → static_pass → validation_pending → validated → active`. Failures go to `rejected` or `disabled` with a reason; never directly to active.

1. Resolve node source and model provenance; pin commits and hashes. Inspect package changes, entry points, dependency constraints, and license records. No model loader may enable remote code implicitly.
2. Run dependency installation/import tests in a disposable environment with no production secrets or personal folders. A virtual environment alone is not a security sandbox. On Windows, use an appropriately isolated worker/VM with restricted filesystem and network access; if safe GPU isolation is unavailable, hold novel executable code for review. Do not auto-test it inside production ComfyUI.
3. Validate API graph and node schemas against an isolated backend. Smoke-test the smallest supported workload, then benchmark actual target profiles under the GPU lease.
4. Capture cold/warm latency, GPU/host memory peaks, failures, artifacts, and quality reports. Run at least three representative samples including difficult identity/motion/audio cases relevant to the capability.
5. Promotion requires matching dependencies, local resource fit, minimum quality, and no disallowed regression on the GVD evaluation set. Templates using already approved nodes/models can promote automatically after these gates. New executable packages require a code-trust receipt from the configured review process before automatic integration.
6. Build a new immutable registry snapshot and activate it atomically between jobs. Retain the previous snapshot. Roll back on regression; jobs already started keep their original snapshot and assets.

Community scores only prioritize validation. New workflow text cannot alter promotion thresholds, allowlists, or permitted hosts. Discovery records an upgrade proposal even when promotion is blocked.

## 7. Memory and VRAM flip-flop controller

### 7.1 Resource policy for 16GB

Use MiB from actual device telemetry rather than assuming all advertised VRAM is available. Proposed starting headroom: **2,048 MiB** for display/driver activity and transient allocations, increased if measured peaks fluctuate. This is a design margin, not a benchmark result.

Cold admission after releasing prior models requires:

`profile.peak_gpu_mib + headroom_mib <= observed_free_gpu_mib`

Define `peak_gpu_mib` as the additional worker footprint above its idle baseline during a cold target-profile run, including the workflow's models, activations, and decode. Capture whole-device peak usage as a cross-check. Warm admission needs a separately measured incremental profile or a conservative total-budget test; do not double-count already resident model memory against free VRAM.

Host-RAM admission likewise uses observed available RAM minus an OS reserve and includes checkpoint loading, offloaded tensors, decoded frames, and audio buffers. Detect installed RAM during inventory. Disk space checks cover checkpoints, temporary frames, and output attempts. Swapping into the Windows pagefile is not an accepted normal execution strategy.

Never reserve all 16GB for diffusion while Ollama remains resident. Plan a batch, unload the planner model, run GPU stages, then reload Ollama if needed. A small CPU planner is an optional alternative if latency permits. Ollama's generate API supports `keep_alive: 0` for immediate unloading. [Ollama generate API](https://docs.ollama.com/api/generate)

A small CPU planner is an optional alternative if latency permits. Ollama's generate API supports `keep_alive: 0` for immediate unloading. [Ollama generate API](https://docs.ollama.com/api/generate)

### 7.2 Scheduling without breaking continuity

Batch means **sequential jobs sharing model residency**, not multiple videos in a tensor batch. Start with GPU batch size one.

Only stages whose dependencies and input artifacts are accepted enter the ready set. Group that set by the hash of actual checkpoints, encoders, VAEs, LoRAs, attention patches, precision, and worker environment. A shared public tool name is insufficient: two H3 variants may need different models.

Choose the ready group with the best combination of deadline, job age, critical-path impact, and saved load time. Keep the current family for a bounded quantum, initially four shots or fifteen minutes of completed work; never interrupt an active shot just to meet the quantum. Increase age priority to prevent starvation.

Example: Generate ready LTX B-roll, unload it, generate a StoryDiffusion anchor group, accept its stills, then animate the newly ready I2V shots together. A continuation segment cannot leap ahead of its predecessor just because its checkpoint is already loaded. Preserve edit order in the output timeline independently of generation order.

### 7.3 Model switch protocol

```text
switch_to(target_family):
    acquire machine-wide cooperative GPU lease
    stop dispatching new production work
    wait for the owned worker's running and pending queue to become empty
    if foreign jobs exist: wait or report resource contention; do not clear them
    unload any GVD-managed Ollama GPU model; verify device telemetry
    POST ComfyUI /free {"unload_models": true, "free_memory": true}
    poll queue and memory until stable or timeout
    if residual allocations prevent admission:
        restart only the owned idle worker once, reconcile state, re-measure
    if target profile still fails resource admission: return RESOURCE_BLOCKED
    submit one target-family job and measure load + inference + decode peaks
    retain family only while the scheduler benefits from its residency
```

`/free` is a memory-release request, not proof that all CUDA allocations are gone or that another process released its models. Verify its exact behavior against the installed backend source and API during bootstrap; the current upstream source and route documentation are reference material, not a substitute for the 0.36.0 runtime check. [ComfyUI source](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/blob/master/server.py)

Calling `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` in the router process cannot free tensors owned by the ComfyUI process. Also, ComfyUI unloading cannot release Ollama's GPU allocations. A worker restart is a recovery mechanism for retained custom-node allocations, not a per-shot routine.

Calling `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` in the router process cannot free tensors owned by the ComfyUI process. Also, ComfyUI unloading cannot release Ollama's GPU allocations. A worker restart is a recovery mechanism for retained custom-node allocations, not a per-shot routine.

### 7.4 Precision, offload, and attention policy

- Use only quantization/attention/tiling settings supported by the exact workflow and measured on this runtime. Blackwell support must include the actual kernel execution test; successful Python import is insufficient.
- Begin with the installed PyTorch attention path as the reference. Treat SageAttention, VSA, NVFP4, and other optimized kernels as separate candidate profiles. Never install a global attention override based solely on another GPU's speed claim.
- Text encoding, diffusion, and VAE decode may have different memory peaks. Prefer staged loading, CPU offload, and validated tiled decode. Test quality changes caused by quantization and tiling.
- Cache text embeddings only with a cache key covering encoder/model/tokenizer revisions, prompt, reference inputs, precision, and preprocessing. Avoid persistent GPU caches by default. Cache model-specific latents only with their full provenance.
- Stream decoded frames to disk and use bounded temporal windows for repair. Avoid keeping a full uncompressed movie in RAM.

### 7.5 OOM and failure policy

| Failure | Response |
| --- | --- |
| Missing node/model or hash mismatch | Disable the affected implementation; emit dependency report; evaluate compatible fallback |
| CUDA OOM | Release owned resources; invalidate the failed profile for that workload; retry only with a prevalidated lower-memory profile |
| No compatible kernel | Return to a previously validated attention backend; never blindly patch the production environment |
| Quality failure | Retry with bounded seed/prompt changes, or route a localized repair; retain original and failed artifacts |
| Ambiguous submission timeout | Reconcile queue/history by attempt metadata before resubmitting; otherwise hold for review to prevent duplicate renders |
| WebSocket disconnect | Reconnect and reconcile by prompt ID; do not treat disconnection as render failure |
| Worker crash | Mark attempt interrupted, restart only the owned worker, reconcile outputs, then retry within budget |
| No acceptable fallback | Return blocked shot with unmet constraints and discovery proposal |

Default attempt budget: initial render plus two retries; at most one owned-worker restart per shot. These are configurable limits. A resolution reduction, duration shortening, cut insertion, audio replacement, or loss of identity constraints is permitted only when named in `allowed_degradations`. Fewer sampling steps generally reduce time; do not assume they solve peak memory.

## 8. Verification and acceptance gates

### 8.1 Bootstrap inventory

The local implementation records: GPU name and memory; CUDA capability; driver; installed Torch/CUDA; Python; ComfyUI backend commit; custom-node commits; model hashes; disk/RAM availability; actual endpoints; and `/object_info` schema. Preserve the existing production environment and lockfile before adding anything. Do not copy historical CUDA/Torch pins from an old model README into a Blackwell installation.

Preserve the existing production environment and lockfile before adding anything. Do not copy historical CUDA/Torch pins from an old model README into a Blackwell installation.

### 8.2 Required tests

| Test | Passing result |
| --- | --- |
| Four-family routing | Independent B-roll, named-character cuts, an uninterrupted extension, and a keyed dream montage select appropriate eligible implementations |
| Combined constraints | A continuous take with strict identity blocks if no active workflow supports both |
| Version separation | FastH3 V1 T2VA cannot accept FL2VA/Ref2VA requests; V2 capabilities reflect its own verified graph |
| Unknown VRAM | Candidate cannot enter production without a local matching profile |
| Scheduling | Ready shots group by model family; a dependent extension never runs before its predecessor is accepted |
| GPU ownership | Ollama and ComfyUI do not simultaneously exceed budget; foreign jobs are not interrupted |
| Discovery attack fixtures | Reject malicious URLs, redirects to local addresses, duplicate keys, oversized/deep JSON, path traversal, shell/eval nodes, and instructions embedded in metadata |
| UI workflow fixture | Staged for compatible API export, never submitted as an API prompt |
| Crash recovery | An interrupted discovery enqueue is reconciled; an ambiguous prompt submission does not create duplicate work |
| Registry rollback | A failed candidate can be removed atomically while in-flight jobs retain their pinned snapshot |
| Repair preservation | Protected decoded regions, source audio, timing, and unaffected shots are preserved |
| End-to-end sample | A short mixed scene renders, passes quality gates, assembles in narrative order, and records full provenance |

For each approved resource profile, measure a cold run and at least three warm runs at its claimed workload. Save median latency, maximum observed GPU/RAM usage, and quality artifacts. Test both a within-budget and an intentionally blocked oversized request. Do not extrapolate one tiny smoke test to production resolution, long duration, or extra references.

Quality evaluation includes identity/wardrobe/prop continuity, motion plausibility, flicker, seamless continuation where requested, dialogue accuracy and lip-sync, and final media integrity. Automatic metrics nominate failures; they do not establish human-quality equivalence by themselves.

## 9. Implementation milestones and handoff

| Milestone | Concrete deliverable | Completion gate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M0: Inventory | `runtime.json`, environment/model lock, node-schema snapshot | Existing installation reproduced and GPU budget measured |
| M1: Registry/executor | Typed loader, API binder, persistent attempts and results | One existing known-good local workflow executes and reconciles |
| M2: Router/scheduler | Four public tool interfaces, stage DAG, GPU lease, bounded fallbacks | Routing and scheduling tests pass without new models |
| M3: Initial profiles | Validated implementations covering the four families where feasible | Local quality/resource evidence; unsupported families visibly blocked |
| M4: Discovery | Search adapters, quarantine store, static validator, durable validation queue | Malicious/invalid fixtures blocked and valid JSON staged |
| M5: Promotion | Isolated validation, policy receipts, atomic activation and rollback | Approved candidate integrates automatically without production mutation during a job |
| M6: Production extensions | Dialogue, lip-sync, mask tracking and repair | Mixed scene assembles with preserved continuity and timing |

Implement M0–M2 around the workstation's existing successful workflow first. This establishes the control plane before large model downloads. Then validate LTX and the still/identity stack, followed by montage and continuation candidates; fit and quality determine activation, not the order listed in a model catalog.

The next local-agent task is to read this specification, inspect the actual GVD repository and any `AGENTS.md`, compare its existing interfaces to these contracts, and implement M0–M2 in the project's normal development workflow. It must report mismatches and verify this specification against installed code before applying changes. Do not claim M3–M6 complete merely because registry entries or documentation exist.

## 10. Deliverable boundary

This specification supplies the registry data classes, routing logic and flowchart, source-linked candidate catalog, discovery function and adapter contracts, quarantine/promotion design, and memory-switching strategy. It intentionally contains no fabricated ComfyUI workflow graphs, benchmark numbers, installed-node inventories, or model hashes. Those become concrete artifacts during local inventory and validation.

chunks.text:
# MiniMax H3 prompt rules — the definitive spec for this project

Supersedes `docs/PROMPT_STYLE_RULES.md`, `docs/PROMPT_REPETITION_RULE.md`, and the
prompt sections of `docs/MINIMAX_H3_PROMPT_OPTIMIZATION.md`. Those were written
before the official guides were read; where they disagree with this file, this
file wins.

Sources, **captured verbatim in `docs/reference/`** so nothing depends on network
access:

| Local copy | Origin |
|---|---|
| `docs/reference/COMFYUI_MINIMAX_H3_TUTORIAL.md` | <https://docs.comfy.org/tutorials/video/minimax/minimax-h3> |
| **`docs/reference/MINIMAX_PROMPT_GUIDE_ref.md`** | MiniMax official R2V guide — **governs this project** |
| `docs/reference/MINIMAX_PROMPT_GUIDE_base.md` | MiniMax official base-mode guide |

Everything here is either quoted from those guides or was established by a
render on this machine. Where it came from a render, that is stated.

---

## 1. The format

R2V prompts have **six named sections, in this order**. Not five, not reordered.

```
subject_definitions:
summary:
retention_analysis:
detailed_description:
overall_soundscape:
non_diegetic_music:
```

### Reference labels

| Label | Use for |
|---|---|
| `<Subject N>` | reusable visible content — a person, a set, a costume, a style |
| `<Picture N>` | an image acting as a **concrete frame anchor**: first frame, keyframe, last frame |
| `<Video N>` | a whole-video relationship — editing, continuation, temporal structure |
| `<Audio N>` | an audio asset that is copied or referenced |

Tags follow **the order the inputs were connected**, which is why the ordered
`ref_audios` arrays in `audio_pass_config.json` matter and why `09B` and `09C`
are wired differently despite both being Kent and Avery.

**An identity-only image does not get a `<Picture N>` entry.** Cite it inside
the `<Subject N>` definition instead. Standalone picture entries are for frame
anchors only.

Limits: 9 reference images, 3 reference videos, 3 standalone audio clips. This
film's worst case is 3 speakers in `27E`, so there is no headroom for a fourth.

## 2. `retention_analysis` — the section that fixed the doubled voice

**This is the most important discovery in the project.** Every reference gets a
line declaring what relationship it has to the output.

Visible content: `fully_preserved`, `partially_preserved`, `attribute_transfer`,
`weak_reference`.

Audio: `fully_copy`, `partially_copy`, **`reference`**, `weak_reference`.

For a voice-timbre master the marker is always `reference`:

```
<Audio 1>: reference - S1 follows <Audio 1>'s voice timbre, pitch, accent, and
delivery without copying the original signal; none of its words, breaths, or
room tone appear in the target video.
```

**Why it matters.** For weeks every Narrator take carried a quieter second vocal
layer underneath, and no amount of prose forbidding echo, chorus, or duplication
removed it. The prompts had no `retention_analysis` at all, so nothing ever told
H3 the master was a reference rather than a source to copy — and a partial copy
of the master laid under freshly generated speech is precisely what that sounds
like. Adding the section removed the doubling on the first attempt.

The guide states the rule directly: *"When only timbre, rhythm, emotion, or
delivery is referenced, do not carry the original dialogue from the reference
audio into the target video."*

---

## 3. Dialogue

### One scripted line, one `<d>` block

```
<d>[English] If all people feel that someone without should be helped so they
are no longer without, but in the process they become without, how do people
really help each other?</d>
```

**Never split a line across two quoted fragments or two beats.** Two quoted
strings read as two separate utterances, and H3 fills the seam between them with
speech-shaped noise.

Observed on `00B`: a hand-written prompt split the line at
`…so they are no longer without,` / `but in the process…`, and the render
produced about a second of gibberish at exactly that seam.

### Quotation marks mean on-screen text, not speech

Double quotes are reserved for lettering actually rendered in frame. Speech goes
in `<d>`. This inverts the project's long-standing rule, which existed because
the old format had no `<d>` tag.

Quote marks must also be stripped from stage direction — `00M` once carried
`his expression cools on the word "but"`, which is performable as dialogue.

### Speaker IDs

Stable `(S1)`, `(S2)`, numbered by order of first vocal event and reused
everywhere. When a defined subject speaks, write `<Subject 1> (S1)`.

`his expression cools on the word "but"`, which is performable as dialogue.

### Speaker IDs

Stable `(S1)`, `(S2)`, numbered by order of first vocal event and reused
everywhere. When a defined subject speaks, write `<Subject 1> (S1)`.

### Delivery goes BEFORE the tag. The mouth closes AFTER it.

This is the second render-confirmed rule, and it follows the guide's own
examples:

> `<Subject 3> (S1) jerks her hand back and, using the clear youthful voice
> timbre referenced from <Audio 1>, exclaims with light annoyance,
> <d>[English] Hey! Watch your dog!</d> **She closes her lips** and guards the
> cookie…`

> `<Subject 4> (S2) says in a casual young male voice with a playful tone…
> <d>[English] He just likes cookies more than me.</d> **He closes his mouth**
> into an apologetic smile…`

Two of the guide's three examples close the speaker's mouth in the clause
immediately after `</d>`.

**Anything describing voice or delivery placed after `</d>` reads as speech
still in progress.** On `00B`, the sentence `The Narrator's delivery cools.`
sat right after the tag and the model kept talking past the scripted words,
producing a tail of gibberish. Moving delivery before the tag and closing the
mouth after it is the fix.

So the shape is always:

```
<Subject 1> (S1) [action], using the voice timbre referenced from <Audio 1>,
in a [delivery] delivery, says: <d>[English] …</d> He closes his mouth and says
nothing further for the rest of the shot.
```

A speaker with more than one line gets `…and is silent until his next line`
instead, so the prompt never contradicts itself.

### Voiceover

Use the exact phrase `says in an off-screen voiceover`, and immediately after
the `<d>` block state that visible mouths stay closed.

---

## 4. Shots, beats and camera

**`[Shot N]` marks a CUT, not a beat.** A continuous take is a single `[Shot 1]`
with no timestamp. Later shots use `[Shot N] At MM:SS.mmm, the shot cuts to…`.

The project's old `[0-1 s]` / `[1-14 s]` bracket notation is **not** the model's
grammar. Timing inside one shot is expressed in prose — "holds for about a
second", "across roughly thirteen seconds".

Camera motion has a controlled vocabulary: `Static Shot`, `Push In`, `Pull Out`,
`Zoom In/Out`, `Pan Left/Right`, `Truck Left/Right`, `Tilt Up/Down`,
`Pedestal Up/Down`, `Arc Shot`, `Tracking Shot`, `Shake Slightly/Strongly`,
`POV`, `Roll Clockwise/Counterclockwise`. Optionally qualified with
`with small amplitude` / `with large amplitude` and `at slow speed` /
`at fast speed`. Write it as natural English inside the shot, not as trailing
labels.

Length: `detailed_description` runs 350–500 words for generation tasks, but
dialogue-dense content prioritises fitting the spoken timeline over word count.

## 5. Soundscape

`overall_soundscape` covers ambience, physical action sounds, and non-verbal
human sounds. Dialogue never appears here — it lives only in `<d>`.

`non_diegetic_music` is audience-only score. **For this film it is always
`N/A`** — the continuous score is added at assembly.

This project adds two house rules to `overall_soundscape` — one because the
doubling bug was expensive, one because the model fills unallotted time with
speech. See §8 for the evidence behind both.

> Most of this shot has no speech in it at all, and silence is correct wherever
> no line is assigned. Never more than one voice at a time: no second voice, no
> quieter duplicate, no echo, no reverb tail, no whisper, no chorus, and no
> backing vocal under the speaker. Once the assigned lines are finished the
> voices stop and only room tone continues to the final frame.

**Do not write "exactly one vocal layer is present at any moment".** That was
the original wording and it parses two ways; the wrong reading is "at every
moment there is one vocal layer", which invites continuous speech. State the
ceiling ("never more than one") and the silence separately.

---

## 6. Rules from this project that still hold

These predate the guides and were confirmed by renders here, not by MiniMax.

- **Every second must be accounted for.** Undirected time gets invented — `10B`
  had nothing scripted after 3 s and filled the room with 8–10 people.
- **Every countable action states its integer.** "They repeatedly offer the
  chair" gave one limp gesture; "exactly three offer-and-refusal exchanges, no
  more and no fewer" gave three.
- **Say each thing exactly once.** 73 of 78 clips once sent every line twice,
  once in the body and once in an appended audio lock.
- **Never describe something not in the shot.** Anything you tell the model to
  light, it may draw. A one-person shot must not carry an identity block
  describing three other people.
- **Name a discriminator between similar characters.** The two visitors wear
  near-identical suits; the standing one has a white pocket square.
- **Light interiors generously even when the mood is sombre.** The daylight
  driving clip `14D` is among the cleanest in the film; the dim interiors in
  scenes 13, 16 and 17 are the worst.
- **Never paste prompt text out of the CSV.** It wraps fields in quotes and
  doubles internal quotes. 0 of 7 quote-wrapped prompts were ever kept.

## 7. How the prompts are generated

`work/build_native_r2v_prompts.py` writes all 124 into
`outputs/equal_shares/prompts_native_r2v/`. It reads `story_config.json` for the
authoritative words and windows, the older prompt sets for scene prose, and
`omni_voice_master_map.json` for which characters have a voice master.

Verified after every run:

- 78 dialogue clips, **one `<d>` block per scripted line**, zero splits
- word-for-word fidelity against `dialogue_timing`, zero words added or dropped
- a mouth-closing clause immediately after **every** `</d>`
- no delivery or voice prose left after any `</d>`
- pronoun and verb agreement on every generated clause

Two bugs found by those checks and worth remembering:

1. `parse_sections` originally required headers to be fully capitalised, so
   `SHOT LIST and DIALOGUE TIMING` — with its lowercase "and" — was not
   recognised, and the first run produced 124 prompts containing **no dialogue
   at all**. Structural checks catch this; eyeballing one file does not.
2. The mouth-close clause was first appended to every line, telling a character
   with two lines to fall silent before speaking the second. It is now attached
   only to a speaker's final line.

## 8. Telling the model when to STOP — added 2026-08-15 after a third failure

Two earlier fixes (one `<d>` per line; mouth closes after the tag) did not stop
gibberish at the **end** of `00B`. Measuring the render explained why.

```
clip duration      15.1 s
scripted window    1.0 - 14.0 s
line               30 words -> ~9-11 s at a natural pace

render speech      0.74-5.53   6.15-8.05   8.68-10.44   |gap 0.95s|   11.39-14.93
```

The scripted line is finished by about **10.4 s**. Then comes the longest gap in
the clip, and then **3.5 more seconds of speech running to the final frame**.
The model delivered the line, found four seconds of unallotted time, and filled
it — because nothing in the prompt said the remainder is silent.

**The native single-shot format carries no timestamps**, so unless silence is
stated in prose the model has no instruction to stop. Two additions:

**1. State the stop explicitly, allowing for an early finish.**

> There is only one spoken line in this entire shot, and `<Subject 1>` delivers
> it at an unhurried natural pace. When the last line is finished — **however
> early in the shot that falls** — every voice stops. Nobody speaks, mutters,
> hums, sighs, or makes any vocal sound for the whole remainder of the shot, and
> the shot plays out on room tone alone. No extra words are invented to fill the
> remaining time.

The "however early that falls" clause is the important part. The script allots
13 seconds for a line that takes 10, and that gap is where invention happens.

**2. Fix an ambiguous sentence that was inviting the opposite behaviour.**

The soundscape previously read *"Exactly one vocal layer is present at any
moment."* The user spotted that this parses two ways, and the wrong reading is
"at every moment there is one vocal layer" — that is, someone is always talking.
Now split into a ceiling and a silence:

> Most of this shot has no speech in it at all, and silence is correct wherever
> no line is assigned. **Never more than one voice at a time**: no second voice,
> no quieter duplicate, no echo… Once the assigned lines are finished the voices
> stop and only room tone continues to the final frame.

**General lesson: state silence positively.** A prompt that only describes sound
gives the model no model of quiet, and H3 fills unallotted time with speech. Say
how many lines exist, and say that everything else is silent.

## 9. When the prompt cannot fix it — shorten the clip. Added 2026-08-15.

**Three prompt fixes failed on the same fault.** After §3's one-`<d>`-per-line
rule, §3's mouth-close rule, and §8's explicit stop instruction, `00B` still
produced fresh speech from the moment the scripted line ended until the final
frame. Different gibberish each time, the same position every time.

> ### CORRECTED 2026-08-17 — read this before believing the section below
>
> This section used to assert: *"H3 fills the clip. Asking it to synthesise
> several seconds of silence is fighting the architecture."* **That is not
> supported by the evidence.** Measured across the operator's 14 known-good
> clips:
>
> | clip | words | duration | speech | silence |
> |---|---|---|---|---|
> | `4_`.mp4` | 13 | 8.0 s | 3.5 s | **56%** |
> | `15.mp4` | 8 | 7.3 s | 5.4 s | 26% |
> | `2.mp4` | 17 | 9.4 s | 7.8 s | 17% |
>
> A clip that is **more than half silence** came out clean. A model that fills
> its window with invented speech could not produce that.
>
> What actually happened: the `00B` failures carried **two** faults at once — a
> prepended `AUDIO-FIRST REFERENCE JOBS` header (see
> `docs/GOLDEN_REFERENCE/README.md`) **and** a long duration. The duration was
> blamed, a whole doctrine was built on it, and the header went unnoticed for a
> week.
>
> **So section 9 is a precaution, not a cause.** Fitting the render to the line
> is still correct — it is cheaper, it removes a variable, and every good clip is
> short. It is not the explanation for gibberish, and it must not be used to
> dismiss a prompt-side fault. Section 10 is the tool that actually addresses
> mispronunciation.

### The measurement that settles it

| | |
|---|---|
| `00B` scripted duration | 15.0 s, 362 frames |
| line | 30 words |
| delivered pace | ~3.5 words/second, measured across three renders |
| speech actually needs | ~9 s |
| **unallotted tail** | **~6 s** |

And across the film: **72 of 78 dialogue clips allot 3 seconds or more beyond
what their lines take to say.** `00A` over-allots by 9.6 s, `00O` by 9.2 s. The
scripted durations were written for picture and pacing; nobody ever checked them
against speech length.

### The rule

**Never ask H3 for silence. Render only as long as the speech needs, and pad
silence at assembly.**

```
Stage 1 (soundtrack)   render audio_pass_frames from audio_pass_durations.json
Assembly               pad the accepted WAV with digital silence to the
                       scripted duration
```

`work/build_audio_pass_durations.py` computes this per clip at **2.5
words/second** with a **1.5 s** tail margin, snapping to the 17-frame grid. `00B`
goes from 362 frames to **345** and gets 0.63 s of padding at assembly.

*(Pace corrected 2026-08-17. It was 3.5 w/s, taken from a single bad `00B`
render. The 14 known-good clips run at a median of **2.75 w/s**, range 1.14–3.89,
so 3.5 was making every clip too short — the opposite of the intended safety
margin. 2.5 sits just under the observed median.)*

**The timeline is untouched.** Picture still runs its full scripted length; only
the soundtrack render is shortened, and the WAV is padded back to match. The film
is still 1266 s.

Two side benefits: silence added in an editor is *perfectly* silent, which is the
one thing a generative model cannot promise — and the pass costs **31% fewer
frames** overall, 6885 frames saved across 75 shortened clips.

### The general lesson

When three prompt revisions fail on the same fault in the same place, the fault
is probably not in the prompt. Ask what the model is structurally trying to do —
here, fill its output window — and change the shape of the request instead of the
wording.

## 10. The DURATION LADDER — how to retry gibberish and mispronounced words. Added 2026-08-18.

**Operator rule, verbatim:**

> "when generating audio and trying to get perfect English words (getting rid of
> gibberish or mispronounced words) use this generation pattern. Example start at
> 10 sec; if gen is bad (has mispronounced words) add a second. If that does not
> work go back to 10 and go down to 9 seconds. The pattern of generation to fix
> gibberish and mispronounced words is the following; 10, 11, 9, 12, 8, 13, 7 and
> so forth."

So from a base length **D**, rungs alternate outward, **up first**:

```
D    D+1    D-1    D+2    D-2    D+3    D-3    D+4    D-4
```

Implemented once, in `work/duration_ladder.py`. Nothing else may reimplement it.

```
python work\duration_ladder.py --seconds 10     # any base
python work\duration_ladder.py --clip 00B       # a story clip, capped at its script
```

```

```

Implemented once, in `work/duration_ladder.py`. Nothing else may reimplement it.

```
python work\duration_ladder.py --seconds 10     # any base
python work\duration_ladder.py --clip 00B       # a story clip, capped at its script
```

### Why duration and not the seed

The number of words is fixed by the script. The size of the window is fixed by
the frame count. So **the speech rate the model has to hit is words ÷ duration,
and only the duration can change it.** A seed changes the noise, not the metre.

When the required rate is one the model cannot speak, it does not slow down or
leave a gap — it slurs, elides, mispronounces, or invents syllables to fill the
bar. That is why re-rolling has been producing *a different flavour of gibberish*
rather than clean speech. One second is roughly a 10% change in rate, which is
enough to land on a metre the model can actually articulate.

Up first because a fractionally slow delivery sounds natural and a rushed one
does not.

### The two knobs, and never turn both

| Symptom | Knob | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Wrong voice** — words are fine, timbre/age/accent is not the character | **Seed** | Only during voice auditions, where no `<Audio N>` is wired and H3 invents the voice. |
| **Wrong words** — gibberish, slurring, mispronunciation | **Duration ladder** | The seed cannot change words-per-second. |
| **Doubled or layered voice** | Neither | That is a `retention_analysis` fault — see §2 — or a prepended header. Fix the prompt, not the length. |
| **Speech in a clip that should be silent** | Neither | The prompt is wrong or the wrong prompt was sent. Extract the embedded graph and check. |

Changing two things at once is how this project spent a week blaming duration for
a fault the header was causing. **One knob per attempt.**

### The 17-frame block grid makes a "second" approximate

H3 snaps to frame counts congruent to 5 modulo 17 at 24 fps, and this project
rounds **up** (CLAUDE.md, non-negotiable). One block is 0.708 s, so a nominal
one-second step realises as 0.71–1.42 s. From a nominal base of 10 s:

| try | rung | nominal | frames | actual |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0 | 10 s | 243 | 10.125 s |
| 2 | 1 | 11 s | 277 | 11.542 s |
| 3 | 2 | 9 s | 226 | 9.417 s |
| 4 | 3 | 12 s | 294 | 12.250 s |
| 5 | 4 | 8 s | 192 | 8.000 s |
| 6 | 5 | 13 s | 328 | 13.667 s |
| 7 | 6 | 7 s | 175 | 7.292 s |

The rungs are always distinct and always ordered. They are simply not exactly a
second apart, and any doc claiming otherwise is wrong.

### Bounds

**Upper: the clip's scripted duration.** A Stage-1 soundtrack is padded with
digital silence up to the scripted length at assembly, so a soundtrack longer
than its picture is unusable. Out-of-range rungs are **skipped, not clamped** —
clamping would render the same length twice and waste an attempt. A clip whose
base already equals its scripted length therefore gets a purely downward ladder;
`00B` is one of these.

**Lower: 3.0 s.** Below that there is no window for the words at any pace.

### The trap: your own validator will reject your correct retries

`work/validate_audio_take.py` raises `WRONG_LENGTH` when a render is longer than
`audio_pass_durations.json` says. **Every upward rung is longer than that by
design.** Pass the rung's length:

```
python work\validate_audio_take.py <take.mp4> --clip 00A --configured-seconds 10.833
```

`work/render_audio_pass.py` records `render_seconds` on every attempt for exactly
this. This is the fifth time in this project a checker has measured the wrong
thing; do not make it the sixth.

### Status — unverified

This is the operator's rule, taken from their own hand-rendering, implemented as
given. **No render has been made under it.** It changes no node, no model, and no
setting in `docs/GOLDEN_REFERENCE/PROVEN_GOOD_AUDIO_GRAPH.api.json` — only the
`length` value fed to the existing graph. Every attempt now records its
`ladder_rung`, so after the first pass the rule can be judged on which rungs
actually produced clean takes, rather than on belief.

Known loose ends: `_ATTACHMENT_RE` in agent.py only matches server.py's attachment block, so phone-bridge attachments may not be listed as "not analysed"; `plan_video_from_reference`'s `operator_decisions_needed` strings repeat the size once, cosmetic; `outputs/stories/_comfy_output/mcp_test/` holds the proof outputs (keep them; evidence).

# Model-aware harness profiles — design (2026-09-04)

Scoping only. No harness code was changed for this document.
Parent analysis: `docs/FARM_EFFICIENCY_EVALUATION_2026-09-04.md` Finding 1
(sharpened). Ticket: `TODO.md` Phase 2, "Farm efficiency, ticket 2".
Routing signal this keys off: `CHANGELOG/2026-09-04i_capability_model_routing.md`
+ live verify `CHANGELOG/2026-09-04k_capability_routing_live_verify.md`.

This is the check-the-design-before-building pass. Small-model tool-selection
regressions are the known failure mode. Do not start implementation until
this design is accepted.

## 1. What this is

When `router.decide("auto", prompt=...)` sends a turn to a **CPU-served or
farm-served** model, the harness switches to a reduced tool surface and a
more directive loop. When the same `decide()` returns a **GPU-resident**
model, today's full schema and free-form hop loop stay as they are.

The switch trigger is the existing `router.Decision`. No new signal.

Two profiles:

| Profile | When | Tool surface sent to the model | Loop |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gpu` | `Decision.tier == "gpu"` (including the GPU-resident 8B fallback and the DeepSeek/Coder 14B pair) | today's `tools.schemas()` — all registered tools, `PROJECT_ONLY_TOOLS` still filtered | free-form native tool calls, current `action_resolver` intents |
| `cpu` | `Decision.tier in {"cpu", "farm"}` or `Decision.backend == "farm"` | three meta-tools (`list_tools` / `describe_tool` / `call_tool`) wrapping the same registry | same hop loop, plus a CPU-only resolver bias (below) |

`lightweight_turn` (empty schemas, tiny prompt) and PowerInfer
(`tools=None`) are unchanged third paths. They are not this ticket.

## 2. Live inventory (measured 2026-09-04, this session)

`local_agent/tools.py::TOOLS` (line 1936) and `schemas()` (line 2679):

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| Registered tools | **67** (eval doc said ~65; live count is 67) |
| `schemas()` | 67 |
| `schemas(include_project=False)` | 54 (`PROJECT_ONLY_TOOLS` = 13) |
| Schema JSON | 40,511 chars / 39.6 KB |
| Description text only | 13,790 chars |

Long descriptions that dominate the budget (unchanged observation from the
eval): `plan_story_image`, `render_story_image`, `schedule_phone_messages`,
plus the seven `comfy_*` wrappers.

Precedent, read from upstream not paraphrased: comfyui-mcp `--compact` /
`COMFYUI_MCP_TOOL_MODE=compact` registers exactly three meta-tools, keeps
the real catalog behind them, and is documented as the right trade for
small local models. Default remains the full surface. Forgiving quirks:
`args` may be an object **or** a JSON string; aliases `tool_name` /
`arguments` accepted; validation errors return the expected schema.
Source: https://comfyui-mcp.artokun.io/docs/local-llms.md

`MAX_TOOL_HOPS = 6` (counts model turns). A naive `list → describe → call`
chain spends 3 of those 6 before any real work. That hop budget is why the
meta-tool shape has to be slightly richer than names-only (see §5).

## 3. Switch trigger — read `Decision`, do not invent a flag

`router.Decision` already carries everything needed
(`router.py` ~406–413):

```text
tier:    "gpu" | "cpu" | "farm"
backend: "ollama" | "powerinfer" | "farm"   (default "ollama")
host, model, gpu_busy, reason, detail
```

Proposed helper (new, tiny, in `tools.py` or a new `harness_profile.py` —
prefer `tools.py` so schema + profile stay in one place):

```python
def profile_for(decision) -> str:
    """'cpu' compact or 'gpu' full. PowerInfer callers never reach this."""
    backend = getattr(decision, "backend", "ollama")
    tier = getattr(decision, "tier", "gpu")
    if backend == "farm" or tier in ("cpu", "farm"):
        return "cpu"
    return "gpu"
```

Mapped onto today's live `decide("auto")` outcomes (2026-09-04k):

| Live decision | Profile |
|---|---|
| farm / Qwythos (`CAP_TOOL`, farm reachable) | `cpu` |
| gpu / DeepSeek or Josiefied Coder (`CAP_LOGIC` / `CAP_CODE`, GPU free) | `gpu` |
| cpu / Huihui 8B (`CAP_CODE`/`CAP_LOGIC` refused because :8188 / thermal / queue_owner) | `cpu` |
| gpu / Huihui 14B (legacy auto, no capability override) | `gpu` |
| gpu / Huihui 8B GPU-resident fallback (`fallback_after_primary_failure`) | `gpu` — still GPU-resident, full schema |
| prefer=`cpu` (operator or pending `gpu_gate`) | `cpu` |
| PowerInfer | not this ticket (`stream_tools = None` already) |

Do **not** key off `classify_capability() == CAP_TOOL` alone. An unpinned
tool turn with the farm down falls through to the ordinary GPU/CPU auto
path; if the GPU is free that is a 14B with the full schema, which is
correct.

Do **not** key off `classify_capability() == CAP_TOOL` alone. An unpinned
tool turn with the farm down falls through to the ordinary GPU/CPU auto
path; if the GPU is free that is a 14B with the full schema, which is

### 3.1 When in `answer()` the profile is chosen

Today `tool_schemas = tools.schemas(...)` is built **once**, before the hop
loop (`agent.py` ~1287), and `router.decide()` runs **inside** every hop
(~1522), including a `skip_farm=True` retry if Qwythos returns None
(~1537). `gpu_gate` can also force `effective_prefer = "cpu"` on that hop
(~1511).

So the profile can change hop-to-hop. That is intended:

- Hop 0 farm (compact) → Qwythos returns `call_tool` → host executes it
  locally via `run_one()` → hop 1 re-decides. If hop 1 is GPU 14B, send
  the full schema for that hop.
- Hop 0 GPU 14B, then a render claims the card, hop 1 CPU 8B: switch to
  compact for hop 1.

Implementation rule: **recompute `tool_schemas` from that hop's Decision
after farm-fallback, before `chat_stream` / `try_qwythos_on_farm`.** Do
not freeze the profile at the start of `answer()`. The pre-loop
`tool_schemas` used for `estimate_context_tokens` can stay full (a
slightly pessimistic token estimate is safe).

`try_qwythos_on_farm(msgs, tools=tool_schemas)` already forwards whatever
list the host built (`farm_offload.py` ~264–286;
`worker_farm/tasks.py::_qwythos_evaluate` passes `envelope["tools"]`
straight to `ollama_client.chat`). No Mac-side schema logic. Compact vs
full is a host decision.

## 4. Meta-tool wrapper — concrete API

Do **not** add `list_tools` / `describe_tool` / `call_tool` to `TOOLS`.
`test_all_schemas_and_enums` asserts `len(tools.TOOLS) == len(schemas())`
and `set(tools.TOOLS) == schema names`. Default `schemas()` must keep
returning the 67-tool GPU surface.

Virtual tools, dispatched inside `tools.call` before the `name not in
TOOLS` error (`tools.py` ~2714):

```text
META_TOOL_NAMES = ("list_tools", "describe_tool", "call_tool")
```

META_TOOL_NAMES = ("list_tools", "describe_tool", "call_tool")

### `schemas(*, include_project=True, profile="gpu")`

- `profile="gpu"` (default): identical to today's list. Never includes
  the three meta names.
- `profile="cpu"`: exactly three OpenAI-style function schemas, still
  honouring `include_project` for what the catalog *contains*, not for
  which meta-tools are advertised.

CPU schemas (parameter names match comfyui-mcp so Qwythos / 8B can reuse
the published compact convention):

**`list_tools`**

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "category": {"type": "string", "description": "Optional group filter"},
    "search":   {"type": "string", "description": "Optional substring over name+summary"}
  }
}
```

Return a token-light catalog: name + one-line summary, grouped. One-line
summary = first sentence of the existing `TOOLS` description, truncated
to ~160 chars. Groups (stable, derived from the comment headers already
in `TOOLS`):

```text
project, memory, batch, comfy, file, web, story_image, storyboard,
sonic_pi, sensory
```

`PROJECT_ONLY_TOOLS` omitted when `include_project=False`. Same visibility
as GPU `schemas()` — do not also filter by phone `ToolContext.permits()`.
GPU models already *see* tools they cannot call; compact must not become
stricter, or tests/behavior diverge.

**`describe_tool`**

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "name":  {"type": "string"},
    "names": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}
  }
}
```

Accept `name` or `names` (cap 3). Return that tool's full description +
`_SCHEMAS` JSON. Unknown / project-only-hidden names: `ERROR:` with the
list of visible names, not an exception.

Cap-3 exists because `MAX_TOOL_HOPS = 6`. One describe hop can arm three
`call_tool`s.

**`call_tool`**

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "required": ["name"],
  "properties": {
    "name":      {"type": "string"},
    "tool_name": {"type": "string"},
    "args":      {"description": "object or JSON string"},
    "arguments": {"description": "alias of args"}
  }
}
```

Resolution order: `name` or `tool_name`; `args` or `arguments`; if the
value is a string, `json.loads` it. Then **one** call:

```python
return tools.call(inner_name, inner_args, context=context)
```

No second permission path. `tools.call` already checks existence,
`ToolContext.permits()`, trusted identity injection, `remote_security.audit_tool()`,
and converts exceptions to `ERROR:`. `call_tool` of a hidden project-only
name still hits that chokepoint and fails the same way a GPU model calling
it would.

### 4.1 Hop-loop unwrap

`agent.py::run_one()` (~1729) must unwrap `call_tool` *before* the
specialist / batch / `__conversation_id` guards, so those guards see the
inner name:

```text
if name == "call_tool":
    inner_name, inner_args = tools.parse_call_tool_args(args)
    # then run the existing run_one body with inner_name, inner_args
```

If we only unwrap inside `tools.call`, `run_one` would skip the
`start_current_chat_render` conversation-id bind and the
`_SPECIALIST_PROJECT_TOOLS` / `_BATCH_RENDER_TOOLS` blocks — those key off
the outer name `call_tool`. That is a real hole. Unwrap in `run_one`.

Direct real tool names remain legal on the CPU profile. Compact *advertises*
three tools; the dispatcher still accepts the 67. Reasons:

1. Qwythos / 8B may emit a remembered real name instead of `call_tool`.
2. Existing `test_native_tool_calling.py` tests inject real names via
   mocked `chat_stream` while `_Route` defaults to `tier="cpu"` (see §8).
3. `action_resolver` / `_execute_plan` already call real names.

`list_tools` and `describe_tool` are pure reads → add to
`CONCURRENCY_SAFE_TOOLS`. `call_tool` is **not** concurrency-safe as a
name; after unwrap, use the inner name's membership.

Stuck-call guard (`recent_tool_attempts`): hash the *inner* `(name, args)`
for `call_tool`, otherwise the model can loop `call_tool` with a changing
wrapper and a fixed inner call, or the opposite.

Legacy `TOOL: name {json}` fallback stays. On the CPU profile it is a
feature (small models that cannot native-call still have a path).

## 5. CPU prompt profile

Today `system_prompt()` (~569) is built once before routing and is the
verbose GPU prompt (`CONVERSATION_RULES` plus optional coding/project
prefixes). After the hop's Decision, if profile is `cpu` and this is not
a `lightweight_turn`, replace `msgs[0]` (the system message) with a short
directive. Do not rebuild memory / project prefixes on every hop unless
the profile actually flipped.

CPU system rules, in this order, short:

1. You are a local desktop assistant. Reply in English.
2. Tools: only `list_tools`, `describe_tool`, `call_tool` are in your
   schema. To use a real tool: `call_tool` with `name` + `args`. You may
   skip `list_tools` if you already know the name; call `describe_tool`
   before the first `call_tool` of a name you have not used this turn.
3. Do not invent tool names. If `call_tool` returns `ERROR`, read it and
   either describe or pick a different name. Do not tell the operator to
   run a command you can run.
4. Never claim an action happened without a tool result this turn.
5. Never mention tool names to the operator.
6. Keep the existing specialist-scope boundary paragraph when it is
   already inserted.

Do **not** paste `CONVERSATION_RULES`'s per-tool essays (`start_batch_render`,
Sonic Pi, storyboard, PowerInfer JSONL, …) into the CPU prompt. Those
essays exist to steer a 14B that can see 67 schemas. On compact they
recreate the token cost we just removed, and they name tools the model
cannot see in its schema.

Coding-mode (`router.is_coding_model(model)`): Coder-14B is GPU-profile
only. CPU fallback of a code turn (Comfy :8188 refused the swap) still
gets the compact CPU prompt, **plus** the existing four-step `run_code`
debug loop from `CODING_RULES`, because that loop is how the 8B is
supposed to behave. Do not send the rest of `CODING_RULES`'s tool-name
catalog.

## 6. Leaning harder on `action_resolver.py`

`classify()` already runs for every non-lightweight turn, before the
model, on both GPU and CPU (`agent.py` ~1335). Five intents, first match
wins: `comfyui_stop`, `jsonl_repair`, `calibration_continue`, `list_dir`,
`read_file`. All guards still go through `tools.call`.

That global pre-resolution stays. GPU does not lose it.

"Lean harder" on the CPU profile is **additive and gated**, not a rewrite
of `classify()`'s current five. Two layers, in order:
