That global pre-resolution stays. GPU does not lose it.

"Lean harder" on the CPU profile is **additive and gated**, not a rewrite
of `classify()`'s current five. Two layers, in order:

### 6.1 Layer A — v1, no new intents (ship with the meta-tool PR)

After `classify()` returns `None`, if the hop profile is `cpu` **and**
`_ACTION_REQUEST_RE` matches the user text, inject one system sentence
before the model runs:

> This is an action request. You have not used a tool yet. Call
> `list_tools` or `call_tool` this turn. Do not answer with instructions
> for the operator.

This is the existing execution-first retry (`agent.py` ~1659) pulled
*forward* so the CPU model does not burn hop 0 on prose. The current
retry still exists as a backstop.

Do **not** expand regex intents in the same PR as the meta-tool wrapper.
The architecture audit (`docs/design_notes/architecture_audit_2026-08-27.md`
§1) already named "patch the description, add a regex escape hatch"
as the thing that does not scale. Combining a new classifier with a new
schema surface in one change makes a tool-selection regression
undiagnosable.

### 6.2 Layer B — follow-up PR, extra CPU-only intents, each with a test

`classify(..., profile="gpu"|"cpu")`. Extra branches run only when
`profile=="cpu"`, after the existing five, still evidence-or-path
required, still `None` on ambiguity:

| Intent | Trigger (high precision) | Plan |
|---|---|---|
| `web_search` | explicit "search the web / look up / google" and no URL | `web_search` |
| `capabilities` | "what can you see/hear/transcribe" / "what tools do you have" | `capabilities` |
| `list_memory` | "what do you remember" / "list remembered facts" | `list_memory` |

Do **not** add `write_file`, `run_code`, `start_batch_render`, or
`render_story_image` as CPU-only regexes. Those are the cases the
resolver was extracted to *stop* guessing.

Chicken-and-egg: `classify()` currently runs before `decide()`. For
Layer B, compute profile from a `decide()` call *before* `classify()`,
and reuse that Decision on hop 0 unless `gpu_gate` / farm-fallback
changes it. `ensure_gpu_evicted` on that early call must match hop 0
(`True` for a real turn). Status polling stays `ensure_gpu_evicted=False`.

Layer A does not need the early `decide()`: the execution-first sentence
can wait until hop 0's Decision, which is the first model call anyway.

## 7. What this must not do

- Must not change default `tools.schemas()` (GPU / direct callers /
  `test_all_schemas_and_enums`).
- Must not register meta-tools in `TOOLS`.
- Must not bypass `tools.call` for inner tools.
- Must not filter the compact catalog by phone identity more strictly
  than GPU schemas.
- Must not send compact schemas to a GPU-resident 8B fallback.
- Must not send full schemas to Qwythos "because 9B is bigger than 8B".
  Farm is the compact path; that is the point of the ticket.
- Must not auto-`git revert` or otherwise implement Finding 2.
- Must not offload `run_code` (Finding 3).
- Must not bump Mac Celery concurrency (ticket 1, separate).

# Stage 3 — RerankedScorer (FlashRank) — implementation proposal

**Status: proposal only. 2026-09-03ae close-call — do not implement.
Keep HybridScorer as default.**

Research is done. This is a short handoff for another agent. Nothing here
authorizes installing packages, flipping `_DEFAULT_SCORER`, or editing
`local_agent/retrieval.py`. Stage 3 stays deferred until the operator names
the new dependency in an explicit approval.

## Current state (do not rewrite HybridScorer)

`local_agent/retrieval.py` already has Stages 1–2, and they are the default
as of `CHANGELOG/2026-09-02ab_phase2_hybrid_default.md`:

- `LexicalScorer` — stdlib BM25
- `EmbeddingScorer` — cosine over CPU `nomic-embed-text`
- `HybridScorer` — Reciprocal Rank Fusion of the two. Only chunks that
  clear BM25 > 0 **or** cosine ≥ `MIN_EMBED_SIMILARITY` enter the pool, so
  empty still means "local docs don't establish the claim"
- `_DEFAULT_SCORER = HybridScorer()` — `search` / `search_docs` use it
  unless a caller passes another `ScorerProtocol`

FlashRank is Stage 3 via a **new** `RerankedScorer` that wraps Hybrid and
reorders the fused top-N. It is not a HybridScorer rewrite, not a second
fusion method, and not a default-path change. See `TODO.md` Phase 2 item 4
and `RAG_EVALUATION.md` Stage 3.

## What FlashRank is here

Cross-encoder retrieve-then-rerank of Hybrid's fused top-N. Query and
document are scored jointly (unlike `EmbeddingScorer`'s independent cosine).

- Package: `flashrank`, **pairwise only** (do not pull listwise / RankGPT
  models)
- New runtime dep: `onnxruntime`
- **No torch**, no `sentence-transformers`, no `transformers`

`CHANGELOG/2026-09-02ab_phase2_hybrid_default.md` already said no to this
dependency. That deferral stands until a new explicit approval.

## Models (correct the 2026-09-02m pick)

`CHANGELOG/2026-09-02m_rag_stage3_reranker_research.md` named
`ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2` (~80 MB). **That model is not in the FlashRank
catalog** (PrithivirajDamodaran/FlashRank issue #26). Do **not** recommend
installing L-6-v2. Do not add a custom ONNX of it.

| Role | FlashRank id | Size | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Default / first | `ms-marco-TinyBERT-L-2-v2` | ~4 MB | FlashRank's own default. Start here. |
| Quality fallback | `ms-marco-MiniLM-L-12-v2` | ~34 MB | Pairwise catalog model. Opt-in only if TinyBERT quality is insufficient. |

Do not ship L-12 as the first install.

## Sketch — wrap Hybrid, do not flip the default

Same `ScorerProtocol.score(query, chunks) -> list[tuple[float, dict]]`.
Wrap an inner Hybrid; do not rewrite it.

```python
class RerankedScorer:
    """Stage 3: cross-encoder reorder of HybridScorer's fused top-N.

    Opt-in only. Do not assign to `_DEFAULT_SCORER`.
    """
    TOP_N = 50           # clamp 20–50; start at 50, tune down
    MODEL = "ms-marco-TinyBERT-L-2-v2"
    RERANK_CHARS = 2000  # under 512-token CE max; CHUNK_CHARS is 3000

    def __init__(self, inner: ScorerProtocol | None = None, top_n: int = TOP_N):
        self.inner = inner or HybridScorer()
        self.top_n = max(20, min(50, top_n))
        self._ranker = None  # lazy

    def _ranker_or_none(self):
        if self._ranker is not None:
            return self._ranker
        try:
            from flashrank import Ranker
        except ImportError:
            return None
        self._ranker = Ranker(model_name=self.MODEL, max_length=512)
        return self._ranker

    def score(self, query: str, chunks: list[dict]) -> list[tuple[float, dict]]:
        fused = self.inner.score(query, chunks)
        if not fused:
            return []
        ranker = self._ranker_or_none()
        if ranker is None:
            return fused  # missing flashrank/onnxruntime → Hybrid order
        head, tail = fused[: self.top_n], fused[self.top_n:]
        from flashrank import RerankRequest
        passages = [
            {
                "id": i,
                "text": (ch.get("text") or "")[: self.RERANK_CHARS],
                "meta": ch,
            }
            for i, (_score, ch) in enumerate(head)
        ]
        reranked = ranker.rerank(RerankRequest(query=query, passages=passages))
        # CE scores replace RRF on the head only. Do not globally re-sort
        # with tail — the two scales are not comparable.
        out = [(float(item["score"]), item["meta"]) for item in reranked]
        out.extend(tail)
        return out
```

Notes for the implementing agent:

- Call `Ranker.rerank(RerankRequest)` — that is the pairwise FlashRank
  surface. Do not use listwise helpers.
- Lazy-import `flashrank` inside the class so `retrieval.py` still imports
  with no new packages installed.
- Fallback on `ImportError` (and treat ranker runtime errors the same way
  Hybrid treats a dead embedding endpoint): return the inner Hybrid
  ranking; do not fail `search_docs`.
- Preserve `_match_by` on the shallow-copied chunks Hybrid already tags.
  Do not mutate index chunks.
- **Do not flip `_DEFAULT_SCORER`.** Callers opt in:

## Truncation

`CHUNK_CHARS = 3000` (~800 tokens). FlashRank pairwise CEs are 512-token
max (query + document). Passing a full chunk silently truncates inside
ONNX and can drop the relevant span. Truncate to `RERANK_CHARS`
(candidate 2000 chars, ~500 tokens so query+doc fits) **before** building
`RerankRequest` passages. Prefer the start of the chunk (heading-aware
splits already put useful text first). Do not change `CHUNK_CHARS` or the
indexer.

## Risks (why this is still gated)

1. **New `onnxruntime` dependency.** `2026-09-02ab` explicitly deferred
   FlashRank/onnxruntime as a new runtime intake, same bar as PowerInfer /
   TinyChatEngine. `retrieval.py`'s module docstring still promises the
   default path has no FlashRank/onnxruntime. Approval must name the
   packages (`flashrank` + `onnxruntime`) and the first model
   (`ms-marco-TinyBERT-L-2-v2` only).
2. **Per-query CPU.** The cross-encoder scores every (query, candidate)
   pair. Top-N of 20–50 × TinyBERT-L-2 is workstation-CPU-sized; L-12 is
   slower. Keep `search_docs` on `CONCURRENCY_SAFE_TOOLS` only while
   rerank stays off the default path. `agentic_search_docs` already calls
   a model and is not concurrency-safe — do not silently hang a CE on
   that path either without approval.
3. **No farm rerank queue.** Embed and summarize already offload. There
   is no rerank Celery task and this proposal does not add one. If
   approved, rerank runs on **local workstation CPU only**. Do not touch
   `farm_offload.py`, `agent.py`, or `worker_farm/` files.

   `worker_farm/.venv`). Confirm no torch pull. First model:
   TinyBERT-L-2-v2 (~4 MB). Do not install L-6-v2.
3. Add `RerankedScorer` to `local_agent/retrieval.py` as sketched. Do not

This file is a design handoff. It does not install FlashRank, does not add
onnxruntime, does not flip the default scorer, and does not change

## Addendum — TinyBERT local-CPU cost (2026-09-03)

Research-only. No package was added to the workstation agent env, and
`retrieval.py` was not edited. This bounds the "workstation-CPU-sized"
claim in Risks item 2 for the proposed default
`ms-marco-TinyBERT-L-2-v2` at fused top-N 20 and 50.

### Published numbers

- HuggingFace `cross-encoder/ms-marco-TinyBERT-L2-v2`: 4.39M params.
  Sentence-Transformers table: **9000 docs/sec on a V100 GPU**
  (NDCG@10 69.84, MRR@10 32.56). That is GPU, not CPU.
- FlashRank pairwise catalog: default id `ms-marco-TinyBERT-L-2-v2`,
  ~4 MB ONNX, no torch. README: speed is a function of passage tokens,
  query tokens, and layer count. Official CPU table is still **TBD**.
  The nano example constructs `Ranker(max_length=128)`.
- Third-party CPU claims for this same tiny CE (not always FlashRank
  Python):
  - Dixit, "Reranking in RAG" (Medium): FlashRank TinyBERT about
    **15–30 ms for N=50 on CPU**; a MiniLM cross-encoder 100–250 ms
    at the same N.
  - flashrank-js (`tiny` = `Xenova/ms-marco-TinyBERT-L-2-v2`) on a
    typical Windows x64 desktop, Node 24, CPU-only: load ~190 ms;
    median rerank **3 / 6 / 10 ms for 5 / 10 / 20 docs** (end-to-end,
    tokenization included, warmup excluded). Different runtime
    (transformers.js ONNX) than Python `flashrank`. Linear in N would
    put N=50 around 25 ms if the slope holds.

### Local dry-run (throwaway venv, dummy data)

`flashrank==0.2.10` + `onnxruntime==1.29.0`, Python 3.13.5.
API: `Ranker(model_name="ms-marco-TinyBERT-L-2-v2", max_length=...)`
then `ranker.rerank(RerankRequest(query=..., passages=...))`. No torch.
Cold download is a 3.26 MB zip; on-disk cache is **4.725 MiB**
(`flashrank-TinyBERT-L-2-v2.onnx` 4.28 MiB + tokenizer).

Host is **not** the workstation. Linux throwaway venv on a generic
Intel Xeon, 8 logical CPUs, 16 GiB RAM. Workstation for comparison:
AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D (8C/16T, 4.7 GHz) + 32 GiB. Treat Xeon numbers as
a conservative ceiling, not a DuranGamingPC measurement.

**Short dummy passages** (`max_length=256`, ~70-word passages, 40
timed iters after 3 warmups):

| N | mean | p50 | p95 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 20 | 13.6 ms | 12.7 ms | 20.0 ms |
| 50 | 28.5 ms | 28.0 ms | 37.9 ms |

Cold load 815 ms (includes first download). Peak RSS ~153 MiB.

**Proposal-shaped passages** (sketch settings: `max_length=512`,
dummy passages exactly `RERANK_CHARS=2000` / ~283 words, 30 timed
iters, warm cache):

| N | mean | p50 | p95 | min | max |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20 | 43.4 ms | 42.1 ms | 59.7 ms | 31.0 ms | 62.6 ms |
| 50 | 95.0 ms | 94.9 ms | 105.4 ms | 76.6 ms | 128.3 ms |

Warm load ~100 ms. Peak RSS ~510 MiB. Pairwise tensor width was 455
tokens (attn nonzero ~448), not 512. FlashRank pads to the **batch
max**, not to `max_length`, so ONNX is not paying for 512-wide
padding on these inputs. Cost is ~linear in N (~1.9 ms per candidate
at this length on the Xeon).

Same 2000-char passages at `max_length=128` (FlashRank nano
example): ~20.6 ms / 40.6 ms for N=20/50, peak RSS ~167 MiB, but
sequences are **hard-truncated to 128 tokens**, which drops most of
a 2000-char chunk. Do not use 128 with `RERANK_CHARS=2000`.

### Estimate for the workstation

Nothing was installed on DuranGamingPC. A 9800X3D is a faster
desktop CPU than the Xeon used above. Expect **similar or better**
than the proposal-shaped run:

- **~40–100 ms** per query to rerank Hybrid's fused top-20–50 at
  `RERANK_CHARS=2000` / `max_length=512`
- **<600 MiB RSS** once loaded (peak on the Xeon was 510 MiB)
- **~5 MB disk** for the TinyBERT ONNX + tokenizer
- Cold start: one-time 3.3 MB download + ~0.1–1 s load; then lazy
  `Ranker` as sketched

That is inside a local `search()` budget and matches Risks item 2
("workstation-CPU-sized"). It does **not** change the onnxruntime
approval gate. Latency is not the reason Stage 3 stays deferred; the
new native runtime still is.

follow-up answer; ordinary tool evidence remains capped at 2,400 characters.

been downloaded, opened, and modified. There were no tool events or tool
results in that chat, so none of those claims count as completed work. The
agent now refuses access-control bypass requests before model inference and
will replace an unsupported “I did it” claim with an explicit statement that no
verified local action happened. The server stores concise tool-result evidence
in the assistant message metadata for later audit. Live tool cards remain the
operator-facing proof during a response.

Dataset review found that OpenHermes 2.5, FineWeb-Edu, and The Stack v2 should

needs `--execute` for the explicit Hugging Face download gate. It never embeds

## Current state

### Native tool-loop responsiveness

Read-only tools returned together from one native tool-call hop now share the
same bounded GPU-status snapshot for their immediate follow-up model turn.
Any tool outside the reviewed read-only allowlist forces a fresh GPU check.
Cross-chat retrieval runs only for an identified conversation, preventing an
ad-hoc request from paying latency or inheriting unrelated chat context. The
native-tool suite (45 tests), router suite (41 tests), and 124-prompt H3
validator all passed after this change.

### Current-chat render recovery

If `start_current_chat_render` reports that the current chat has no complete
fenced H3 prompt set, the agent now stops with a deterministic recovery message.
It will not let the model substitute the repository root, a different folder,
or prompts from another chat. The operator must add the complete H3 prompt set
to the current chat before retrying. The native-tool suite passed 46 tests after
this regression fix; no renderer was started by the test.

has `validate_powerinfer_calibration`. It validates only the existing approval

### Direct writes and truthful failures

A specific desktop request authorizes ordinary text-file creation/editing; the
agent no longer asks for a redundant sidebar approval for `.ini`, `.cfg`,
`.json`, `.bat`, or `.vbs` files. Protected records remain refused, phone
identities still require their explicit remote `write_file` capability, and
binary patching still needs its exact-byte approval. If any file write fails for
another reason, the agent reports that no file or directory was created rather
than carrying a nonexistent file into later validation.

### Execution-first action requests

For a direct desktop request to do a safe task, the expected behavior is now:
use the appropriate local tool, then return a concise account of what happened
and any specific blocker. If the model initially emits a command-style answer
without attempting a tool, `agent.py` appends one execution correction and asks
for tool selection before returning it to the operator. The retry happens at
most once and never bypasses protected-file, binary-edit, remote-identity,
GPU, download, or render safeguards. It also does not manufacture capability:
when a required input, permission, or external service is genuinely absent, the
agent reports that exact condition rather than directing the operator to do
work the agent can do itself.

### Failed JSONL formatting recovery

The agent now treats a tool-reported JSONL path as durable task evidence. On a
desktop follow-up such as “fix it” after `validate_powerinfer_calibration`
reports a parsing failure, it deterministically repairs only a top-level JSON
object array into JSONL at that exact path and revalidates the same file. It
will not use an ellipsis, a documentation example, or an invented replacement
path. A successful syntax conversion is not an approval or schema pass; the
agent reports any remaining structural failure and does not begin model,
predictor, GPU, render, registry, or PowerInfer work.

Saved chats now replay only bounded same-chat tool receipts as facts into the
next request. This preserves tool-discovered paths and errors across a server
restart without treating another chat as context or generating orphaned native
tool protocol messages. A 2026-09-01 reliability audit found the previous
receipt was too lossy: it kept only a 240-character text summary, which could
truncate a long Windows `.jsonl` path and make the agent fall back to a bogus
`review-only/.../approved.jsonl` placeholder. Future receipts now preserve
structured fields (`path`, `valid`, `reason`, `records`, and repair status),
and the agent can recover exact `.jsonl` paths from older truncated receipts.

The same audit fixed a Windows status-file race in `atomic_io.atomic_write_text`.
The helper now writes unique sibling temp files and retries replacement briefly,
so nearby requests do not collide on shared names such as `chat_busy.tmp`.

The ComfyUI Whisper-tiny checkpoint exists locally. Its cold import on this
machine can exceed 30 seconds, so `capabilities.comfy_whisper_available()` now
uses a longer bounded timeout before reporting transcription unavailable.

### Action-resolution layer

`local_agent/action_resolver.py` is a new current-turn classification layer that
runs in `agent.answer()` before the model generates prose. It inspects the
operator's current message plus same-chat tool evidence and returns an
`ActionPlan` (ordered `(tool_name, args)` steps) when the request maps
unambiguously to a known safe tool. If no intent matches, it returns `None` and
the normal model turn proceeds unchanged.

The two prior inline regex/special-case branches in `answer()` — JSONL repair
and ComfyUI stop — have been replaced with the resolver call. The resolver now
owns both cases and three more:

| Intent | Fired by | Evidence required |
|---|---|---|
| `comfyui_stop` | "stop/kill/abort the render" | none |
| `jsonl_repair` | "fix it / fix the formatting error" | pending failed calibration path |
| `calibration_continue` | "continue with the approved JSON" | pending calibration path, non-render turn |
| `list_dir` | "show/list/browse … folder/files" | alias or explicit path token |
| `read_file` | "read/open/view … file" | explicit path token |

### Source citation contract

The agent now requires source-backed factual claims. A `# Source citation`
section in `CONVERSATION_RULES` specifies:

- **Web / internet** claims must name the URL or page title fetched.
- **Project documents** claims must cite file path and section heading.
- **Files / system state** must include the file path or directory from the
  tool result.
- **Memory and prior chats** must note that provenance explicitly.
- **Unsupported pre-training knowledge** must be labelled "from model
  knowledge" or "unverified".
- Exception: casual chat, creative writing, brainstorming, and code
  generation do not require source labels unless a specific factual claim
  is made within them.

Implementation: `_tool_source_label(name, result)` in `agent.py` extracts
provenance from six tool types (`fetch_url`, `web_search`, `search_docs`,
`read_file`, `list_dir`, `list_memory`/`remember_fact`). The label is passed
to `artifacts.prune_large_text(source_label=…)` so provenance survives context
pruning into the artifact pointer. `read_file` now prepends `[File: path]`;
`list_memory` prepends `[Source: persistent memory]`. 24 new tests in
`test_source_citation.py` cover extraction, artifact embedding, tool headers,
the citation contract, and stale H3/ComfyUI source leak prevention. All 57
existing tests and all 24 new tests pass. GUI source cards are a remaining gap.

### Source citation contract

The agent now requires source-backed factual claims and preserves provenance
through context pruning. See `CHANGELOG/2026-09-02b_source_citation_contract.md`.

**What changed:**

`agent.py` — `# Source citation` section added to `CONVERSATION_RULES`:
- Web / internet claims must name the URL or page title.
- Project documents claims must cite file path and section heading.
- Files and system state must include the file path or directory.
- Memory and prior chats must note that provenance explicitly.
- Unsupported pre-training knowledge must be labelled "from model knowledge"
  or "unverified".
- Exception: casual chat, creative writing, brainstorming, and code generation
  do not require source labels unless a specific factual claim is made within them.

`agent.py` — `_tool_source_label(name, result) -> str | None` — new helper
that extracts provenance from the raw tool-result string for six tool types:

| Tool | Label extracted |
|---|---|
| `fetch_url` | Final URL from leading `[url]` bracket |
| `web_search` | Backend + query from leading `[backend: query]` bracket |
| `search_docs` | `"docs: path1, path2, …"` from JSON `source` fields |
| `read_file` | File path from leading `[File: path]` header |
| `list_dir` | Directory path from first line of result |
| `list_memory` / `remember_fact` | `"persistent memory"` |
| All other tools | `None` — no label, no format change |

`artifacts.py` — `prune_large_text(kind, text, limit=2400, source_label=None)`:
optional `source_label` keyword argument (backward compatible). Pruned pointer
now embeds `source=<label>` when a label is supplied, so provenance survives
context compaction into the artifact pointer.

`tools.py`:
- `read_file` now prepends `[File: {resolved_path}]\n\n` before content.
- `list_memory` now prepends `[Source: persistent memory]\n` to both return paths.

retry path) now pass `source_label=_tool_source_label(name, result)`.

path, or tool name) visible in the tool results above; label unsupported
conclusions 'unverified' or 'from model knowledge'."

## Thread 1 — Mac persistence: LaunchAgent → LaunchDaemon, WireGuard login-item bug fixed

**Problem:** Ollama and Celery ran as per-user LaunchAgents on Louises-MBP.
LaunchAgents only start at GUI login, so neither survives an unattended/
headless boot — an explicit open blocker carried in both of the prior
session-handoff notes (`CHANGELOG/2026-09-03h_session_handoff.md`,
`CHANGELOG/2026-09-03i_session_handoff.md`).

**Fix:** `com.local-agent.celery-worker` and `com.local-agent.ollama`
converted to `/Library/LaunchDaemons/*.plist`, running as
`UserName=rhineduran GroupName=staff` (uid 503, not root) — LaunchDaemons
start at boot regardless of GUI login.
(`CHANGELOG/2026-09-03z_mac_headless_launchdaemons.md`)

**Proof it tracks boot, not login:** cold boot with nobody at the GUI
(`kern.boottime` Thu Sep 3 15:53:17, no autologin user). Both daemons
started **15:53:49** (~32s after boot): Ollama pid 336 (curl `127.0.0.1:11434`
→ 200), Celery pid 339 (children 582/585, ready log line 15:54:18). Rhine's
GUI login came later, ~15:58 — a recheck at 16:00:16 showed **the same
pids/`lstart`** (336/339, still 15:53:49), i.e. login spawned nothing new.
That's the actual proof: if login had produced new pids near 15:58, the
LaunchDaemon conversion would have failed to matter.

**WireGuard login-item bug:** WireGuard.app's GUI login-item helper
(`com.wireguard.macos.login-item-helper`) could silently re-register as an
enabled login item across reboots even after being told to stay off.
`launchctl disable` on the GUI helper labels was the wrong layer —
`print-disabled` showed them disabled, but that isn't a substitute for
unchecking the item in **BTM** (macOS's Background Task Management /
"Login Items & Extensions" list), which is the actual control point that
persists. The fix was unchecking it there, not launchctl.

Mac low-power sleep with inactive TCP keepalive, but isn't guaranteed —

## Thread 3 — WSL Docker-at-boot: the real blocker was standard-user S4U, not permissions; rhine made local admin

**Blocking constraint:** S4U + BootTrigger registration for principal
`rhine` failed consistently with `0x80070005` — from an elevated admin
session, from SYSTEM, from raw XML, from COM — **while rhine was a standard
(non-admin) user**. This exactly confirmed Thread 2's finding: a
standard-user account cannot be registered as an S4U task principal on this
machine, even by an elevated caller or SYSTEM acting on its behalf. Admin
accounts registering *themselves* as S4U already worked fine, isolating the
constraint to the target principal's account type, not the caller's
privilege level.

**Decision:** granted rhine local-Administrators membership
(`Add-LocalGroupMember -Group Administrators -Member DURANGAMINGPC\rhine`,
done by an already-elevated admin account). Explicitly flagged in its own
changelog entry as **"an account privilege change, not a boot-task
footnote"** and standing, not scoped or reverted. Stated rationale: this was
"the approved remaining lever that does not store a password and does not
fall back to a Logon trigger" — the alternatives considered and rejected
were storing a password-based task credential, or degrading to the weaker
Interactive/Logon-trigger pattern (which is what the tunnel relay ended up
using instead, in Thread 2, since it wasn't elevated to admin). No further
risk analysis is recorded beyond that.

## Thread 4 — farm-routing caller: `agent.py` now actually calls the farm, and live verification caught two real bugs unit tests missed

This closes the single biggest gap flagged in the 2026-09-02 handoff.

**Design:** `farm_offload.should_route()` reads the daemon-written
`farm_status.json` snapshot rather than calling live `Celery inspect.ping()`
— live inspect takes 1–5s and needs the farm venv, unacceptable to pay on
every hot-path decision. Reachable = snapshot exists, `checked_at` not older
than 90s, `status=="ok"`. Missing/stale/non-ok → run locally immediately,
avoiding a 25–30s helper timeout.

Summarize vs embed are routed differently based on measured Mac latency
(warm ~18.5s / cold ~55s summarize vs. a 12s local timeout budget):
**summarize is prefetch-only** — `should_route("summarize", blocking=True)`
is always `False`; the hop loop only ever consumes an already-ready
prefetch result or falls back local, never blocks waiting on Celery.
**Embed may block** `search_docs` when the farm is reachable, since it's
cheap once warm (~0.58s); falls back to local `_embed()` when the farm is
down. `agent.py` gained `_maybe_start_farm_summary_prefetch`, called from
the hop loop at 80% context. 90/90 tests passed in this pass (unit-level
only, no live Celery job submitted yet).
(`CHANGELOG/2026-09-03aw_farm_routing_caller.md`,
`CHANGELOG/2026-09-03ax_harness_4a_implemented.md` — marks
`HARNESS_OPTIMIZATION.md` §4a implemented, docs-only)

**Live verification, in two passes, found two real bugs:**

First pass found a **prefetch-timeout bug**: the ceiling was 25s (inherited
from 2026-09-02s), but real Mac cold/slow summarize takes ~90–117s — nowhere
near the 18.5s warm-only figure — so every first-of-session prefetch missed
and fell back local. Fixed by raising `PREFETCH_SUMMARIZE_TIMEOUT_S` to 135
(above the worker's own 120s timeout), since prefetch runs in a background
thread and correctness doesn't need a tight ceiling. With the fix, a
consume-win succeeded at 117.3s; `test_farm_offload_live.py` (real Mac
worker) ran 4/4 OK in 121.5s.
(`CHANGELOG/2026-09-03bd_farm_offload_live_verify.md`)

   30s timeout expired and returned `None`, but the Celery task **kept

   already been attempted and never retried it — permanently, for that
   slice, until restart. **Fixed:** the fingerprint is now cleared on
   `None`/exception so the same slice can retry.

## Thread 5 — Security: Windows `.env` ACL lockdown made durable; rhine's admin grant flagged again

**What was locked down:** three live secret-bearing files under
`local_agent/worker_farm/` — `.env` (hub Redis password, broker/result
URLs, AES key), `.env.mac_worker.generated`, and
`runtime/redis-acl/.env.mac_worker.generated`. Before: all three inherited
the parent directory's wide DACL — readable by rhine, a second interactive
admin account, `BUILTIN\Administrators`, a sandbox-users group, ten stale
unresolvable SIDs, and SYSTEM. Described explicitly as "the Windows
equivalent of the Mac world-readable `.env`" (mirroring an earlier Mac-side
fix that tightened that copy to `600`). Fixed with `icacls
/inheritance:r` + `/grant:r` to exactly `NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM:(R,W)` and
`DURANGAMINGPC\rhine:(R,W)` — `Administrators` deliberately not re-granted
since it still contained the second admin account at the time.
(`CHANGELOG/2026-09-03aj_windows_env_acl_lockdown.md` — one of three `aj`
files today, see the collision note below)

**Made durable:** the first pass only locked files that existed at that
moment; the credential-generation scripts (`Initialize-Phase1Secrets.ps1`,
`Add-Phase1SecondaryWorkerCredential.ps1`) write *new* secret files without
setting any ACL, so a future run would silently re-inherit the wide parent
DACL and undo the lockdown. Fixed with a shared
`Lock-Phase1SecretFile.ps1` helper, wired to run automatically after every
secret write across all three scripts. Directory-level ACL was deliberately
left wide/inherited — the design is per-secret-file locking, not directory
locking, since tightening the directory would break normal legitimate
writers. New `-LockdownProbe` mode added to both scripts for safe
verification (never touches the live `.env`). 4/4 tests pass.
(`CHANGELOG/2026-09-03al_phase1_secret_write_acl_lockdown.md`)

**Standing privilege change, flagged again:** rhine's promotion to local
Administrator (Thread 3) is cross-referenced here deliberately — it changes
who "Administrators:(F)" in an inherited DACL actually means, which is part
of why both ACL passes above deliberately keep the Administrators group off
the locked secret files rather than relying on group membership.

## Current state

Equal Shares remains a preserved, paused specialist profile. Do not resume its
audio pipeline, launch a Stage-1 render, or alter evidence/manifests. The
active product is the local general-purpose assistant.

Today was the single largest day of feature work in this project's recent
history: a full dynamic capability-based model routing system (pull → build →
live-verify), the comfyui-mcp third-party tool integration exercised across
its **entire** risk ladder (read-only through irreversible), harness profile

found and fixed via live investigation (not just unit tests), and a full
GPU/ComfyUI time-sharing feature that went through two rounds of post-ship
review catching real correctness bugs before they mattered. Two proposed
"efficiency" changes were also tested and correctly rejected with real
measurements rather than built on assumption. Every thread below is closed;
none are mid-flight.

A parallel-session coordination near-miss is worth flagging explicitly for
whoever reads this next: multiple Grok sessions were operating against the
same shared ComfyUI instance without a hard lock, and one session's restart
briefly looked like an unexplained crash to another. Nothing was corrupted,
but "One ComfyUI, ever" (`CLAUDE.md`) is a real constraint that needs an
actual coordination mechanism if multiple agent sessions become routine, not
just an operator manually tracking which session currently "owns" ComfyUI by
memory.

## Thread 1 — Capability-based dynamic model routing (done, live-verified)

**What:** `router.py` extended with task-type capability routing across three
specialized models: a lightweight tool-calling/classification model on the
farm worker (`richardyoung/qwythos-9b-abliterated`), a reasoning model
(`huihui_ai/deepseek-r1-abliterated:14b-qwen-distill`) and a coding model
(`josiefied-qwen2.5-coder-14b:q4_k_m`, built locally via `ollama create` since
no ready Ollama tag existed) both host-GPU-resident. Since the GPU holds only
one 14B at a time, swapping between the two host models sends `keep_alive:0`
to the currently-loaded model and polls `/api/ps` until eviction is confirmed
before loading the next — reusing the pattern `context_compactor.py` already
established rather than inventing a second one.

**VRAM sizing:** `MODEL_VRAM_BUDGET.md` — Q4_K_M @ `num_ctx=8192` recommended
(11.74GB total, 4.3GB headroom). Q8_0 fails outright; the 32B alternative
fails at every tested quant/context combo; the 8B alternative fits with large
headroom but is a reasoning-depth tradeoff, not a sizing one.

**Live-verified, not just unit-tested:** a real tool-routing request reached
Qwythos on the farm and got a real response back (62.4s cold load). A real
DeepSeek→Coder swap was captured end to end: `keep_alive:0` POST captured,
`/api/ps` confirmed empty (70 MiB) before Coder loaded (10149 MiB) and
answered correctly.

Evidence: `CHANGELOG/2026-09-04h_capability_routing_model_pulls.md`,
`2026-09-04i_capability_model_routing.md`,
`2026-09-04k_capability_routing_live_verify.md`.

## Thread 2 — comfyui-mcp integration, full risk ladder exercised

**What:** the third-party `comfyui-mcp` Node.js MCP server is wired into
`local_agent/tools.py` behind seven individually-named, whitelisted wrapper
tools (`comfy_generate`, `comfy_workflow`, `comfy_assets`, `comfy_models`,
`comfy_nodes`, `comfy_system`, `comfy_process`) — no raw "call any MCP tool"
passthrough. `local_agent/mcp_client.py` is a minimal hand-rolled
JSON-RPC-over-stdio client (spawns `node npx-cli.js` directly, not
`npx.cmd` via `cmd.exe`, which dropped the handshake on first live spawn).

**Verification followed an explicit risk ladder, one tier at a time:**
mocked tests first → one live read-only call (`comfy_system`) → one live
generation (`comfy_generate`, real 512×512 PNG, verified via `/view`) →
the three state-changing tools, each exercised separately with real refusal
conditions forced first (GPU heat, a fake owner-lock byte-for-byte restored
and sha256-verified) and every "success" case run against a throwaway
artifact only — a no-op custom-node pack, a 37-byte dummy model file. No
real operator weights, references, or evidence were ever touched.

**Two bugs found along the way, both fixed:**
- `comfy_generate` wasn't audit-logged at all, and a separate investigation
  (see Thread 4) traced two "mystery" red-mug images to unrelated Grok
  test/probe scripts writing into the same shared output folder as real
  jobs with colliding default filenames. Fixed: `comfy_generate` now appends
  to `comfy_mcp_audit.jsonl` like the other state-changing tools, and
  probe/test scripts write to an isolated `output/mcp_test/` subfolder via a
  dedicated non-tool enqueue path instead of sharing the operator's real
  output root.
- `filename_prefix` silently not taking effect on image generation was
  traced to a genuine upstream `comfyui-mcp` limitation (its image-generation
  action never forwards that field to the workflow composer, confirmed
  against the pinned package's own source and the official tool schema) —
  correctly *not* worked around by rebuilding comfyui-mcp's graph
  construction ourselves.

## Thread 3 — Harness profiles (done, live-verified, two layers)

**What:** when a request routes to a CPU- or farm-served model,
`tools.profile_for(decision)` now selects a compact 3-meta-tool schema
(`list_tools`/`describe_tool`/`call_tool`, following comfyui-mcp's own
"compact mode" precedent) instead of the full ~67-tool, 40,511-character
schema. The GPU-resident model is unaffected. Profile selection happens
fresh per hop off the live routing decision, not frozen at turn start.

**A test-suite hazard was caught and closed, not left as a caveat:** both
existing regression suites defaulted their routing mock to the CPU tier, so
once schema selection keyed off that decision, the suites passing would not
by itself prove the GPU path still sent the full schema. New spy tests
explicitly forcing `tier=gpu` and asserting the full 67-tool schema were
built before this was called done (`test_native_tool_calling.py` grew
65→76→80 across the two layers; `test_action_resolver.py` grew 29→46).

**Two layers, because the first alone wasn't enough:** shipping the
meta-tool schema-switching mechanism (Layer A/v1) alone left a real
performance cliff — a live compact-profile directory-listing request took
**589.6 seconds** because the small model had to discover through
`list_tools`→`describe_tool`→`call_tool` that a listing tool existed at all.
Layer B added deterministic pre-resolution (reusing the existing
`action_resolver.py` pattern) for the specific request shapes measurement
showed were actually costing hops — the same request then took **4.3
seconds**. Destructive-guess intents (`write_file`, `run_code`, render
actions) were deliberately not added to the deterministic path.

Evidence: `CHANGELOG/2026-09-04l_harness_profiles_scoping.md`,
`2026-09-04o_harness_profiles_v1.md`, `2026-09-04p_cpu_resolver_intents.md`.

## Thread 4 — Two real bugs, found via live investigation

**Empty-completion bug.** A chat turn could complete with real generated
tokens (HTTP 200, hundreds of tokens) and still get persisted as an empty
reply — root cause was `chat_stream` never reading `message.thinking` and
the hop loop treating "no content + no tool_calls" as a finished, successful
answer, rather than a fault. This was a pre-existing gap that harness
profiles' CPU compact schema made more likely to trigger (the 8B model plans
in its thinking channel instead of calling `call_tool` more often under the
reduced schema) but did not introduce — confirmed by not reverting the
compact schema to "fix" it. Fixed: the hop loop now retries once with
`think:false` on an empty/no-tool completion, and persists a visible
`_EMPTY_COMPLETION_REPLY` instead of ever storing `""`; `chat_stream` now
sends `think:false` on CPU/chat tool hops, matching the existing KV-cache
probe's own precedent for why that's necessary. A farm hop returning empty
content with no tool_calls is now also correctly treated as not-successful.

A related, separately-diagnosed **wrong-image scare** turned out to be
nothing: two red-mug images the operator saw appear during a stalled chat
turn were unrelated Grok live-verification/probe artifacts sharing the same
output folder (see Thread 2's audit-logging fix), not a hallucinated or
mis-wired generation from the operator's actual request — no scene
generation had actually occurred yet when the mugs appeared, since the chat
was still stuck in the empty-completion bug above.

**CPU-only Ollama silently advertising the GPU.** The dedicated CPU-only
Ollama instance (port 11435) was dying/falling through during GPU discovery
despite `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1`, which is why a turn sometimes fell through
to the GPU-serving instance (11434) and attempted a real GPU model load while
ComfyUI held the card. Root cause: Ollama 0.32.15's `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1`
only disables CUDA discovery, not Vulkan (confirmed against upstream
`ollama#16508`) — the "CPU-only" server was advertising the RTX 5080 over
Vulkan the whole time. Fixed in the actual launcher
(`START_LOCAL_AGENT_GUI.ps1`'s `Start-Server`, not a manual workaround):
`OLLAMA_VULKAN=false` and `GGML_VK_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1` added alongside the
existing `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1`. Verified through the actual patched
function (not a hand-rolled replica): before, `library=Vulkan` and the RTX
5080 discovered; after, `library=cpu`, `total_vram="0 B"`, and the original
fallthrough no longer reproduces.

Evidence: `CHANGELOG/2026-09-04r_empty_completion_guard.md`,

## Thread 5 — GPU/ComfyUI time-sharing (done, including two post-ship fix rounds)

**Problem:** `router.gpu_busy()` treats any ComfyUI process listening on port
8188 as "GPU busy," full stop — a deliberate, coarse, race-condition-safe
default (a render can claim the port before its backend finishes loading a
model; a naive VRAM check would read "idle" mid-claim). This meant the
agent's own GPU-routed models always yielded to ComfyUI even when ComfyUI
was sitting completely idle with nothing loaded.

**A VRAM-threshold refinement (option A) was proposed, measured, and
correctly killed before implementation.** Real instrumentation across
ComfyUI's idle/loading/loaded-idle/generating phases showed used VRAM stayed
flat at 345 MiB through three of those four phases (ComfyUI's own
DynamicVRAM staging keeps weights on CPU until first sampler use), with a
~29-second lag after generation genuinely started before `nvidia-smi` moved
at all. A VRAM threshold could not have distinguished "truly idle" from
"actively claimed, about to load" — exactly the race the original blunt
check exists to prevent.

**Option B shipped instead:** explicit time-sharing via `comfy_system`'s
`clear_vram` (`POST /free`), gated on real ownership signals — a live PID in
any of three owner-lock files stays authoritative and blocks the claim; an
empty ComfyUI queue (checked via cheap `urllib` first, MCP only as fallback)
is required; only then does the hook `/free` ComfyUI's VRAM, verify it
dropped to ≤800 MiB via `nvidia-smi`, and proceed to load the agent's model.
No explicit ComfyUI reload after `keep_alive:0` — the next real
`comfy_generate` call reloads lazily, at a documented ~17-29s cost. A kill
switch (`EQUAL_SHARES_COMFY_TIMESHARE=0`) restores today's blunt behavior
with no code revert needed.

**Two post-ship review rounds caught real bugs before they mattered, not
after:** PR 2 fixed a queue-check ordering issue, a host-GPU-gate hole that
incorrectly triggered for farm/CPU-only routing, and stripped stale
VRAM-threshold-era occupancy checks. Both PR 1 and PR 2 were independently
live-verified (six cases each: idle claim, same-hop reuse, live-owner
refusal, post-generate claim, farm-turn no-op, kill-switch restore) — the
second pass specifically re-exercising the bugs PR 2 fixed, live.

**Two deliberately-deferred follow-ups shipped today too, closing the loop
completely:** the `status()` badge now shows a real third state ("8188 up,
idle, agent may claim") derived only from the owner+queue signals already
computed — no extra network call from `status()` itself — and `agent.py`

## Thread 6 — Two efficiency proposals tested and correctly rejected

**Mac worker `--concurrency=2`:** measured against a real 8-job embed batch.
Wall-clock throughput barely moved (+1.3%: 90.973s → 89.769s) while per-job
latency nearly doubled (11.3s → 20.8s mean) — a real regression against the
farm's 30-second interactive ceiling for no real gain. Reverted same day,
left at `--concurrency=1`, full numbers kept in the record.

**Offloading `run_code` to the farm:** no evidence existed that host CPU
contention from `run_code` was a real bottleneck. A forced worst-case test
(a synthetic 8-second CPU-bound spin loop running alongside live model
inference) showed only a 2% throughput dip. No offload code was written; the
ticket closed with the measurement as its own resolution.

Evidence: `CHANGELOG/2026-09-04n_mac_celery_concurrency_2_reverted.md`,
`2026-09-04m_run_code_cpu_contention_not_worth_building.md`.

chunks.heading: # Local image generation — fallback for boundary frames
chunks.text:
# Local image generation — fallback for boundary frames

A local alternative to `docs/GEMINI_REFERENCE_IMAGE_GUIDE.md` for producing a first or last frame when one is genuinely needed.

The model inventory at the end of this document was verified against `A:\Users\rhine\ComfyUI-Shared\models\` on August 10, 2026. The workflows themselves have **not** been built or tested — treat the recommended approach as a plan, not a working pipeline.

---

## When this applies

Only after the salvage ladder is exhausted. In order: vary prompt and seed at 20 steps; simplify or slow the motion; split the action into ordered beats; shorten the clip; clean cut or hold on an approved frame; build an insert or subtle motion from existing approved frames. Working examples of the last rung live in `work/salvage_*.py`, `work/select_*.py`, and `work/repair_*.py`.

A new boundary image is the last resort, because every new image is a new opportunity for identity to drift. An approved frame that already exists is always safer than a generated one that doesn't.

## Local versus Gemini

Gemini's advantage is that it follows multi-image identity references and long prose constraints unusually well, which is why `docs/GEMINI_REFERENCE_IMAGE_GUIDE.md` exists and is the primary path.

Local generation is worth reaching for when: the render is between clips and the GPU is free; the needed frame is a *variation* on an existing approved frame rather than a new composition, which makes it an inpainting or img2img job rather than a text-to-image job; or you want the frame to inherit the exact grain, palette, and lens character of the surrounding footage, which a local pass conditioned on a real neighbouring frame does better than any external service.

That last case is the strongest argument for local. A Gemini frame is a photograph of the scene; a local img2img pass over an adjacent approved frame *is* the scene.

## The GPU constraint comes first

**Do not run local image generation while the render supervisor is working.** One ComfyUI backend at a time, on port 8188. Check for a running `render_until_complete.py`, check whether 8188 is bound, and check that `outputs/equal_shares/runtime/render_supervisor.log` has stopped advancing.

If the supervisor is alive, either wait for a clip boundary and ask the human to pause it, or use Gemini instead. Starting a second backend to make one image is not worth corrupting a 124-clip run.

chunks.heading: ## The GPU constraint comes first
chunks.text:
8188. Check for a running `render_until_complete.py`, check whether 8188 is bound, and check that `outputs/equal_shares/runtime/render_supervisor.log` has stopped advancing.

If the supervisor is alive, either wait for a clip boundary and ask the human to pause it, or use Gemini instead. Starting a second backend to make one image is not worth corrupting a 124-clip run.

## Step 1 — pick the approach that matches the need

**Tier A — instruction editing over an approved neighbour. This is the recommended path.** `Qwen-Image-Edit-2509-Q5_0.gguf` is installed in `models\unet\`. It takes an existing image plus a plain-language instruction — "move his right hand to the closed wallet," "turn the seated man's head toward the window" — and edits only what the instruction names. Identity, wardrobe, architecture, lighting, and film grain are inherited from the source frame rather than regenerated, which sidesteps the drift problem entirely.

Feed it the nearest approved boundary frame from `outputs/equal_shares/frames/scene_###/`. This is the single best tool available locally for this project, because almost every boundary frame the film needs is a small variation on a frame that already exists and is already approved.

**Tier B — img2img at low denoise.** Where the whole frame must shift slightly and no clean instruction describes it, run the nearest approved frame through img2img with `flux1-dev-fp8.safetensors` or an SDXL realism checkpoint at a denoise low enough to preserve identity — start around 0.35 to 0.45 and go lower if faces move. Above roughly 0.6 you are generating a new person and should expect to fail the acceptance gate.

Add a ControlNet over the neighbouring frame whenever geography must hold. `controlnet-union-sdxl-1.0-promax.safetensors` covers depth, softedge, and pose in one model, and `mistoLine_rank256.safetensors` is available for line conditioning. Both are SDXL-family, so pair them with an SDXL checkpoint, not with Flux. Screen direction and room layout are among the things the acceptance gate checks hardest.

**Tier C — text-to-image for a genuinely new composition.** Weakest option, because the installed stack has **no IP-Adapter and no PhotoMaker** — the `photomaker`, `style_models`, `inpaint`, and `facerestore_models` folders are all empty, and no `ipadapter` folder exists. There is no direct way to condition a fresh generation on `alex_vale_master_v1.png`.

There is an indirect route: `insightface\inswapper_128.onnx` with the `buffalo_1` pack is installed, which means a ReActor-style face swap is possible. Generate the composition with Flux or SDXL, then swap Kent's face in from the master reference. Treat this as a last resort — `inswapper_128` operates at 128 pixels, so at a 736 × 416 target it will hold identity in close shots and add little in wides, and it can leave a visible seam under the mustache. If Tier C is where you have ended up, Gemini is very likely the better answer.

chunks.heading: ## Step 1 — pick the approach that matches the need
chunks.text:
the composition with Flux or SDXL, then swap Kent's face in from the master reference. Treat this as a last resort — `inswapper_128` operates at 128 pixels, so at a 736 × 416 target it will hold identity in close shots and add little in wides, and it can leave a visible seam under the mustache. If Tier C is where you have ended up, Gemini is very likely the better answer.

**Not available locally:** dedicated inpainting checkpoints, IP-Adapter, PhotoMaker, style models, face restoration. Do not write a workflow that assumes any of them.

## Step 3 — match the target format

The frame must be usable as an H3 anchor, which means it must match generation geometry:

- **736 × 416**, 16:9, a multiple of 32 in both axes.
- 8-bit, sRGB, PNG.
- No alpha channel.

Generating larger and downsampling to 736 × 416 is acceptable and often better, since more pixels during generation means a better-resolved face before the downsample. Do not deliver a frame at a different aspect ratio and expect the runner to letterbox it sensibly.

Write to `outputs/equal_shares/frames/scene_###/` alongside the existing boundary frames, following their naming convention, and **always as a new version**. Never overwrite an approved reference.

## Step 4 — the acceptance gate is the same one

A locally generated frame earns no leniency for being local. Reject it if any character fails to match the correct reference sheet; if the number or position of people is wrong; if hands or anatomy are malformed; if architecture, props, wardrobe, or screen direction drift from the neighbouring approved frame; or if it contradicts the clip's entry in `story_config.json`. Looking good is not the standard.

Check the opening locks specifically if the frame belongs to scene 000: one woman, the receptionist, always behind the staff window; exactly two male visitors, both on the public side, entering through the separate doorway; one chair at screen-left; no glass gate, fence, invented divider, extra chair, or third man; a Narrator who does not resemble Kent.

chunks.heading: # Character LoRA runbook — MiniMax H3
chunks.text:
# Character LoRA runbook — MiniMax H3

Written 2026-08-11. Two things in here are verified because I ran them: the dataset
builder, and the dataset it produced for the Narrator. **The training config is a
template I could not execute or validate** — no GPU and no ai-toolkit in this
environment. Check every key against the current ai-toolkit H3 guide before you
trust it, and expect the schema to have moved.

---

## Step 1 — build the dataset (verified, ready to run)

```powershell
$Py    = "A:\Users\rhine\ComfyUI-Installs\Rockernow\ComfyUI\.venv\Scripts\python.exe"
$Story = "A:\Users\rhine\ComfyUI-Shared\output\story"

& $Py work\build_lora_dataset.py --name narrator --trigger ohwx_narrator `
  --caption "a man in his late fifties, lean face, dark hair combed back, dark 1960s suit, white shirt, narrow black tie, black and white television lighting" `
  --sources "outputs\equal_shares\frames\scene_000\boundary_narrator_close_v3.png" `
            "outputs\equal_shares\frames\scene_000\boundary_00_v2.png" `
            "outputs\equal_shares\frames\scene_000\boundary_04_v2.png" `
            "$Story\00A" "$Story\00B" "$Story\00C"
```

Test run result: **40 crops kept, 26 near-duplicates discarded, face sizes 102–167 px
in source.** Output in `outputs\equal_shares\lora_datasets\narrator\` as `.png` +
`.txt` pairs, with `_contact_sheet.jpg` and `dataset_manifest.json`.

The tool samples videos once per second, finds the largest face, crops head and
shoulders at 3.2× face width, drops anything under `--min-face-px`, removes
near-duplicates, and upscales to 1024×1024.

**The size filter is the important part.** In the wide shots the Narrator's head is
about 22 px. Those frames contain no identity information and would teach the LoRA a
blurred average. They are excluded automatically.

### Then cull, by hand

Open `_contact_sheet.jpg`. Delete any crop that is the wrong person, blurred,
mid-blink, or has a second face intruding at the edge — and delete its matching
`.txt`. **Fifteen clean crops beat forty with five wrong faces.**

### One real weakness in this dataset

All 40 crops come from `00A` and `00B` — 34 and 6 — which are the same setup: same
angle, same lighting, same background, same wardrobe. A LoRA trained on it learns
"this man, shot this way." It will be strong for the opening and weak anywhere else,
and it has no profile or three-quarter views at all.

For the Narrator that may be fine, since he only ever appears in that setup. If you
want it to generalise, add varied angles first — which realistically means generating
a character sheet from `references\narrator_master_v1.png` with your Mickmumpitz
workflow and feeding those in alongside these.

---

## Step 2 — check the base model before you spend a night on this

Your inference checkpoint is `minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors` —
**pruned and int8-quantised**. LoRA training wants the base weights.

So: pull the full-precision H3 weights for the training run, then confirm the
resulting adapter actually loads against your quantised checkpoint at inference.
Rank and target-module names have to line up. Do this check on a 200-step throwaway
run before committing to a real one.

If the adapter will not load against the quantised model, your options are to run
inference on the full model too — much slower, more VRAM — or to abandon the LoRA
and use the post-hoc face swap described at the end.

---

## Step 3 — train (template, verify before use)

Install ai-toolkit per its own instructions, then a config along these lines:

```yaml
job: extension
config:
  name: narrator_h3
  process:
    - type: sd_trainer
      training_folder: A:/Users/rhine/lora_training/output
      device: cuda:0

      network:
        type: lora
        linear: 32          # rank. 16-32 is plenty for one face
        linear_alpha: 32

      save:
        dtype: float16
        save_every: 250
        max_step_saves_to_keep: 6

      datasets:
        - folder_path: A:/Users/rhine/Documents/Codex/2026-08-07/referenced-chatgpt-conversation-this-is-an-2/COMFYUI_STORY_HANDOFF_2026-08-09/outputs/equal_shares/lora_datasets/narrator
          caption_ext: txt
          caption_dropout_rate: 0.05
          shuffle_tokens: false
          cache_latents_to_disk: true
          resolution: [512, 768, 1024]

      train:
        batch_size: 1
        steps: 2000
        gradient_accumulation_steps: 1
        train_unet: true
        train_text_encoder: false
        gradient_checkpointing: true
        noise_scheduler: flowmatch
        optimizer: adamw8bit
        lr: 1e-4
        dtype: bf16

      model:
        name_or_path: <full-precision MiniMax H3 weights>
        is_video: true

      sample:
        sampler: flowmatch
        sample_every: 250
        width: 736
        height: 416
        prompts:
          - "ohwx_narrator, a man in a dark 1960s suit addressing the camera in a sterile waiting room, black and white"
          - "ohwx_narrator standing in a spotlight, three-quarter view, black and white"
        neg: ""
        seed: 42
        walk_seed: false
        guidance_scale: 4
        sample_steps: 20
```

Keys I am least confident about, in order: `model.is_video`, the H3 model loader
name, `noise_scheduler`, and whether target modules need naming explicitly for this
architecture. Those are exactly the ones the guide will specify.

Watch the sample images at each save. When the face locks and before the background
starts baking in, stop — usually somewhere between 1200 and 2000 steps at rank 32 on
a set this size. Overtraining shows up as the model reproducing `00A`'s exact
background whatever you prompt.

## Step 4 — use it in ComfyUI

Drop the `.safetensors` into `A:\Users\rhine\ComfyUI-Shared\models\loras\`, add a
LoRA loader between `UNETLoader` and `BasicGuider` in your working graph, and put the
trigger word at the front of the prompt:

```
ohwx_narrator. One continuous unbroken take.

CAMERA
...
```

Start at strength **0.6–0.8**. Too high and it flattens expression and drags the
background of the training set in with it.

### Apply it to nine clips, not all 124

The Narrator appears in `00A`, `00B`, `00C`, `00I`, `00K`, `00L`, `00M`, `00N`, `00O`
— and nowhere else in the film. Every one of the 43 accepted clips was rendered
without a LoRA, so the safe move is to load it only for those nine and leave the rest
of the baseline untouched.

**Record it.** A LoRA is a change to the generation stack, and `generation_audit.json`
exists to prove which stack produced which clip. Note the LoRA name, strength, and
which clips used it.

---

## What this will and will not fix

**Will fix:** the Narrator looking like a different man in `00A` than in `00K`. That
is what a character LoRA is for.

**Will not fix:** the morph in the `boundary_03_v2 → boundary_04_v2` shot. He and the
standing man occupy nearly the same screen position between those two anchors, so the
model grows one into the other. A LoRA changes the face the morph arrives at; it does
not stop the morph. That shot still needs the entry-edge, depth cue and
anti-transformation clause.

**Will not fix:** the wides. At 22 px there is nothing for a LoRA to express.

---

## The cheaper alternative, if the base-model check fails

`insightface\inswapper_128.onnx` and the `reactor` nodes are already installed. A
post-hoc face swap onto already-rendered footage, using a canonical Narrator face,
gives cross-clip consistency with no training and no re-render.

It operates at 128 px, so it is good for his close and medium shots and useless in
the wides — which are the shots where his face is unreadable anyway. For a character
in nine shots this is a genuinely reasonable answer, and it is an afternoon rather
than a night.

chunks.heading: # Driving the H3 graph by hand in ComfyUI
chunks.text:
# Driving the H3 graph by hand in ComfyUI

Two traps that only bite when you run the workflow manually rather than through
`minimax_story_runner.py`. Both were hit on 2026-08-10.

## Trap 1 — the saved workflow says 1:1 (Square), and always has

`ResolutionSelector` is stored as `1:1 (Square)` in **both** graph files:

- `outputs/equal_shares/runtime/proven_manual_minimax_h3_api.json` — node 115
- `outputs/equal_shares/runtime/proven_manual_minimax_h3_workflow.json`

The automation never produced square video because the runner overwrites that
field at submit time from `story_config.json`:

```python
selector["aspect_ratio"] = config.get("aspect_ratio", "16:9 (Widescreen)")
selector["megapixels"]   = float(config.get("megapixels", 0.3))
selector["multiple"]     = int(config.get("resolution_multiple", 32))
```

So **the file on disk has never matched what actually rendered.** Load it in the
GUI and you inherit a setting every automated run discarded.

Set it by hand every time:

| field | value |
|---|---|
| aspect_ratio | `16:9 (Widescreen)` |
| multiple | `32` |
| megapixels | see below |

`1:1` cannot give you 736×416. 736×416 is 1.769 — essentially 16:9. At 1:1 and
0.3 MP the selector returns roughly 544×544.

Worth fixing the two graph files so they say `16:9 (Widescreen)`, since the
runner overrides the field anyway and the stored value serves no purpose except
to mislead whoever opens it next.

## Trap 2 — resolution is megapixels, not width and height

`{{WIDTH}}` and `{{HEIGHT}}` are only used when no `ResolutionSelector` exists in
the graph. This graph has one, so those tokens are dead. Editing width and height
changes nothing.

| megapixels | output at 16:9, multiple 32 | vs baseline |
|---|---|---|
| 0.30 | 736×416 | everything rendered so far |
| 0.59 | 1024×576 | 1.9× pixels |
| 1.43 | 1600×896 | 4.6× |
| 1.54 | 1664×928 | 5.0×, about the native size of the reference frames |

## Use the real reference frames, not the thumbnails

The anchors are **1672×941**:

```
outputs\equal_shares\frames\scene_###\boundary_##.png
```

The 520×293 files in `EQUAL_SHARES_GENERATION_LIST\thumbs\` on the Desktop are
downscaled copies made for browsing the HTML list. They are 3.2× smaller on each
edge. Feeding one to the model discards detail for nothing, and it will
invalidate any test of whether resolution drives the face failures.

`index.html` prints the full original path under every image.

## Frame count is yours to compute when running manually

The runner normally derives it. By hand, round the frame count **up to the next
value congruent to 5 modulo 17**:

```python
base = round(duration * 24)
frames = base + (5 - (base % 17)) % 17
```

8 s → 192 frames (already 5 mod 17). 12 s → 288 → 294. 15 s → 360 → 362.

Recompute it if you change duration. It does not change with resolution.

## Everything else to hold constant

`qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors`, video VAE

`minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors`, `res_multistep` / `simple`, denoise 1.0,
20 steps, 24 fps, 8-bit, SageAttention on. Never a Turbo model, node, or LoRA.

## And the prompt itself

Use the `optimized_prompt` column from `generation_list.csv` — the manual-paste
variant, which carries the dialogue once. The `optimized_prompt_for_runner`
column omits the spoken line because the runner appends its own AUDIO LOCK; that
variant is wrong for manual use. See `PROMPT_REPETITION_RULE.md`.

# Your manual ComfyUI session — reconstructed

Recovered from ComfyUI's own PNG metadata. Every generation writes a PNG beside the video, and ComfyUI embeds the entire API graph in that PNG's `prompt` text chunk, so the session is fully recoverable — clip, anchors, duration, aspect ratio, seed, steps, and the exact prompt text that was submitted.

**24 attempts, 20:31 to 01:46. 7 videos kept. 29 % keep rate.**

## What you did, in order

| Time | Clip | Anchors | Attempts | Kept |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20:31–22:17 | `00A`/`00C` hybrid — **not a configured pair** | `narrator_close_v3` → `entry_start_v2` | 8 | `MiniMax_H3_00002` |
| 22:32–00:25 | `00B` revised pull-back — **not a configured pair** | `narrator_close_v3` → `boundary_00_v2` | 7 | `00003`, `00006` |
| 00:32 | `00C` | `boundary_00_v2` → `entry_start_v2` | 1 | `00007` |
| 00:40–01:15 | `00D` | `entry_start_v2` → `boundary_01_v2` | 5 | `00008` |
| 01:28–01:38 | `00D2` | `boundary_01_v2` → `boundary_02_v2` | 2 | `00009` |
| 01:46 | `00E` | `boundary_02_v2` → `boundary_03_v2` | 1 | `00010` |

**You left off having just rendered `00E`. Next in story order is `00F`.**

`00D` cost five attempts and `00B` seven — the same clips, roughly the same ratio as the automation's history. `00C`, `00D2` and `00E` came quickly.

| 01:46 | `00E` | `boundary_02_v2` → `boundary_03_v2` | 1 | `00010` |

**You left off having just rendered `00E`. Next in story order is `00F`.**

`00D` cost five attempts and `00B` seven — the same clips, roughly the same ratio as the automation's history. `00C`, `00D2` and `00E` came quickly.

## Three problems the metadata exposes

**The first eight runs were rendered at 1:1 Square.** Every run from 20:31 to 22:17 has `ResolutionSelector.aspect_ratio = "1:1 (Square)"`. You fixed it at 22:32 and everything since has been 16:9. This is the trap in `MANUAL_COMFYUI_SETTINGS.md`: the saved workflow ships with 1:1 and the automation only ever looked correct because the runner overwrites that field at submit time. Roughly two hours of work went into square renders. **Worth fixing the value inside both graph files so it cannot happen again.**

**Seven prompts arrived wrapped in quotation marks** — including the most recent, the `00E` run at 01:46. The submitted text begins `"One continuous unbroken take.` and ends `…never leaves the window."`, so the entire prompt is one quoted string.

That is almost certainly a copy-paste artefact: CSV wraps any field containing commas or newlines in double quotes, so copying a cell out of the raw `generation_list.csv` in a text editor brings the escaping with it. It matters because the prompt also says *spoken words appear only inside quotation marks* — wrapping the whole prompt in quotes tells the model the entire thing is a line to be spoken. This is very likely a contributor to the random speech you noticed.

**Fixed:** there is now a `prompts\` folder with one `.txt` per clip, 124 files, containing exactly the column-U text with no escaping. Copy from `prompts\00F.txt` rather than from the CSV.

**Rejected raws were deleted.** The video numbering has gaps — `00001`, `00004`, `00005` are gone — and only 7 of 24 attempts survive. That is your call in your own workspace, but it does mean the failed attempts can no longer be compared against the keepers, and it is the one house rule the project otherwise holds firmly. The automation preserves every attempt.

## What your workflow does that the automation does not

Comparing your graph against `proven_manual_minimax_h3_api.json`, the model stack is identical — same UNet, same `qwen3vl_32b` text encoder, both VAEs, `res_multistep` / `simple`, 20 steps, denoise 1.0, 0.3 MP. You have not changed resolution.

You added three things:

**1. Automatic frame count.** A `PrimitiveFloat` duration feeds a `ComfyMathExpression`:

```
max(5, round(a * 24)) + (5 - (max(5, round(a * 24)) % 17)) % 17
```

That is exactly the 5-mod-17 rule, computed in the graph. You type 8.0 and the length derives itself. The runner already does this in Python, so the automation matches — but this is a real improvement for manual work and removes the one number that is easy to get wrong by hand.

**2. Last-frame extraction.** `SaveVideo` → `GetVideoComponents` → `GetImageSize` → `ComfyMathExpression` (`min(max(int(a if a >= 0 else b + a), 0), b - 1)`, with `a = 361`, which clamps to the final frame) → `ImageFromBatch` → `SaveImage`. Every generation also saves its own last frame, so the end of one shot can become the opening anchor of the next.

The automation had no equivalent. It does now — `work\save_last_frames.py` does the same thing with ffmpeg, which keeps the proven graph untouched and works retroactively on clips rendered before the idea existed.

**3. A dead node.** `ImageScaleToTotalPixels` at 1 MP (node 119) feeds only a `GetImageSize` that feeds nothing, and its own image input is unconnected. It has no effect on generation. If that was an attempt to upscale the reference images, it never took — worth deleting or wiring up deliberately.

## Two anchor pairings that are not in the config

Your `00B` runs use `narrator_close_v3` → `boundary_00_v2`. The config has `00B` as **single-anchor** from `boundary_00_v2` with no last frame. Your pairing is the corrected pull-back and it is better, but the automation will not reproduce it until the config is changed:

```json
"first_frame": "frames/scene_000/boundary_narrator_close_v3.png",
"last_frame":  "frames/scene_000/boundary_00_v2.png"
```

Your first eight runs use `narrator_close_v3` → `entry_start_v2`, which is not any configured clip. It spans what the config splits into `00A` and `00C`. I have not guessed at what you intend — if those two are merging into one shot, the config needs to say so, and `00A`'s and `00C`'s durations and narration need reconciling.

python work\save_last_frames.py            # every clip in the manifest

```powershell

& $Py ".\outputs\minimax_story_runner.py" ".\outputs\equal_shares\story_config.json" --check

chunks.heading: # Prompt optimization against the MiniMax H3 guide
chunks.text:
# Prompt optimization against the MiniMax H3 guide

Source: **MiniMax H3 Prompting Guide + 44 Video Examples**, Bennett Heyn, fal.ai, last updated 2026-07-30 — <https://fal.ai/learn/devs/minimax-h3-prompting-guide>

**Coverage note.** I read the introduction, the "Three Input Modes" section, and the full "Prompting MiniMax H3: Key Techniques" section, which is where all the actual guidance lives. I sampled but did not read all 44 worked examples in the middle of the page. Nothing below rests on an example I did not read.

One caveat throughout: the guide describes fal's **hosted** endpoints. Equal Shares runs H3 locally in ComfyUI, so endpoint names map to workflow shapes rather than URLs, and the hosted defaults are not binding on a local run. Where that distinction matters I say so.

---

## The headline finding: you are running the model at 29 % of its native short edge

The guide states the native output spec plainly:

> "Every endpoint returns 5 to 15 seconds at 24 FPS in **2K**, which puts **1440 pixels on the short edge** for ratios between 16:9 and 9:16 and reaches roughly **3.7 megapixels** on wider formats."

Equal Shares generates at **736 × 416 — a 416-pixel short edge, 0.31 MP.**

| | Guide's native spec | This project | Ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| Short edge | 1440 px | 416 px | 29 % |
| Megapixels | ~2.1 at 16:9 (3.7 at 21:9) | 0.31 | ~15 % |
| Frame rate | 24 fps | 24 fps | matches |
| Duration | 5–15 s | 5–15 s | matches |

Everything else about the configuration sits inside the documented envelope. Resolution is the one axis that is far outside it.

This is now the best-supported explanation for the failure that has dominated review — distorted and morphing faces. At 416 px tall, a face in a medium shot is 20 to 30 pixels. The features that make Kent recognisable (mustache, receding hairline, brow) have almost no pixels to live in, and the model fills the gap with a generic face. It also explains the `16A` furniture drift: at this scale the model is failing to hold static set geometry, not just faces.

Two things follow.

**This is the first thing to test in ComfyUI**, ahead of any prompt rewriting. Take one rejected clip — `17C` and `18A` are good candidates, both rejected purely for face failure — and re-render it at a substantially larger size with everything else held constant. If identity holds, resolution was the problem and no amount of prompt work would have fixed it.

**Expect a real cost.** 1440 px short edge is roughly 12× the pixels of 416, so VRAM and time per clip both rise steeply on a 5080. There is likely a usable middle: 1280 × 720 is 2.9× the short edge and 3× the pixels of the current setting. Find the largest size that fits and holds identity, rather than jumping straight to 2K. Whatever you choose, the frame-count rule still applies — round up to the next value congruent to 5 modulo 17.

## How the current prompts measure against the eight techniques

Measured across all 124 prompts in `story_config.json`. Median prompt length is **1,361 characters against a 7,000-character budget** — you are using about a fifth of the space available.

| # | Technique | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Assign a job to every reference | **partial** |
| 2 | Timed shot list for anything longer than one beat | **absent — 0 of 124** |
| 3 | Direct the audio | **done** |
| 4 | State what you do not want | **partial — wrong mechanism** |
| 5 | Lock identity explicitly | **done, and done well** |
| 6 | For edits, name change and constraint together | n/a — not doing edits |
| 7 | Use camera and film language | **absent — 0 of 124** |
| 8 | Describe transitions as events | n/a — you want no transitions |

### 2. No timed shot list — the biggest gap

> "With 7,000 characters to work with and up to 15 seconds of output, you can storyboard inside the prompt. Timecoded blocks work well… MiniMax H3 follows the structure, and **it keeps the pacing from drifting into a slideshow**."

Every prompt carries **dialogue** timing — `[1s-8s] Faith White, calm, looking at Kent: "…"` — and no **visual** timing at all. The picture is described as a single undifferentiated paragraph covering 7 to 15 seconds.

That is very likely why the failures cluster where they do. When the model is given no structure for seconds 4 through 15, it invents one. Look at what it invented:

- `10B` — nothing scripted for seconds 3–15, so it filled the room with eight to ten people.
- `11C` — nothing scripted after the opening beat, so it cut to a new angle at 4 s and put its own name on the counter.
- `12B`, `12C`, `14A` — same shape, jumps between 1 s and 4 s.
- `17A`, `17B`, `18D` — props left undescribed over time, so they morph.

The dialogue timecodes prove the model honours timed blocks; that instruction is being followed. The visual track just is not being given any.

### 4. Negative direction is in the wrong place and the wrong form

The guide's examples are natural-language prohibitions written as sentences: *"No soft dissolves or fluid morphs." "Do not introduce Chinese text, garbled characters, or misspellings." "Do not show giant eyes, split mouths, fangs, threatening behavior, lunges, sudden black frames, or jump scares."*

The project has a 251-character comma-separated keyword list in a separate `negative_prompt` field:

> cruel sneering people, obvious villain, dystopian grime, identity drift, face change, wardrobe change, continuity error, duplicate person, missing person, deformed anatomy, extra limbs, flicker, jump cut, text artifacts, watermark, low quality, blurry

That is Stable-Diffusion-style negative conditioning, not the H3-style in-prompt prohibition the guide describes. Note that your prompts already end with a sentence-form prohibition list — *"No subtitles, captions, visible prompt text, logos, watermarks, identity drift, duplicate people, glass barriers, or Turbo generation"* — which is the right mechanism. It is just short, abstract, and doing less work than it could.

Abstract nouns are weak here. `duplicate person` did not prevent two Kents in `13A`. A sentence would have: *"Exactly one person is in this shot. No second figure appears in the doorway, in a mirror, or anywhere in frame at any time."*

Also worth removing: **"Turbo generation" is not a visual concept.** Every prompt ends by telling the model not to be a Turbo model. It cannot act on that, and it spends tokens in the highest-attention position in the prompt. The Turbo prohibition is a pipeline rule, and it belongs in the config and the docs where it already is — not in the prompt.

### 7. No camera or film language

> "MiniMax H3 reads cinematography vocabulary directly. Lens choice, movement, exposure behavior, and stock character all translate."

Not one of the 124 prompts contains a lens, a camera move, or a framing term. The only camera instruction anywhere is the negative phrase *"one continuous shot with no internal edit."*

That is a prohibition without a positive alternative — you have told the model what not to do with the camera and nothing about what to do. Given the number of rejections caused by the shot jumping, this is a cheap, high-value addition: *"Locked-off camera on a tripod, 50 mm, eye level. The framing does not change at any point. No pan, tilt, zoom, push, or reframe."*

### 1. References have jobs, but only two of them

Your anchors are labelled — *"`<Picture 1>` is the opening visual anchor and `<Picture 2>` is the closing visual anchor"* — which is exactly right for first-and-last-frame work.

What the guide points at is bigger. Reference to Video accepts **up to nine images**, and the technique it calls highest-leverage is giving each one a distinct job. You have `references/alex_vale_master_v1.png` and `references/ensemble_cast_master_v1.png` sitting in the project as authoritative identity sheets, and they are currently used only by humans and by Gemini — they are never passed to H3 at generation time.

If your local workflow can take additional reference images alongside the boundary frames, passing the character sheet as a dedicated identity reference is the single most direct attack on the identity problem: *"Use Image 1 as the opening frame and Image 2 as the closing frame. Use Image 3 only as the identity reference for Kent Brentwood — match his face, hairline, mustache, and build exactly; do not take composition, lighting, or wardrobe from it."*

**Check whether `proven_manual_minimax_h3_api.json` supports extra reference inputs before planning around this.** I have not verified that it does, and changing the graph is a bigger step than changing prompt text.

### 3 and 5 — already good

Audio direction remains specific, but the old suppression rationale is
superseded. Native H3 audio is now the Stage-1 deliverable. Dialogue, ambience,
music cues, and effects must be generated and validated at 0.2 MP before picture
work begins. The accepted full WAV is then referenced during Stage 2 and muxed
unchanged onto the selected picture. For clips whose direction says no music,
keep that lock; the continuous score is one master track across the final edit,
not a new H3 song per clip.

Identity locking is genuinely well done and matches technique 5 closely — named features rather than vague description: *"short dark receding hair, distinctive dark mustache, teal cardigan, cream shirt, charcoal trousers, worn brown shoes, canvas shoulder bag."* Keep this exactly as it is.

One speculative note on audio. The model generates speech natively and has been inventing gibberish dialogue throughout. If it is driving lip movement to match invented speech, that is a plausible contributor to face distortion, and the two problems may be one problem. Your prompts already say *"Keep each speaker's mouth closed outside their assigned line."* Worth testing a fully silent variant — *"No speech, no voices, no vocalisations from anyone in frame at any time. All mouths remain closed."* — on a clip with no scripted dialogue, and seeing whether faces improve.
