chunks.heading: # 2026-09-23a — edge gateway audit fixes, stopped before phone cutover
chunks.text:
# 2026-09-23a — edge gateway audit fixes, stopped before phone cutover

Code and host ACL changes from the 2026-09-23 edge audit were applied. Firewall
narrowing, proxy shutdown, phone private-launcher install, and credential
rotation were not. The operator said stop after the gateway had already been
restarted onto this code.

## Code

- Ledger: expire every overdue lease inside claim, admin view, and complete.
  A live lease is not handed to a second claim. Completion requires the owning
  device, the attempt number, and an unexpired lease. Replay of a stored result
  is limited to that owner. Queue cap 32. Terminal rows older than 14 days are
  deleted on inject. Context check rejects prompts that cannot share the
  512-token phone window with generation. Body cap is 262144 bytes.
- TLS material: device ids are checked before any certificate file is written.
  `../escaped` no longer creates a sibling directory. An existing device
  directory is not overwritten.
- Admin API requires a bearer token from `runtime/admin.token`. The file was
  created on the restarted gateway. Its contents were not printed.
- Phone TLS handshake runs on the worker thread with a 10s handshake timeout,
  a 30s request timeout, and a cap of 4 in-flight connections.
- Worker: gateway host pinned to `https://10.90.91.1` unless loopback is
  explicitly allowed with `EDGE_TLS_PIN_SHA256`. Redirects are refused.
  `EDGE_SSL_NO_HOSTNAME` no longer disables name checks. Completion is retried
  from a private outbox. Stdout and stderr captures are capped. Every runtime
  branch passes `-c 512` and `-ub 4`.
- Desktop proxy and client response bodies are capped and the proxy closes the
  backend response on success and error paths.
- Private phone launcher sources are `local_agent/worker_farm/phone/edge_boot.py`
  and `edge_watch.py`. The same bytes were copied to `practice-score\work`.
  They were not installed on the phone.

## Verification

`python -m unittest local_agent.edge_gateway.test_edge_gateway local_agent.worker_farm.test_termux_powerinfer2_edge_worker` — 27 tests, OK. No model inference.

## Host

Runtime DACLs under `local_agent/edge_gateway/runtime` were rebuilt so files
allow only `NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM`, `BUILTIN\Administrators`, and
`DURANGAMINGPC\rhine`. The first `icacls /grant` used directory-only
`(OI)(CI)` flags on files and left those files with an empty DACL. Explicit
file grants were applied before the gateway was started again. Confirmed on
`tls\ca.key.pem`, `edge_ledger.sqlite3`, and `admin.token`.

The previous gateway PID 22000 was stopped. The replacement is listening on
`10.90.91.1:8743` and `127.0.0.1:8744` (PID 40300 at restart). The phone still
runs the previous worker, which does not send `attempt`, so a live completion
from that worker is rejected until the phone copy is updated.

chunks.heading: # 2026-09-23b — prompt-pack plain headers, Flux override actually enforced
chunks.text:
# 2026-09-23b — prompt-pack plain headers, Flux override actually enforced

Trigger: chat `a051127dca4b4a25`, 18:07. An 837,724-char paste (EDITOR
OVERRIDES preamble + 102 clips) failed `ingest_prompt_pack` with "No clip
prompts were parsed". The paste was never saved (only empty `clips/` and
`outputs/`), and `managed_prompt_pack.py` was edited at 19:08, after the
failure. So the exact failing input and code cannot be replayed. The error
proves zero `##`–`####` `C\d+` headers matched and the plain-header parser
did not run. Plain `C001 — START FRAME IMAGE` headers with no FULLY MERGED
title fit that. It is the most likely shape, not a proven one.

## Code

- `local_agent/managed_prompt_pack.py`
  - Plain-header parser and `is_prompt_pack` no longer require the
    `FULLY MERGED` / `CAMERA-LOGIC CORRECTED` title. Threshold is START FRAME
    headers: 12 without the title, 4 with it. Before, the whole-regex count
    included LAST/VIDEO headers, so "12 matches" meant 4 clips.
  - `backrooms_compile` is loaded by file path from the project root. The old
    `from backrooms_compile import …` raised `ModuleNotFoundError` on every
    Python version, because `local_agent/` is not the root. A bare `except`
    swallowed it, so no ingested clip ever got `model_profile`, and
    `initial_frame_job` fell back to realvisxl even for "Flux, not SDXL"
    packs. The loader restores `sys.path`, because the module prepends the
    project root on import.
  - Flux is forced only when the source asks for it (`## EDITOR OVERRIDES`,
    `### 0. Flux`, "still-image generator is Flux"). `JobSettings` defaults to
    Flux, but packs without overrides keep their production behavior
    (unset → realvisxl). If the compile module cannot load, the marker
    fallback still sets flux, and every clip carries `compile_fallback`.
  - A failed ingest writes `failed_ingest_<sha>.diagnostics.json`: regex
    counts, branch, sample clip-id lines, head/tail 200 chars, compile-load
    status. The summary is appended to the error text.
  - `progress.json` records `model_profiles` counts.
- `backrooms_compile.py`: regex pulled out of the f-string. It was a
  SyntaxError on 3.10. On 3.12 the `\\s` inside it was a literal backslash, so
  the `## APPENDIX` alternative never matched.
- `local_agent/tools.py`: `ingest_prompt_pack` and a completed
  `export_prompt_pack_outputs` return `operator_message`, for example "N clips
  exported and ready … Say 'render it' to start stills+video production."
  The model is told to relay it and not end the turn silently. The render
  gate and the GPU gate are unchanged.

Spec: `backrooms-frame-chaining-spec.md`. `batch_run_backrooms_gvd.py` renders a
fresh FLUX still for every clip. This change lets it start a clip from the
previous clip's actual last frame when `work/scene_reasoner.py` says
`context_video` and two deterministic guards allow it. **Default is `off`**, so
existing invocations behave as before. No render was run.

## Code

- `local_agent/video_chain.py` (new)
  - `extract_last_frame()` uses the same ffprobe + ffmpeg subprocess pattern
    as `dspy_optimizer.extract_eval_frames` (CREATE_NO_WINDOW, 15 s/60 s
    timeouts, check=True). It seeks to duration−1 s and writes with
    `-update 1`, so the file ends as the true last frame.
  - Unlike eval frames, any failure raises `ChainFrameError`. There is no
    guessed 2 s fallback duration.
  - Output name is stem + content digest (not path digest), under
    `local_agent/runtime/gvd_backrooms_batch/chain_frames/`.
  - `upload_to_comfy_input()` POSTs `/upload/image`, the same multipart form as
    `gvd_qa/smoke_i2v_from_receipt.py`. Nothing uploaded frames before:
    `bind_h3_image_frames` passes a basename that ComfyUI's input dir must
    already hold.
- `local_agent/dspy_orchestrator.py`: new `prune_unreferenced_flux_nodes()`,
  called in `build_minimax_graph` when a first frame is bound and the run is
  not stills-only.
  - Rebinding `first_frame` already orphaned the FLUX branch. Pruning makes
    the skipped still explicit in the payload dump (`_meta.flux_still_skipped`,
    `pruned_flux_nodes`).
  - This also affects the single-clip CLI when a QA-accepted still is passed.
    Its FLUX nodes were already orphaned there, so what executes is unchanged.
- `work/scene_reasoner.py`
  - `decide_shot` / `reason_about_shot` accept an optional explicit `history`.
    The append-only log follows decision order, which differs from story
    order on resume, `--force`, or repeated passes.
  - History rows may carry `camera_mode`, `speakers`, `shot_summary`. Before
    this, the model was asked about character reappearance while seeing only
    prior decisions, never what the shots contained.
- `batch_run_backrooms_gvd.py`
  - `--continuity off|shadow|live`, `--chain-max-consecutive`
    (`CHAIN_MAX_CONSECUTIVE = 4`), `--continuity-story`.
  - Policy: `continuity_policy()`. Guards on top of the reasoner:
    camera-mode change (`Camera Mode:` in the clip header) and the ceiling.
  - Live fallbacks, every one to a fresh still:
    - reasoner error or blocked (including confidence < 0.6)

# 2026-09-23e — Backrooms chaining: refine checkpoint at the chain ceiling

Follows 2026-09-23d, which wired the clip-to-clip chaining from
`backrooms-frame-chaining-spec.md` but left out step 5. In 23d, a clip past
`CHAIN_MAX_CONSECUTIVE` got a **fresh FLUX still**. That is a hard visual cut
in the middle of a continuous scene, and the spec rules it out.

Now a `context_video` clip past the ceiling gets a **refine checkpoint**. The
previous clip's actual last frame goes through a low-denoise FLUX img2img
pass, and MiniMax animates the result. The chain counts from 0 again after it.

Real cuts are unchanged and still get a fresh still:

- the reasoner answers `reference_image` or `none`
- the camera mode changes
- a character re-enters

`--continuity` still defaults to `off`. No render was run.

## Code

- `local_agent/dspy_orchestrator.py`
  - New `bind_refine_checkpoint()`. It rewires the existing FLUX branch:
    `LoadImage 1003` → `ImageScale 1004` (to node 5's size, 1280×704,
    lanczos, center crop) → `VAEEncode 1005` (FLUX VAE `10`) → `KSampler 3`
    `latent_image`, with `denoise` set to the refine value.
  - `EmptyFlux2LatentImage 5` is removed.
  - Node 3 keeps its model (`41`), positive (`12`←`6` start_prompt) and
    negative (`7`). The refine is therefore steered by the same model and
    text a fresh still would use. This path has no LoRA nodes to carry over.
  - `20.first_frame` stays `["8",0]`: MiniMax gets the refined image.
  - Optional core `ImageSharpen 1006` (alpha > 0 only). Every consumer of
    `["8",0]` is rewired to it.
  - Raises if nodes 3, 5, 8 or 10 are not the expected classes, or if denoise
    is not strictly between 0 and 1. The alternative, silently falling back
    to a plain T2I still, is worse.
  - `build_minimax_graph` / `generate_minimax_clip` take `refine_frame_path`,
    `refine_denoise` and `refine_sharpen_alpha`.
    - A refine frame cannot be combined with `start_frame_path`, because that
      path bypasses FLUX: this raises `ValueError`.
    - Refine params are part of the output-prefix hash.
  - `trim_graph_to_stills_only` saves from `1006` when it exists. Stills-only
    plus refine yields just the refined PNG.
  - New helper `_comfy_input_name()`, factored out of `bind_h3_image_frames`
    with no behavior change.
- `generate_video.submit_comfy`: passes the three refine kwargs through.

    Scene-change guards are checked first, so a real cut past the ceiling is
    still a fresh still.
  - New CLI flags:
    - `--chain-reset refine|fresh_still` (default `refine`)

# 2026-09-23f — Refine-checkpoint denoise tuned live: REFINE_DENOISE 0.30 → 0.15

This is the first live run of the refine checkpoint from 2026-09-23e.
It ran FLUX only (stills-only); MiniMax was not used.

## Backend

- The operator asked me to start Rockernow.
- Before starting, nothing listened on 8188 and there was no ComfyUI process.
  The only Python processes were two `practice-score` uvicorn servers on
  :8000. The GPU was idle at 31 °C.
- Started through the sanctioned path,
  `.grok\long-running-background-tasks\restart_comfy_rockernow.ps1`. It logged
  "no listener on 8188" and spawned `start_comfy_rockernow.bat`, so only one
  listener exists.
- `/system_stats` answered after 183 s: ComfyUI 0.36.0, RTX 5080. The queue
  was empty.
- **Rockernow was left running.**

## Upscale-node question from 23e, now closed

- `/object_info` confirms `LoadImage`, `ImageScale`, `VAEEncode`,
  `ImageSharpen`, `KSampler`, `EmptyFlux2LatentImage` and `UltimateSDUpscale`.
- `UpscaleModelLoader` lists all 10 models from
  `ComfyUI-Shared\models\upscale_models` (4x-UltraSharp, RealESRGAN_x2plus, …).
  They reach Rockernow through the Desktop extra-model-paths config.

## The run

- C012 has never been rendered: `progress.json` has C001–C008 only, and C009
  is interrupted. The requested C012→C013 pair was therefore impossible.
- I used the latest real consecutive pair instead: **C008's actual last
  frame, refined with C009's batch prompts**.
  - Both clips are camera mode A, and shadow v3 says chain.
  - Prompts come from `apply_pipeline_rules`, rules v2026-09-18.v1,
    env `apartment_tripod`.
- Tool: `scripts/refine_denoise_compare.py`.
- Source frame:
  `local_agent/runtime/gvd_backrooms_batch/chain_frames/gvd_br_c008_4f1bb60c4c_00001__6ee934a38d_last.png`
- Outputs: `ComfyUI-Shared\output\dspy_opt\dspy_opt_gvd_refine_tune_c009_d{10,15,20,35}_*.png`
- Reports: `refine_tuning/C009_20260923T212627.json` (0.20, 0.35) and
  `C009_20260923T213140.json` (0.10, 0.15).
- Payload dump `debug_refine_tune_c009_d20_payload.json` confirms the refine

  - node 5 absent
  - `3.latent_image=["1005",0]`, `3.denoise=0.2`

  - Saved from node 8

## What I saw, at native resolution on the face crop

- **At every value:** pose, blocking, tripod, camera position, room, and
  lighting layout are preserved.
- **0.35:** a different, younger, clean-shaven face and tidier hair. Rejected;
  it is a fresh generation wearing the old pose.
- **0.20:** the face is already smoothed and de-aged, with stubble fading.
  The T-shirt print text and the camcorder brand text are regenerated
  (different glyphs).
- **0.10–0.15:** reads as the same person, with stubble, mouth shape, and hair
  mass kept.
- **No value measurably sharpened the face.** Edge variance is flat. The
  ~12% rise in whole-frame edges is grain and texture.
- Every value warms the image a little (R +1.4 to +5.5), so the refine adds
  colour drift instead of removing it.

## Decision

`REFINE_DENOISE = 0.15`. It is the highest value that kept identity at face
scale, and it leaves some headroom for resetting drift. The
`--refine-denoise` help no longer says "untuned".

55/55 tests pass (`test_batch_run_backrooms_continuity`,
`test_batch_run_backrooms_gvd`).

## Side finding

`C001_first_frame.png` (in `refine_tuning/`) shows a different actor from
C008:

- C001: a teenager with short straight hair and a grey tee, in a blue bedroom
- C008: a curly-haired adult, in a bare pale room

That is the current `--continuity off` behaviour, a fresh independent FLUX
still per clip. Identity has already been lost by clip 8. So even a refine
that cleans little is far better for continuity than a `fresh_still` reset.

## Still unverified

- The source frame is first-generation. It has plain codec softness but no
  accumulated chain drift, so whether 0.15 actually *reverses* drift is
  unmeasured. Repeat on the last frame of a 4-deep chain after the small live
  test.
- The refine has only been checked in stills-only mode. No MiniMax clip has
  been rendered from a refined frame. The render-level check in 23e step 2
  (`ffprobe` embedded workflow) is still to do.
- Prompt-only conditioning has no identity anchor: this path has no LoRA or

# 2026-09-23g — render_story_image_batch: port-8188 refusal now structured, named, and correctly retried

## Symptom
Chat `1d4a42d3b5834081`, 22:23:15: `render_story_image_batch` (7 jobs) failed job 0
and left 6 `not_started_after_failure`. The agent paraphrased it as a vague
"ComfyUI backend issue on port 8188".

## Evidence (live, not inferred)
- Raw failure (`local_agent/runtime/agentic_tasks/1d4a42d3b5834081.json`):
  `"error": "image-render preflight refused: a ComfyUI backend is listening on port 8188", "phase": "launch"`.
- No new `work/runtime/agent_image_jobs/*.log` since 2026-09-07 → nothing was spawned.
- `netstat`: 127.0.0.1:8188 LISTENING pid 52504, created 21:18:03, command line
  `ComfyUI\main.py --listen 127.0.0.1 --port 8188 ...` (Rockernow install),
  launched by `cmd.exe /c A:\Users\rhine\.grok\long-running-background-tasks\start_comfy_rockernow.bat`.
  Its log (`comfy_detached.log`) shows it served today's video prompts
  (13:11, 11:08; last prompt 22:00:51, globally interrupted 22:12). Queue idle at 22:4x.
- `work/runtime/image_render_owner.json`: released (pid 0, 2026-09-14) — not implicated.

## Root cause
1. `render_story_image` checks `router.gpu_busy()` first and re-raised its reason
   verbatim. That wording ("a ComfyUI backend is listening on port 8188") contains
   neither `"owns the backend"` nor `"already listening on port 8188"`, so the
   batch's 60-attempt retry loop broke on attempt 1 (zero retries), and the
   error never named who held the port.
2. Latent, same mechanism: `image_render.py` writes its manifest *before*
   `_stop_owned_backend()` in `finally`, so `await_story_image_job` reports job N
   complete while job N's own backend still holds 8188. Job N+1 then hit the same
   unmatched router wording and could fail with no retry.

The refusal itself was correct ("One backend, ever"); the bug was classification
and reporting.

chunks.heading: # 2026-09-23h — `_execute_plan` stop-on-ERROR scoped to prompt-pack plans

# 2026-09-23h — `_execute_plan` stop-on-ERROR scoped to prompt-pack plans

## Symptom

`python -m unittest test_native_tool_calling` (in `local_agent/`) had one
pre-existing failure:
`NativeToolTests.test_execute_plan_second_step_still_runs_after_first_raises`
— expected `['repair_jsonl_format', 'validate_powerinfer_calibration']`, got
`['repair_jsonl_format']`. It also failed with
`tools.py.bak_port8188_20260923T224853`, so it predates the 2026-09-23g
port-8188 change.

## Root cause — code regression, not a stale test

2026-09-03ad established the contract that the test encodes: a failing
`_execute_plan` step becomes an `ERROR:` result and **later steps still run**
(the jsonl_repair plan then revalidates and `_jsonl_repair_summary` reports
"No file was changed … repair failed: RuntimeError: …").

Later, prompt-pack plans were added to `_execute_plan` together with an
unconditional

```
if str(result).startswith("ERROR:"):
    # Never export the old source after the revised source failed ingest.
    break
```

The reason is valid for prompt-pack plans (ingest → export / render /
production must not continue from the old source after a failed ingest), but
the guard applied to **every** plan. `jsonl_repair` is the only other
multi-step plan in `action_resolver.classify`, so it alone regressed: the
revalidation step was skipped, `len(executed) >= 2` failed, and the canned
repair summary was bypassed. No changelog entry recorded the break.

## What changed

- **`local_agent/agent.py`** `_execute_plan`: the break now fires only when
  `plan.intent.startswith("prompt_pack_")`. Other plans keep the 2026-09-03ad
  continue-after-ERROR contract. Backup:
  `agent.py.bak_planerrorbreak_20260923T225456`.
- **`local_agent/test_native_tool_calling.py`**: added
  `test_execute_plan_prompt_pack_stops_after_failed_ingest` so the prompt-pack
  stop behaviour (previously untested) is locked alongside the jsonl_repair
  continue behaviour. Backup:
  `test_native_tool_calling.py.bak_planerrorbreak_20260923T225511`.

## Evidence

- `python -m unittest test_native_tool_calling` → `Ran 104 tests … OK`
  (was 103 with 1 failure).
- `python -m unittest discover -s . -p "test_*.py"` in `local_agent/` →
  1511 tests, 20 failures, 4 errors, 16 skipped. None are in
  `test_native_tool_calling`, and none go through `_execute_plan`:
  - `worker_farm.test_farm_core` (5) — need the farm `.venv` (Celery), per
    their own failure message; `worker_farm.test_tasks_mainprocess_exceptions`

    model; no ActionPlan runs).

    `test_production_integrity` hparam/POSIX-kill tests.
  These are left as-is and are outside this fix.

# 2026-09-24a — real still-QA wired into `render_story_image(_batch)`; `flux_still_batch.py` QA import regression fixed

## Why

Operator chat `1d4a42d3b5834081`: a `render_story_image_batch` still (a plain
empty living room) was followed, in later turns that made **no tool call**,
by a fabricated "the QA process confirmed… now marked as SELECTED" narrative,
including for a "Fall & Arrival" second image that was never rendered (that
turn's batch call was refused by the stale-specialist-project guard). The
chat still path had zero QA; the model had no data and invented a verdict.
The repo *does* have a working still QA (`creative_still_qa.py`), it was just
not reachable from this tool path.

## Part 0 — `flux_still_batch.py` QA call was broken (two latent bugs)

`import creative_still_qa as csqa` (still in `flux_still_batch.py.bak_people`)
was later rewritten to
`from creative_still_qa import empty_pov_prompt_boost, infer_visibility_expectation as csqa`.

1. `auto_approve(creative=True, prompt=…)` called `csqa.creative_approve(...)`
   on the *function* → `AttributeError: 'function' object has no attribute
   'creative_approve'` on every call (confirmed by loading the pre-fix file).
2. The same rewrite left the name `infer_visibility_expectation` **unbound**,
   so the empty-POV prompt/negative hardening (`_exp = infer_visibility_expectation(...)`
   near line 390) raised `NameError`, was swallowed by its `try/except`, and
   printed `WARN empty_pov_prompt_boost failed` — that hardening has silently
   never run since.

Fix: import line → `from creative_still_qa import empty_pov_prompt_boost, infer_visibility_expectation`;
call → `creative_still_qa.creative_approve(...)`. Exactly two lines differ from
backup `flux_still_batch.py.bak_csqafix_20260924` (CRLF preserved).

Verified on real stills (`ComfyUI-Shared/input/astra_backrooms_stills`) with
their compiled prompts, anchors and clip dicts: `auto_approve` now returns real
`(ok, reasons, report)` tuples — C001_last reject (room 0.251 / clothing 0.392 /
SFace 0.291; the known-bad frame), C002_last reject (SFace 0.177), C005_start
pass, C017_last reject (`unexpected_person_in_empty_pov` top_conf 0.863).
Pre-fix module: `AttributeError`, and `hasattr(module, "infer_visibility_expectation") == False`.

Pre-fix module: `AttributeError`, and `hasattr(module, "infer_visibility_expectation") == False`.

## Part 1 — `creative_still_qa` in the chat still path

`render_story_image` only *spawns* `work/image_render.py` and returns before a
PNG exists, so QA cannot run inside it. The output file first becomes known in
`story_image_job_status` (state=complete), which `await_story_image_job` and
`render_story_image_batch` both go through — so QA hooks there and covers both
the single-render and the batch path.

**`local_agent/tools.py`** (backup `tools.py.bak_stillqa_20260924`):

- `story_image_job_status` → on `state == "complete"` attaches `qa` =
  `_story_still_qa_cached(manifest)`: runs
  `creative_still_qa.creative_approve(png, prompt=<manifest prompt>, anchor=<see below>, clip=None, kind="last")`.
  Record: `checker, advisory, scope, anchor, verdict (pass|fail|error|not_run), ok, reject_reasons, report`.
  Cached at `outputs/stories/<story>/still_qa/<manifest stem>.json` (outside
  `manifests/`, so image_render's `image_*.json` glob never sees it);
  re-run if the anchor changed; errors/not_run are never cached and never
  reported as a pass.
- `render_story_image_batch`: `completed[i]["qa"]`, the stills passed to
  `present_story_stills_for_review` carry `qa`, new `qa_summary`, and
  `next_step` requires the reply to state each verdict as recorded.
- `present_story_stills_for_review`: returns `qa_summary`; note carries the same rule.
- `approve_story_stills`: records each story's last approved output in
  `work/runtime/story_qa_anchors.json` (keyed by `image_render._safe_segment(story)`),
  returned as `qa_anchors_recorded`.

**Decisions**

- *Anchor*: last **operator-approved** still for the story (never merely the
  last generated one); none yet → `anchor=None` (compare_stills then skips only
  the continuity comparisons).
- *clip/kind*: `clip=None, kind="last"`. `compare_stills` reads `clip` only for
  `camera_mode`/`visibility_mode` overrides and `require_room_continuity`;
  `kind` is accepted but unused by `infer_visibility_expectation`. The chat
  path has no clip register, so there is nothing real to pass.
- *Advisory, not blocking*: a failed still is still presented, labelled with
  its reasons; the human review gate is unchanged. A hard stop for clear cases
  (e.g. unexpected face in an empty-POV prompt) is an operator decision not
  taken here.

**Scope limit — measured, stated in every QA record.** `creative_still_qa`
checks people/face presence against what the prompt implies, plus continuity
against an anchor. It does **not** check that the environment matches the
prompt. Real run on the operator's bad image
(`renders/fd51e60dfcda49ef8ac0fa8c9b1c860f_00001_.png`):

  fabrication happened in follow-up turns with no tool call, so it could not
  have fired. `_stills_claim_correction` now also reads the chat's persisted
  review state (`tools.story_stills_review_status`).
- Split into `_STILLS_FALSE_SELECTION_RE` (SELECTED / approved / meets required
  standards — always false while pending) and `_STILLS_QA_PASS_CLAIM_RE`
  (false unless every pending still's recorded QA verdict is pass; added
  "passed all … checks", the turn-5 phrasing). Original patterns unchanged.
- Correction text no longer claims "there is no automated QA": it cites the
  recorded per-still verdicts and the QA scope, or says no QA verdict was
  recorded (stills presented before this change). `_STILLS_FALSE_APPROVAL_RE`

  and cached; batch → `completed[i].qa` → review state + `qa_summary`; QA crash

  `expected_actor_visible_but_no_face_detected`, carried into the review state;

- `python -m unittest test_native_tool_calling test_story_stills_batch_review test_render_media_announce`

## Live verification

Real GPU run, 2026-09-24 01:09–01:20 (GPU gate mode `allow`, GPU idle 34 °C,
port 8188 free before and released after): `tools.render_story_image_batch`
called directly with the new code (not through the GUI server), one
`realpro_flux` job, story `stillqa-live-verify-20260924`, the full scene-1
prompt, seed 424242. 682 s end to end (Flux text-encoder load on CPU dominated;
"Prompt executed in 00:10:18").

- `completed[0].qa` = verdict **pass**, `ok: true`, `reject_reasons: []`,
  `anchor: null`, mode `actor_visible`, `candidate_face_count: 1`,
  prompt_source `manifest image_918f29f3-….json`. Image inspected: the actor is
  in frame, so the pass is correct.
- `qa_summary.counts = {"pass": 1}`; review state
  `work/runtime/story_stills_review/stillqa-live-verify-20260924.json` is
  `pending_review` with `stills[0].qa.verdict == "pass"`; QA cached at
  `outputs/stories/stillqa-live-verify-20260924/still_qa/`.
- Full result: `live_jobs/stillqa_live_verify_20260924.json`.

Not preflight, port 8188, or GPU-busy. It was the agent's own specialist-scope

`_requests_specialist_project_context("looks good proceed") == False`,

# 2026-09-24aa — still-QA continuity anchor for chat stills: chat-scoped fallback, provenance, first live anchored comparison

## Why

Operator chat `149209bf6e4b42ce`: "Scene Start Image 2" showed a visibly different
actor from "Scene Start Image 1" for the same character (Leo), and still QA passed
it. Both QA records (`outputs/stories/Scene-Start-Image-{1,2}/still_qa/`) say
`"anchor": null`, so the room/clothing/face continuity checks never ran.
`work/runtime/story_qa_anchors.json` did not exist.

Checked offline, read-only, with the real checker: Image 2 against Image 1 as
anchor → **fail** `face_identity_sface=0.124<0.35` (plus `room_drift 0.149`,
`clothing_drift 0.195`; the scene legitimately moved from the apartment to a
Backrooms corridor). The checker would have caught the actor swap; it was never
given the anchor.

## What was actually missing (differs from the task brief)

The story-keyed registry the brief asks for **already existed** since
`2026-09-24a`: `approve_story_stills` → `_record_story_qa_anchors` writes
`work/runtime/story_qa_anchors.json`, `_story_still_qa` reads it. It never fired
for two reasons, both confirmed in the live state:

1. **No operator approval ever reached `approve_story_stills`.** Every review
   state in `work/runtime/story_stills_review/` is `pending_review`,
   `approved_at: null` (the chat `149209bf…` state holds only Image 2; Image 1's
   pending state was overwritten when Image 2 was presented). Only
   `approve_story_stills` writes anchors, by design (last *human-approved*, never
   last generated), so the file was never created.
2. **The chat labelled one character's stills with one story slug per image**
   (`Scene Start Image 1`, `Scene Start Image 2`). A registry keyed by
   `_safe_segment(story)` can never link those, even after an approval.

So this entry does not rebuild the registry; it closes the two gaps above and
proves the whole loop live.

## Why

`'fail' != 'not_run'` and `error: no rendered output file was found on disk to
check`, confirmed by revert-and-rerun to be unrelated to the face_detail fix, and
attributed it to a same-day edit of `local_agent/tools.py`'s output-path handling.
This session's brief: find the root cause, make `error` / `fail` / `not_run`
three distinct states, prove it fail-then-pass.

## What was actually wrong (differs from the brief)

- **Not a regression from any same-day `tools.py` edit.** `_resolve_story_still_outputs`
  is byte-identical in every backup since `2026-09-24a` landed it
  (`tools.py.bak_promptprefix_20260924T012949` 01:07, the three
  `bak_facedetailflux_*` copies, `bak_qaanchor_20260924` 21:26, and current: same
  md5 of the function body). The four tests' fixtures are also unchanged since
  `24a`; `24aa`'s test-file diff is additive only.
- **On this host the tests pass.** First thing checked: current code, Windows
  Python 3.12.10, `python -m unittest test_story_stills_batch_review.StoryStillQATests`
  → 13 OK, including all four named tests.
- **Reproduced under a POSIX Python.** WSL Ubuntu-24.04, Python 3.12.3, same
  tree via `/mnt/a/...`: FAILED (failures=7, skipped=2). The seven are the four
  from `24u` minus `test_regression_operator_empty_room_fails_real_qa_and_reaches_review`
  (skipped there: no cv2 in WSL), plus three of `24aa`'s new anchor tests. Every
  failing test locates the still through the manifest; every passing one hands
  `_story_still_qa` a path directly. All seven report `verdict=not_run`.
- **Mechanism.** ComfyUI on Windows reports `subfolder` as `stories\<story>\renders`
  and `work/image_render.py` stores it verbatim — every real manifest under
  `outputs/stories/` has it (e.g. `Scene-Start-Image-1/manifests/image_fb498057-….json`:
  `"subfolder": "stories\\Scene-Start-Image-1\\renders"`). The test fixture writes
  the same shape. `_resolve_story_still_outputs` did `comfy_root / subfolder / filename`;
  pathlib splits only on the *running* interpreter's separator, so under a POSIX
  pathlib the backslashes are literal filename characters, `is_file()` is False,
  `path` is `None`, `_story_still_qa` has nothing to check and returns `not_run`
  with "no rendered output file was found on disk to check" — for a file that
  exists exactly where the manifest says. The `24u` session evidently ran the
  suite under a POSIX Python that also had cv2 (its real-QA test failed rather
  than skipped). The `/history` output parser at `tools.py:1153` already
  normalises `\` → `/` for the same reason; the still resolver did not.
- **The three verdict states were already distinct in the verdict logic:**
  `error` = `creative_still_qa` failed to import or `creative_approve` raised;
  `fail` = the checker ran and rejected; `not_run` = no file or no prompt to
  check. Nothing mapped an `error`/`fail` to `not_run`; the file lookup failed
  before QA could run. The consequence `24u` feared was real for that platform:

## Changes — `local_agent/tools.py` (backup `tools.py.bak_qaposixpath_20260924`)

- New `_split_comfy_subpath(value)`: splits a ComfyUI-reported subfolder or
  filename on both `\` and `/`, dropping empty and `.` segments.
  `_resolve_story_still_outputs` now builds the path with
  `comfy_root.joinpath(*segments)` instead of `comfy_root / subfolder / filename`.
  The manifest's `subfolder` string is still recorded verbatim in each entry;
  `expected_path` is the normalised location.
- `_story_still_qa` `not_run` diagnostics: a manifest with no outputs →
  `"the render manifest lists no output file to check"`; outputs listed but none
  on disk → `"no rendered output file was found on disk to check (looked for:
  <expected_path>; …)"`, so a mis-resolved or missing path is visible to the
  operator instead of reading like a QA verdict. Verdict semantics unchanged.
- Not touched: verdict/caching logic, the `24aa` anchor registry, `24u`'s
  face_detail / model_profile validation, `creative_still_qa.py`, `image_render.py`.

## Tests — `local_agent/test_story_stills_batch_review.py` (backup `.bak_qaposixpath_20260924`)

- `test_missing_output_file_is_not_run_not_pass` additionally asserts the record

# 2026-09-24ac — GVD curriculum: strict bar 0.85 → 0.80

Follows 2026-09-24q (judge rewrite) and 2026-09-24r (held-out check). Both
left one item as an operator decision: the fixed judge scores correct
Backrooms-batch clips at aesthetic 0.80–0.85, so at the 0.85 strict bar 8 of
12 good held-out clips failed for a scoring-range mismatch, not a defect.
The operator decided: lower the strict bar to 0.80. This entry moves only that
threshold. `video_judge.py` (detector, VLM prompt, caps table),
`dspy_orchestrator.py` and the labels are untouched. No VLM run, no ComfyUI,
no renders: the scores in `results_v2b.jsonl` / `results_heldout_v2b.jsonl`
are re-read against the new bar (the bar is applied in Python after scoring,
so re-scoring would give the same triples).

Backups: `local_agent/{media_accuracy_gate.py,test_media_accuracy_gate.py,gvd_judge_eval.py}.bak_curriculum080_20260924T223830`.

## Where the bar lives

Not in `dspy_orchestrator.py`. `dspy_orchestrator.evaluate_live_candidate`
and `generalized_video_director` both call
`media_accuracy_gate.video_director_passes_curriculum()`, which reads
`media_accuracy_gate._CURRICULUM_STEPS` via `curriculum_threshold(iteration)`
(iteration from `GVD_CURRICULUM_ITERATION`). Steps were
`(0, 0.60), (3, 0.70), (6, 0.80), (9, 0.85)`.

## Why exactly 0.80 (re-derived from the data)

Minimum-axis score of every labeled clip, fixed judge, 8 frames:

| set | good | partial | reject ≥ 0.70 |
|---|---|---|---|
| tuning (50) | 0.80 ×3, 0.85 ×2, 0.90 ×2, 0.95 | 0.40, 0.80 ×2, 0.90 ×2, 0.95 ×2 | 0.80 ×2, 0.85 ×2, 0.90 ×4, 0.95 ×2 |
| held-out (29) | 0.00 ×2, 0.25, 0.80 ×5, 0.85 ×2, 0.90 ×2 | 0.00 ×3, 0.80 ×2 | 0.80, 0.90 |

Scores are quantized to 0.05 and no clip sits between 0.80 and 0.85, so any
bar in (0.80, 0.85] behaves exactly like 0.85 and any bar in (0.60, 0.80]
behaves exactly like 0.80. 0.80 is the only choice that admits the good
Backrooms clips; there is no bar that admits them and still excludes the
three rejects that also score exactly 0.80 (below).

  backup): `_CURRICULUM_STEPS = ((0, 0.60), (3, 0.70), (6, 0.80))`. The
  `(9, 0.85)` step is gone; iteration 6+ is 0.80 and stays there. Iterations
  0–8 are unchanged.
- `test_media_accuracy_gate.py`: `test_curriculum_tightens_from_060_to_080`
  (was `…_085`), the 0.66-minimum case still fails at iteration 9 with
  threshold 0.80, plus a new `test_curriculum_strict_bar_admits_080_minimum`
  (1.0/1.0/0.80 passes at iteration 99).
- `gvd_judge_eval.py`: `THRESHOLDS = (0.60, 0.80, 0.85)` so `report` shows
  the new strict bar and keeps 0.85 for comparison. Report and run code
  otherwise unchanged.
- Not changed, on purpose: the legacy `VIDEO_DIRECTOR_VLM_SYSTEM_PROMPT` in
  `media_accuracy_gate.py` still says "tightening to 0.85". It is the
  pre-fix judge prompt, kept verbatim so `gvd_judge_eval.py --variant
  baseline` stays a faithful baseline; the production judge (`video_judge.py`)
  has its own prompt, which names no threshold.

## Before / after at the strict bar (`gvd_judge_eval.py report`)

Reports: `runtime/dspy_opt/judge_eval/report_{v2b,heldout_v2b}_curriculum080.json`.
FP = reject clips that pass, FF = good clips that fail; hc = high-confidence labels.

| set | bar | FP | FF | hc FP | hc FF | partial pass |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| tuning (50) | 0.85 (old) | 8/35 | 3/8 | 4/27 | 2/4 | 4/7 |
| tuning | **0.80 (new)** | 10/35 | **0/8** | 4/27 | **0/4** | 6/7 |
| held-out (29) | 0.85 (old) | 1/12 | 8/12 | 1/7 | 2/5 | 0/5 |
| held-out | **0.80 (new)** | 2/12 | **3/12** | 1/7 | 2/5 | 2/5 |

The 0.60 rows and AUC (0.821 tuning, 0.809 held-out) are unchanged: the
bottom tier was not touched.

Good clips that failed at 0.85 and now pass at 0.80: **8 of 11**.
- tuning, all three: c005, c017, c029 (all 1.0 / 1.0 / 0.80).
- held-out, 5 of 8: c028, c033, c038, br_c002, br_c003 (all 1.0 / 1.0 / 0.80).
- held-out, still failing 3: c004 (0.00, flicker read as a location change),
  c018 (0.25, CPU cut-detector false positive), c035 (0.00, disputed label,
  near-black cap). These are the 24r false fails at 0.60 too; the bar is not
  what fails them.

Reject clips that newly pass at 0.80 (side effect): **3**, all medium
confidence, all scoring exactly 0.80 on the aesthetic axis, and all already
counted as false passes at the 0.60 tier in 24q/24r (so the judge's ranking
of them is unchanged; only the strict tier stops excluding them):
- tuning: GVD-B01 `93fb` (geometry_instability, wall wobble), c036
  (wrong_viewpoint, operator in frame).
- held-out: c021 (color_or_location_drift).
No high-confidence reject newly passes on either set.

Net at the strict tier, both sets combined: false fails 11/20 → 3/20; false
passes 9/47 → 12/47.

## Consequence worth knowing

With the current judge, every clip scores either ≤ 0.40 or ≥ 0.80 on its
minimum axis (the checks fire together, as 24q noted). So today the 0.80
strict tier and the 0.60 base tier accept exactly the same clips on both
labeled sets; the curriculum only tightens again if future judge changes
spread the scores. That is expected and acceptable per the operator's
decision, but it means the curriculum is currently not doing extra work above
iteration 2.

chunks.heading: # 2026-09-24ad — GVD live metric: judged clips floored above every failure penalty
chunks.text:
# 2026-09-24ad — GVD live metric: judged clips floored above every failure penalty

Follows 2026-09-24ac (strict bar 0.80). This closes the second open operator
decision from 2026-09-24q/r: a rendered clip that the judge scored all-zero
got MIPRO scalar 0.0, **below** a render timeout (0.05), a mechanical /
prompt-format failure (0.02) and a pipeline failure (0.01). Near-zero verdicts
collided too: 0.0/0.0/0.15 gives 0.7·0 + 0.3·0.05 = 0.045, under the timeout.
So the optimizer could prefer a program that never renders over one that
renders a bad clip, and the fixed judge returns all-zero far more often than
the old one did (24q). No VLM run, no ComfyUI, no renders: read-only analysis
of existing results plus unit tests.

Backups: `local_agent/{dspy_orchestrator.py,test_dspy_orchestrator.py}.bak_judgedfloor_20260924T223830`.

## Change (`local_agent/dspy_orchestrator.py`, LF kept)

- New `JUDGED_SCORE_FLOOR = 0.10` and `_judged_scalar(minimum, mean)` =
  `max(0.10, 0.7·min + 0.3·mean)`, next to `_fail_penalty`. 0.10 is twice the
  largest failure penalty.
- `evaluate_live_candidate` uses it for the judged-clip `mipro`. The feedback
  row gains `mipro_raw` (the unfloored value) so history keeps the judge's
  full ranking; `mipro_raw` and `mipro` differ only below 0.10.
- A clamp, not a rescale: every judged clip scoring ≥ 0.10 keeps exactly the
  scalar it had, so the 24q statement "the 0.7·min + 0.3·mean MIPRO scalar is
  unchanged" still holds for everything that was ranking correctly. The
  ordering "any judged clip > any failure" now holds by construction.
- Failure penalties (0.05 / 0.02 / 0.01), the curriculum, `passes_curriculum`
  and the judge itself are untouched. A floored all-zero clip still has
  `passes_curriculum = False`.
- Not changed: the mock path in `generalized_video_director.py` uses
  `mipro = minimum` with failure = 0.0; it has no timeout penalty so it has no
  inversion, and it never produces all-zero scores. `gvd_judge_eval.py`'s AUC
  still uses the raw scalar, on purpose: it measures the judge's ranking, and
  the floor is an optimizer concern. With the floor the only effect on AUC
  would be ties among the bottom rejects.

## Effect on the labeled sets (raw scalar, `results_v2b` / `results_heldout_v2b`)

| set | judged clips | raw < 0.10 (now 0.10) | of which ≤ 0.05 (tied with / under a timeout) | all-zero | good clips moved |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| tuning (50) | 50 | 18 (all reject) | 17 | 9 | 0 (lowest good 0.84) |
| held-out (29) | 29 | 6 (5 reject, 1 partial) | 6 | 2 | 0 (lowest good exactly 0.10: c004, c035) |

So on these sets 23 of 79 real renders used to rank at or below a timeout;
none does now, and no good clip's scalar changes.

none does now, and no good clip's scalar changes.

## What the live history shows (`runtime/dspy_opt/gvd_live_metric_history.jsonl`, 261 rows, read only)

Of 201 non-mock judged rows, **138 have minimum 0.0 and `mipro` 0.0**, while
the 60 failure rows include 15 timeouts at 0.05, 6 mechanical at 0.02 and 17
pipeline at 0.01. So under the old judge and scalar, roughly two thirds of
every real render the optimizer ever saw ranked below a timeout. Caveat:
those rows were written by the pre-fix judge and an older scalar (one row has
mean 0.11 with `mipro` 0.0, i.e. `mipro = minimum` at the time), so the
figure shows how common the collision was, not what the current formula
would have produced.

## Why a floor rather than lowering the penalties

Lowering the penalties (e.g. timeout 0.005) would keep the all-zero clip at
0.0, still the worst possible outcome, tied with nothing but itself. The
operator's framing in 24q is that a rendered and judged clip carries
information a timeout does not, so the fix has to lift judged clips, not push
failures down. The floor also leaves the three failure modes distinguishable
from each other, which is what `_fail_penalty` exists for.

## Tests

- `test_dspy_orchestrator.py` +2: an all-zero judged clip (legacy two-arg
  judge hook) returns exactly `JUDGED_SCORE_FLOOR`, exceeds every
  `_fail_penalty` string, records `mipro_raw = 0.0` and still fails the
  curriculum; `_judged_scalar` lifts 0.0/0.0 and 0.0/0.15 (raw 0.045) to
  0.10 and leaves 0.30/0.6833, 0.74/0.7867 and 1.0/1.0 unchanged. Existing
  scalar assertions in `test_dspy_orchestrator.py` and `test_video_judge.py`
  (all ≥ 0.10) pass unchanged. CRLF kept in the test file.
- `python -m unittest test_dspy_orchestrator test_video_judge test_generalized_video_director test_media_accuracy_gate`: 117 OK.
- Full non-live suite, `python -m unittest $(ls test_*.py | grep -v _live | sed 's/\.py$//')`:
  **1529 OK (2 skipped)**, 247 s, exit 0 (2026-09-24 22:50–22:55 local)
  (`runtime/dspy_opt/judge_eval/full_suite_20260924_judgedfloor.log`).
  24ac reported 1527; +2 tests here.

## Open

- History rows ≤ 260 were written by the old judge and are not comparable
  anyway (24q); rows from now on carry both `mipro` and `mipro_raw`.
- The next real MIPRO run is the first that exercises the floor in anger.

chunks.heading: # 2026-09-24ae — llama.cpp client forwards repeat_penalty; the checklist judge keeps it off (measured)
chunks.text:
# 2026-09-24ae — llama.cpp client forwards repeat_penalty; the checklist judge keeps it off (measured)

Follows 2026-09-24r, which found that `media_tools._run_vision_gpu` sets
`repeat_penalty: 1.08` but `llama_cpp_client.chat` only ever sent
`temperature` and `max_tokens`, so every VLM call in the agent has run with
the penalty effectively off (1.0) since the llama.cpp runtime was adopted.
24r left it alone because it would alter every VLM call; the operator asked
for it to be fixed. The plumbing is fixed. The effect on the GVD judge was
then **measured**, and it is bad enough that the judge now pins the penalty
off explicitly; free-text callers get the intended 1.08.

VLM only, under the usual guards (`gvd_judge_eval.preflight`: port 8188
closed, owners idle, GPU ≤ 70 °C at start; owner held; 82 °C check before
every clip; release and cool-down after each run). Four llama-server
launches, 0 crashes, 0 connection resets, GPU 37 °C afterwards. No ComfyUI,
no renders.

Backups: `local_agent/{llama_cpp_client.py,media_tools.py,dspy_orchestrator.py,dspy_optimizer.py,test_video_judge.py}.bak_repeatpenalty_20260924T223830`.

## 1. The fix (`llama_cpp_client.py`, LF)

`_SAMPLER_FIELDS` = repeat_penalty, repeat_last_n, presence_penalty,
frequency_penalty, top_k, top_p, min_p, seed, stop. Each is copied into the
`/v1/chat/completions` body, cast, **only when the caller set it**; nothing
is invented, and callers that set none get the exact old body. llama-server
(build 10516, `--repeat-penalty` in `--help`) copies unknown OpenAI-body
fields through to its native sampler params.

Confirmed live (`runtime/dspy_opt/judge_eval_20260924/probe_repeat_penalty.py`,
result `probe_repeat_penalty_result.json`, text-only, same launch args as
production): `/completion` echoes `generation_settings.repeat_penalty = 1.08`;
through `llama_cpp_client.chat` at temperature 0, "write yes 40 times" gives
120 "yes" tokens at 1.0, 60 at 1.08 and 58 (with case drift) at 1.5. The
field is honoured on the endpoint the agent uses.

New `test_llama_cpp_client.py` (5): forwarding, Ollama-only keys never
reach the body, unset fields not invented, casts, image data URLs.

New `test_llama_cpp_client.py` (5): forwarding, Ollama-only keys never
reach the body, unset fields not invented, casts, image data URLs.

## 2. Measured on the judge: 1.08 forwarded (`results_v2c.jsonl`, `results_heldout_v2c.jsonl`)

Same 50 + 29 labeled clips, same judge code as 24ac, only difference: the
penalty now reaches the server. 45/50 and 29/29 clips changed at least one
score.

| set | bar | FP (1.0 → 1.08) | FF (1.0 → 1.08) | hc FP | hc FF | AUC | parse failures |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| tuning (50) | 0.60 | 10/35 → **4/35** | 0/8 → **2/8** | 4/27 → 1/27 | 0/4 → 1/4 | 0.821 → 0.875 | 0 → **2** |
| tuning | 0.80 | 10/35 → 4/35 | 0/8 → 2/8 | 4/27 → 1/27 | 0/4 → 1/4 | | |
| held-out (29) | 0.60 | 2/12 → **0/12** | 3/12 → **6/12** | 1/7 → 0/7 | 2/5 → 3/5 | 0.809 → 0.812 | 0 → **1** |
| held-out | 0.80 | 2/12 → 0/12 | 3/12 → **7/12** | 1/7 → 0/7 | 2/5 → 3/5 | | |

Reports: `report_v2c.json`, `report_heldout_v2c.json`. Per-clip: 10 verdict
flips on tuning (8 rejects/partials caught, 2 goods lost), 6–8 on held-out
(2 rejects caught, 3–4 goods lost, 1 partial regained). ~8 s per clip both
ways.

Why it is not simply "stricter": the mechanism is token frequency, not
evidence.
- The output is a fixed checklist of seven yes/no answers. After several
  "yes" tokens the penalty makes "yes" more expensive and "no" cheaper. The
  goods lost are Backrooms hallway walks now answered
  `same_place_in_all_frames: no` with rationales such as "a different place
  (empty hallway) compared to the BRIEF's backroom scene" (c016) or "change
  in lighting and door position, indicating movement through the hallway"
  (c017, movement is the brief). c038 was answered "abrupt cut" with the CPU
  detector reporting none; c025 "requested subject not visible" for a
  hallway that is visible in every frame.
- Several rejects are "caught" for the wrong reason: `constraint_broken` is
  now filled with the CONSTRAINTS line quoted verbatim (D02 `614e`, S05, D01
  `086a`/`3032`), which rule (a) from 24q accepts because it is not a dump
  of check answers. Right verdict, ungrounded evidence.
- **3 of 79 outputs close the JSON object right after the checks**, before
  the three scores, and fail parsing (`missing or invalid float score`).
  0 of 79 did at 1.0. In production that is a `_fail_result` (0.01), not a
  judged clip. This is the opposite of the runaway that 24r hoped the
  penalty would curb; no runaway occurred at 8 frames in either run.

The false-pass reduction is real but comes from a bias that also fails good
clips and breaks the schema. The judge stays at the behaviour validated in
24q/24r/24ac.

## 3. Production state after this entry

- `media_tools._run_vision_gpu(..., repeat_penalty=1.08)`: new parameter,
  default unchanged, **now live** for free-text callers: `_vision_direct`,
  the media watcher's queued vision jobs, `extract_video_actions` batches,
  the caption/lifecycle diagnostics. These run at 1.08 for the first time;
  their output is prose or beat lists, where a mild anti-loop penalty is what
  the value was written for. Unmeasured beyond the probe.
- `dspy_orchestrator.run_qwen_director_scores`: `repeat_penalty=1.0`,
  with the measurement in a comment. `test_video_judge.py` +1 asserts it.
- `dspy_optimizer.py` (CRLF/LF mix preserved: +4 CRLF lines, LF count
  unchanged): the still semantic verdict, its FORMAT RETRY, and the video
  semantic verdict pass `repeat_penalty=1.0`. They return a structured JSON
  verdict (they even have a JSON-format retry path), were validated with the
  penalty effectively off, and gate real renders; not changed unmeasured.
- `gvd_qa/caption_v4.py` sets no penalty and is unchanged (stays 1.0).
- Switching the judge to 1.08 later is one keyword argument; `results_v2c`
  is what that produces.

## 4. Verification that the judge is unchanged at explicit 1.0

`results_v2d_check.jsonl` / `results_heldout_v2d_check.jsonl`: the 13
clips that flipped or failed to parse in v2c, re-judged with the final code
(penalty sent as 1.0). **All 13 identical to v2b** in scores, checks and parse status (`run_v2d_check_chain.log`), including the three that failed to parse at 1.08. Sending `repeat_penalty: 1.0` is byte-for-byte the disabled sampler, and the judge is deterministic at temperature 0, as 24q found.

chunks.heading: # 2026-09-24b — local_agent GUI: review stills/video inline, announce renders that land after the reply
chunks.text:
# 2026-09-24b — local_agent GUI: review stills/video inline, announce renders that land after the reply

## Why

Operator asked for (1) generated stills/video to appear in the chat for human
review instead of being hunted down in Explorer, and (2) the GUI to announce
finished generations even after the agent's turn has ended.

The GUI already had a complete inline-media card system (`mountMediaArtifact`,
`/api/generated_media`, `media_artifacts` on stored replies). Measured on the
84 stored chats: 38 assistant turns called story-image tools
(`render_story_image` 25, `story_image_job_status` 7, `render_story_image_batch` 6)
and **zero** media artifacts had ever been stored.

## Root causes (three, not one)

1. `server.collect_story_media_artifacts()` only understood the single-job
   result shape. `render_story_image_batch` returns an aggregate
   (`{"batch": true, "completed": [...], "failures": [...], "pending": [...]}`)
   with no top-level state/status → it returned `[]` for every batch.
2. `agent.py` clips every emitted `tool_result` to `result[:4000]` before
   `server.push` sees it. One real realpro_flux manifest is ~4.4 KB on disk, so
   batch results *and* single-job `story_image_job_status` results
   (manifest + up to 3 KB log tail) arrived as truncated JSON → `json.loads`
   failed → `[]` regardless of shape.
3. Found in the live run: live cards were mounted inside the tool-result
   lifecycle card, a collapsed `<details>`, so the stills were hidden until the
   operator expanded it (history reload mounted them visibly in the bubble).

Also fixed, because (2) would otherwise have exposed it:
`tools.story_image_job_status` reported the story's *newest manifest on disk*
even when it predated the job being polled. Re-rendering an existing story
would have shown the previous still inline as though it were the new result.

## Changes

- `local_agent/agent.py`: `MEDIA_SOURCE_EVENT = "tool_media_source"`,
  `MEDIA_SOURCE_TOOLS`, `_emit_tool_result()`. Visible `tool_result` is
  unchanged (still clipped at 4000); for media tools (non-ERROR results) one
  extra internal event carries the full result. Used in `_execute_plan` and the
  native tool loop. The phone bridge ignores unknown event kinds.
- `local_agent/server.py`:
  - batch-aware `collect_story_media_artifacts()` → per-job `_story_job_artifacts()`;
    failures/not-started entries yield nothing (follow-up task filed).
  - `media_artifact_key()` / `extend_unique_artifacts()`: one card per file per turn.
  - `push()` consumes `tool_media_source` (never forwarded to the browser,
    not recorded by `learning`, not in the activity trace).
  - Render-watch registry: `runtime/render_watch.json`, `register_render_watch`
    (render_story_image pid/story/log; comfy_generate prompt_id),
    `poll_render_watches` (5 s check TTL, 2 h expiry, 24 h retention),
    `_attach_late_artifacts` (saves late cards onto the chat's latest
    assistant reply, skipping files the turn already showed; failures become an
    error card). Watches for a chat are not resolved while that chat has an
    active turn (`_active_turns`). New `GET /api/render_watch`.
  - `media_queue` deliberately not reused: it is a work queue the media
    watcher claims; a render parked there would sit pending forever and
    "Clear queue" would cancel it without stopping anything.
- `local_agent/tools.py`: `_story_job_started_at()` parses the launch time from
  render_story_image's `<story>_<YYYYmmdd_HHMMSS>.log`; `story_image_job_status`
  then only considers manifests written after launch (earliest wins). Unparsable
  log names keep the old behaviour. (2026-09-24a's still QA now runs on this
  job-scoped manifest.)

  `mediaKey` de-dup; "Finished after the reply" label and error note on cards;
  `pollRenderWatch()` every 10 s + 1.5 s after each turn; toast (click opens the
  chat and scrolls to the card) and `(n) ● Local Agent` title unread count when
  the window is unfocused/hidden; a turn that delivered media while the operator
  was away also toasts. No Notification API / sound (operator: not wanted).

chunks.text:
# 2026-09-24e — local_agent: refuse still jobs whose prompt truncates an operator-pasted prompt

## Symptom

Chat `local_agent/chats/1d4a42d3b5834081.json` (Backrooms Sitcom Audition pack
pasted as message 0). Manifest
`outputs/stories/Backrooms-Sitcom-Audition-Prompt-Pack/manifests/image_f02381ec-….json`
(created 04:20:34Z) rendered with prompt = only the first sentence of
"Scene Start Image 1" (120 chars, "…for a sitcom casting tape"). The result,
`_comfy_output/…/renders/fd51e60dfcda49ef8ac0fa8c9b1c860f_00001_.png`, is an
empty living room with no actor. The earlier manifest `image_62e576a9-….json`
(03:53:51Z) had the full prompt.

chunks.heading: ## Symptom
chunks.text:
-Pack/manifests/image_f02381ec-….json`
(created 04:20:34Z) rendered with prompt = only the first sentence of
"Scene Start Image 1" (120 chars, "…for a sitcom casting tape"). The result,
`_comfy_output/…/renders/fd51e60dfcda49ef8ac0fa8c9b1c860f_00001_.png`, is an
empty living room with no actor. The earlier manifest `image_62e576a9-….json`
(03:53:51Z) had the full prompt.

## Where the truncation happened — the model, primed by our own tool output

Evidence, all read-only:

- `knowledge/traces.db`, trace `54751f9e…`, tool span `render_story_image_batch`
  at 04:08:10Z: `arg_sha256=5448b458…`, `arg_json_bytes=360`. The span is
  recorded in `agent._trace_tool_call`, whose args are the Ollama native
  `tool_calls` arguments plus only the server-injected `__conversation_id`.
- **The hash reproduces exactly** from
  `{"__conversation_id":"1d4a42d3b5834081","flux":true,"jobs":[{"model_profile":"realpro_flux","prompt":"<first sentence>","story":"Backrooms Sitcom Audition Prompt Pack"}],"model_profile":"realpro_flux","stop_on_failure":true,"timeout_s":900}`
  (`json.dumps(sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False)`, as `tracing.summarize_tool_args`).
  The 03:41:46Z call's hash `3eef75f4…` (751 bytes) reproduces from the same
  dict with the **full** prompt. So the two calls are identical except the prompt.
- The turn went through the native tool-call path (review → decide → tool_call),
  not `action_resolver` (which short-circuits the turn), not the managed prompt-pack
  plans, and not the Backrooms adapters. `ollama_client.chat_stream` and
  `tools.parse_call_tool_args` do not alter string values. `tools._normalize_batch_job`
  only `.strip()`s, and it runs after the span was hashed anyway.
- Why the model sent that string: `tools.render_story_image_batch` labels
  each job `"prompt_preview": job["prompt"][:120]`. For this prompt, 120 chars
  ends **exactly** at the first period, so the preview reads as a whole

chunks.text:
# 2026-09-24f — local_agent GUI: inline cards for failed and not-started batch stills

## Why

After 2026-09-24b, `render_story_image_batch` got one ready card per completed
still. `failures[]` and `pending[]` produced nothing, so in a half-failed batch
the operator saw the frames that rendered and no sign of the ones that didn't.

## What changed

`local_agent/server.py`
- `collect_story_media_artifacts()` now adds `_batch_status_cards()` after
  the ready cards of a batch result:
  - **one error card per `failures[i]`** (`status: "error"`, no filename),
    in the same locator shape as the `poll_render_watches()` error cards.
    `label` = `batch item <index>: <prompt_preview>`. `note` is the
    `blocked_by` summary when present (e.g. `foreign_backend: port 8188 is
    held by pid …`). Otherwise it is the error (`finished_without_manifest` /
    `timed_out` / the launch error), plus `(pid N)` and the last `log_tail`
    line. Capped at 240 chars. Also carries `batch_index` and `phase`.
  - **one summary card for all of `pending[]`** (`status: "not_started"`),
    labelled `N batch items (i, j, …)` and noted `not started after failure —
    story <s>`. Decision: one card, not one per entry. With
    `stop_on_failure` (the default), every job after the first failure lands
    in `pending[]`. Twenty identical "not started" cards would bury the one
    real failure. The label still lists every missing index.
- These file-less cards carry a `card_key`. `media_artifact_key()` uses it,
  and `extend_unique_artifacts()` de-duplicates on it just as it does for
  files. Pending/error locators without a `card_key` (render-watch cards)
  still always pass. Real duplication path found: `agent._emit_tool_result`
  sends the clipped `tool_result` **and** the full internal media event, and a
  batch result under 4000 chars (e.g. an all-launch-failure batch) parses on
  both. Without the key every error card appeared twice. The key includes the
  pid, so a retry that fails again with a new pid is a new card. It is
  per-turn only: the turn's `_media_artifacts` list starts empty.

`local_agent/static/index.html` — `mountMediaArtifact()`
- The error branch also renders `status === "not_started"` with the headline
  "not started" instead of "generate failed".
- Error/not-started cards show `label` inline unless `art.late` (late cards
  already show it in their tag). The GUI's own `mediaKey` de-dup is unchanged
  (files only), so a retried batch that fails again in a *later* turn still
  shows its card.

chunks.heading: # 2026-09-24g — render watch extended to chat video batches (`start_current_chat_render`)
chunks.text:
# 2026-09-24g — render watch extended to chat video batches (`start_current_chat_render`)

## Why

`2026-09-24b` added `/api/render_watch` so a still (`render_story_image`) or a
`comfy_generate` job that lands after the agent's reply ends is announced and
saved onto the reply. Video batches started from a chat ("start render") were
not covered, and they are the renders most likely to finish long after the
turn ends.

## How a chat render job is identified and observed (read-only)

Established from `local_agent/chat_render_jobs.py`, `tools.start_batch_render`
and `work/batch_render_folder.py`. No runner code changed.

- **Identity:** `start_current_chat_render` returns
  `{"prepared": {...}, "launch": {"started", "pid", "job_folder", "planned_renders", "limit", "log"}}`.
  `job_folder` is `local_agent/render_jobs/<cid>/render_<stamp>[_NN]/`; `pid`
  is the runner process. The watch id is `chat_render:<pid>:<cid>/<job>`.
- **Progress / outputs:** the runner writes `<job>/batch_manifest.json`
  (`renders[<key>].status` = `done` / `failed` / `invalid` / `error`, with
  `output_path` for `done`) and moves each finished take to
  `<job>/renders/<key>[_attemptN].mp4`.
- **Completion:** the runner logs `Batch complete: N/M renders done` as its
  last line, *after* releasing `batch_render_queue_owner.json`. A crash
  (for example `RuntimeError: ComfyUI exited during startup rc=1`, seen in the
  real job `5b3352e81fdb4f08/render_20260824_184105`) leaves only a traceback
  in `<job>/batch_runtime/logs/agent_batch_*.log`.
- The watch treats the job as finished when the log shows the marker or the
  PID is no longer live (`tools._pid_is_live`, the same tasklist check the
  launch preflight uses). It reads the manifest and log only. It does not touch
  the queue lock, the ports, ComfyUI or the runner.

## Changes

`local_agent/server.py`
- New media root id **`chat_render`** → `CHAT_RENDER_JOBS_ROOT`
  (`local_agent/render_jobs`). It serves **video only**, and only files at
  exactly `<cid>/<job>/renders/<file>`. The job folder also holds copies of the
  chat's uploads (`img0/`, `img1/`, `video_refs/`) and the Comfy scratch
  (`batch_runtime/`). None of those are servable. `forbidden_media_roots()` is
  unchanged: `outputs/equal_shares`, chats, uploads and Shared input are still
  refused for every root.
- `media_kinds_for_root()` replaces the duplicated
  `"media" if shared_output else "image"` choice in `generated_media_payload`
  and `reveal_generated_media`.
- `chat_render_job_dir()` and `collect_chat_render_media_artifacts(job, manifest)`
  turn `done` manifest entries into ready video locators through
  `resolve_generated_media` + `media_artifact_for`.
- `register_render_watch` accepts `start_current_chat_render` (nested `launch`)
  and a bare `start_batch_render`, but only when `job_folder` is a chat job
  folder. An operator-supplied folder elsewhere is not watched, because its
  files could not be served.
- New watch kind `chat_render`:
  - Still running → keep waiting.
  - At least one video, all planned renders done → `complete`.
  - Some videos plus failed/invalid entries, or fewer than `min(planned, limit)`
    → `complete` with the videos plus one summary error card
    (`card_key chat_render_partial|<id>`), e.g.
    `1 of 3 renders done; 0002 failed: …`.
  - No videos → `failed`, with the manifest error or the log's last line.
- Expiry for this kind is 72 h, because each attempt may run 120 min. It only
  ends a watch whose PID Windows reused. Failure cards for this kind are
  `kind: video`.

`local_agent/agent.py`
- `MEDIA_SOURCE_TOOLS` += `start_current_chat_render`, `start_batch_render`.
  Their result carries `prepared.provenance`, which can push `launch` past the
  4000-char clip.
- The deterministic "start render" path (`_explicit_folderless_render_request`)
  now calls `_emit_tool_result(...)` instead of `emit("tool_result", result[:4000])`,
  so it registers the watch the same way a native tool call does.

`static/index.html` is unchanged. `mountMediaArtifact` already renders
`<video controls>` and passes `art.root` through to `/api/generated_media`.

`server.py` / `test_render_media_announce.py` concurrently. The edits were
kept to separate regions, and the new tests are a new class appended at the
end.)

# 2026-09-24i — director mock metric and live-metric feedback read `start_prompt`/`video_prompt`

## Why

On 2026-09-16 the Generalized Video Director signature
(`generalized_video_director.director_signature_class`) moved from Wan's
`positive_prompt` to FLUX.1 `start_prompt` + MiniMax I2V `video_prompt`.
Earlier today the mock director LM (`build_mock_lm`) was updated to emit the
new fields. Two readers still only looked at `positive_prompt`:

1. `generalized_video_director.mock_vlm_scores()` scored alignment, motion and
   the Backrooms physics phrase against `positive_prompt`. For a
   current-signature prediction that field is empty, so every candidate got
   alignment 0.05 and temporal 0.42, and mock MIPRO compiles could not tell
   candidates apart.
2. `dspy_orchestrator._fail_result()` wrote
   `"positive_prompt": _field(pred, "positive_prompt")` into the failure
   feedback, so live-metric failure rows carried an empty prompt. The
   success-path feedback in `evaluate_live_candidate` recorded no prompt at all.

`mechanical_director_gate` was checked. It already resolves through
`_director_start_prompt`/`_director_motion_prompt` and reports
`start_prompt is empty` / `video_prompt is empty`, so it needed no change.
Tests were added to lock that in.

## What changed

- `local_agent/generalized_video_director.py` (CRLF preserved):
  - New `_mock_scoring_texts(pred) -> (scene_text, motion_text)`. When either
    `start_prompt` or `video_prompt` is set, the scene text is
    `start_prompt + video_prompt` and the motion text is `video_prompt` alone.
    Otherwise both fall back to legacy `positive_prompt`.
  - `mock_vlm_scores`: intent-token alignment, the `stylized_2d` style lock and
    the Backrooms `yellow`/`backrooms` look bonus read the scene text. Motion
    cues, the length bonus and the Backrooms `handheld walking momentum`
    phrase read the motion text. The local `positive` was renamed to
    `scene_text`. Legacy-only predictions score exactly as before.
- `local_agent/dspy_orchestrator.py`:
  - `_fail_result` feedback: `positive_prompt` key replaced with
    `start_prompt` and `video_prompt`, each resolved through
    `_director_start_prompt(example, pred)` / `_director_motion_prompt(pred)`
    and capped at 500 chars. Those resolvers already fall back to
    `positive_prompt`, so legacy rows still carry their prompt.
  - `evaluate_live_candidate` success feedback now also records the resolved
    `start_prompt` and `video_prompt` (500-char cap).
  - No other code reads a `positive_prompt` key out of the feedback JSON.
    Checked with a scoped grep of `local_agent/*.py`, excluding vendor dirs.

# 2026-09-24k — test triage; director instructions restored; MiniMax steps decoupled from FLUX

Covers two rounds of work in one session. The first round (test triage) was
done without a CHANGELOG entry; this entry records it too.

`dspy_orchestrator.py.bak_mmsteps_20260924T013437`,
`test_dspy_orchestrator.py.bak_mmsteps_20260924T013437` (round 2).

## Round 1 — 16 failing non-live tests (13 failures + 3 errors)

Full non-live suite after: **1417 tests OK (2 skipped)**.

Real regressions, fixed in code:

- `START_LOCAL_AGENT_GUI.ps1`: `$ExpectedAgentRevision` was `…-r98`, server
  `APP_REVISION` is `2026-09-22i-gvd-video-pipeline-readiness`. `Test-AgentReady`
  therefore never matched: every launch treated a current server as stale and
  killed it. Updated (CRLF kept).
- `remote_security.py`: `plan_shot_reasoning` (loads a model, writes
  `shot_decisions.jsonl`) was unclassified; added to `GATED_REMOTE_TOOLS`.
- `agent.py`: bare "image/picture/photo" opened the specialist render scope,
  so "Describe this attached image." lost the scope boundary. Now an
  inspection-only turn does not open it; generation turns still do.
- `generalized_video_director.py`: **`Signature.instructions =
  DIRECTOR_SIGNATURE_INSTRUCTIONS` restored.** `_patch_safety3.py`
  (2026-09-16) replaced the signature class with a lookahead for
  `\.instructions=` (no spaces); the file had `.instructions = …`, so the
  match ran to `return` and deleted the line. The student saw only the
  one-line docstring from then on. Mock LM now emits start/video prompts.
- `dspy_orchestrator.py` `_fail_penalty`: matched `"positive_prompt is empty"`;
  the pivot renamed the error, dropping empty-prompt failures 0.02 → 0.01.
  Now matches `"prompt is empty"`.
- `test_production_integrity.py`: `test_kill_pid_posix_sends_sigkill` did not
  force the POSIX branch, so on Windows it ran a real
  `taskkill /PID 4321 /T /F`. It could never have killed anything: Windows PIDs
  are multiples of 4 (all 496 live PIDs checked), 4321 is not. Test now forces
  POSIX and asserts `subprocess.run` is never called.

Stale tests updated: launcher/revision pin, tracing default-DB check (now
asserts the unittest guard, not file absence), denoise expectations (pinned
1.0), pivot field names, `_fail_penalty` scalars, 0.7·min+0.3·mean MIPRO
scalar, retired `build_wan_graph` → `build_minimax_graph` test.

`server.py` relaunched as PID 43244, logs

check passes.

chunks.heading: # 2026-09-24n — tracing: WAL first-open race no longer disables tracing
chunks.text:
# 2026-09-24n — tracing: WAL first-open race no longer disables tracing

Found while verifying `2026-09-24l`. `test_tracing.TracingTests.test_concurrency_two_threads`
failed intermittently (`AssertionError: 6 != 1`): in two consecutive full
non-live suite runs, and 1 in 6 runs of `python -m unittest test_tracing` alone.

Backups: `local_agent/tracing.py.bak_wal_race_20260924T105158`,
`local_agent/test_tracing.py.bak_wal_race_20260924T105158`.

No ComfyUI, no GPU. Unit tests only.

## Cause (measured, not inferred)

A harness wrapped `tracing._mark_broken` to record its exception and ran the
two-thread turn→hop→reason scenario against a fresh DB each time:
**29 of 200 runs failed**. Every failure was
`sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked`, always raised at
`PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` in `tracing._connection()`.

On a brand-new DB that pragma converts rollback-journal mode to WAL. The
conversion needs an exclusive lock, and SQLite reports "locked" immediately
to the losing connection instead of waiting out the 10 s busy timeout.
`span()` caught it and `_mark_broken()` set `_BROKEN` (OperationalError is a
DatabaseError). After that, `enabled()` returned False for the rest of the
process and every later span was a dummy.

Production impact: the first time two threads opened a new `knowledge/traces.db`
at once, tracing could silently switch itself off until the process restarted.

## Change — `local_agent/tracing.py` (LF)

New `_enable_wal(conn)`, called from `_connection()` in place of the bare pragma:
- The pragma runs under a module-level `_WAL_LOCK` (`threading.Lock`), which
  serializes the conversion within the process. On an existing WAL DB it is a
  no-op read, so the lock is held only briefly.
- On `OperationalError` containing "locked"/"busy" it retries up to
  `_WAL_RETRIES = 50` times, `_WAL_RETRY_SLEEP = 0.02` s apart (~1 s). This
  covers a second process creating the DB at the same moment. Other errors, or
  the last failed attempt, raise as before, so a genuinely broken DB still
  marks tracing broken.
- "Tracing never raises into the caller" is unchanged.

## Verification

- Same harness after the fix: **0 of 1000** runs failed (before: 29/200).
- New `test_tracing.TracingTests.test_concurrent_first_open_never_marks_broken`:
  25 rounds, each on a fresh DB with 4 threads. It asserts `_BROKEN` stays
  False, 4 spans per DB, and journal mode `wal`. Against the pre-change
  `tracing.py` (temp copy) it fails in round 0 with `database is locked`.
- `python -m unittest test_tracing`: 16 OK, **30/30** consecutive runs clean.
- Full non-live suite from `local_agent/`:
  `python -m unittest $(ls test_*.py | grep -v _live | sed 's/\.py$//')` →
  **1466 tests OK (2 skipped)**. That is 1460 from `2026-09-24l` + this test
  + 5 tests another agent added in parallel (`bak_labelecho_20260924T105305`).

# 2026-09-24p — partial chat video batch: card and toast wording

Follow-up to `2026-09-24g` (known limit 1). This change touches only
`local_agent/static/index.html`. Backup:
`static/index.html.bak_partialcard_20260924_153900`. CRLF line endings are
preserved.

## Why

When a chat video batch finished with some renders done and some failed, the
server's one summary card (`card_key` `chat_render_partial|<watch id>`) was
drawn by the generic error branch:
"RENDER ENDED AFTER THE REPLY · … / generate failed — 1 of 3 renders done; …".
That wording implied the whole job failed, even though the videos directly
above it were real and playable. The toast said "1 video ready for review"
and did not mention the failures.

## Change

- `mountMediaArtifact`: a card whose `card_key` starts with
  `chat_render_partial|` gets the tag "Batch finished after the reply · <label>"
  and the status "**some renders failed** — <note>". Every other error,
  not-started or late card renders exactly as before.
- `pollRenderWatch` toast: a `complete` watch that carries a note appends the
  note's first clause, e.g. "1 video ready for review — video job
  render_… (1 of 3 renders done)". Only a partial chat video batch completes
  with a note. Story-still and comfy watches always complete with `note: ""`,
  so their toasts are unchanged.

## Evidence

- `node --check` on the extracted page script: syntax OK.
- `mountMediaArtifact` was evaluated in isolation in the browser pane (the
  page's own startup needs the live server) with three cards:
  - partial batch → "BATCH FINISHED AFTER THE REPLY · VIDEO JOB … / some
    renders failed — 1 of 3 renders done; 0002 failed: …"
  - whole-job crash → unchanged "RENDER ENDED AFTER THE REPLY … / generate
    failed — RuntimeError: …"
  - story batch failure card → unchanged "generate failed — batch item 2 —
    finished without manifest"
- **Not verified in the live GUI.** A real partial batch is needed for that;
  no render was started.

## Coordination

Another agent was working on the GVD VLM judge (score collapse / false
passes) in `generalized_video_director.py`, `dspy_orchestrator.py` and

   the wrong reason. The echo renders scored 1.0 against their own echoed
   field descriptions.
2. **Anchoring on the prompt text.** The M03 rationale restates the MiniMax
   prompt almost word for word.
3. **Scores before reasoning.** The schema had the three numbers first and the
   rationale after, so the model committed to a default triple first.
4. **Not frame coverage.** `extract_eval_frames(count=3)` is clamped to 8
   uniform frames at 2%..98% (0.16 … 7.84 s for 8 s). The failing late regions
   of D01 (drift from ~5 s) and M03 (cut at 4.7 s) are inside the sample. More
   or re-placed frames were **not** tested.
5. **Not temperature.** Decoding was already 0.0 (only temperature and max_tokens
   reach llama.cpp; `repeat_penalty` is set but not forwarded).

## 3. Fix

- New `local_agent/video_judge.py`:
  - CPU detector over every decoded frame (64×36). A hard cut is a colour-histogram
    step ≥ 0.20, ≥ 8× the local median, grayscale correlation < 0.70, not in
    the first two steps (the I2V conditioning pop), not a flash (the picture
    returns within 12 frames, forward or backward), and not a step into or out
    of a near-black frame. Near-black fraction = frames with mean luma < 16.
    On the set: cuts flagged in D01 `8358` (0.88 s), M03 `371a` (4.71 s),
    D03 `5c73` (1.08 s), D03 `ffd4` (0.92 s); near-black ≥ 25% in 5 rejects;
    **no good or partial clip flagged.** Only 4 of 10 labeled cuts; gradual
    (morph) cuts are left to the VLM. Narrow margin: c017's lights-off frame is
    14.7 luma, M03's post-cut frame 17.2.
  - VLM prompt judged against **BRIEF + CONSTRAINTS** (student prompts no
    longer sent). Order: one line per frame with timestamps, then 7 yes/no
    checks plus `constraint_broken`, then the three scores and rationale.
  - Python caps: subject not visible → alignment ≤ 0.20; medium mismatch
    (only when the brief names a stylized medium) → ≤ 0.30; wrong subject count
    or a real constraint quote → ≤ 0.40; unrequested text/logo → alignment
    ≤ 0.30 and aesthetic ≤ 0.40; location change or cut → temporal ≤ 0.30;
    time-of-day change → ≤ 0.40; detected hard cut → ≤ 0.25; near-black → aesthetic ≤ 0.20.
- `dspy_orchestrator.py`: new `judge_rendered_clip()`; `evaluate_live_candidate`
  uses it (new optional `signals_fn` hook). Output keeps the
  `parse_video_director_scores` shape, so `_fail_penalty`, the curriculum and
  the 0.7·min + 0.3·mean MIPRO scalar are unchanged. Feedback rows add
  `scores_vlm`, `checks`, `caps`, `signals`; `vlm_raw` kept to 4000 chars.
  `run_qwen_director_scores` `num_predict` 1024 → 1536.
- `media_accuracy_gate.py` (CRLF kept): literal-mode override factored into
  `literal_override_block()` and shared by both judges. Old builder output is
  byte-identical in all three modes (verified against the backup).

Two rules were added after the first run (`results_v2a.jsonl`) showed the VLM
misusing checks. Both are general, not per-clip:
(a) `constraint_broken` counts only if the brief has constraints and the text
isn't a dump of check answers; (b) medium mismatch binds only for stylized
briefs (it called clean Backrooms hallways "3D renders"), plus one prompt line
saying a brief that names no medium accepts any realistic look.

D01 `3032`; camera operator in shot: c036), late location drift (D01 `086a`,
D01 `3032`, c030), style (S01 photographed print, S05 full colour instead of
B&W ink), M04 dry-adult "teleports" (`15e7`, `cfa7`), B01 wall wobble.
@0.85 the three failed good clips are Backrooms clips at aesthetic 0.80.

Caveats:
- Small set (8 goods), labeled by one reviewer.
- The detector thresholds and rules (a)/(b) were tuned on this same set, so
  these numbers flatter the judge. A held-out set is needed before trusting
  the absolute rates.
- The VLM is prompt-sensitive: between v2a and v2b individual verdicts flipped
  both ways (M05 caught, M04 `15e7` lost).
- Scores are now bimodal (checks fire together: a halo). Collapse is reduced,

The VLM score ranks clips; it does not accept them.

chunks.text:
# 2026-09-24r — GVD judge: held-out check and frame-count experiment

Follows 2026-09-24q. Operator asked for both a held-out set and a test of
more frames. Existing renders only: no ComfyUI, no renders. The VLM ran under
the same guards as 24q (port 8188 closed, owners idle, GPU ≤ 70 °C at start,
owner held, 82 °C check before every clip, release plus wait for ≤ 58 °C after
each run). Six runs, 0 server crashes, GPU idle afterwards (37 °C).

**Outcome: production stays at 8 uniform frames.** No production code change
in this entry (`dspy_orchestrator.py` untouched).

## Held-out set (labels frozen before any fixed-judge run)

`local_agent/runtime/dspy_opt/judge_eval/gvd_judge_labels_heldout.json`,
sha256 `c915d3adef4dd12b2665a3aaff344a025472030cb676e0058e23f859c88821d9`.
29 clips not used in 24q tuning: **12 good, 12 reject, 5 partial**. Sheets are
in `runtime/dspy_opt/judge_eval_20260924/heldout/`. Excluded as ambiguous, with
reasons in the file: c015, c027, c012 (their prompts ask for, or contradict,
the "fault"), the br_c002/c008/c009 boilerplate prompts, and c031 (a
duplicate).

Bias: every good clip is a Backrooms-batch clip, and 6 of 12 rejects are GVD
Beta clips. Old-judge history scores were visible for the GVD clips while I
scanned; no fixed-judge score was seen before freezing.
