## Job 2 — native calls in `ollama_client.py`

Add `tools=` to `chat()` and `chat_stream()`, passed through to the request body.

Streaming plus tool calls needs care: Ollama emits tool calls in the message
object, sometimes with no content tokens at all. Make sure a turn that is purely
a tool call does not render as an empty reply.

## Job 3 — rewrite the loop in `agent.py`

- Pass `tools.schemas()` on every request.
- Read `message.tool_calls` instead of regex-parsing the text.
- **Support multiple tool calls per turn.** Run them all, append one
  `{"role": "tool", "name": ..., "content": ...}` message per result, and
  continue. This is the main capability gain — "compare 00B and 27E" becomes one
  hop instead of two.
- Raise `MAX_TOOL_HOPS` to 6 now that hops are not wasted one-per-tool.
- **Keep a fallback.** If a model returns no `tool_calls` but its text matches
  the old `TOOL:` pattern, honour it. Some models will not support the native
  path and must still work. Log which path was used.
- Delete the now-redundant nagging from `CONVERSATION_RULES` — the whole
  "NEVER answer from memory / NEVER describe what a tool would return" block
  exists only because the text protocol was unreliable. Keep the short version:
  prefer tools for state, counts, clips and files. Reclaimed context is the point.

## Job 4 — the GUI keeps working

`server.py` streams `tool` and `tool_result` events and `static/index.html`
renders them as action cards. Preserve that. With several calls in one turn,
emit one card per call.

## Verify — all of it, no shortcuts

```powershell
python local_agent\tools.py
python -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'local_agent');import tools,json;print(json.dumps(tools.schemas(),indent=2)[:1500])"
```

- [ ] all 14 tools have a valid schema; every enum matches the real whitelist
- [ ] a live question through the GUI produces a real `tool_calls` response
- [ ] a two-part question ("compare the ladders for 00B and 00A") triggers **two
      tool calls in one turn** and both results reach the answer
- [ ] the legacy `TOOL:` fallback still fires for a model that does not support
      native calling — test by stubbing a reply
- [ ] **the guard rails still refuse**: unknown tool, clip id `../etc`, doc name
      `/etc/passwd`, build action `rm -rf /`, and `write_file` onto a protected
      manifest
- [ ] Stop, Regenerate, attachments and persistence all still work
- [ ] `python local_agent\validate_h3_prompt.py --dir outputs\equal_shares\prompts_native_r2v`
      still reports **124/124 valid**

Then measure and report: how many tokens the system prompt lost, and whether the
model called tools on questions where it previously answered from memory. Give
the numbers.

## Do not stop

A failing test is a task, not a stopping point. Stop only when every box above is
ticked and you have written the `CHANGELOG/` entry.

# Claude Code prompt — retrieval over the whole doc tree (refreshed 2026-08-23)

Paste into your coding agent. Run from the repo root
(`COMFYUI_STORY_HANDOFF_2026-08-09/`). Read `local_agent/README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`,
`local_agent/agent.py`, and `local_agent/router.py` first.

## What this is (and what already changed since the original 02)

The original upgrade 2 had two halves. **Half one — raising `num_ctx` — is already
done** and must NOT be redone: the adaptive reasoning pair now sets context
per-model in `router.Decision.options()` (primary 14B → 20480, fallback 8B → 32768)
with predictive routing at ~16K tokens. **Do not blanket-edit `GPU_OPTIONS`
num_ctx** — that would fight the adaptive logic.

This prompt is the **half that was never built: retrieval.** Today the agent only
knows `knowledge/SYSTEM_PROMPT.md`, a compiled ~9.5 KB digest of a ~200 KB tree.
Ask about a specific CHANGELOG measurement or a paragraph of `H3_PROMPT_RULES.md`
and it either reads a whole file or guesses. Give it lexical search over the tree.

## Job 1 — a retrieval index, no model required

New file `local_agent/retrieval.py`. Index, chunked to ~800 tokens with ~100-token
overlap, chunk boundaries on headings where possible:

    docs/**/*.md      CLAUDE.md      README.md
    CHANGELOG/*.md    START_*.md     FINISH_LOCAL_AGENT.md
    local_agent/UPGRADE/*.md
    outputs/equal_shares/runtime/agent_questions.md

**Skip** `archive/`, `_QUARANTINE_*`, `*.BACKUP*`, and anything bannered SUPERSEDED
— those are deliberately not current and must never be retrieved as fact.

- **Scoring: BM25 in plain Python** (~40 lines). No `rank_bm25`, no `sklearn`,
  nothing to install — offline forever.
- Make the scorer swappable: `score(query, chunks)` behind a small interface with
  `LexicalScorer` as default, so upgrade 5's `EmbeddingScorer` drops in later
  without touching callers.
- Persist the index as JSON next to the code, keyed by each file's mtime + size;
  rebuild only changed files. Startup stays under a second.

## Job 2 — expose it as a tool

Add `search_docs` to `tools.py` (registry + schema), `{"query": "...",
"max_results": 5}`, returning the top chunks each with its **source file and
heading** so the agent can cite where a claim came from — a claim without a source
is not evidence in this project. It is a read-only tool; it never writes.

Update `CONVERSATION_RULES` in `agent.py`: for any question about a rule, a
decision, why something is the way it is, or project history — **search the docs
first**; `read_doc` stays for reading a whole named file.

the num_ctx values themselves.)

## Job 4 — a context-trim guard that respects the adaptive window

Add a guard: if a request's estimated tokens would exceed the **effective** window
for the chosen model (use `router.Decision.options()["num_ctx"]` /
`router.estimate_context_tokens`, which already exist), trim the **oldest**
conversation turns — never the system prompt, never the current turn — and emit a
`note` event when trimming happens. This complements the predictive 14B→8B switch;
it does not replace it.

- Index builds over the real tree — report file count, chunk count, index size.
- Touching one file re-indexes only that file.
- `search_docs "why was the pace corrected to 2.5"` returns the 2026-08-17b
  CHANGELOG chunk in the top 3; `search_docs "duration ladder"` returns the right
  `H3_PROMPT_RULES` section.
- Archived / superseded docs never appear in results (add a test asserting this).
- `test_native_tool_calling.py` still green; `search_docs` schema registered.
- Brief is under 6 KB.
- `validate_h3_prompt.py` still **124/124**.

Write `CHANGELOG/<today>_retrieval_over_tree.md` (what/why/evidence/verified/

02 was outstanding; the num_ctx half was already delivered by the adaptive pair.

Every chat currently starts blind. Add a persistent facts file the agent reads at

New file `local_agent/memory.py`, storing to `local_agent/memory.json`:

```

forget(index)              move to a `_forgotten` list, never hard-delete
```

Expose `remember` as a tool. **Do not** let it write silently on every turn —
that fills up with noise. It writes when the operator says something like
"remember that…" or states a durable preference.

Cap it at ~1 KB; if it grows past that, report so it can be pruned deliberately.

Seed it with what is already established: prefers concise answers, is on a phone
hotspot so downloads need approval, runs an RTX 5080 with 16 GB, and is the only
one who can accept a take by ear.

Also seed the **end goal**, from `local_agent/ROADMAP.md`: a Reticulum mesh
linking phone and workstation, so this agent becomes reachable from an Android
client with file access — one assistant available on both devices, with all the
compute staying on the workstation. The agent should know this, because it
changes what "add remote access" means if it is ever asked.

## Job 3 — harden web search

`web_search` scrapes DuckDuckGo lite. That will rate-limit and its HTML will
change. Make it degrade honestly rather than silently returning nothing:

- distinguish **no internet** from **blocked/rate-limited** from **zero results**,
  and say which
- a short retry with backoff on a transient failure
- if the HTML shape no longer parses, say *that* rather than returning empty —
  a silently empty search is the kind of wrong-measurement failure this project
  has been bitten by repeatedly
- add a `search_docs`-first note in the tool description: local docs before the
  web, for anything about this project

without dumping binary into the context.

ChatGPT Desktop runs Python in a sandbox. **Do not simply add that here.** This

- the project tree mounted **read-only in effect**: the snippet may read project

- output truncated; a non-zero exit reported plainly
- refuse outright if the snippet text matches obvious destructive patterns

If you judge this too risky to do safely, **say so and skip it** — write the
reasoning in the CHANGELOG instead. A missing feature is better than a
plausible-looking sandbox that isn't one.

`local_agent/ROADMAP.md` records the end goal: phone and workstation linked over
a Reticulum mesh, with an Android client acting as a thin terminal onto this
agent. Nothing in this upgrade should make that harder.

Two hard rules while you work:

- **Never bind the server to `0.0.0.0`**, not even temporarily to test something
  from another device. The agent executes actions and writes project files; the
  remote path will get its own authenticated transport, not an open HTTP port.
- **Keep transport out of `agent.py`.** `answer()` takes a history list and an
  event callback and knows nothing about HTTP — that seam is where a mesh

The main chat model stays **text-only and smart**. Vision and audio are *tools it
calls*, not a multimodal model it becomes. That way you never trade reasoning
quality for the ability to look at a frame, and each sense can be swapped

## Job 1 — a capability registry

chunks.heading: # Upgrade 6 — reach the agent from your phone over cellular. Before the mesh.
chunks.text:
# Upgrade 6 — reach the agent from your phone over cellular. Before the mesh.

Paste everything below the line into Claude Code. Run **after** upgrade 3.

Needs internet **once**, to install Tailscale. After that it works on cellular.

---

Make the local agent reachable from the operator's phone over the cellular
network, as an interim step before the Reticulum mesh in `local_agent/ROADMAP.md`.

```
A:\Users\rhine\Documents\Codex\2026-08-07\referenced-chatgpt-conversation-this-is-an-2\COMFYUI_STORY_HANDOFF_2026-08-09
```

## Read this before writing any code

**The agent currently has NO authentication.** None. Zero. Its entire security
model is the single line binding it to `127.0.0.1` — the assumption that only a
process on this machine can reach it.

That assumption is about to be removed. And this agent can:

- write files anywhere not on the protected list
- run build actions that regenerate project state
- read any file on the machine
- (if upgrade 3 added it) execute Python

So **transport alone is not enough.** Even on a private network, the app itself
needs authentication. A phone left on a table is now a key to the workstation.
Both layers, or neither.

## Job 1 — the transport: Tailscale, not port forwarding

**Do not port-forward. Do not use ngrok or a public tunnel.**

Cellular carriers put phones behind CGNAT, so nothing can connect *in* to the
phone, and many home ISPs now do the same. Tailscale solves this: it is a
WireGuard mesh with NAT traversal and a relay fallback, so both devices dial out
and meet in the middle. Traffic is end-to-end encrypted between devices.

The free Personal plan covers this comfortably — as of August 2026 it allows six
users and **unlimited user devices**, with no expiry.

Install on the workstation and on the phone, sign both into the same tailnet.
Verify the phone can ping the workstation's `100.x.x.x` address over cellular
with Wi-Fi **off** — that is the actual test, not Wi-Fi.

**Alternatives, if a third-party coordination server is unacceptable:**
`headscale` is a self-hosted control plane but needs a VPS with a public IP;
plain WireGuard is free and fully self-hosted but requires a reachable endpoint
at home, which CGNAT may prevent. Tailscale is the pragmatic choice here.
Record which was chosen and why.

chunks.text:

## Job 2 — bind to the tailnet interface only, never 0.0.0.0

This is the important line of code.

`server.py` currently binds `127.0.0.1`. Change it to bind **the Tailscale
interface address specifically** — not `0.0.0.0`.

The difference matters: `0.0.0.0` exposes the agent on every network the machine
joins, including hotel Wi-Fi and coffee shops. Binding the tailnet IP exposes it
only on the encrypted overlay, which no other network can route to.

Implement as `--bind` with a default of `127.0.0.1`, plus `--tailscale` which
discovers the tailnet address and binds that **in addition to** loopback. If the
address cannot be found, **fail loudly and stay on loopback** — never silently
fall back to a wider bind.

Update `ROADMAP.md`: the "never bind 0.0.0.0" rule stands unchanged; this is a
narrower exception, not a repeal.

## Job 3 — real authentication on the app

Add a token layer to `server.py`:

- a long random token generated on first run, stored in
  `local_agent/remote_token.txt` with a note that it is a secret
- every `/api/*` request requires it, via `Authorization: Bearer` header or a
  cookie set once from a `?token=` URL
- **loopback requests are exempt** so the desktop experience is unchanged
- constant-time comparison; never log the token
- a `--rotate-token` flag

Also add basic rate limiting on `/api/send` — a phone reconnecting in a loop
should not be able to queue fifty generations.

## Job 4 — remote gets fewer powers than the desk

A request arriving over the tailnet is not the same as one from the keyboard.
Add a permission tier keyed on whether the connection is loopback:

| | desktop (loopback) | remote (tailnet) |
|---|---|---|
| read tools — `project_state`, `clip_info`, `read_prompt`, `duration_ladder`, `search_docs`, `read_file`, `list_dir` | yes | **yes** |
| `run_build` — regenerates derived files | yes | **no by default** |
| `write_file` | yes | **no by default** |
| `run_python` if it exists | yes | **no** |
| `propose_gpu` — proposes only, starts nothing | yes | yes |

Make it configurable in one obvious place, defaulting to the table above. The
operator can widen it deliberately; it must not be wide by accident.

This is also the groundwork for Reticulum, where permissions will key on
cryptographic identity instead of loopback. Structure it so that swap is easy.

## Job 5 — make the UI usable on a phone

`static/index.html` is a fixed desktop layout with a 262 px sidebar. On a phone
it will be unusable.

- responsive breakpoint: below ~700 px the sidebar becomes a slide-over drawer
- touch targets at least 44 px
- the composer must not be hidden by the on-screen keyboard
- `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">`
- show a clear **REMOTE** indicator with the reduced permission set, so it is
  never ambiguous which mode you are in
- assume a slow, flaky link: if the SSE stream drops mid-generation, reconnect
  and recover the reply rather than losing it. The conversation is already
  persisted server-side, so the answer survives — make the client re-read it.

## Job 6 — the workstation has to be awake

The agent cannot answer if the machine is asleep. Document, do not automate:

- how to disable sleep while allowing the monitor to turn off
- Wake-on-LAN over the tailnet if the operator wants it
- what happens if a render is mid-flight — the router already sends replies to
  CPU, so remote use during a render is fine and expected

- [ ] the server binds the tailnet address and loopback, and **not** `0.0.0.0` —
      confirm with `netstat -ano | findstr 8760`
- [ ] a request with no token from the tailnet is **rejected**
- [ ] a request from loopback with no token still works
- [ ] a remote request to `write_file` or `run_build` is **refused**, with a clear

chunks.text:
# Upgrade 6a — phone over a USB cable. Do this BEFORE 06.

Paste everything below the line into Claude Code.

One small download: Android platform-tools (~10 MB). Nothing else.

---

Get the agent working on the operator's phone over a **USB cable**, using
`adb reverse`. This is the right first step: it proves the entire mobile
experience while changing nothing about how the server is exposed.

```
A:\Users\rhine\Documents\Codex\2026-08-07\referenced-chatgpt-conversation-this-is-an-2\COMFYUI_STORY_HANDOFF_2026-08-09
```

## Why this approach is better than it sounds

`adb reverse tcp:8760 tcp:8760` makes a port on the **phone's own localhost**
forward, over the USB cable, to the **workstation's localhost**.

From the phone's browser, `http://127.0.0.1:8760` *is* the workstation's agent.

That has a property nothing else does: **the server keeps binding `127.0.0.1`
and nothing changes.** No `0.0.0.0`, no tailnet address, no firewall rule, no
network exposure of any kind. The transport is a physical cable. `ROADMAP.md`'s
"never bind 0.0.0.0" rule is not bent — it is not even touched.

It also needs no internet, no account, and no coordination server, which suits an
operator currently on a hotspot.

## What this DOES prove

Everything except the network:

- the UI on a real phone screen, with a real on-screen keyboard
- SSE streaming into a mobile browser
- the token layer
- the remote-vs-desktop permission tier
- conversations shared between phone and desktop
- reconnect behaviour when the stream drops

## What it does NOT prove

Be honest about this in the CHANGELOG — do not let it be mistaken for a
completed 06:

- NAT traversal and CGNAT, the actual hard part of remote access
- real latency and packet loss over cellular
- behaviour when the link drops for minutes rather than seconds
- whether the workstation is reachable at all when the operator is out

## Job 1 — the cable path

Install Android platform-tools on the workstation (~10 MB — state the exact size
before downloading). Then:

1. Phone: Settings → About → tap Build Number seven times → Developer Options →
   **USB debugging on**
2. Connect by cable, accept the RSA fingerprint prompt on the phone
3. `adb devices` — the device must show as `device`, not `unauthorized`
4. `adb reverse tcp:8760 tcp:8760`
5. Phone browser → `http://127.0.0.1:8760`

Write `local_agent/START_PHONE_USB.ps1` doing all of it: check adb is present,
wait for a device, set up the reverse, start the server if it is not running,
print the URL, and tell the operator plainly what to do if the device shows
`unauthorized` or `offline` — those two are the failures they will actually hit.

`adb reverse` does not survive unplugging. Have the script re-establish it if the
device reconnects.

- generate a token into `local_agent/remote_token.txt` on first run

  `X-Client: phone` header is set by the phone UI — not merely by source address
- desktop browser on the same machine stays token-free
- constant-time comparison, never logged, `--rotate-token` provided

| | desktop | remote |
|---|---|---|
| reads — `project_state`, `clip_info`, `read_prompt`, `duration_ladder`, `search_docs`, `read_file`, `list_dir` | yes | **yes** |
| `run_build` | yes | **no by default** |
| `write_file` | yes | **no by default** |
| `run_python` if present | yes | **no** |
| `propose_gpu` — proposes only | yes | yes |

Configurable in one obvious place. Wide only on purpose, never by accident.

**Mobile UI.** `static/index.html` is a fixed desktop layout with a 262 px
sidebar; on a phone it is unusable.

- responsive breakpoint below ~700 px — sidebar becomes a slide-over drawer
- touch targets ≥ 44 px
- the composer must stay visible above the on-screen keyboard

address; Reticulum will answer it by cryptographic identity. Three transports,

# Upgrade 6b — make it a real phone app. Run after 06a.

Paste everything below the line into Claude Code. **No downloads.**

---

Turn the mobile web page from 06a into something that behaves like the ChatGPT
app: installed on the home screen, able to take files from the phone, able to use
the camera and voice. **No Android development, no app store, no downloads** —
this is a Progressive Web App, which Android treats as a real installed app.

```
A:\Users\rhine\Documents\Codex\2026-08-07\referenced-chatgpt-conversation-this-is-an-2\COMFYUI_STORY_HANDOFF_2026-08-09
```

## Read this first — the constraint that shapes everything

**A browser cannot browse the phone's filesystem.** Android does not permit it,
and no amount of web code changes that. What a browser *can* do is receive files
the operator hands it: through a file picker, through the camera, or through the
Android share sheet.

So "file access on the phone" here means **push, not pull.** The operator shares
or picks a file and it goes to the workstation as an attachment. The agent cannot
go looking through the phone on its own.

Genuine filesystem access needs the native Android app in `ROADMAP.md`. Say so
plainly in the CHANGELOG rather than letting this be mistaken for it. What is
below covers most of what the ChatGPT app actually gets used for.

## The HTTPS catch — read before you start

PWA features (installability, service worker, share target) require a **secure
context**: `https://`, or `http://` on `localhost` / `127.0.0.1`.

- **Over 06a's USB `adb reverse`** the phone connects to `http://127.0.0.1:8760`,
  which **counts as secure**. Everything in this prompt works.
- **Over 06's Tailscale** the address is `http://100.x.x.x`, which does **not**
  count. Service workers and install will be blocked.

The fix for that case is Tailscale's own HTTPS — `tailscale cert` / `tailscale
serve` issues a real certificate for the machine's `*.ts.net` name. Note this in
06 as a dependency, but **build and test everything here over USB first**, where
it just works.

## Job 1 — installable app

Add `local_agent/static/manifest.webmanifest`:

- `name`, `short_name`, `start_url`, `display: "standalone"` so it opens without
  browser chrome
- `theme_color` and `background_color` matching the existing dark palette
- icons at 192 and 512 px, **generated as plain SVG/PNG in the repo** — no
  external asset, nothing fetched

Add a service worker that caches the app shell — HTML, CSS, the icons — so it
opens instantly and shows a clear "workstation unreachable" screen instead of a
browser error when the cable is out or the machine is asleep.

**Never cache API responses.** Conversation state lives on the workstation and
must never be served stale from a phone cache.

Verify Chrome on Android offers "Install app" / "Add to Home screen", and that
launching from the icon opens standalone.

chunks.heading: # Upgrade 7 — point it at folders, get renders. The automated ComfyUI maker.
chunks.text:
# Upgrade 7 — point it at folders, get renders. The automated ComfyUI maker.

Paste everything below the line into Claude Code. **No downloads.**

---

Build a **generic batch renderer**: the operator points the agent at a job folder
of prompts and reference assets, and it renders the whole sequence through
MiniMax H3 unattended.

```
A:\Users\rhine\Documents\Codex\2026-08-07\referenced-chatgpt-conversation-this-is-an-2\COMFYUI_STORY_HANDOFF_2026-08-09
```

This is **not** Equal Shares. It must never read or write
`outputs/equal_shares/**` state — no touching `audio_pass_manifest.json`,
`story_config.json`, or `voice_requirements.json`. It is a second, general
pipeline that happens to reuse the same proven render infrastructure.

## Read first

- `docs/reference/MINIMAX_PROMPT_GUIDE_ref.md` §2.1–2.5 and §4.1 — the reference
  label and marker rules. **Quoted below where they matter; verify them.**
- `docs/GOLDEN_REFERENCE/PROVEN_FACTS.md` §1 — the settings that must not change
- `work/render_single_pass.py` — `build_ref2va_workflow`, `build_fl2va_workflow`,
  `start_comfy`, `stop_comfy`, `submit_workflow`, `wait_for_completion`. **Reuse
  these. Do not rewrite the render path.**
- `work/thermal_guard.py`, `work/duration_ladder.py`

## THE MOST IMPORTANT THING IN THIS DOCUMENT

**Socket numbers are zero-based. Prompt tags are one-based.** They are not the
same number and confusing them is the single most likely way this ships broken.

| Operator's name | ComfyUI socket | Prompt tag | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| img 0 | `ref_images.ref_image_0` | **`<Picture 1>`** | character reference |
| img 1 | `ref_images.ref_image_1` | **`<Picture 2>`** | setting — stays the same |
| img 2 | `ref_images.ref_image_2` | **`<Picture 3>`** | second character, when present |
| video ref | first video socket | **`<Video 1>`** | motion only |

Tags follow **connection order**, so if a slot is empty the later tags shift down.
Three images wired means `<Picture 1>`, `<Picture 2>`, `<Picture 3>`. Two images
wired means `<Picture 1>` and `<Picture 2>` — never `<Picture 3>`.

This project already has a scar from exactly this class of bug: a prompt declared
`<Audio 2>` while the reference was wired into `ref_audio_0`, so every voice in
the clip was mis-attributed. Four clips were affected. See
`CHANGELOG/2026-08-18c_one_off_speaker_rule.md`.

**Also: the operator's existing hand-made renders used `<Video 0>`.** That is
non-conforming — the guide is one-based throughout. A tag of `<Video 0>` likely
bound to nothing, which would explain why those prompts needed heavy prose to
compensate. Emit `<Video 1>`.

## Job 1 — verify the video socket before building anything

**Do not assume `MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo` accepts a video reference.** The
project's 15 proven-good graphs use image and audio references only; a video
reference socket has never been exercised here.

Establish the truth, in this order:

1. Query the running ComfyUI at `/object_info` for the node's real input schema
2. If a video socket exists, record its exact name
3. If it does not, **stop and report that** — the motion-reference feature cannot
   be built on a socket that is not there, and the operator needs to know rather
   than receive something that silently ignores the video

Write what you find into the CHANGELOG. This is the one genuine unknown.

## Job 2 — the job folder layout

The operator points at one folder. Detect this structure:

```
<job>/
  prompts/       0001.txt, 0002.txt, ...      one per render, sorted
  video_refs/    00.mp4, 01.mp4, ...          motion reference per render
  img0/          character reference
  img1/          setting reference
  img2/          second character (optional)
  renders/       created by you — output goes here
```

**Slot filling rule — auto-detect, do not ask:**

- a slot folder holding **one** file → that file is used for **every** render
- a slot folder holding **numbered** files → matched **sequentially** to the
  prompt index

So `img1/` with a single `setting.png` stays fixed across the whole batch, while
`img0/` with `00.png, 01.png, …` advances per render. That covers both cases the
operator described without any configuration.

Accept flat layouts too — files named `prompt_001.txt`, `video_001.mp4`,
`img0_001.png` in one folder. Sort **naturally**, so `2` comes before `10`.

**Report the plan before rendering anything.** A dry run that prints, per render:
prompt file, video ref, each image slot, resolved tags, duration, output path.
The operator must be able to see the whole batch is correctly paired before a
single frame is generated. Mismatched counts are reported as a warning with the
pairing shown, not silently truncated.

The operator must be able to see the whole batch is correctly paired before a

## Job 3 — the motion-only lock, done properly

The operator's rule: **the video reference supplies motion only. The model must
never copy imagery from it.**

The guide has a canonical construction for exactly this. From §2.1:

```text
<Subject 1> is the woman whose appearance comes from <Picture 1> and whose
walking motion comes from <Video 1>.
```

That is the correct way to say it — appearance sourced from the image, motion
sourced from the video, in the subject definition where the model expects it.

And `retention_analysis` gets the matching marker. From §4.1 the visible-content
markers are `fully_preserved`, `partially_preserved`, `attribute_transfer`,
`weak_reference`, and the guide's own example for a structural video reference is:

```text
<Video 1> (cut and pacing structure): weak_reference - ...
```

So emit, for a motion-only video:

```text
<Video 1> (motion and camera structure only): weak_reference - only the movement,
timing, and camera behaviour are taken from <Video 1>. None of its people,
faces, bodies, clothing, setting, or lighting appear in the target video.
```

Plus the identity line pinning appearance to `<Picture 1>`.

**This is stronger than prose alone** because `retention_analysis` is the section
this project already proved the model actually acts on — adding it is what
removed the doubled voice after weeks of prose failing to.

Build all three pieces automatically: the subject definition, the retention line,
and a short confirming sentence in `detailed_description`. The operator's prompt
files should not have to contain any of it.

## Job 4 — the renderer

New `work/batch_render_folder.py`. Reuse the existing infrastructure; do not
reimplement it.

Non-negotiable, from `PROVEN_FACTS.md` §1:

```
ref2va      minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_nvfp4.safetensors
fl2va       minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors
encoder     qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors
VAEs        minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16 + minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32
sampler     res_multistep / simple, denoise 1.0, 20 steps
fps/depth   24 / 8-bit
frames      congruent to 5 modulo 17
```

Megapixels is a **CLI argument**, defaulting to 0.9 for picture work. Turbo
checkpoints, nodes and LoRAs stay prohibited.

Operational rules, all reusing what exists:

- **one backend per render**, stopped after, `thermal_guard` before and after
- claim `render_queue_owner.json` — never run beside the Equal Shares pass
- resume: skip renders whose output already exists, unless `--force`
- **never overwrite.** Attempt N goes to a new file; nothing is replaced
- per-job manifest inside the job folder, recording for every render: prompt
  file, every reference path, resolved tags, seed, duration, frames, megapixels,
  output path, status
- `--limit N` so the operator can try three before committing to eighty
- on VRAM failure, drop 0.1 MP and record it; floor at 0.4 MP for picture

If a prompt has dialogue, reuse `duration_ladder.py` for retries — same rule,
duration not seed. If it has none, a failed render retries once then reports.

## Job 5 — validate before spending GPU time

Every assembled prompt goes through `local_agent/validate_h3_prompt.py` **before**
it is submitted. A prompt that fails is reported with its faults and **skipped**,
not rendered.

Eighty renders at several minutes each is hours. Catching a malformed prompt
beforehand costs milliseconds.

Note honestly in the CHANGELOG: that validator was written for this project's
six-section dialogue prompts and passes 124/124 of them. Behaviour on
motion-reference prompts is **unproven** — if it produces false positives on
valid batch prompts, fix the validator with a recorded measurement, do not
disable the check.

## Job 6 — expose it to the agent

Two tools in `local_agent/tools.py`:

- **`batch_plan`** — `{"folder": "..."}`. Scans, pairs, resolves tags, validates
  every prompt, returns the plan. **Read-only, renders nothing.**
- **`batch_render`** — proposal only, exactly like `propose_gpu`. Returns the
  command for the operator to approve. **The agent must never start a batch.**

Then the operator can say *"look at D:\jobs\scene12 and tell me if it's ready"*
and get a real answer, followed by a command they run themselves.

## Verify

Build a synthetic job folder with 3 prompts, 3 video refs, a sequential `img0/`,
a single fixed `img1/`, and a two-file `img2/`. Then:

- [ ] pairing is correct and reported before anything renders
- [ ] the fixed slot repeats; the sequential slots advance
- [ ] natural sort puts `2` before `10`
- [ ] tags are **one-based and contiguous**, and match the sockets actually wired
- [ ] a render with only two images emits `<Picture 1>`/`<Picture 2>` and **no**
      `<Picture 3>`
- [ ] the motion lock appears in all three places: subject definition, retention
      line with `weak_reference`, and detailed description
- [ ] mismatched counts warn and show the pairing rather than truncating silently
- [ ] an invalid prompt is skipped with its faults listed, not rendered
- [ ] `--limit 1` renders exactly one
- [ ] re-running skips completed renders; `--force` redoes them
- [ ] nothing under `outputs/equal_shares/**` is read or written — verify by
      timestamp
- [ ] the queue owner is claimed and released
- [ ] `batch_render` refuses to execute and returns a command instead
- [ ] guard rails still refuse; `validate_h3_prompt.py` still **124/124** on the
      Equal Shares set

## Do not stop

Work through. The one legitimate stop is Job 1 finding that no video reference
socket exists — report that clearly and continue building everything else, with
the motion reference disabled and the reason recorded.

Finish with a `CHANGELOG/` entry: the real socket name you found, the tag mapping
as implemented, and whether the validator needed adjusting for this prompt shape.

chunks.heading: # Claude Code prompt — GUI context ceiling + "Yield GPU" button (refreshed 2026-08-23)
chunks.text:
# Claude Code prompt — GUI context ceiling + "Yield GPU" button (refreshed 2026-08-23)

Paste into your coding agent. Run from the repo root
(`COMFYUI_STORY_HANDOFF_2026-08-09/`). Read `local_agent/README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`,
`local_agent/router.py`, `local_agent/agent.py`, and `local_agent/server.py` first.
**Do not touch the render pipeline, the busy-detection signals, or
`outputs/equal_shares/**`.**

## What changed since the original 08 — read this first

`num_ctx` is no longer a single hard-coded value. The adaptive reasoning pair now
sets it **per model** in `router.Decision.options()`: the 14B primary gets 20480,
the 8B fallback gets 32768, and there is predictive 14B→8B routing at ~16K
estimated tokens. So the GUI control must be a **ceiling that coordinates with**
that logic — never a blanket override that fights it.

## Feature 1 — a GUI context ceiling (num_ctx)

The operator wants to cap how much context the agent uses, live, from the chat
interface, without editing code or restarting.

1. **Control in `local_agent/static/index.html`** — a select of presets
   (`8192 / 16384 / 24576 / 32768`) plus an "Auto" default, labelled "Context
   (tokens)". Persist the choice in `localStorage`, restore on load, show the value
   actually in effect.
2. **Send it each turn** (match how `server.py` already receives `message`/`prefer`).
3. **Apply as a CEILING, after the adaptive value is computed.** Thread the value
   into `agent.answer(...)`. The effective num_ctx for a turn is
   `min(adaptive_value_from_Decision.options(), gui_ceiling)` when the operator set
   one, else the adaptive value unchanged. Never raise num_ctx above what the
   chosen model/tier already allows. "Auto" means: don't cap — use the adaptive
   value as-is.
4. **Clamp** the incoming value to `[4096, 32768]`; a bogus value never crashes a
   turn — fall back to Auto.
5. **Surface the effective value** on the existing `route` event so the GUI line can
   show e.g. `[GPU qwen3-abliterated:14b · ctx 20480 (capped 16384)]`.
6. **One line of UI helper text**: a lower ceiling frees VRAM for a render and can
   push a long chat to the 8B sooner; Ollama reloads the model when num_ctx changes,
   so the first reply after a change is slower. Do not invent numbers.

Interaction to respect, not re-implement: the predictive 14B→8B switch at ~16K
tokens and the reactive OOM failover already live in `router`/`agent`. The ceiling
only *lowers* the window; it must not disable or duplicate that routing.

## Feature 2 — a manual "Yield GPU" button

Reuse `router.unload()` — do not write a second eviction path. Add a thin action
that finds the resident GPU model the way `router.decide()` does
(`router._pick(router._tags(GPU_HOST), GPU_MODELS)` when `router.up(GPU_HOST)`; also
evict anything `router._running_models(GPU_HOST)` reports resident), calls
`router.unload(GPU_HOST, model)`, and reports what it freed. Expose it as a GUI
"Yield GPU" button hitting a new endpoint. Safe to press when nothing is resident
("nothing to free"). Report VRAM via `router.gpu_memory()` if available but never
block on `nvidia-smi`. It never starts/stops a render and never touches
`render_queue_owner.json`.

## Constraints

Stdlib only; server stays on `127.0.0.1`; `agent.answer()` stays
transport-agnostic (the ceiling is a plain optional argument). Never weaken
`gpu_busy()` or the one-owner rule.

## Verify (show commands + output; mockable)

1. `python local_agent/test_native_tool_calling.py` and `test_router_switching.py`
   → still green.
2. New stdlib test: with the adaptive value mocked at 20480, a GUI ceiling of 16384
   yields an effective 16384; a ceiling of 32768 leaves 20480 unchanged (never
   raised); "Auto" passes the adaptive value through; out-of-range clamps to Auto.
3. New stdlib test: the Yield endpoint calls `router.unload(GPU_HOST, <model>)` once
   for the resident model and returns "nothing to free" when `up(GPU_HOST)` is False.
4. Manually: change the ceiling, send a turn, confirm the effective value shows in
   the route line; press Yield with and without a model resident.

## Record it

Write `CHANGELOG/<today>_gui_ctx_ceiling_and_yield.md` (what/why/evidence/verified/
unverified), add its row to `CHANGELOG/README.md`, mark UPGRADE 08 built in
`local_agent/UPGRADE/00_INDEX.md`, and note both controls in
`local_agent/README.md`. State plainly that the control is a ceiling coordinating
with the adaptive pair, not a replacement for it.

chunks.heading: # Claude Code prompt — tiered vision load, "GPU Busy" queue, and a GPU watcher
chunks.text:
# Claude Code prompt — tiered vision load, "GPU Busy" queue, and a GPU watcher

> **Source preserved from Google Drive (2026-08-24):**
> [`09_media_gpu_queue.md`](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Z3Wdu3Xcj1AAUdEjSQPepQsy7WKvZKbJ5GoC59KmzQU/edit?usp=drivesdk).

Paste into Claude Code, run from the repo root
(`COMFYUI_STORY_HANDOFF_2026-08-09/`). Self-contained. Read `local_agent/README.md`
and `CLAUDE.md` first — they are binding. Internet **is** available now, so
`ollama pull` is allowed. Do not touch the render pipeline or `outputs/equal_shares/**`.

## The behaviour to build

When the operator asks the agent to look at an image/video or listen to audio, the
sensory model must load on the **GPU**, but the GPU is often occupied by a render.
The required policy, in order:

1. **Primary model, full GPU load.** If the GPU has enough free VRAM to hold the
   primary abliterated Qwen vision model *fully*, load it there and process now.
2. **Smaller model, full GPU load.** If the primary will not fully fit, try a
   smaller vision model that needs less VRAM. If *it* fully fits, use it now.
3. **Queue + "GPU Busy".** If even the smaller model will not fully fit, do **not**
   run it half-offloaded to CPU. Emit **`GPU Busy`** to the GUI and enqueue the
   file(s) in a persistent watch queue, telling the operator it will be processed
   when the GPU frees.
4. **Watcher drains the queue.** A background watcher polls the GPU; the moment
   enough VRAM is free to fully load a model (and no render owns the card), it
   loads the best-fitting model and processes the queued items in order, writing
   results back so the GUI shows them. Then it idles until more work or more VRAM.

This is a deliberate change from today's behaviour in `media_tools._vision`, which
falls back to the **CPU** Ollama server when the GPU is busy. A Qwen-VL model on
four CPU threads is unusably slow, so **remove the CPU fallback for vision** and
replace it with the tiered-GPU + queue policy above. (Whisper transcription stays
CPU-side as it is — see "Audio" below.)

chunks.heading: ## The behaviour to build
chunks.text:
VRAM.

This is a deliberate change from today's behaviour in `media_tools._vision`, which
falls back to the **CPU** Ollama server when the GPU is busy. A Qwen-VL model on
four CPU threads is unusably slow, so **remove the CPU fallback for vision** and
replace it with the tiered-GPU + queue policy above. (Whisper transcription stays
CPU-side as it is — see "Audio" below.)

## What "fully fits" means — detect it deterministically

Ollama will silently offload layers to system RAM when a model does not fit,
producing a slow "partial" load. Detect fit **before** loading, by free VRAM:

1. Add `router.gpu_free_mb() -> int | None` next to `router.gpu_memory()`, reading
   `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.free --format=csv,noheader,nounits` (same
   subprocess/except pattern; `None` when nvidia-smi is unavailable).
2. Define per-tier VRAM requirements (weights + KV headroom), as named constants,
   e.g. in `capabilities.py`:
   - primary `qwen3-vl-abliterated:8b-q8_0` → ~11500 MB
   - smaller `qwen3-vl-abliterated:4b`      → ~7000 MB
   Add a safety margin constant (e.g. `VRAM_SAFETY_MB = 1024`) on top.
   Tune the numbers with a comment citing the model file sizes (8B Q8_0 = 8.71 GB
   + f16 mmproj 1.16 GB; 4B ≈ 6.1 GB).
3. A tier "fully fits" iff `gpu_free_mb() is not None and free >= need + margin`
   **and** `router.gpu_busy()` reports no render owning the card (queue owner /
   port 8188 / foreign compute process). **Fail safe:** if `gpu_free_mb()` is
   `None` (nvidia-smi missing), treat as *does not fit* → queue. An unknown GPU is
   never permission to load.

## The smaller model

Add the smaller tier to `capabilities.VISION_PREFERENCES` (created in the
2026-08-22 vision-watcher change) so selection stays deterministic. Pull it (net is
allowed):

    ollama pull huihui_ai/qwen3-vl-abliterated:4b

or import a local 4B GGUF if the operator prefers. Give `capabilities.py` a way to
report, per tier, `(model_name, vram_need_mb)` so both `media_tools` and the
watcher choose the same tiers from one source of truth — e.g.
`capabilities.vision_tiers() -> list[dict]` returning the installed, vision-capable
tiers largest-first with their VRAM needs.

## The queue (persistent, stdlib, atomic)

- Store under `local_agent/media_queue/` — `pending/`, `processing/`, `done/`,
  `failed/` subdirs, one JSON job file per item. No database, no deps.
- A job records: `id`, `created` (pass a timestamp in; do not rely on wall-clock
  inside any workflow), `media_type` (`image`|`video`|`audio`), `path`(s),
  `question`, `crop`/frame args, `status`, and on completion `model`, `tier`,
  `result`, or `error`.
- Writes must be atomic (write temp, `os.replace`) so a crash never leaves a
  half-written job. Move the file between dirs to change state.
- A single module `local_agent/media_queue.py` owns enqueue / claim-next / complete
  / fail / list, transport-agnostic (no HTTP knowledge), so the server, the tools,
  and the watcher all use it.

## Where the tiering plugs in

- `media_tools._vision(...)`: replace the CPU-fallback block. Compute the best
  tier that fully fits (via `capabilities.vision_tiers()` + `router.gpu_free_mb()`).
  If one fits, load that model on the GPU and return the analysis as today. If none
  fits, **enqueue** the item(s) and return a structured
  `{"queued": true, "reason": "GPU Busy", "queue_id": ...,
    "position": N}` result — the tool result the model/GUI shows.
- `see_image` / `analyze_video`: unchanged entry points; they still call `_vision`,
  which now either analyses or queues. `analyze_video` already extracts frames
  first — enqueue the extracted frame paths so the watcher needs no ffmpeg re-run.
- **Audio** (`transcribe`): Whisper runs on CPU, so it does not need GPU VRAM. But
  the operator wants audio queued too when the machine is busy. Enqueue audio jobs
  with `media_type:"audio"`; the watcher processes them through the existing CPU
  Whisper path, gated on "no render active and the CPU chat model can be evicted"
  rather than on VRAM. Keep the existing one-CPU-model-at-a-time eviction.

## The watcher

`local_agent/media_watcher.py`, mirroring the project's watchdog conventions:

- Single-instance (own owner/lock file under `local_agent/media_queue/`), bound to
  nothing (no network server); pure local loop. `--once` does one drain pass and
  exits (for tests/cron); default loops every ~15 s.
- Each pass: if `pending/` is empty, idle. Else pick the largest tier that fully
  fits right now (`gpu_free_mb` + not `gpu_busy`); if none fits and there are only
  vision jobs, stay idle and log "waiting for GPU". For each processable job:
  claim → move to `processing/` → run the same code path as the live tool →
  move to `done/` with the result (or `failed/` with the error). Never delete a
  source file.
- It loads the model once and processes as many queued items as fit that window,
  then optionally `router.unload(GPU_HOST, model)` when the queue drains so it does
  not hold VRAM against the next render. Respect the one-owner rule: never load
  while `gpu_busy()` says a render owns the card.
- Start it from `START_LOCAL_AGENT_GUI.ps1` alongside the server (or document a
  separate launch). Log to `local_agent/media_queue/watcher.log`.

## GUI (`server.py` + `static/index.html`)

  free."**
- Add `GET /api/media_queue` returning `{pending, processing, done, failed}` counts
  and recent completed results. Add a small queue indicator in the GUI (near the
  existing GPU-status pill that already shows "GPU busy — render has it") that shows
  the pending count and lets the operator see a completed result when the watcher
  finishes. Poll it on the same cadence as the status pill.
- When the watcher completes an item, its result must be retrievable in the GUI via
  `/api/media_queue` (surfacing it into the originating conversation is a bonus, not

  fail-safe rule are preserved everywhere.
- One GPU owner ever. The watcher must never load a model while a render owns the
  card. Never delete a raw generation, reference, source media, or evidence.
- `media_queue.py` and `media_watcher.py` stay transport-agnostic; only `server.py`

chunks.heading: # ChatGPT / Codex prompt — dynamic 14B↔8B chat-model fallback on a 16 GB GPU
chunks.text:
# ChatGPT / Codex prompt — dynamic 14B↔8B chat-model fallback on a 16 GB GPU

Paste this whole block into ChatGPT (Codex) or Claude Code. Run it from the repo
root of the local agent (`COMFYUI_STORY_HANDOFF_2026-08-09/`).

---

You are editing a **custom Python script**, not a framework — the offline assistant
under `local_agent/` (stdlib only, no LangChain/AutoGen, Ollama as the backend on
`127.0.0.1`). Read `local_agent/README.md`, `local_agent/router.py`,
`local_agent/agent.py`, and `local_agent/ollama_client.py` before changing
anything. Do not touch the render pipeline or `outputs/equal_shares/**`.

## Goal

The agent's GPU **chat/reasoning** tier must dynamically choose between a 14B and an
8B abliterated model so a growing context never OOMs the 16 GB card, while short
prompts still get the smarter 14B. This is the chat model only — it is separate
from the vision watcher (that has its own tiering) and from the GUI num_ctx control.

### Why (16 GB VRAM budget)

- A 14B model at Q4 is ~9 GB of static VRAM. The OS/display take 1–2 GB.
- KV cache grows with history: at ~32K context it can add 4 GB+, pushing a 14B
  past 16 GB. Ollama then silently offloads layers to system RAM and generation
  crawls — a slowdown, not a clean failure. So **predict and route before sending**,
  and keep a reactive catch as a backstop.

## Step 1 — install the two models (internet is available now)

    ollama pull huihui_ai/qwen3-abliterated:14b     # ~9.0 GB, Q4_K_M — primary reasoning
    ollama pull huihui_ai/qwen3-abliterated:8b      # ~5.0 GB, Q4_K_M — fallback (small weights leave room for a big KV cache)

Confirm both load and answer:

    ollama run huihui_ai/qwen3-abliterated:14b "say ok"
    ollama run huihui_ai/qwen3-abliterated:8b  "say ok"

(The operator asked for `huihui-ai/Qwen3-8B-abliterated`; that is the Hugging Face
repo id. The Ollama tag above is its equivalent. If you prefer higher fallback
quality over headroom, use `:8b-q8_0` (~8.7 GB) instead — but Q4 is the safer
fallback because the point of falling back is to free VRAM for the KV cache.)

Wire them in as the **GPU chat preference**, ahead of the current entries, in
`router.py`'s `GPU_MODELS` (keep the existing ones as later fallbacks so nothing
breaks if a pull is missing):

    GPU_MODELS = ["huihui_ai/qwen3-abliterated:14b", "huihui_ai/qwen3-abliterated:8b",
                  "equal-shares-gpu", "equal-shares", "qwen2.5-coder:14b", ...]

Define the pair as named constants so the routing logic and the model list share one
source of truth:

    GPU_PRIMARY_MODEL  = "huihui_ai/qwen3-abliterated:14b"
    GPU_FALLBACK_MODEL = "huihui_ai/qwen3-abliterated:8b"

chunks.text:

                  "equal-shares-gpu", "equal-shares", "qwen2.5-coder:14b", ...]

Define the pair as named constants so the routing logic and the model list share one
source of truth:

    GPU_PRIMARY_MODEL  = "huihui_ai/qwen3-abliterated:14b"
    GPU_FALLBACK_MODEL = "huihui_ai/qwen3-abliterated:8b"

## Step 2 — Strategy 1: predictive context-length routing (primary mechanism)

Before each GPU turn, estimate the prompt's token count and pick the model:

- Add a token estimator (stdlib, no downloads). A conservative
  `estimate_tokens(messages) -> int` — sum the characters of every message's content
  (and note images add a fixed per-image cost) and divide by ~3.5, rounding up — is
  enough; label it an estimate, not exact. Do **not** add a tokenizer dependency.
- Add `DYNAMIC_SWITCH_TOKENS = 16000` as a tunable constant, with a comment tying it
  to the budget: 14B Q4 (~9 GB) + OS overhead leaves roughly 5–6 GB for KV; ~16K
  tokens is where a 14B KV cache starts to threaten the 16 GB ceiling.
- In `router.decide()` (or a helper it calls), when the tier is **GPU** and both the
  primary and fallback are installed: if `estimate_tokens(history) > DYNAMIC_SWITCH_TOKENS`
  choose `GPU_FALLBACK_MODEL`, else `GPU_PRIMARY_MODEL`. If only one is installed,
  use it. CPU tier is unchanged. Record the choice and the estimate on the
  `Decision` (e.g. `detail["dynamic"] = {"est_tokens": N, "picked": model, "threshold": 16000}`)
  so the GUI route line can show it.
- Coordinate with num_ctx: when the 14B is chosen, cap its `num_ctx` so the KV cache
  cannot blow the budget (e.g. clamp to ≤ 16384 unless the operator's GUI value is
  lower); the 8B may use a larger `num_ctx`. Keep honoring the GUI num_ctx control
  as the ceiling, not a floor.

## Step 3 — Strategy 2: reactive fallback (backstop)

Wrap the model call in `agent.answer()` (and `draft_prompt()`), so a load/OOM/timeout
on the primary transparently retries the **identical** prompt on the fallback:

- Catch `OllamaUnavailable`, HTTP 500 from `/api/chat`, load failures, and timeouts.
- On catch: emit a `note` event ("14B unavailable/over VRAM — retrying on 8B"),
  `router.unload(GPU_HOST, GPU_PRIMARY_MODEL)` to free the card, then re-issue the
  same messages against `GPU_FALLBACK_MODEL` once. If the fallback also fails, surface
  a clean `error` — never a stack trace.
- Only one downgrade step (14B → 8B), never a loop. If already on the 8B, do not
  retry the 8B against itself.

chunks.text:

  `router.unload(GPU_HOST, GPU_PRIMARY_MODEL)` to free the card, then re-issue the
  same messages against `GPU_FALLBACK_MODEL` once. If the fallback also fails, surface
  a clean `error` — never a stack trace.
- Only one downgrade step (14B → 8B), never a loop. If already on the 8B, do not
  retry the 8B against itself.

## Step 4 — model lifecycle (avoid VRAM contention between the two)

- Do not keep both resident. Before loading the fallback, unload the primary
  (`keep_alive:0` via the existing `router.unload`). Set a short `keep_alive` on chat
  requests (e.g. via options) so the inactive model releases VRAM quickly and the
  other can load — consistent with the project's one-inference-model-at-a-time rule.
- The existing render-yield behavior stays: a live render still forces the CPU tier
  and evicts any resident GPU model. This feature only changes *which* GPU chat model
  is chosen when the GPU is free.

## Constraints

- Stdlib only; no tokenizer or framework dependency. Server stays on `127.0.0.1`.
- `agent.answer()` stays transport-agnostic (history list + callback).
- Never weaken `gpu_busy()` / the "unknown GPU = busy" fail-safe. One GPU owner ever.

## Verify before claiming done (show commands + output)

Mockable, no live GPU needed:

1. `python local_agent/test_native_tool_calling.py` → still green.
2. New stdlib test (mock `router._tags` so both models look installed, and patch
   `estimate_tokens`): history under the threshold routes to the 14B; history over it
   routes to the 8B; only-one-installed routes to that one; CPU tier unaffected.
3. New stdlib test: patch the model call to raise on the primary and succeed on the
   fallback — `agent.answer()` emits the `note`, calls `unload` on the primary, and
   returns the fallback's reply; a primary success never triggers a downgrade.

Live checks to hand back to the operator (need real Ollama/GPU — mark unverified):
both pulls succeed and answer; a long (>16K-token) conversation actually loads the 8B
and a short one loads the 14B (watch `ollama ps` and the GUI route line); forcing the
14B to OOM triggers the reactive downgrade with generation still completing on the 8B.

## Record it (mandatory)

Write `CHANGELOG/<today>_dynamic_model_fallback.md` in the same session — the five
required answers (what/why/evidence/verified-after/still-unverified) with the test
output pasted — then add its row to `CHANGELOG/README.md` and note the new models and
routing in `local_agent/README.md`.

chunks.text:
# Claude Code / Codex prompt — the native Android local-agent app over Reticulum

Paste into your coding agent. Run from the repo root
(`COMFYUI_STORY_HANDOFF_2026-08-09/`). This is the `ROADMAP.md` end goal: a real
Android app that is a **thin client onto the workstation agent** over a Reticulum
mesh — the phone contributes camera, mic, and its own files; **all model compute
stays on the RTX 5080.** Read `local_agent/ROADMAP.md`, `local_agent/README.md`,
`CLAUDE.md`, and `local_agent/UPGRADE/06b_phone_app.md` before anything.

This is the largest piece in the project and spans multiple sessions. It is built
in **phases with STOP gates** — do not skip ahead. Each phase ends with a
`CHANGELOG/` entry and, where noted, operator approval before the next begins.

## Non-negotiables (from ROADMAP.md — hold these across every phase)

- **`server.py` stays bound to `127.0.0.1`.** Reticulum is the remote transport.
  **Never** bind `0.0.0.0` to reach the phone — an unauthenticated, tool-executing
  HTTP server must never touch a shared network.
- **`agent.answer()` stays transport-agnostic** (history list + event callback,
  no HTTP knowledge). That seam is where the Reticulum transport plugs in.
- **`store.py` stays transport-agnostic** plain JSON. A chat started on the phone
  and continued on the desktop is the same file. Add a `source` field
  (`desktop`|`phone`) on messages; add nothing that assumes one client.
- **`tools.py` remains a fixed whitelist.** Once a phone can reach the agent, the
  whitelist *is* the security model. Never relax it for convenience.
- **Per-identity permissions.** A remote phone identity and the desktop operator
  are not equal. Reads/chat/attachments from the phone are fine; `write_file`,
  `run_build`, and any render proposal from a phone identity require an explicit,
  logged allow decision. Default deny for state-changing tools from remote peers.
- **No model on the phone.** Ever. The handset is a terminal.

## Phase 0 — research + stack decision spike (MANDATORY; STOP at the end)

The roadmap forbids designing this from memory. Before writing app code, verify
against **current** documentation and record findings in
`local_agent/UPGRADE/notes/android_stack_decision.md`:

1. **Reticulum (`RNS`)** — current Python API for creating a node, announcing a
   destination, and request/response + link streaming. Source: reticulum.network
   manual and the `markqvist/Reticulum` repo.
2. **`LXMF`** — whether the agent link should be LXMF messages (store-and-forward,
   good for slow/interrupted links) or a raw RNS `Link` with resource transfer,
   or both (LXMF for turns, Link for live token streaming). Decide and justify.
3. **Sideband / `sbapp`** — the existing Android LXMF client
   (`markqvist/Sideband`, `sbapp` on PyPI), built with **python-for-android /
   buildozer** (Kivy). Determine whether to: (a) **fork/extend Sideband**,
   (b) build a **new Python-on-Android app** reusing its p4a + RNS packaging, or
   (c) a **Kotlin app embedding RNS via Chaquopy**. Note that the reference
   Reticulum stack is Python — a pure-Kotlin RNS reimplementation is out of scope.
4. **Android toolchain** — what the build actually needs on this Windows box
   (JDK, Android SDK/NDK, buildozer under WSL or Android Studio + Gradle, a device
   or emulator). Internet is available; list exact install steps, do not run them
   yet.

Output a one-page recommendation with the chosen stack and why, the transport
decision (LXMF vs Link vs hybrid), and the build environment plan. **Then STOP and

## Phase 1 — the workstation transport seam (no Android yet)

Make the existing desktop agent reachable over Reticulum without changing its HTTP
behaviour:

- Define a small transport interface that wraps `agent.answer(history, on_event,
  ...)`. Prove it by routing the **existing GUI through it unchanged** (desktop
  experience identical — verify).
- Add `local_agent/reticulum_node.py`: starts an RNS node, loads/creates a
  persistent workstation **identity**, announces the agent destination, and for
  each inbound request builds the history and calls `agent.answer`, streaming
  events back over the chosen transport (chunked/resumable — a mesh link is not a
  low-latency socket; do not assume a held-open stream).
- Add the **per-identity permission layer**: an allowlist of paired phone identity
  hashes with a capability set each; enforce it in the tool-dispatch path so a
  remote identity cannot invoke a gated tool. Log every remote tool call with the
  caller identity.
- Add the `source` field to messages in `store.py`.
- Keep it all off by default — the node only runs when the operator starts it, and
  binding stays `127.0.0.1` for HTTP throughout.

CHANGELOG the seam + node + permission layer, with the tests below.

## Phase 2 — prove it with a CLI peer (STOP at the end)

Before any app: `local_agent/reticulum_cli_peer.py`, a headless RNS client that
pairs with the workstation node (by identity hash), sends a prompt, and prints the
streamed reply and any tool events. Run it from a second machine (or a second RNS
instance locally). This proves transport, identity pairing, streaming, and the
permission gate end to end. **STOP and confirm the link works before writing the
app.**

## Phase 3 — the Android app (chat → files → camera/mic, in that order)

Build per the approved Phase 0 stack. Land it incrementally, each a CHANGELOG:

1. **Chat client** — pair with the workstation identity (scan a QR of the identity
   hash or paste it), one conversation list backed by the *workstation's* store
   (the phone shows what the desktop shows; conversations are the same files),
   send/receive with streaming, offline/queued sends over LXMF when the link
   drops. A background service keeps the RNS connection; a local notification
   fires when a long generation completes so the operator can lock the screen.
2. **Phone file access** — this is the capability the PWA (06b) could not give:
   true handset filesystem access via Android's Storage Access Framework / scoped
   storage, so the operator can pick *any* file (not just push a share) and send
   it as an attachment; large files transfer as RNS resources with a size cap and
   clear progress. Uploads land on the workstation in `local_agent/uploads/`
   (path passed to tools, never binary in conversation JSON — same rule as 06b).
3. **Camera + mic as agent inputs** — capture a photo/video → vision tool; record
   audio → the workstation's local Whisper (never a cloud speech API). Until a
   given model exists, the control says what is missing and its size (the honesty
   rule from upgrades 4 and 06b). Respect Android runtime permissions.

Security in the app: the phone holds only its own RNS identity and the paired
workstation hash; no project secrets on the handset. State-changing tools obey the
Phase 1 permission gate — surface a clear "not permitted from phone" rather than a
silent failure.

## Verify (per phase — show commands/output; say what is live vs mocked)

- Workstation stdlib tests still green (`test_native_tool_calling.py`,
  `test_media_analysis.py`) — the seam must not regress them.

  full turn; `agent.answer` still knows nothing about transport.
- `validate_h3_prompt.py` still **124/124**.

  round-trip; app pairs and chats; a picked phone file reaches `uploads/`; camera
  photo → vision; mic → local Whisper; completion notification on a locked screen;
  desktop GUI unchanged throughout.

- Never weaken a safeguard to pass a test. Whitelist stays a whitelist; the

the handset) — not a script. Recommend whether forking Sideband beats building

chunks.heading: # Claude Code / Codex prompt — the Android local agent by building on Sideband
chunks.text:
# Claude Code / Codex prompt — the Android local agent by building on Sideband

Paste into your coding agent. Run from the repo root
(`COMFYUI_STORY_HANDOFF_2026-08-09/`). Read `local_agent/ROADMAP.md`,
`local_agent/README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and `local_agent/UPGRADE/06b_phone_app.md`
first.

## The idea (why this is the path that actually works with the local agent)

**Sideband** (`markqvist/Sideband`, `sbapp` on PyPI) is an existing, mature Android
client for **LXMF over Reticulum** — it already does identity, pairing, the mesh
transport, message store-and-forward, and Android packaging. We do **not** rebuild
any of that. Instead we make the **workstation agent speak LXMF**, so:

- **Tier A — works with a stock Sideband app, no Android build.** The workstation
  runs the local agent as an **LXMF peer** (a Reticulum destination that receives a
  message, runs `agent.answer`, and replies). The operator adds that peer in a
  normal Sideband install on the phone and chats with the local agent immediately.
- **Tier B — a forked Sideband build for the agent extras.** Only once Tier A works,
  fork Sideband to add what a generic LXMF client lacks: sending **phone files** to
  the workstation `uploads/`, **camera → vision**, **mic → local Whisper**, and
  richer streaming/tool-event display — reusing Sideband's Reticulum stack and its
  python-for-android/buildozer packaging rather than writing an app from scratch.

The phone never runs a model. All compute stays on the RTX 5080. The handset is a
terminal.

## Non-negotiables (from ROADMAP.md — hold these throughout)

- `server.py` stays bound to **`127.0.0.1`**. LXMF/Reticulum is the remote
  transport; **never** bind `0.0.0.0`.
- `agent.answer()` stays transport-agnostic (history + event callback, no HTTP).
  The LXMF bridge calls it exactly like the GUI does.
- `store.py` stays transport-agnostic plain JSON; a chat from the phone and one from
  the desktop are the same files. Add a `source` field (`desktop`|`phone`) on
  messages.
- `tools.py` stays a fixed whitelist — the security model once a phone can reach in.
- **Per-identity permissions.** Map each paired phone LXMF identity to a capability
  set. Reads/chat/attachments from the phone are fine; `write_file`, `run_build`,
  and render proposals from a phone identity are **default-deny** and require an
  explicit, logged allow. Log every remote tool call with the caller identity.

## Phase 1 — the workstation LXMF agent bridge (Tier A; no Android work)

- `local_agent/lxmf_agent.py`: start an RNS + LXMF node, load/create a persistent
  workstation identity, announce an "agent" destination. On an inbound message from
  a **paired** identity: rebuild the conversation from `store.py`, call
  `agent.answer(history, on_event, ...)`, and send the reply back over LXMF (chunk
  long replies per the Phase 0 decision). Unpaired identities get a one-line "not
  authorised" and nothing else.
- Reuse the exact agent path the GUI uses — do **not** duplicate agent logic. Add
  the `source="phone"` tag when persisting phone-originated turns.
- Add the **per-identity permission layer** in the tool-dispatch path so a phone
  identity cannot invoke a gated tool; log every remote tool call.
- Pairing: a tiny operator step on the desktop to add a phone's LXMF identity hash
  to the allowlist with its capabilities (a CLI or a small GUI field). Keep HTTP on
  `127.0.0.1`; the bridge is opt-in and only runs when started.
- A launcher entry (or documented command) to start the bridge alongside the server.

**Acceptance for Tier A:** from a **stock Sideband install** on the phone (or a
second Sideband/CLI LXMF client), the operator sends a message to the announced
agent destination and gets the agent's reply; a non-allowlisted identity is refused;
a gated tool from the phone is denied and logged; the desktop GUI is unchanged. CHANGELOG it.

## Phase 2 — forked Sideband for the agent extras (Tier B; after Tier A works)

Fork/extend Sideband (per the Phase 0 decision), reusing its Reticulum transport and
packaging. Land incrementally, each a CHANGELOG:

1. **Send phone files to the agent** — pick any file via Android storage and send it
   as an LXMF attachment/field; the bridge writes it to `local_agent/uploads/`
   (path to tools, never binary in conversation JSON — the 06b rule) and routes
   images → vision, audio/video → transcribe/audio_measure.
2. **Camera → vision, mic → local Whisper** — capture and send; transcription runs on
   the workstation's Whisper, never a cloud speech API. Until a model exists, the
   control names what is missing and its size (the honesty rule from upgrades 4 /
   06b).
3. **Agent-aware display** — show tool/route events and chunked streaming so a long
   generation reads well on the phone; a local notification when it completes.

Keep Sideband's normal LXMF messaging intact; the agent is an added peer type, not a
replacement. No project secrets on the handset — it holds only its RNS identity and
the paired workstation hash.

- Workstation stdlib suites still green (`test_native_tool_calling.py`,

- New tests (mock LXMF/RNS I/O): a paired identity streams a full turn; an unpaired
  identity is refused; a gated tool from a phone identity is denied; `agent.answer`
  still knows nothing about transport.
- Live checks (need real RNS + a device — mark unverified until run): stock Sideband
  round-trip in Tier A; forked build installs and sends a file/camera/mic capture in
  Tier B.

## Rules that hold (CLAUDE.md / ROADMAP.md)

Never weaken a safeguard to pass a test; whitelist stays a whitelist; GPU-busy check
keeps failing safe; never bind `0.0.0.0`. Never start a render from the phone
(propose only, and only if permitted). Never delete a raw generation, reference,
manifest, audit record, or source media. Every phase ends with a `CHANGELOG/` entry
(what/why/evidence/verified/unverified) and its new files added to
`local_agent/README.md`.

## Note to the operator up front

State in the Phase 0 note: **Tier A gives a working phone agent through a stock
Sideband install with no Android build at all** — do that first and confirm it
before any fork. Tier B (the fork) needs an Android toolchain and a device, and
should reuse Sideband rather than rebuild its Reticulum stack.

chunks.text:
# Claude Code / Codex prompt — resource + safety hardening (five items)

> **Source preserved from Google Drive (2026-08-24):**
> [`12_resource_and_safety_hardening.md`](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1sgMlp75p1Y6OysP3laKDXaX5OexP1HS5O1uLAItEhGU/edit?usp=drivesdk).

Paste into your coding agent. Run from the repo root
(`COMFYUI_STORY_HANDOFF_2026-08-09/`). Read `local_agent/README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`,
`local_agent/router.py`, `local_agent/ollama_client.py`, `local_agent/media_watcher.py`,
`local_agent/media_queue.py`, and `local_agent/tools.py` first. **Do not touch the
render pipeline or `outputs/equal_shares/**`.** Stdlib only — no FastAPI, Pydantic,
Chroma, or any new dependency. Each job below is independent; land and CHANGELOG
each one. Verify with the existing suites plus the new tests noted; keep
`validate_h3_prompt.py` at **124/124** throughout.

## Job 1 — explicit `keep_alive` so models release VRAM promptly

**Built 2026-08-25.** Interactive chat retains its selected model for five
minutes; non-interactive Ollama planning and vision calls explicitly use zero
retention. Regression coverage verifies the API payload.

Today `keep_alive` is only used inside `router.unload()` (`:0`); every normal chat
and vision request uses Ollama's default **5-minute** retention, so a model can sit
in VRAM and delay a render launch.

- Add a `keep_alive` parameter through `ollama_client.chat` / `chat_stream` into the
  `/api/chat` and `/api/generate` payloads (default: unset = Ollama default).
- **Non-interactive callers pass a short window** or `0`: the media watcher
  (`_vision` path), the batch/queue processing, and standalone Whisper. Interactive
  desktop chat keeps a **modest** window (e.g. `"5m"` or `"2m"`) so the operator
  does not eat a reload on every message — do not set interactive chat to `0`.
- Where a queued job finishes and nothing else is pending, the watcher still
  explicitly `router.unload()`s (existing behaviour) — belt and suspenders.

Test (mock the HTTP post): a watcher/queue request carries the short `keep_alive`;
an interactive chat request carries the modest one; the value reaches the payload.

  explicitly `router.unload()`s (existing behaviour) — belt and suspenders.

Test (mock the HTTP post): a watcher/queue request carries the short `keep_alive`;
an interactive chat request carries the modest one; the value reaches the payload.

## Job 2 — quantized KV cache to reclaim VRAM at 32K

**Harness built; live measurement blocked on the exact 14B model.** See
`measure_ollama_kv_cache.py` and UPGRADE 18. Do not enable this setting until a
baseline and candidate report are recorded.

A 32K KV cache on an 8B–14B model is ~2–4 GB. Ollama can shrink it with
flash-attention + a quantized K/V cache — a **server-level** setting, not per
request.

- In `START_LOCAL_AGENT_GUI.ps1` (and any other place the GPU Ollama server is
  launched), set before `ollama serve`: `OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION=1` and
  `OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0`. Do this only for the **GPU** server; leave the CPU
  server default.
- **Measure, do not assume.** With it on, load the 14B at its 20480 context, read
  `nvidia-smi`, and record the VRAM delta vs off in the CHANGELOG. If q8_0 hurts
  answer quality noticeably, note it and fall back to f16 cache (still with flash
  attention). Confirm a render can still launch alongside the resident model.
- Document the tradeoff in `local_agent/README.md`: quantized KV saves VRAM, needs
  flash attention, and slightly lowers cache precision.

(No unit test — this is config + a measured VRAM figure. The measurement IS the
evidence.)

## Job 3 — mid-job render pre-emption in the media watcher

**Built 2026-08-25.** `MediaPreempted` is checked between video analysis frames
and action-extraction batches. The watcher requeues the same job with a
timestamped pre-emption record rather than failing it, then releases its VLM.

`media_watcher.py` checks `router.gpu_busy()` **before** loading a model but cannot
stop once a vision pass is running. Add cooperative pre-emption:

- Between queued items — and between frames within an `analyze_video` job — re-check
  `router.gpu_busy()`. If a render has claimed the card (queue owner / port 8188),
  **abort the in-flight Ollama request**, `router.unload()` the vision model, and
  **requeue the current job as pending** (do not mark it failed — it was pre-empted,
  not broken). Log a clear "pre-empted by render" line.
- The abort must be cooperative and clean: stop consuming the stream / close the
  request; never kill the render. One GPU owner ever; the render always wins.
- Guard against thrash: after a pre-emption, the watcher waits for the GPU to be
  free again (its normal poll) before reloading.

Test (mock `gpu_busy` to flip to True mid-drain): the current job returns to
`pending/`, the model is unloaded, and no partial result is written to `done/`.

- Guard against thrash: after a pre-emption, the watcher waits for the GPU to be

Test (mock `gpu_busy` to flip to True mid-drain): the current job returns to

## Job 4 — `propose_file_diff` tool (review before write)

**Built 2026-08-25.** The native tool returns a unified diff without writing;
it has the same protected-file refusal as `write_file`. Conversation rules now
require preview-before-apply.

For coding tasks the agent can call `write_file` directly. Add a safer default:

- New tool `propose_file_diff` in `tools.py`: given a path and proposed new content,
  return a **unified diff** (`difflib.unified_diff`) against the current file
  **without writing anything**. Same path guards as `write_file` (protected files
  refused; no traversal).
- Update `CONVERSATION_RULES`/tool guidance: for a file edit, **propose the diff
  first**; `write_file` applies it only after the operator sees it. Mirrors the
  project's existing "propose, don't auto-run" stance for builds/renders.

Test: `propose_file_diff` returns a correct unified diff and leaves the file
unchanged on disk; a protected path is refused; the schema is registered.

## Job 5 — interactive vs batch priority in the media queue

**Built 2026-08-25.** Queue records carry `interactive` or `batch` priority.
Direct desktop media requests are interactive; the watcher uses stable FIFO
within a tier and drains interactive jobs before batch work.

`media_queue.py` drains in arrival order. Add a priority tier so a live phone
photo/voice note is not stuck behind background frame extraction:

- Add a `priority` field to each job: `"interactive"` or `"batch"` (default
  `"batch"`). Phone-originated / live captures and direct operator `see_image` /
  `analyze_video` calls enqueue as `"interactive"`; bulk/background work as
  `"batch"`.
- The watcher's claim-next picks the **oldest `interactive` job first**, then oldest
  `batch`. Keep it stable (FIFO within a tier) — no starvation logic needed yet, but
  note in the code that a future change may age batch jobs up.

Test: with mixed jobs queued, claim order is all interactive (oldest→newest) then
batch; the field persists across the atomic move between queue dirs.

One `CHANGELOG/<today>_resource_safety_hardening.md` covering all five (or one entry
per job if you prefer), each answering what/why/evidence/verified/unverified — with
the Job 2 VRAM measurement pasted. Add the row(s) to `CHANGELOG/README.md` and note
the new tool + queue field + KV setting in `local_agent/README.md`.

chunks.heading: # Claude Code / Codex prompt — uncensored image + reference + storyboard generator
chunks.text:
# Claude Code / Codex prompt — uncensored image + reference + storyboard generator

Paste into your coding agent. Run from the repo root
(`COMFYUI_STORY_HANDOFF_2026-08-09/`). This builds the project's stated core goal:
**feed a story in → get a character-locked storyboard of reference images out**,
with a **reference-image overview for approval before mass generation**, wired into
the existing MiniMax H3 video pipeline.

Read first: `local_agent/README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`,
`work/batch_render_folder.py`, `work/render_single_pass.py` (or the current single-
render path), `work/thermal_guard.py`, `docs/reference/MINIMAX_PROMPT_GUIDE_ref.md`,
and how `outputs/equal_shares/runtime/render_queue_owner.json` is claimed. Internet
is available (downloads allowed). **Do not touch `outputs/equal_shares/**`** — image
output lives in its own tree.

## Target stack (decided; confirm availability in Phase 0)

- **Workhorse base (bulk storyboard):** a photoreal **SDXL** checkpoint —
  **RealVisXL V5.0** or **Juggernaut XL (Ragnarok)**. Fast (~4–6 s/1024px), ~8 GB,
  uncensored-friendly, best identity ecosystem.
- **Hero-frame tier (max realism):** **Chroma1-HD** (FLUX-family, Apache, no safety
  alignment) or **FLUX.1-dev GGUF Q8**, ~12–13 GB.
- **Identity (looks like a real person, consistently):**
  - **Personal LoRA** trained via the installed **`kohya_ss`** — the accuracy/
    consistency backbone for recurring characters.
  - **InstantID + IPAdapter-FaceID** on SDXL (you already have `insightface`,
    `photomaker`, `reactor`) for zero-training drop-ins from one photo.
  - **PuLID** (`ComfyUI-PuLID-Flux-Chroma`) for the Chroma/FLUX tier.
- **Realism polish:** a Detail-Tweaker / skin LoRA (SDXL) or XLabs RealismLoRA (Flux).

## Hard rules (hold across every phase)

- **One GPU owner, ever.** This pipeline claims/respects the same render lock as the
  H3 pipeline (`render_queue_owner.json` + port 8188). It must never generate while
  an Equal Shares render or the audio pass owns the card, and it must yield the same
  way. Reuse `thermal_guard`.
- **Reference overview before mass generation** (the project's founding requirement):
  character reference sheets are generated and **presented for operator approval
  first**; full storyboard generation only proceeds on approval.
- **Consent boundary:** identity/likeness tools are for the operator's own likeness or
  a consenting adult only — never a minor, never a non-consenting real person. Put a
  one-line gate in the character-ingest step stating this; do not build face tooling
  that targets arbitrary scraped faces.
- Never delete a source photo, a generated frame, a reference sheet, or a manifest.
- Every phase ends with a `CHANGELOG/` entry (what/why/evidence/verified/unverified).
